They had designated viewing areas too, near the main ring. I’ll have a look on their website later, see what they specifically offer this year. Don’t want you ending up exhausted before lunchtime.      Oh, good thinking, Mum! That’d be brilliant. I’m happy to push him around a bit, but it’s a massive site. Speaking of massive... I’ve been looking at houses in Bournemouth, just idly, you know? And the prices… honestly! You wouldn't believe.      Bournemouth, eh? Always was pricey, that place. Used to go down there as a lad, on day trips. Fish and chips on the pier, that was the height of luxury. Used to be able to get a decent house in Southbourne for a few thousand back then. A  few  thousand!      Now it’s half a million for a two-bed terrace, if you're lucky. It’s madness. We’re lucky we got this place when we did, even though it needs… a bit of doing up.      That’s what I was thinking. You and Dad have a lovely garden, but moving all the furniture around last week… it was a nightmare! Seriously, how did you manage that sideboard? It felt like it weighed a ton.      Years of experience, love. Years of experience! And a very strong back in my youth. Though my back wasn't thanking me afterwards, I can tell you. It's like trying to shift the pyramids, some of that stuff.      It's mostly solid oak, isn’t it? Proper stuff. Speaking of shifting things, have you seen Mrs. Higgins' cat, Mittens? She’s been missing for two days.

...Honestly, the traffic getting here was  awful . Just gridlocked all the way from Northallerton. You’d think a Tuesday afternoon wouldn’t be so bad!      Aye, well, Thirsk’s getting busier, lass. All these southerners moving up, thinking they've discovered paradise. Paradise it is, mind, but it wasn’t  made  for this many cars. Did you manage to find a parking spot alright?      I nipped out and grabbed one for you, Mum. Right outside the bakery, actually. Thought we could grab a sausage roll… or maybe a Eccles cake for you?      Oh, you’re a star, lad. A sausage roll sounds lovely, thank you. Though, I do worry about all that pastry… still, a little treat won't hurt. Leo, how are you finding Thirsk? Quite a change from Newcastle, eh?      It's… quieter. A lot quieter. And loads of old people. No offence, Grandma!      Leo! Be polite. Thirsk has a lovely community spirit, and it’s nice and peaceful, isn’t it? It's good for concentrating on your schoolwork. How’s that history project coming along?      It's okay. We're doing the Reformation. It's really boring. Lots of dates and Kings and… arguments.      Ah, the Reformation! A turbulent time, that. All that theological wrangling… a right mess, if you ask me. Trying to define God, eh? As if  we  could manage that.      It's fascinating stuff when you get into the politics of it, though. Henry VIII, purely self-serving, breaking with Rome for a divorce. Still ripples through things today. Speaking of ripples, have you seen what’s happening on Twitter? Apparently, old Mr. Henderson from the church has started a whole debate about the proper length of hymns.      No! Seriously? Mr. Henderson? He's the most staunch traditionalist I know! He'll be wanting us all back in ruffs and farthingales next.      Honestly, these young people and their… Twitter. It’s a wonder anyone has a sensible thought these days with all that noise. Still, I suppose if it keeps him occupied… He always did have a lot to say.      It's generated quite a following, apparently. People chiming in from all over. He’s got opinions on everything, that man.      Can I have my phone back now? I was checking out a gaming streamer.      After dinner, Leo. No screens at the table. Now, Mum, are you comfortable? Shall we talk about the move?

Honestly, teenagers. It's like communicating with aliens. Leo's been muttering about the dentist all morning, and when I actually  asked  him what was wrong, it was just… vague anxiety. Something about “the pointy things.”      Pointy things are scary. Like… vampire teeth!      Vampires aren’t real, Lily. Daddy says so. But the dentist  is  real, and he has pointy things.      That's… a surprisingly accurate summary, actually. He needs a check-up, it’s just a routine one. And I’ve booked him a hearing test too. Mrs. Davies at school mentioned he sometimes seems to miss instructions, and it’s worth ruling things out.      Does that mean he’ll have to wear headphones? Like when we watch films?      Possibly, yes. It’s not a big deal, sweetheart. It just checks how well he can hear different sounds. Speaking of things being a big deal – have you both remembered Ashaad’s birthday is next week?      Ashaad? Is that the boy who's really good at maths? He told me three times eleven yesterday!      That’s the one. He and Leo are best mates, remember? It’s tricky, isn't it? Because it's so close to your birthdays. All three of you bunched together like that... it makes it a bit chaotic.      I like chaotic! It means more cake.      You always do have your priorities straight, don’t you? We were talking about presents for Ashaad, and I was wondering if maybe a museum trip? He's really interested in art.      Can we go to a museum too? To see the Monet paintings? The ones with the water lilies and the blurry colours.      Maybe. We’ll see. Your school trip to the farm is coming up, isn’t it? That’ll be exciting.      Will there be chocolate eggs at the farm? It's nearly Easter!      Probably not  at  the farm, love. But we’ll have plenty here, don't worry. Although, I'm trying to limit the amount… all that sugar. Leo needs brain food for his maths homework, not a sugar rush.      He needs to stop worrying about the dentist and do his maths! Miss Thompson said he was a bit distracted today.      Precisely! See? Teenager mystery. It all ties together. He's worried about pointy things, and can't concentrate on fractions. It’s a vicious cycle.      Can we have radishes with our dinner? They look like little pink noses.

Honestly, it feels so weird being back here. Like stepping into a time capsule. Remember when we tried to redecorate this whole room with just blankets and fairy lights? Mum nearly had a fit.      Oh god,  nearly  doesn't cover it. She was incandescent! She said it looked like a student squat, and not in a cool, ironic way. Though, to be fair, it  did  smell slightly of stale pizza and desperation.      Desperation is the operative word. Uni life was… a vibe, but not always a practical one. Speaking of practical, how’s work going? Still battling with patients recovering from strokes and things? Sounds incredibly draining.      It is, but it’s also… rewarding, you know? Had a little win this week, actually. An older gentleman, had a really difficult time finding the words again after his stroke. We worked on some strategies, and yesterday he managed to tell his granddaughter he loved her, unprompted. Honestly, I nearly cried. It's those moments that make the paperwork and endless meetings worthwhile.      That’s amazing! Seriously. You always were the empathetic one. I remember you spent half of sixth form comforting Mark after his hamster died.      Don’t remind me! Hammy the hamster. A national tragedy, apparently. What about you? Copywriting still fulfilling the creative soul? Is it all just… slogans and social media posts?      It’s a bit of a mixed bag, to be honest. I landed a really good client last month – a local brewery actually, so I get to write all their beer descriptions. That’s fun. But a lot of it  is  churn-and-burn stuff, crafting clickbait headlines. It pays the bills though, and lets me save a tiny bit. Which, let's be real, is essential. Rent in London is a joke.      Tell me about it. I’m still living with Mum and Dad, which feels… adult-ish but also deeply embarrassing. I’m saving for a deposit, but it feels like I’m filling a bucket with a hole in the bottom. I keep calculating and recalculating, and it's always hopelessly far off.      Seriously. We need to invent a house-winning lottery or something. Mum’s been subtly hinting she wants grandchildren, which just adds to the financial pressure! Like, how am I going to afford a kid  and  a house?      Don't even get me started on the parent pressure. Dad cornered me last week and started listing potential blokes he’d “approve of.”

...Honestly, the sheer audacity of it! They wanted to put those solar panels right on Green Man Hill. Green Man Hill! It’s a landmark, you know. Used to cycle up there as a boy, all the way from Ramsgate. It felt like Everest, honestly. Proper cobbled streets leading up to it too, a real killer.      Oh, cycling. I remember my brother and I, we’d go miles on our bikes around Almondsbury. Not hills like that, thankfully, mostly lanes and fields. Though Dad did try to teach me to cycle properly  on  a hill once. Disaster, absolute disaster. Ended up in a ditch.      Sounds about right. A bit like my first few patients after qualifying. Speaking of qualifying… the NHS back then, you know? It wasn't just a job, it was… well, it had perks. Proper perks.      Perks like what, Arthur? Holiday camps at reduced rate? A free cup of tea?      Better than that, George! We had access to the Royal Naval sailing facilities. The rationale was, keeping your hand in with practical skills, maintaining dexterity... utter balderdash, really. But glorious! I remember one ‘lecture’ all at sea with your oral surgeon, battling a bit of a swell. Trying to explain the intricacies of root canal treatment while the boat pitched and rolled!      Incredible! It's all budget airlines and package tours these days. We were looking at Prague, actually. Found a deal, all inclusive, quite reasonable. Apparently, you can get around it remarkably easily.      Prague! Oh, I’ve heard it’s beautiful. I’ve always wanted to go. And you can get into practically anything, even if it’s ‘sold out’. A friend of mine went last year, used some kind of concierge service, bypassed all the queues for the theatre and the art exhibitions. Apparently, it’s a little… network.      A bit of ‘who you know’, then. That's the way of the world. Reminds me of trying to get a decent seat at the Free Trade Hall back in the 60s. Always needed a connection. Still, we're luckier than some. We've got the barn, haven't we?      That  is  lucky. A converted barn! Perfect for the jive night. It's going to be amazing. Old Mr. Henderson really did us a favour letting it out. It's not much to look at yet, needs a lot of work, but the space is fantastic. We're thinking of getting a proper sprung floor put in, for dancing.

…Right, so I’ve been playing with some ideas based on what we were talking about yesterday. The whole 'visual literacy' thing, and how kids – honestly,  everyone  – struggles to critically assess what they see online. It feels like a really potent gap.      Potent is a good word. It's terrifying how easily people accept things at face value now. Especially with the deepfakes getting so sophisticated. I was reading an article about one that fooled a whole news channel… honestly. But turning that anxiety into a business… how are you thinking we do that? Just materials for teachers?      That’s the initial thought, yeah. But I’m wondering if we could go further. Imagine a series of short, online 'case studies' - almost like mini-documentaries. Breaking down how a specific image or video  was  manipulated. Showing the layers, the techniques. Something visually engaging, not just a lecture. Like, "Deconstructing the Viral Meme," or "Spotting the Edited News Footage." We could build a subscription service for schools.      I like the case study idea  a lot . It feels much more… dynamic than a textbook chapter. And the titles are catchy. But are schools going to pay for something like this when there’s so much free stuff already out there, even if it's not great quality? That's always the hurdle.      Fair point. Which is where the ‘mini-doc’ angle comes in. We wouldn’t be relying on text. We’d be aiming for proper production value, clever editing, storytelling. Think something that  students  would actively want to watch and share. And maybe tiered subscriptions – basic access for free, more detailed breakdowns and downloadable resources for a fee?      That’s smart. And perhaps targeting different age groups. Primary schoolers might need something very different than high school students prepping for media studies. I’d be happy to contribute to the curriculum side of things, obviously. I've got a pretty good handle on what works in the classroom. What about leveraging social media? A TikTok account breaking down simplistic examples?      Ooh, I liked the TikTok idea! Short, punchy, could go viral. That’s you, by the way. You're much more savvy with that platform than I am. I'm still trying to figure out Reels. I was thinking we could also build a community forum. A place where teachers can share their own examples of misleading content they've encountered, and discuss how they've addressed it with their students.

Honestly, this is exactly what I needed. Just… walking, fresh air, not staring at a screen. Even if it  is  a bit bracing. Feels good to be away from marking essays for an hour.      Tell me about it. I think I’ve read the word ‘postmodernism’ so many times this week, it’s started appearing in my dreams. And don't even get me started on the referencing. It’s a nightmare. Remember Sarah complaining about her student citing Wikipedia?      Oh, goodness, yes! Poor Sarah. She was incandescent. Though, secretly, I think she found it a little bit amusing. It’s the principle, isn't it? Reminds me a bit of old Mr. Henderson, my history teacher at school. He'd have a fit if anyone tried to pull a fast one. He used to say history was like the sea – vast, powerful, and you couldn't just skim the surface.      That's a brilliant analogy, actually. The sea… it’s deceptive, isn't it? Looks calm one minute, completely raging the next. A bit like some of our students, really. All smiles and politeness until deadline week hits.      Exactly! And layered. So many hidden currents, things going on beneath the surface. Like when we went to Cornwall last summer? Remember that tiny cove near St Ives, the one with the smugglers’ tunnels?      How could I forget? You nearly tumbled down the rocks trying to get a better picture! I thought my heart had stopped. It was beautiful, though. That turquoise water… completely different to the grey North Sea you grew up with, wasn’t it?      Worlds apart. The North Sea was… moody. Dramatic, but unforgiving. You respected it, you didn't  play  with it. My grandad was a fisherman, you know. He always said the sea gave and the sea took. Said you had to be humble in its presence. He had stories… genuine, proper sea yarns. About storms, and lost ships, and… well, everything.      He sounds amazing. I always imagined your childhood being very… landlocked, given Norwich isn’t exactly a coastal city.      It's not. But we'd go to Cromer every summer. It was a proper seaside holiday – arcades, fish and chips, building sandcastles. And Grandad would always take me out on his boat, even when I was tiny. He'd let me ‘help’ with the nets, which mostly involved getting tangled. He instilled a real awe for it in me, I think.

Ooh, look at that dress! Proper stunning, innit? Though… a bit much for a trip to Tesco, eh? It’s all sequins and feathers.      It  is  a bit extra. I think it’s meant to be, though. It’s a runway show, isn't it? They’re trying to push boundaries. It’s more about the art of it, really. Though, I agree. Practicality’s not exactly high on the list.      It’s interesting seeing how quickly trends cycle. Last season it was all minimalist chic, and now suddenly we’re back to maximalism. Remember when everything had to be beige?      Beige! Don't even  mention  beige. I had a beige phase in uni. Terrible. Mum kept buying me beige cardigans. Thought she was trying to blend me into the furniture! This is much more… lively. Still, I reckon it’s all about how you  wear  things, isn’t it? You could tone down something flamboyant with a really simple jacket and boots.      Definitely. It’s all about styling. I’ve been trying to get into more sustainable fashion lately, though, and it makes things harder. You can’t just hop on the latest trend when you’re trying to buy less, you know?      Oh, I feel that. I'm trying to shop my own wardrobe more. It’s amazing how many things you forget you own! I found a beautiful silk scarf last week that I hadn’t touched in ages. Completely changed an outfit.      Ay, that's a good shout. I’m terrible for that. I’ll buy something, wear it once, then shove it to the back of the wardrobe and forget about it. It’s a proper waste. I've been meaning to have a clear-out for ages… maybe after this weekend?      We should have a clothes swap! I’ve got a bunch of things I never wear anymore. And you always have good taste, even if you  do  occasionally fall for beige.      Oh, that’s a fantastic idea! I’d be all over that. I’ve got some dresses that haven’t seen the light of day since before teaching. Too… sparkly for the classroom, to be honest.      Brilliant! We can do it here, can't we? Plenty of space. And we can order a takeaway while we're at it. That sparkly dress sounds perfect for a night out though, you know?      Perfect! I’m free Saturday afternoon.

Honestly, Mum, this one of me with the wonky teeth and the oversized glasses… why did you  keep  this? It’s mortifying.      Oh, darling, don’t be silly. It’s a lovely picture! You were about seven, I think? And you were absolutely beaming. You were so proud of that gap tooth. Besides, it’s good to look back and remember… how far we’ve come, you know? It's a good reminder that awkward phases  do  pass.      Easy for  you  to say, you always looked amazing in photos. Seriously. You still do, by the way. Anyway, I’m trying to curate a selection for my photography project, and this is just… not the vibe. I'm trying for atmospheric, a bit moody, you know? Not “first grade school portrait”.      Atmospheric and moody at sixteen? Sounds a bit dramatic, doesn’t it? What’s the project  about  anyway? Still the Hastings coastline?      Yeah, mostly. But I'm trying to capture something beyond just pretty pictures of the beach. I want to show the… the loneliness of it sometimes. The way the light falls on empty benches, things like that. It feels a bit silly saying it out loud.      Silly? Not at all. That sounds really thoughtful. And ambitious. It’s good you’re trying to say something with your photos, not just taking pretty pictures. Speaking of things that feel silly saying out loud, I had Mrs. Henderson asking me today if I was feeling ‘challenged’ at work.      Challenged? At a receptionist job? What does that even  mean ?      Apparently, they’re trying to implement some new scheduling system. It's more complicated than rocket science, honestly. And old Mr. Peterson keeps calling asking for Brenda, who retired three years ago. It's… repetitive. But it pays the bills. It's just... sometimes I wonder if I should've stuck with my research.      You were a researcher? What did you research? I don't think you've ever told me.      Oh, various things. Mostly Victorian literature, actually. I did my Masters on the representation of fear in Gothic novels. It's funny, isn't it? Spending years dissecting fictional fears, and then having perfectly real ones of your own.      What fears? Not spiders, I hope. Because I will absolutely judge you.      No, no spiders. It's silly, really. Just… worrying about you. About you going to university, being away from home. I know you’re capable and bright, but the world is… a bit scary right now, isn’t it?

Honestly, Arthur, this application form is a  nightmare . They want to know my mother’s maiden name, my primary school headteacher’s address… it’s ridiculous! What on earth does any of that have to do with joining a gardening club?      Oh, they just like havin’ a nose, Doreen. Always do. Bureaucracy, innit? Just fill it in as best you can. Doesn't matter if you’re a tad off. No one checks. I never filled anything in properly in my life, and I managed alright.      Speaking of things no one checks… the state of the fence panel young Timmy next door ‘fixed’ is appalling. Honestly, it looks like a badger built it. He’s got potential, that lad, bright as a button in class, but…handiwork? Forget it.      Timmy? Oh, that one! He’s a handful. Little terror, bless him. Though I did have one once, little Lewis, who was just… constant motion. Used to climb the curtains. Drove his mother round the bend.      Sounds like my nephew, back in the day. Always climbin' things. Ended up a chimney sweep, he did. Odd profession, that. Reminds me, there's a right racket goin’ on outside. That cockerel of Mrs. Peterson’s is at it again. Cock-a-doodle-doo at half past seven in the mornin’. Trying to get a lie-in is impossible!      You’re lucky to get  any  sleep, Arthur. You mentioned last week you were struggling, were you not?      Aye, not sleepin’ well. Keeps me mind racin’. Thinkin’ about the football mostly. Norwich were dreadful on Saturday, absolutely dreadful. Three-nil down at half-time…a disgrace.      Oh, don’t get me started. My grandson, Charlie, tried to explain VAR to me last week. I told him, “I just want to watch the footie, not study for a law degree!” It’s ruined the game, it has. Reminds me, Charlie’s birthday is next month. I was thinking of getting him one of those… what are they called… 3D printers?      Smart. They’re quite good fun. I’ve been messing around with one at school, trying to get the kids to design things for the science fair. Mostly they just print pointless plastic dinosaurs, though.      Dinosaurs, eh? Now there’s a thought. I was lookin’ at houses online yesterday. Down in Suffolk. Lovely little cottage, but the photos showed the plaster was crackin’ in several places. Just… awful workmanship.

…and honestly, the thought of her navigating the NHS on her own gives me palpitations. It's just  different  over there, you know? Everything is so…streamlined in Australia, efficient. Here, well, you need a PhD in bureaucracy just to get a doctor’s appointment. You always did exaggerate, Moira. Though, you’ve got a point. It's not exactly renowned for its speed. But she’s a resourceful girl, your daughter, always has been. She managed to build a life  in  Australia, didn’t she? That speaks volumes. It does, it does. But building a life is one thing, starting over is another. Especially when she's doing it to…well, to support  me , really. I feel awful about that. She was perfectly happy, established, with a good job…and now she’s uprooting everything to come and look after her dithering mother. Dithering? Now, that’s just harsh on yourself. You’re not dithering, you’re…adjusting. And she’s not doing it out of obligation, Moira. She  wants  to. She’s told me herself. She misses you dreadfully. And she’s worried, naturally. Worried about me, or worried I'll turn into a complete eccentric and start hoarding garden gnomes? Honestly, I've been having moments... moments where I consider buying a parrot just because it would be  something  to talk to. Oh, Moira. You are a character. No parrots, promise me. Though, honestly, having her here will be good for both of you. You’ll have company, someone to bounce ideas off, someone to actually  see  regularly. And she’ll have a base, a proper home. She’s been hopping between rentals for years. I know, I know. Logically, it makes perfect sense. But it feels…a burden. She's just completed that Masters, doesn't she deserve to enjoy it, to build her career  on  it? Not shelve it to deal with…this. My declining health, this awful feeling of uselessness… You’re not useless! You were a brilliant teacher, generations of children benefitted from your patience and wisdom. And look at the garden you've created! This house is  full  of your touch. It's not about what you  were  doing, it’s about what you are  now . And now you need a little help. It's not a sign of weakness, Moira, it’s a sign of strength to accept it. Easy for you to say, you’ve always been the practical one.

...Honestly, the whole thing with the Scottish referendum has left me feeling a bit drained. All that energy, all that debate…and for what? It feels like everyone’s just digging in their heels even further now. Did you catch any of the aftermath coverage, Arthur?      A bit, yes, a bit. Turned the news off after a while, to be honest. Too much shouting. It’s always the way, isn’t it? Regardless of the outcome, someone’s going to be unhappy. Still, I suppose it’s good they had the chance to voice their opinions. Reminds me a little of when they tried to reorganise the local education authority here years ago. A right kerfuffle, that was.      Brighton and kerfuffles, a classic combination, I imagine. Speaking of kerfuffles, did you hear anything more about the History department interview? They were saying they’d made a decision.      Oh, yes! Apparently, they went with Dr. Ainsworth. From York, wasn’t it? A bit of a surprise, I thought. I'd put money on old Professor Davies getting it. He's been angling for that Head of Department role for ages.      Really? That  is  a surprise. Ainsworth’s good, technically brilliant, but… a little lacking in the people skills department, wouldn’t you say? Davies might be a bit past it, but he at least knows how to navigate the politics of the place.      Exactly! Ainsworth strikes me as the sort who won't suffer fools gladly. Which, don’t get me wrong, isn't  bad , but… academic politics. You need a certain level of diplomacy. Anyway, I feel for Sarah. She was really hoping Davies would get it; they’re quite close.      Yes, poor Sarah. She’s been shouldering a lot lately, hasn't she? I saw her looking utterly exhausted in the staff room on Friday. It must be hard, trying to balance everything. How  is  she coping, actually?      She's… managing. It’s her daughter, Emily, really. Hasn't been sleeping properly since starting university. Worrying constantly about her settling in. It's the first time Emily’s been away from home, you see. Sarah’s constantly on the phone, trying to reassure her. A mother’s work is never done, is it?      Absolutely. My sister went through the same thing when her youngest went off to Leeds. She was a wreck for the first month, checking in every few hours!

Right, so, the critical element is the trigger mechanism. Honestly, building this mousetrap game is proving more complex than I anticipated. Remember that terrible fairground game where you had to hit the whack-a-mole things? It’s giving me those vibes – infuriatingly fiddly.      Fiddly is putting it mildly, Penelope. You've been muttering about 'spring constants' and 'projectile trajectories' for the last hour. It's a mousetrap game, not a NASA launch. Honestly, I thought you’d be finished by now.      Well, it  would  be finished if someone hadn't insisted on the 'realistic physics' angle! Realism isn't exactly key when you're trying to entertain a fourteen-year-old, David.      Speaking of entertaining, did you guys see that video of the kid in Florida trying to wrestle an alligator? Completely mental.      Nah, saw one where a kid built a whole miniature golf course in his backyard. Proper dedication. Americans are… different, aren’t they?      Different is one word for it. I spent three months volunteering at a library in Massachusetts a few years back. The sheer  scale  of everything is striking. And the children… they’re so… assertive.      Assertive? What do you mean?      Well, they weren't rude, not at all. But they'd just  tell  you what they wanted. No ‘please’ or ‘thank you’ initially. It was all direct requests. And so loud! It took some getting used to. It's not a bad thing, just… a different cultural norm, I think.      Sounds exhausting. I remember when we were in California, trying to get little Oliver to understand queuing etiquette. He kept trying to just… barge to the front. They just stared at us.      That's hilarious. I met a couple of American students during my year abroad in Berlin. They were absolutely obsessed with British tea and biscuits. Like, they'd bring bags of Walkers shortbread everywhere.      Walkers are good. They’re way better than those American cookies. Way too sweet.      Actually, talking about working abroad... I've been thinking about applying for that secondment to Washington D.C. next year. It's a long shot, obviously, with the cuts, but…      Washington? David, you? Our David, who gets anxious ordering a curry? That’s… ambitious.      Don't underestimate me, Penelope! It's a fascinating opportunity. And honestly, a year away from the office politics couldn't hurt. Plus, it would be good for Thomas to experience a different culture.

Right, operation ‘wardrobe refresh’ is… mostly complete. Prepare yourself.      Oh dear. That sounds ominous. And expensive. What have you done, Amelia? Don’t tell me you bought another silk scarf.      No scarves this time, though I  did  see a beautiful one. No, this is more… practical. And layered. It’s been so grey here lately, I felt like my clothes needed a bit of brightening up, you know? Plus, winter’s coming.      Practical and layered in Shanghai? You'll be boiling in November. Let me guess… cashmere jumpers? You always go for the cashmere when it gets even slightly chilly.      Okay, one cashmere jumper. A very soft, beautiful, oatmeal-coloured one. But honestly, it was on sale! And it’s versatile. I can wear it with jeans, a skirt… even over a dress, I suppose. But that's not the main event.      Oh? Do tell. What  is  the main event? Is it the shoes? Please don’t say it’s the shoes. Remember the incident with the red boots?      Those boots were fabulous! And these are… different. They're ankle boots, actually. A dark teal suede. They’re really comfortable, and they’ll go with almost everything. They finally had my size in the shop. It's been weeks I've been looking.      Teal suede? That's… bold. Not exactly subtle for navigating the metro. But if you like them…      They're more muted in person, honestly. And they'll look lovely with the new trousers I got. That's more of the main event, I think. I found this amazing tailor near the university, and I had a pair of wide-leg trousers made. Proper, high-waisted, slightly flared.      Made to measure? That sounds… expensive. And very you, actually. You’ve been talking about wanting a good pair of tailored trousers for ages. What fabric did you go with?      A charcoal grey wool. It’s beautiful, really. And the tailor was brilliant. She altered them  while  I was wearing them, which felt a bit strange but was incredibly effective. They fit perfectly. I'm thinking I can dress them up with a blouse and heels, or down with a chunky knit and the teal boots.      That does sound good. A really versatile piece. Better than another silk scarf, definitely. So, cashmere, teal suede, tailored trousers… anything else escaping the bags?      Oh, there’s a long-sleeved, floral print dress. It's a bit… flamboyant.

Go on, have another slice, Oisin. You barely touched your dinner, and you were roaring at the match like a proper banshee.      It was  amazing  though, Dad! That try by Bundee Aki? Unbelievable. Did you see the step?!      He was brilliant. Honestly, a bit of a game-changer. Though I was more worried when Johnny Sexton went down. Gave me a fright, he did.      Aye, a fright for all of us, hen. Johnny’s a good lad, a good leader. But they’ve got strength in depth now, thankfully. Used to be, if Johnny was off, you’d be fearing the worst.      That’s true, Maggie. They’ve really built a squad. Makes a difference. Speaking of building… Oisin, your birthday’s next week, isn’t it? Have you given any more thought to what you want?      I was thinking… a new rugby ball, maybe? Or one of those weighted vests the professionals use for training?      A weighted vest?! Oh, darling, isn’t that a bit… much? You’re eleven!      But I want to get stronger for the team! Mr. Davies is really pushing us hard in PE. We’re doing a lot of tackling drills now.      Mr. Davies, is it? Is he the one who's making you do all those press-ups? I heard tell he’s a taskmaster.      He  is . And running laps. It’s brutal. But it's good, I guess. We’re doing really well in the league.      Good for you, lad. Always good to put the effort in. I always told my wee ones, sport teaches you more than just how to kick a ball. Discipline, teamwork… all important life lessons.      Absolutely. And it keeps them active, which is the main thing. Although, honestly, watching them get tackled… makes  me  wince.      Right, Oisin, it's getting late. Past your bedtime, it is. You've got school tomorrow.      Aw, Dad! Just five more minutes? I want to finish talking about the match.      Five minutes, and then it’s straight to bed. No arguing. And maybe we can look at the stars a wee bit later, if the clouds clear. There's supposed to be a meteor shower.      Really?! A meteor shower? Cool!      That sounds lovely, actually. It’s been ages since I’ve seen a proper starry sky. City lights, you know? Makes it hard in London.      Aye, you need to get out into the countryside for a good view.

Honestly, the thought of unpacking  all  my books again is giving me actual palpitations. It’s not the furniture, it’s the books. They’re…sentient, I swear.      You and your books. You’d think after three moves, you'd be used to it. Though, I get it. A house isn’t a home until the bookshelves are full, right? How’s the new place shaping up, anyway? Did you manage to get the curtains up in the living room?      Mostly. It's…smaller than we anticipated, which is a learning curve. The curtains are up, yes, although one of the rails is a bit wonky and my partner, Ben, is convinced he can fix it. He'll probably just end up making it worse. It's cozy, though. And closer to the station, which is a massive win for my commute. Though, thinking about commutes… Aunt Carol keeps hinting that we should start  thinking  about…you know.      About expanding the family? Oh, Carol. She’s been on that bandwagon since we finished our degrees! Is Ben on board with this ‘thinking’?      He’s… diplomatic. He says we need to get settled first, which is fair. But she showed me pictures of her friend’s new grandchild this morning. Like, fourteen pictures. And then launched into a detailed explanation of how easy modern nappies are. It was a lot. What about you and Tom? Any baby plans brewing?      Definitely not yet! Tom's still obsessing over learning Mandarin. It's amazing how quickly he's picking it up, but he wants to be fluent before he even considers anything else. He says it’ll be good for Leo if we ever do have kids, to grow up bilingual. Which is a good point, I suppose. Though Leo’s already got a head start with your mum’s constant French chatter when she babysits!      Oh, Mum. She's convinced every child needs to be trilingual by the age of five. Although, she mostly corrects Leo's pronunciation of ‘bonjour’. It’s endearing, in a slightly terrifying way. Speaking of Leo, how's he doing? You said he had a slightly dodgy cough last week.      He's much better now, thankfully. Just a little cold. He’s at that age where he collects everything – leaves, stones, bits of fluff… you name it. It’s adorable, but I’m constantly on high alert for things ending up in his mouth.

Right, so you’re tellin’ me this bloke actually tried to argue with you about whether ‘Bath’ is pronounced ‘Bahth’ or ‘Basth’? Honestly, some people. It's  Bahth , innit? Absolutely  Bahth .      It was unbelievable, Liam. He’d lived in Bristol for five years! Five years steeped in West Country vowels, and he was insisting on ‘Basth’. I tried to explain the historical etymology, the influence of the Celtic substrate… you know, the full language teacher spiel.      Sounds exhausting, mate. Waste of breath, really. People ‘ear what they wanna ‘ear. Like tryin’ to tell old Man Hemmings that tetherin’ his dog up all day in that heat is cruel. Didn't bat an eyelid.      Old Hemmings is a character. Proper stubborn as a mule. Speaking of stubborn, I’m still trying to get my hands on a decent Les Paul. Been scouring eBay for weeks, but they’re either butchered or cost more than my van. You play anymore, Ben? Haven’t heard you pick up a guitar in ages.      Not as much as I used to, no. Honestly, marking essays takes up all my free time. And when I  do  have a bit of downtime, I’m usually trying to recover. My mate keeps trying to get me into MMA. Says it's a good stress reliever.      MMA? You? Seriously? You look like a strong breeze would knock you over, no offence.      None taken. The idea terrifies me, frankly. Though, he assures me it's about technique, discipline… learning to protect yourself. More important than anything these days, I reckon.      True enough. Seen a few dodgy characters lurkin' around town lately. Though my protection strategy usually involves a quick detour. You ever think about moving out of Bedford, Ben? Just... getting away?      I do. I’ve considered teaching English abroad, maybe in Spain. The thought of paella and sunshine… it’s appealing. Though my mum would have a fit. She's convinced Bedford is the center of the universe.      Spain’s alright. Went with me cousin, years ago. Too many tourists, though. And the blokes tryin' to sell you knock-off watches are relentless. Speaking of relentless, did you know Mrs. Davies is selling her greenhouse? Absolute bargain, apparently.      No way! How much? I've been meaning to get somethin' sorted for starting seedlings. My flat’s too small, and me mum keeps complainin’ about soil everywhere.      Don’t know the exact figure, but she said somethin' about needin’ the space for… well, she didn't say.

Right, so I was thinking… realistically, we  need  to talk about the car situation again. This commute is killing me. Three hours a day, just  gone . And honestly, my back is starting to hate me.      Here we go. I knew offering to make dinner was a trap. I thought we’d agreed to hold off on this until we’d at least saved another couple of hundred.      Hold off? Liam, we've been “holding off” for six months! Another couple of hundred won’t magically make a reliable car appear. And it's not just the commute, it's the cost. The train is extortionate, and even the bus feels like I’m throwing money away incrementally.      Okay, okay, you’re right. It's grim. But realistically, what are we even looking at? Everything is so expensive, and I still feel a bit weird about taking out a loan. Remember what happened with your brother and his fancy sports car?      Trust me, I remember. That was a disaster. But we’re not talking about a sports car! I’ve been browsing online, just looking at sensible things. Something small, fuel-efficient, and…reliable. I saw a few older Honda Civics going for around three thousand.      Three thousand… and then insurance, tax, MOT… it all adds up. I did a quick check on insurance for me adding a driver, and it jumped up quite a bit. I’m still on my dad’s policy for a lower rate, which helps, but…      It will still be cheaper than the train, I promise. And think about the freedom, Liam! We could actually  go  somewhere on weekends without needing to plan everything around train schedules. Remember that hiking trail we wanted to try in the Peak District?      Okay, you’re getting to me with the Peak District. You know I can’t resist a good hike. But realistically, can we even afford the upkeep? I’m still paying off that dodgy laptop for work, and you've got your student loan...      I’ve been looking at budgeting apps, honestly. And I'm picking up extra admin shifts at work when I can. I've already squirrelled away another £300 this month. We could aim for £500 a month towards a car fund, cutting back on…takeaways, maybe. And less impulse buying on Amazon. Guilty as charged on both counts.      So, you’re admitting your Amazon addiction is a problem?

Now then, lad, you’ve finished your A-Levels, haven’t you? Proper done, I hope? Don't tell me you've been spending all your time glued to that computer again. Your grandma keeps asking after your results!      Yeah, finished. And yeah, Grandma, I did alright. Got the grades I needed for uni. Thanks for asking, though. And I wasn’t  all  the time on the computer, honestly. Bit of gaming, a bit of research...      “Alright” doesn’t tell us owt, does it, Arthur? Was it a star, or a splodge? We want to know if our grand lad is going to be a doctor, or a… well, not a dustman, mind you. No offence.      Now, now, Elsie. A dustman’s an honest day’s work. Though I suppose university is a grand thing. Better than me and your mother’s days, eh? Just left school and straight to work in the docks. Hard graft, that was.      Speaking of work, this marking is relentless. GCSE papers this year are… well, let’s just say the standard isn’t what it was. Kids can’t even do basic fractions anymore! Honestly, it’s enough to make a person despair. I had one paper where the lad thought pi was 3.1416…  squared .      Seriously? Pi squared? That's… impressive in a terrible way.      Oh, dear. They don’t teach ‘em nothing anymore, do they? In my day, you knew your times tables off by heart. And you respected your teachers! None of this backchat.      Times tables are a dying art, Elsie. A dying art. Anyway, are you two comfortable? Can I get you another cup of tea? Perhaps a biscuit? I made some shortbread this morning. Though it might be a bit dry. I’m still getting the hang of this new oven.      Shortbread sounds lovely, lass. I’ll have one, thank you. Elsie here always says my sweet tooth will be the death of me.      It might be, Arthur! It just might. You’ve been enjoying those Werther’s Originals again, haven’t you? I found wrappers under your chair again this morning.      A man needs a little treat, Elsie. A little treat. After all these years with you, a man deserves a wee bit of sweetness in his life!      You two are terrible. Honestly.      Oh, they're enjoying themselves. It's good to see them happy. Now, young man, about university… have you sorted out accommodation yet?

Right, who wants more pirate-themed biscuits? Honestly, I think I’ve aged ten years just cutting out all those tiny swords and eye patches.      Me! Me! Look, Mummy, I drew Captain Bluebeard! He's  really  scary. He's got, like, a million gold coins!      Mine’s got a parrot. A really loud parrot that shouts “Pieces of Eight!” all the time.      Oh, wow, that  is  a fearsome Bluebeard, darling. And a lovely parrot! You’ve both been working so hard on your pirate pictures. It's almost as much effort as trying to explain Shakespeare to Year 5.      Shake-spear? Is he a pirate too?      No, sweetheart, not a pirate. He was a writer, a very,  very  famous writer. It’s Shakespeare Week at school, you know. We're doing Romeo and Juliet. Bit complicated for pirates, honestly. Although, there  is  a shipwreck in The Tempest... maybe we could link them?      Shipwrecks are cool. Do pirates have shipwrecks?      Oh, absolutely. Lots of shipwrecks. Filled with treasure, hopefully! Speaking of cool, guess what I was looking at?      What?! A real pirate ship?      Not quite. But I was looking at tickets to Stratford-upon-Avon. Shakespeare’s birthplace. We could go and see a play! Maybe  A Midsummer Night’s Dream .      Stratford? Is that far?      It’s a bit of a drive, but we could make a day of it. And think of all the Shakespeare-y things we could see. But… before that, something even  more  exciting is happening next week.      More exciting than meeting a real pirate?!      Potentially! Remember I told you about the circus workshop?      The one with the trapeze?      That’s the one! Well, it's not just  any  workshop; it’s being held in a real circus tent. A proper, travelling circus! They've got aerial silks, juggling equipment, everything.      Wow! Can I learn to fly on the silks?      You can definitely try! It'll be brilliant. It’s after Easter, so we’ll need to finish those Easter pictures first. We haven't even started decorating eggs yet.      I want to make an egg that looks like a treasure chest! With little jewels on top.      That's a fantastic idea! And after the circus, perhaps we can work on that stop-motion animation you’ve been talking about? The one with the Lego pirates?      Yes! And we can make them do magic tricks! Captain Bluebeard can make his gold coins disappear!

...Honestly, the whole thing was utterly ridiculous. They just didn’t  believe  I was attempting a legitimate sailing trip. Jeddah to Cyprus, in a little 22-footer! Can you imagine?      Goodness me, Arthur! Jeddah to Cyprus? That  does  sound… ambitious. Though, knowing you, probably beautifully planned in your head. What did they think you were up to? Smuggling?      Worse, apparently. Espionage! They kept muttering about international waters and sensitive areas. It was the height of the first Gulf War, you see. Security was… heightened, shall we say. They kept asking about my ‘connections’ - as if a retired geography teacher has shadowy contacts!      Connections? You? You barely managed to connect a map to reality half the time when I was at university, Arthur. No offence, old boy.      None taken, Brian! You always were a pedant. And I  did  have a detailed chart! I'd spent months plotting the course, accounting for currents… Honestly, the inefficiency of it all! Hours of questioning, then impounding the boat…      Impounding the boat? That sounds expensive. Was it insured?      Insured? For a trip like that? Don’t be daft, Reginald. I was a teacher, not a City banker! Eventually, after involving the British Consulate – a process that took another three days – they let me go. Said I was “naive.” Naive! I was trying to have an adventure!      I can imagine the frustration. You always were one for a challenge. It reminds me a bit of teaching in Saudi Arabia, actually. Everything was a challenge, navigating the cultural expectations. Though, thankfully, no arrests involved.      Ah, Saudi Arabia. You did that for how long, Margaret? Ten years wasn’t it? It’s a world away from Almondsbury, I imagine.      A world away, Brian. Absolutely. It was fascinating, immensely challenging, and… rather dry. That's the first thing you notice, the absolute lack of readily available alcohol. I mean, you could get it, of course. Through… other channels. Let's just say the diplomats were popular.      Diplomats always are. They’ve got access to everything. Reminds me of a trip to Iran many years ago. Impossible to get a drink anywhere. Ended up having to rely on… medicinal brandy. For a cough, naturally.      Medicinal brandy! A classic excuse, Reginald. I remember a similar situation in Morocco. Though, I think in that case, it was for 'blood pressure'.      It’s astonishing how adaptable we become when faced with a lack of something we're used to.

Honestly, the state of that bathroom this morning… It looked like a bomb had gone off. Hair everywhere, toothpaste splattered… you wouldn't believe it.      Oh, tell me about it! It’s a constant battle with teenagers, isn’t it? Remember when Michael was that age? The same. Absolutely the same. I’d find his socks  in  the sink. The sink, Fiona!      It wasn’t  that  bad.      Oh, really, Liam? I distinctly recall stepping on something suspiciously sticky on my way to the shower. And the smell…      Okay, maybe a  little  bit bad. I was rushing. Had to get online for that team thing.      “Team thing”? Is that what we’re calling it now? Sounds like trouble brewing. Are you seeing someone, Liam? You’ve been awfully secretive lately.      No! It’s… it's just a gaming clan. We’re practicing for a tournament. Honestly!      A tournament? Right. Well, as long as you’re not neglecting your schoolwork. Remember, GCSEs are around the corner. Have you thought any more about work experience? Mrs. Davies at the school said they have links with that engineering firm in Lichfield.      Ugh, engineering? No way. It's boring.      Now, now, Liam. Don’t knock it ‘til you try it. You never know what sparks your interest. It's good to have options. I wish I’d had more options when I left school. Just straight into a job, you know?      Exactly. It’s about exploring. Remember that documentary we watched about Ranulph Fiennes? Now  there’s  a man who grabbed opportunities. Trekking across Antarctica… incredible.      He’s mental. Why would anyone want to go to Antarctica? It’s freezing!      That's a teenager for you. Everything's extreme. Still, he did something no one else had done. That takes guts. It’s good to push yourself. Speaking of pushing yourself... I'm thinking of taking on a few extra shifts at the school. They're short-staffed in the lunch hall. It’ll be exhausting, but the extra money would be useful. Plus, keeps me out of trouble!      You’re a saint, honestly. You always put everyone else first. I'm swamped with proofreading at the moment, thankfully. Mrs. Henderson, the novelist, has been a lifesaver. Constant work. It's not glamorous, but it pays the bills. And it means I can work from home, which is a bonus with… well, with  this  one.      Hey!

Oh, this is lovely, isn’t it? Just driving through Istria… smells like pines and…well, everything good, really. Much better than the M60 back home.      Aye, miles better, love. Though, I wouldn’t mind a proper brew right now. This Croatian coffee is a bit…weak, for my liking. And honestly, I'm starving. Did we see anywhere decent to stop for lunch coming through Grožnjan?      There was that place with the truffle pasta, Mum. The one with all the little flags? Looked pretty busy though.      Truffle pasta, eh? That’s the whole point of coming to Istria, isn’t it? I read this article about a chef, a real innovator, who's foraging his own truffles and incorporating them into modern Slavic cuisine. Apparently, it’s phenomenal. Name was… damn it, slipped my mind.      Oh, you and your chefs, Dad! Always reading about them. I just want a decent plate of pasta! Although, truffles  are  nice. Remember when Auntie Brenda brought back that truffle oil from Italy, and tried to put it on everything? Even toast!      Oh, Brenda. Never one to do things by halves. Scared the life out of poor old George, she did, with that stuff. He thought it smelled like petrol! Still, she meant well. She’s been quiet lately though, haven’t heard from her in weeks.      She’s probably watching that American crime show she likes. The one with all the detectives. She told me she tapes it so she doesn't miss it.      Good old Brenda. Still a bit old-fashioned with the taping though. Streaming is where it’s at. Speaking of which, anyone seen that new docuseries on Netflix about stem cell research? It's fascinating, utterly mental what they're doing now.      Stem cells… yes, I skimmed an article about that. The ethical implications are rather complex, aren’t they? And the cost! Absolutely astronomical. Seems like healthcare in America… well, it's a different world. Everything's driven by profit over there.      It is. You remember Carol, from antenatal classes? Her daughter moved to California last year for university. She’s racking up debts like you wouldn’t believe, just for a degree. Here, you get student loans, support… it’s not perfect, but it’s fairer.      My mate Ben’s thinking of applying to universities in America. Says the football’s better, the campus life is amazing… I told him to be careful about the money though.

Honestly, this halloumi wrap is…fine. It's just…a bit beige, isn't it? All beige. Considering we're practically living  in  a printing house, I was hoping for a bit more colour on my lunch.      Beige is Cambridge’s signature colour, I think. Stone buildings, grey skies, beige lunches… it’s all very on brand. Mine’s pretty underwhelming too, ham and cheese. Reliable, if not exciting. Though, I’m mostly here for the gossip, frankly. Have you heard anything more about the restructure in Marketing?      Oh,  please  don’t even start on that. My team is bracing for impact. Rumour has it old Mr. Henderson is finally being forced into retirement, and they’re streamlining everything. Which, translated, means fewer jobs. I just finished training a new intern, and I’m already feeling guilty.      That's awful, Leo. Honestly, companies need to be more transparent about these things. It’s not fair to leave people hanging. Speaking of unfair, did you see the email about the funding cuts to the dialect research project? It's... frustrating. We were making genuinely interesting headway with the East Anglian vowel shifts.      Really? I hadn’t seen that. That’s… brutal. I mean, I get that budgets are tight, but dialect research feels so important. It’s like, losing a part of the cultural fabric, isn't it? What exactly are they cutting?      The fieldwork mostly. So no more travelling to villages, recording natural speech, actually  talking  to people. It’s all going to become desk-based analysis of existing corpora – which, don't get me wrong, is useful, but it’s not the same. It's all a bit academic and sterile. I grew up in Aylesbury, you know? Seeing how language changes even within Buckinghamshire is captivating.      Aylesbury! That's practically a different world from Cambridge. My nan’s from just outside there. She’s got this  very  particular way of pronouncing ‘bath’… drives my mum mad. I try to emulate it sometimes just to wind her up.      Oh, I completely get that. Everyone has their quirks. And that ‘bath’ thing is a classic. It’s a brilliant linguistic marker. It really highlights the North-South divide, and then even finer regional accents  within  those areas.      You two are making my ham and cheese feel even more inadequate. I’m in marketing, so I mostly deal with messaging designed to be utterly bland and universally appealing.

Right, so according to this slightly terrifying Polish satnav, we’re about forty minutes from Anya’s. Honestly, the roads are…character building. Not quite the M6, are they?      Character building is a polite way of putting it, darling. It feels like we’re navigating a particularly enthusiastic goat track at times. Still, beautiful though, isn’t it? All that…green. It’s a very different green to Cambridge. So much more…alive.      It is lovely. And Anya’s place is supposed to be fantastic. She sent pictures - little garden, loads of flowers. She’s really settled in, hasn’t she? It’s amazing she’s been there five years already.      It is. Feels like yesterday she was telling me she was off to Poland on a whim. A very brave whim, I thought at the time. I was still stuck in that awful loop of applying for jobs I didn’t really  want  and getting nowhere. I'm glad she found her feet so quickly.      She’s always been resourceful. Remember when she organised that whole festival in second year at uni with practically no budget? She’s a whirlwind. Speaking of feet...did you manage to sort out the luggage situation? It looked a bit precarious when we left your place.      Oh, the luggage. Yes, well, "sorted" is perhaps a strong word. It's… contained. I had to sit on it for the final ten miles. I rather suspect I'll be feeling it tomorrow. It's just...I always overpack. What if I need the velvet evening gown? What if there’s a gala? One has to be prepared!      A gala in Tarnow? Mum, you’re hilarious. Anya’s promised home cooking and probably a lot of pierogi, not black tie. Honestly, you brought three pairs of heels. Footwear logistics alone were a challenge.      One must have options! And you know how my feet swell on journeys. I need sensible options  and  glamorous options. Besides, I thought I'd bring that cashmere cardigan you admired last Christmas. It's not a gala item, precisely, but it's lovely.      Oh, that  is  a lovely cardigan. You’re a soft touch, you are. Right, so Anya said she’d meet us at the edge of town, lead us back to her place. She was worried about us getting completely lost, apparently the addresses are a bit… ambiguous.      Ambiguous addresses. Sounds like Poland.

...Honestly, that Adidas design for the new Man U kit is just  awful . All those little red diamonds? It looks like someone spilled a box of sprinkles on a perfectly good shirt. And they’re charging seventy quid for it! Seventy!      Seventy quid is robbery, aye. Though, to be fair, you’re paying for the brand as much as the design, aren't you? It's the Adidas swoosh people want, not necessarily... diamond chaos. Though I agree, it  is  a bit much. It screams 'trying too hard'. Remember the Newcastle one a few years back? The purple and orange sash? That was a disaster.      Oh god,  don't  remind me! My dad nearly had a coronary. He’s still muttering about it now. It's just...the tradition, isn't it? Football shirts have a history. You expect certain things. Adidas and Nike, they're supposed to be leading the way, not churning out something a five-year-old designed after a sugar rush. It's greed, that’s what it is.      Totally. And it's interesting, isn’t it, how much sponsorship dictates things now? I was reading an article about how clubs are practically  begging  for gambling sponsors, and then pretending to care about responsible betting when the cameras are on. Hypocrisy at its finest.      It’s dreadful. And it's not just football, is it? Everything's sponsored. Even the Olympic games are basically just a very fancy advert. I saw a thing about the potential for McDonald's to sponsor the Women's World Cup. I mean, seriously? McDonald's? Promoting healthy lifestyles?      Right? That’s…a choice. A very cynical choice. It's almost comical, isn’t it? They'll be running adverts showing athletes enjoying salads while simultaneously selling Big Macs. Classic. You know, it makes you wonder what they pay for that kind of exposure. Probably enough to fund a small nation’s healthcare system.      Probably! And then you think about the sheer volume of plastic waste generated by all the kits, the sponsorship banners, the throwaway merchandise… It's a monumental environmental impact. They greenwash everything, say they’re committed to sustainability, then release another garishly coloured, polyester monstrosity.      It's a systemic problem, isn’t it? You can’t just blame Adidas or Nike. It's the whole infrastructure. And the fans are complicit too, to a degree. We all buy the kits, we get swept up in the hype.

Honestly, this is a proper mess, isn't it? Mum's been going on about the electric bill all morning. Says it’s nearly doubled since last winter. How are people supposed to cope?      Tell me about it. I got a letter from… well, not  from  them exactly, more like a strongly worded notification, about overpayment of Jobseeker’s Allowance. Apparently, I didn’t declare that fiver I made selling a comic on eBay last month. A  fiver !      Seriously?! They’re going after you for five quid? That’s just… absurd. Did you explain?      Tried to. Spent half an hour on hold, then the woman on the phone just kept repeating policy. “All income must be declared, sir.” Like I’m trying to pull a fast one! It's not like I’m living large here. I just wanted to get rid of that old  2000 AD  annual.      I know, it's ridiculous. Speaking of eBay, my new gardening gloves finally arrived. Took nearly two weeks. And they’re the wrong size. Typical.      Everything’s a hassle, innit? Remember when we were kids, things just… happened? No letters about benefits, no crippling energy bills, no endless waiting on hold.      Yeah, Mum and Dad always made it seem easy. Although, thinking about it, Uncle Barry did blow a fair chunk of his inheritance on a speedboat, then complained he couldn't afford to fix the roof. Some people…      Don’t even get me started on Barry. He always was a bit clueless. And Dad kept saying how lucky we were, growing up in a stable home. Easy for him to say. He had a job for life. Nobody has that anymore.      True. It feels like everything is up in the air constantly. I'm worrying about after I finish my Masters. The job market's frightening.      You'll be alright, you're educated. I left school with bugger all. Honestly, I try applying for things, you know? Retail, warehouse work… and I always get knocked back. They just look at my CV and... well, you can see it a mile off. Long gaps. No sustained employment.      Have you thought about retraining? There are courses, aren't there?      Retraining? For what? To be a barista? No offence, but I’m nearly forty. I need something… realistic. I saw a bloke at the Job Centre the other day, proper smart fella, told me I needed to “upskill” and “reimagine my career trajectory”.

Honestly, Mum, the traffic this morning was  brutal . Sat nav sent me the scenic route…through three villages and a farm. Said it was the quickest way to get to Cambridge. Quickest to a heart attack, more like!      Oh, you and your sat navs, dear. Always think they know best, don't they? I reckon a good old map and a bit of common sense gets you further. Remember when we used to travel to Skegness and just  go ? Didn’t need no fancy gadgets then.      Skegness! Now  that  was a holiday. Real seaside fun. Not like these package deals everyone goes on now. All rushing around, barely looking at where they are. And the food! Fish and chips in paper, properly done. Not this…posh stuff.      Mum, you’re showing your age! Though I do agree about the fish and chips. Still, Cambridge was worth it. Landed a potentially huge contract. A new logistics firm, needing all sorts of accountancy help.      That’s lovely, dear. Good for you. It’s a bit different from my work, isn’t it? Though I tell you, cleaning some of these houses…you hear some stories. You wouldn’t believe.      Oh? Do tell! Though maybe not over the coffee, Mum gets a bit… sensitive.      Sensitive? I’m not sensitive! I just don’t need to hear about everyone’s messy habits. Honestly. Though, speaking of habits, did you see on the news about that little plane crash near Norwich? Dreadful.      Yes, awful. So close to home. Always makes you think, doesn't it? I was supposed to be flying to Amsterdam next month for a conference, but I’m seriously considering the train now.      Trains are good. Though the buffet car hasn’t been the same since they changed the sandwiches. Remember those prawn mayonnaise ones? Absolute treat.      Everything always comes back to the food with you two, doesn’t it? It’s endearing, honestly. I was trying to get Dad to come to the conference with me. He always enjoyed Amsterdam.      Your father? He wouldn’t go to Amsterdam for all the tea in China. He says it’s too ‘foreign’ these days. And his knees aren’t what they used to be for all that walking.      I know, I know. He’s a creature of habit. He'd rather stay here and watch  Bargain Hunt . Speaking of habits… have you seen the size of those convenience store prices lately?

...Honestly, it's just  stressful , isn’t it? Mrs. Davies keeps saying the mocks aren’t 'real' tests, but then she gives us back papers covered in red pen like we’ve personally offended her.      Tell me about it! She marked down my essay on  Jane Eyre  because apparently, “Charlotte Brontë wouldn’t approve of a twenty-first century interpretation.” Like, hello? It’s an assignment, not a séance!      Exactly! It’s like she  wants  us to regurgitate everything she said in the lesson. Did you hear she’s got a trainee teacher shadowing her now? A Mr. Finch, I think?      Oh, the really quiet one? I saw him in the corridor. He looked completely terrified. Poor thing. Probably realised what he’s walked into. Mrs. Davies could scare a badger back into its sett.      Seriously! He was trying to ask her a question about the curriculum and she just…launched into a ten-minute speech about the decline of grammar. It was brutal. I felt bad for him.      I bet. Speaking of brutal, have you started revising for the science test? Mr. Lewis is threatening us with a practical exam. A  practical ! On titration.      Ugh, don’t even  mention  titration. I completely blanked in the last lesson. Apparently, the pink colour has to be  just so , otherwise it doesn’t count. It's ridiculous. It's not a delicate art, it’s science!      It's like he's expecting us to be professional chemists already. I’m much more comfortable with the art stuff, honestly. Ms. Ellis has been amazing lately, she’s letting us experiment with mixed media. I’m doing a portrait of my cat, Winston.      Ooh, that sounds good! Winston  is  very photogenic. Is it realistic or more abstract?      Bit of both, actually. I’m trying to capture his…essence. Which mostly involves him looking unimpressed and demanding biscuits. It's going okay, but getting the colours right is a nightmare. I keep ending up with a vaguely orange blob.      That sounds about right for Winston. You're really good at art though, you always have been. Remember when we were little and tried to paint Grandma’s garden? It ended up looking like a psychedelic jungle.      Oh god, yes! She was surprisingly gracious about it. Although I think she had to prune a few bushes to disguise our “creative additions.” But seriously, with English and science piling up…I’m starting to think I’ll just live in the art room.

So, you’re telling me… nuns actually  choose  to live like that? Like, willingly? It seems… intense.      Well, Liam, it’s about their faith, isn’t it? They believe they’re dedicating their lives to God. It’s a vow, a commitment. Not everyone understands it, and it's definitely not for everyone. It’s a big sacrifice of…normal life, I suppose.      Goo! Nuns!      But  why  sacrifice normal life? I mean, look at us. We moan if the Wi-Fi’s down for five minutes. They’ve given up… everything! It’s like… a really extreme version of the Matrix, isn’t it? People choosing the blue pill, but, like, for God instead of ignorance.      That’s…an interesting comparison. The Matrix! You and your films, Liam. It's not about escaping reality, though. For them, it’s about finding a different  kind  of reality, a spiritual one. A deeper meaning. Though I can see why you’d see it as a choice, a deliberate opting-in to something different.      But doesn't it seem… controlling? Like, all those rules. All those… vows. It reminds me of that documentary we watched about Scientology. Remember? All those people handing over their money and doing what they were told?      That’s a very different situation, Liam. Scientology is widely considered a cult, and there are serious concerns about how they operate and the harm they cause. Nuns aren't being exploited for money or forced to do things against their will. They genuinely choose this life. Their order provides for them, they dedicate themselves to prayer and service. It's… a very established religion.      Established doesn’t mean it’s automatically good. Loads of bad stuff has been established for centuries. Like, the idea that women couldn't vote!      That’s a fair point. And you're right to question things, to be critical. I'm not saying it’s perfect, or that everyone agrees with it. It's just… complicated. It’s rooted in thousands of years of tradition. I remember Mrs. O'Malley from down the road, she was a nun for fifty years. Lovely woman. Always cheerful. She said she felt more free  in  the convent than she ever did outside it.      Pea! Liam pea!      Okay, okay, I’ll eat a pea, Finny. But seriously, how can someone feel  more  free giving up all that? It's like… giving up your agency.

Right, honestly, that was a  brilliant  cha-cha. I’m still buzzing. Never thought I’d be saying that about a Tuesday night, mind.      Buzzing? You were practically radiating competitive energy. I thought for a moment you were going to accidentally hip-check Mrs. Higgins into next week. Though, to be fair, she IS a bit of a hazard on the dance floor.      Aye, she is. Keeps trying to lead! But seriously, I’m starting to enjoy it. It’s… liberating, you know? Just letting go and being silly. A far cry from staring at spreadsheets all day. Speaking of which, I’m dreading getting back to the corpus tomorrow. It’s just… endless tagging.      Tell me about it. I spent half of today arguing with a client about stress tolerances on a bridge design. They wanted to use slightly cheaper materials. Slightly. As if 'slightly' doesn't matter when we're talking about tons of steel and the potential for… well, you know.      Oh, don’t even. It's all risk assessment, isn’t it? Like everything. Remember old Mr. Henderson at uni, always going on about the risk assessment of crossing the road? Said you had a higher chance of being struck by lightning.      Oh God, Henderson. The man lived and breathed statistics. Did he ever actually finish his book on the origins of the English language? He was always rabbitting on about Old English and how it influenced modern slang.      I think he did, actually. A really niche thing, apparently. Mum got it for him as a Christmas present, something about acknowledging his, and I quote, ‘eccentric brilliance’. It’s probably gathering dust somewhere. Anyway, are we almost there? This roundabout seems to go on forever.      Nearly. Just another couple of turns. We should be at your Auntie Brenda's in about fifteen minutes. Are you still convinced she's plotting to marry you off to the vicar's son?      Don't even  start  me. She keeps subtly mentioning how "suitable" he is. As if 'suitable' is the only thing that matters! He spends his weekends birdwatching and making his own elderflower cordial. No offense to birdwatchers or cordial makers, but…      None taken. He does sound… particular. Actually, talking of particular, have you seen what Ricky Gervais said about that new reality TV show on LoveFilm? Absolutely ripped into it.      Heard bits and pieces. He's usually spot on, isn't he?

Are we  nearly  there yet? My legs are going numb. And this music… honestly, Mum, is this all you listen to when Dad’s not here?      Now, now, Ethan. Don’t be rude. It’s Fleetwood Mac, a classic! And no, we’re not  nearly  there. We’ve still got another hour or so to Rovinj. Though I reckon we’ll stop at that little olive oil place Gran mentioned, near Bale.      Fleetwood Mac is good, Ethan, but a bit… mellow for a Croatian road trip, don’t you think? I was hoping to find some proper Croatian folk music. Maybe something with an accordion?      Accordions? Really, darling? You’re going full tourist, aren’t you? I was rather hoping for something a bit more… sophisticated. Perhaps some jazz, to match the scenery. Though, admittedly, the scenery is doing most of the work. This Istrian countryside is stunning.      Sophisticated? You and your “sophisticated” tastes. We’re on holiday, love! It’s about embracing the local culture, not pretending we’re at Ronnie Scott’s. And that olive oil place  is  worth the stop. Old Man Luka makes the best olive oil this side of the Adriatic. Apparently, you can taste the sun in it.      Taste the sun? Sounds… weird. Can we at least get some ice cream at the market in Bale if we go? I saw pictures online, it looked huge. And they had like, everything.      Yeah, a market sounds good. Gran was saying they have loads of local produce, and those little lavender sachets. I need to get some for my uni room, it smells awful in there. It’s like a student-y, damp smell.      Lavender sachets? You and Gran… Honestly. Alright, market stop is approved. But then we’re sticking to the plan, okay? Rovinj, dinner at that Konoba recommended by your Auntie Carol, and then a proper glass of Malvazija. Not that fizzy stuff you usually drink, darling.      Oh, don't start on the fizzy stuff! A Prosecco’s a perfectly acceptable apéritif, thank you very much. Besides, we’re on holiday. Rules are made to be broken. Remember that time we tried camping in the Lake District and the tent blew away in the middle of the night?      Oh god,  that  was a disaster. You and Dad huddled in the car, trying to stay warm, while I was convinced a wild animal was going to attack us.

…and honestly, I still can’t believe Liam tried to convince us a badger built his shed. A  badger , I ask ya! He was dead serious.      Liam's a walking disaster, bless him. Though, knowing Doncaster, it's not entirely implausible a badger  could  have started something resembling construction. Are we still on for that escape room on Saturday?      Oh aye, the one in the Frenchgate? I’m in. Need to brush up on my puzzle skills, mind. I'm rubbish at those things. Always get stuck.      Count me in too. It’s ages since we’ve all done something proper fun. Though, honestly, after last time, I’m slightly terrified of escape rooms. Remember the one with the hidden camera?      Don’t remind me! Old Man Hemmings nearly had a heart attack when he realised he was being watched while trying to decipher the riddle about the teapot. Speaking of things watched…did anyone see that weird post on Chloe’s Insta story last night?      The one with the… muted video and a bunch of emojis? I did. It looked…suspicious. She said it was just a ‘game’ with someone, but…      A game? What kind of game needs to be muted and covered in suspicious looking eye and padlock emojis? Sounds a bit dodgy to me.      I overheard her on the phone earlier, talking about “keeping it safe” and “no screenshots.” It was vague, but… unsettling.      Right? It's started a whole conversation in our group chat. Everyone's speculating. Some are saying it's just a silly challenge, like those TikTok things, but… well, you know Chloe. She can be a bit extra.      Extra is an understatement. Remember when she tried to organise a Renaissance-themed picnic in the park in November? It rained the  entire  time. But still, this feels different. Someone mentioned it might be about…well, recording stuff?      Recording what stuff? Don’t tell me she’s gone down that route. That’s proper messed up.      That's what I thought! It's just whispers at the moment, but apparently, someone on her course was talking about some kind of… intimate content being shared? I really hope it's not true.      It's awful even to think about. And the power imbalance if it is… Ugh. I wasn’t really paying attention to understand what exactly they were talking about, just snippets. I think… they said something about physical stuff too?

Right, honestly, this library coffee is…criminal. It tastes like someone brewed it with dust and disappointment.      Harsh, Kev! But… not entirely wrong. It’s functional, I suppose. Gets the caffeine in ya. Though, after that disastrous panini last week, I’m steering clear of anything  made  here. Remember that one? All soggy bread and suspiciously grey chicken?      Oh god, don’t even  mention  the panini. I think I’m still traumatised. I brought my own lunch today, thankfully. Homemade curry. Smells a lot better than whatever’s lurking in the café.      Curry, you say? Now you're talkin’. Properly talkin’. I'm stuck with a cheese and pickle butty. Mam made it for me, bless 'er. Can't complain, she tries, but it just doesn't hit the same as a good proper dinner, does it? Especially when you've been explainin' PowerShell to a load of students all mornin'. Brain needs fuel.      A cheese and pickle is a classic, Kev! Comfort food. But yeah, long mornings teaching can drain you. I was going to grab something from that new Vietnamese place near campus, Banh Mi Heaven. Have either of you been? Apparently, their pork belly rolls are amazing.      Ooh, Banh Mi Heaven? I've seen it, been meaning to try. Vietnamese is always a good shout. Anything’s better than another limp jacket potato from the Uni shop. They seem to think “jacket potato” solely means a potato that’s been vaguely warmed.      Vietnamese, eh? That sounds a bit fancy for our usual lunchtime fodder. I'm a simple man, I am. Give me a good bit o' fish and chips, or a proper Sunday roast and I'm a happy lad. Though, I did try that sushi place in Spinningfields once… disaster. Too much raw fish. Felt like somethin' was lookin' back at me.      You’re such a traditionalist, Kev! It  is  good stuff though. And it’s quick. Which is essential with our break being only half an hour. Though, maybe we should all try Banh Mi Heaven together next week? A team lunch, you know?      I'm in for that. A bit of a change of scenery would be good. Plus, I'm always up for trying new food. My girlfriend’s a brilliant cook, constantly experimenting. Last week she made some sort of Korean fried cauliflower… it was ridiculously good, but I haven't got a clue what went into it.

...and honestly, I nearly choked on my biscuit when Brenda from Admissions announced she’d started a TikTok account.  TikTok , of all things! She’s barely mastered email.      Oh, you’re telling me? I saw her practicing dance moves in the corridor yesterday. It was…an experience. She kept bumping into the book displays. I tried to offer some advice about lighting, having done a bit with Instagram for the library’s book of the month, but she just looked at me like I’d grown a second head.      You know, it’s funny. We’re all so quick to judge, aren’t we? But Brenda's trying! It's good she’s attempting to reach students where  they  are. We can't just expect them to come to us anymore. Though, admittedly, a book display casualty is a bit concerning.      I get the  reaching  students part, I really do. But the library’s Facebook page already feels like shouting into the void. We post about new acquisitions, research workshops… crickets. My nephew, he lives on that… what’s it called? BeReal? Apparently, it’s all about ‘authentic’ life. No filters, no editing.      BeReal, yeah. My daughter practically force-fed it to me last weekend. You get a notification at a random time, and you’ve got two minutes to take a photo of  whatever  you’re doing. It's wildly popular with her generation. I just ended up with a blurry picture of my Sunday roast.      Oh, that's brilliant! The contrast is perfect. Honestly, I find the whole thing exhausting just thinking about it. I’m on LinkedIn, mostly for professional development, and I occasionally dabble with Twitter for library news. But trying to keep up with all these platforms… it’s a full-time job in itself. I'm ancient, compared to these kids.      Ancient? Come on, now. Mid-fifties is practically the new thirty. Though I did read an article saying TikTok’s algorithm is designed to be… addictive. Like, deliberately engineered to keep you scrolling. It’s a bit unsettling.      Addictive is the word. I saw a statistic the other day – something about the average user spending over 90 minutes a day on it. 90 minutes! That’s almost a whole working day lost to short-form videos. Imagine the academic papers someone could write in 90 minutes!      True. But think of the outreach! I saw a fascinating campaign run by a library in the States – they were using TikTok to recreate famous book covers with staff.

...Honestly, Richard, I’m still not entirely convinced Tunbridge Wells is the  optimal  location. It’s lovely, don't get me wrong, beautifully presented - you’ve always had a good eye for that – but strategically? We're trying to serve a broader catchment area than just the well-heeled residents of this town.      Now, Penelope, we've been over this. The land acquisition was incredibly favourable.
