It’s amazing how much mental load there is, even when you’re not  doing  anything. Remember when I used to just...be? Before Leo came along? It feels like a lifetime ago. This is probably similar to what you feel at school, just a different kind of pressure, yeah?      It's the modern world, so it is. Everything's 'urgent'. At work, it's relentless. We were just talking about stress levels in a team meeting. Someone mentioned those heart rate variability things – fancy watches that supposedly tell you how stressed you are just by looking at your pulse. Seemed a bit… much.      Heart rate variability? Sounds complicated. Is it like, if your heart beats too fast, it means you’re stressed?      That's a very simplified version, apparently. It’s about the  variation  in the time between beats. Less variation can indicate your body is under stress. There are apps for your phone, too, though I’d rather just have a cup of tea and a lie down, thanks very much.      Tea and a lie down is the Irish solution to everything, isn't it? Though, speaking of complicated… did you hear about the latest fallout over that equality vote back in Ireland? People still arguing about the age of eligibility for kids to be brought to the Pride parade. It’s… a mess.      It is. You’d think after the marriage equality referendum, things would have settled down. But there’s always someone looking for a fight, isn’t there? It feels incredibly backwards.      Um… is everything okay? You both went a bit quiet there.      Sorry, lad. Just thinking about the state of the world, I suppose. It gets to you, you know? Though, on a lighter note, have you been listening to any good podcasts lately? I’ve been hooked on this one about the history of bad jokes.      A history of bad jokes? Only you, Declan.      What can I say? It’s fascinating! They explain the psychology behind  why  we like them, even when they're awful. Like a really terrible pun…  why  do we laugh?

Are we nearly there yet? Honestly, this journey is  ages .      Now, Leo, don’t start. We left Bolton barely an hour ago. And it’s a lovely drive, look at the scenery. All those fields… reminds me of when your Grandad used to point out the different birds. He could name ‘em all, could your Grandad. Even the tiny ones.      He was proper good, wasn't he? Remember that time he tried to convince us that a pigeon was a 'flying rat'? Proper wound everyone up. And then got cross when we told Grandma.      Flying rats! Wonderful. Reminds me of the sheer volume of pigeons in Trafalgar Square. It's quite a sight, although not exactly ornithologically enriching. It's funny, isn't it, how something so mundane – a bird – can provoke such strong reactions. Like that whole debate about the Heathrow expansion… birds versus planes, essentially.      Aye, that’s right. And it’s not just the birds, David. It’s the disruption to people’s lives, the noise… I remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road used to complain about the planes rattling her windows. Lived in one of those lovely little villages on the hill, didn’t she? Real postcard perfect.      Horwich, wasn't it? Proper quaint. Makes you wonder why anyone would want to build anything  near  those places. It's like ruining something beautiful just for convenience. Speaking of ruining things... how’s the law conversion going, anyway? Still feeling optimistic?     Yeah, it's… a lot. Honestly, sometimes I just want to give up and become a birdwatcher or something. It’s all contract law and torts and… ugh. It’s a million miles away from what I did for my first degree. And all the reading! Honestly, I’d rather wrestle a bear.      A bear? You’d last about five minutes. Though, I suppose you could learn a thing or two from Bear Grylls. Resourcefulness… it’s a valuable skill, even in a courtroom. But stick with it. It’s a tough course, but worth it in the end. I always thought a good lawyer needed to be able to weigh things up impartially, you know? Like, someone trying to argue that 5 kilograms is heavier than 11 pounds... ridiculous.      Absolutely ridiculous! Kilograms are easier anyway. Everything’s metric these days. Though, I still instinctively think in miles when I’m driving. And speaking of driving, this parking situation at the supermarket is  always  a nightmare.

Honestly, this veggie shepherd’s pie is…fine. It’s just…missing  something . Like, a proper gravy depth, you know? It feels a bit…wishy-washy.      You’re a tough critic, Liv. It’s good! And, realistically, it’s massively better for everything than actual lamb. Thinking about it, I saw a documentary about the methane emissions from sheep farming the other day. Terrifying.      Yeah, it’s brutal. I was chatting to old Mr. Henderson, one of my clients, about it. He's a proper country chap, always going on about shooting and fishing. We got into a proper debate. He argues hunting is more ‘humane’ than the abattoir.      Humane? Please. That’s…a justification, isn’t it? Like, 'Oh, at least I gave it a chase!' It’s still ending a life, just with added adrenaline for the hunter. It feels…oppressive. Like asserting dominance over another living thing.      Exactly! And it’s the  scale  of it all. The number of animals processed, crammed into awful conditions. It’s just… overwhelming. That’s why I’ve been looking into this cultured meat stuff. Have you guys heard much about it? "Shmeat," as some people ironically call it.      A little. Isn’t it grown in a lab? Feels a bit…  Black Mirror , doesn't it? Like, meat without the animal, but still… weird.      It’s a bit unsettling, I’ll admit. But if it genuinely removes suffering, then I think it’s worth getting over the ‘ick’ factor. I read an article saying the environmental impact could be drastically lower too. Less land use, less water…      That’s what I’m hoping. But it's expensive at the moment, and there’s the whole regulatory side of things. Plus, I wonder if some people would still feel… guilty? Like it’s ‘playing God’ or something.      Knowing people, absolutely. My auntie would have a meltdown. She's convinced everything's a conspiracy. She spends half her time taking vitamin tablets because she read something online about a vitamin D deficiency epidemic.      Oh, bless her. My nan's the same. She's convinced calcium supplements will stop her shrinking. She’s five foot two! It’s the power of suggestion.      It is! And it’s interesting, isn’t it, how we’re so willing to pop pills, but balk at the idea of lab-grown meat? It’s like we’ve accepted synthetic intervention in other areas of health, but food feels…different.

Setting:   The living room of a modest home in Whitehaven, England. A slightly worn sofa faces a flickering television screen. Empty crisp packets and half-finished mugs of tea are scattered on a coffee table. It’s a cold November evening.   Characters:       Liam :   23, Student, currently studying History at Newcastle University. Relaxed, a bit sarcastic, trying to be responsible.     Callum :   26, Unemployed, a recent graduate who hasn't found his footing. Slightly melancholic, prone to rambling.     Chloe :   21, Student, studying Nursing, practical and grounded.   Conversation:     Callum:   Honestly, this bloke’s making a Wellington. A  Wellington . Who even  makes  a Wellington anymore? It’s just…effort. Pure, unadulterated effort.   Liam:   You could apply that logic to just, like, everything, couldn’t ya, Callum? It’s a Saturday night. You’ve been ‘applying logic’ to everything for the past six hours.   Chloe:   Leave him be, Liam. He's in his existential Wellington phase. Did you get those books you were ordering, Liam? For uni?   Liam:   Aye, most of 'em. Amazon Prime's a lifesaver, innit? Got that biography of Cromwell, a load of stuff on the English Reformation… proper nerdy. Though, the delivery driver nearly threw it over the fence this time. Honestly, like I'm living in the middle of nowhere.   Callum:   Amazon's getting ridiculous. They track your every move. I read an article… something about manipulating consumer behaviour with targeted ads. It's frightening.   Chloe:   Oh, here we go. Callum's conspiracy theories. You're just bothered they keep suggesting trainers you definitely don’t need.   Callum:   It's not just the trainers! It's the principle! And actually… they  are  nice trainers. They've got these… breathable mesh panels. But I shouldn't. I really shouldn't. I haven’t even applied for a job this week.   Liam:   That's... not ideal, is it? You said you were gonna look at some retail jobs. Just to get something going.   Callum:   I did! I  thought  about looking. Then Netflix suggested ‘The Crown’ and… well, you know. It’s historical research, basically. Understanding the nuances of power structures.   Chloe:   It's procrastination, Callum. Plain and simple. Are you coming Christmas shopping with us next weekend? Mum’s already making a list the length of your arm.   Callum:   Shopping? Urgh. The crowds… the Christmas music… the sheer…  festive cheer . It’s overwhelming. Can't we just order everything online?   Liam:   Mum'd have a fit.

...Honestly, the whole thing was just  bonkers . Trying to explain to a shopkeeper in rural Italy that I didn't want Parmesan  on  my carbonara felt like negotiating international peace treaties. They just wouldn't understand!      Oh my god, that sounds perfectly Italian though, doesn’t it? They're so passionate about their food! I’ve had similar experiences trying to order a simple black coffee. They insist on adding sugar, or cream, or a tiny biscuit… it’s relentless. So, was that the highlight of the holiday, battling over pasta?      It was definitely  a  highlight. The scenery was incredible, obviously, Tuscany is stunning. But the little cultural clashes are always the most memorable, aren’t they? It’s a good reminder that what’s “normal” is so subjective. You know, after all this linguistic research, you’d think I’d be better at navigating that stuff.      You’d think! Though knowing  about  a language and actually  using  it under pressure are two different beasts. How  was  the research going before you jetted off, by the way? Still drowning in dialectal variations of ‘hello’?      You’re too accurate. It’s the East Anglian stuff that’s killing me. So much subtle variation, even within relatively small geographical areas. It’s fascinating, genuinely, but trying to catalogue it all and pinpoint consistent patterns… exhausting. It’s good to be back, though. Cambridge feels… sane, comparatively.      Sane-ish. It’s Alumni Day, after all. Full of people reminiscing about all-nighters in the library and pretending they understood everything Professor Davies said. How’s your mum handling retirement? Last time we spoke, she was planning to learn pottery.      She’s embraced it wholeheartedly! The house is filling up with slightly wonky mugs and bowls. She’s joined a local pottery club, apparently, and is now fiercely competitive. It’s amazing to watch, honestly. She always said she wished she'd had more creative outlets. Dad’s just relieved she’s not following him around trying to “help” with the garden.      Oh, bless him. He’s a lovely man, but he does take gardening  very  seriously. My folks are travelling again. This time they're off to New Zealand. They're doing that gap-year-at-60 thing.      No way! New Zealand? That’s ambitious. Are they the adventurous type?      Not particularly. Mum’s already complained about the lack of decent tea shops and Dad is worried about the bugs.

Right, I’m officially broken. Absolutely  broken . That lecture on Post-Structuralism… honestly, I think Derrida just scrambled my brain.      Sounds rough. Still tackling that one, then? Thought you said you were making headway with it yesterday.      Headway? I was  pretending  to make headway. I understood about… three words the lecturer said. And she spoke so fast! It was like trying to catch smoke with a sieve. You, with your fancy postgraduate brain, wouldn’t understand the struggle.      Oh, I remember the feeling alright. Though to be fair, my postgraduate brain is mostly fuelled by copious amounts of coffee and pretending I know what I’m doing. What bit tripped you up particularly? Was it the deconstruction of… well, everything?      Everything! Exactly! It’s like, they’re taking apart language just to prove language is… apart? It's mental. I’m starting to think I picked the wrong degree. Should’ve done something sensible, like… veterinary science. At least then I’d be cuddling puppies instead of dissecting philosophical concepts.      Puppies are nice, yeah. But you’re brilliant at English Lit, love. Don't sell yourself short. Remember that essay you wrote on  Wuthering Heights ? Your tutor was raving about it. It’s just a tricky module, that’s all.      It wouldn't be so tricky if my back didn’t feel like it's been through a washing machine. I swear, lugging all those books around campus is a genuine occupational hazard.      You really need to get one of those backpack things with the proper support. And stop trying to carry the entire library in one go. Seriously.      I  have  a backpack! It's just... tempting to get all the readings at once, so I don't have to keep going back. And my shoulders are killing me and I need a massage. A proper one. Not one of your 'helpful' attempts.      Hey! My attempts are perfectly adequate! Okay, maybe a bit enthusiastic… and I did once nearly dislocate your shoulder. But I'm learning!      Learning by endangering my skeletal system. No thanks. I need a professional. Someone with actual training. I saw a leaflet for that new place near the university, “Zenith Massage”. Looks fancy.      Zenith, yeah. I’ve heard good things. A bit pricey though, isn't it?      Worth it. A sixty-minute deep tissue is an investment in my sanity. And in preventing me from snapping at everyone I meet because my back is screaming.

...Honestly, the sheer volume of marking I had last week was ridiculous. Little Timmy still thinks a semicolon is a type of bird. A  semi -colon, Timmy! Honestly.      Sounds familiar, though thankfully my days of assessing anything are long gone. Give me a good crossword any day. Less emotional investment, you see. Though even  those  are getting trickier, I swear.      It’s the same with the Year 10s, David. They’re clever, but their grasp of basic grammar...well, it’s…optimistic. And the essays! They all seem to think they're writing the next great novel, full of purple prose and very little substance.      Exactly! It’s exhausting trying to gently steer them towards clarity. Anyway, enough shop talk. This chicken is  lovely , Mum. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself.      Oh, thank you, dear. It’s just a simple roast, really. A bit of rosemary, garlic…nothing fancy. I was reading an article this morning though, about the cost of chicken feed going up again. It's frightening, isn't it? Everything’s getting so expensive.      It is. And you see what’s happening in Calais, too. Appalling. All those people… desperate. It’s a right mess. I was reading the  Telegraph  and…      Dad, please. Not the  Telegraph . It just makes me feel helpless and angry. It’s so easy to dehumanise people when you’re reading headlines. I saw a piece on the BBC News about a volunteer worker, a young woman actually, helping with food distribution. That felt… more real.      She’s right, David. Sensationalism doesn't help anyone. It’s a humanitarian crisis, plain and simple. And we’re just sitting here, comfortable and well-fed. Although, even ‘comfortable’ feels relative these days with energy bills through the roof.      I just… I struggle to understand it all. It feels like the world’s gone mad. And frankly, our government’s response feels… inadequate.      They're always inadequate, aren't they? It feels like they're more concerned with soundbites than solutions. Speaking of solutions, what about our holiday plans? Mum, have you had any luck with that cottage in Cornwall?      I have, actually! I spoke to Mrs. Pengelly yesterday. It’s available for the week after your half-term, Sarah. It’s the same one we stayed in a few years ago, remember? The one with the ridiculously small kitchen but wonderful sea views?      Oh, brilliant! That’s fantastic.

…and honestly, Gareth, the plumber. Honestly. Said he’d be here Tuesday, didn't show. Wednesday, a text - “family emergency.” Thursday, nothing. Finally rings  today , apologises, says he double-booked. Double-booked! As if my time is worthless. It's the bathroom, you see, the downstairs one. The tile’s coming loose, it’s driving me mad.      Oh, the joys of tradespeople, Alistair. Sounds like you’ve encountered a classic. You know, I was telling Mair about Bryn last week - the electrician? - promised he’d sort the lights in the hallway, then turned up with a sunburn and a story about a stag do in Blackpool. Said he couldn't  possibly  focus on wiring after a weekend like that.      Blackpool! Good heavens. They treat it like a holiday, not a job. My father, he always said, a man is only as good as his word. He built our house in Cairo, you know. From the ground up. Didn’t rely on anyone, just his own two hands and a crew he trusted implicitly. None of this… flaky behaviour.      Cairo, now there’s a building site I’d like to have seen. My grandfather was a miner, down in Tredegar. Hard work, honest work, he'd say. These lads… well, they see a chance to pull a fast one, they’ll take it. What’s the actual problem with the tile? Is it a big job? Maybe I know someone reliable. I’ve got a chap, Dai, does bits and pieces, generally sound.      It’s not  massive , thankfully. Just a strip, about a metre long, where the grout’s crumbling and a couple of tiles are loose. It’s more the principle of the thing, Gareth! I need to get it sorted before my daughter comes down with the grandchildren next month. She's very… particular about hygiene.      Ah, the maternal instinct. Understandable. A loose tile  is  a breeding ground, isn't it? You've got to please the younger generation. I'm no good at the DIY stuff myself, absolutely hopeless. My wife, Enid, she’s the practical one. She’s currently redesigning the kitchen. Apparently, it’s “dated.” Honestly, it was perfectly serviceable, but try telling her that.      Dated is a dangerous word. My wife, Penelope, had a similar phase a few years ago. Wanted to rip out the perfectly good kitchen and install something… minimalist. All stainless steel and sharp angles.

There ya go, lad. Not  too  spicy, I hope? Young Finn there seems to think anything's fair game for consumption. Honestly, I’m starting to worry he’ll try swallowing a Lego brick next.      Thanks. It smells amazing, actually. Not too spicy is good, my mum makes curry that makes your eyes water. And yeah, Finn’s… adventurous. He tried to eat a pebble in the garden earlier.      Don't I know it. That's toddlers for you. Always exploring with their mouths. Though, pebbles are a step up from metal, darling. Honestly, the things he puts in his mouth… it's terrifying. Are you  sure  he doesn’t have some sort of… superpower? Like a steel stomach or something?      A steel stomach would be helpful, considering the state of his nappy sometimes. No superpowers, just a complete disregard for sensible ingestion. Speaking of sensible, anyone fancy a small glass of wine with this? Bit of a Thursday treat?      I’m good, thanks. Got football training tomorrow. Need to be… functional.      Oh, go on, just a small one. It’s been a long day wrangling a tiny human. Plus, we need to finalize plans for your birthday, Ethan. Any thoughts? We were thinking the park Saturday? They've got that Sci-Fi themed event on, the one with the robots.      The park sounds good. It's a grand spot. Finn will love running around. I just hope he doesn't  try  to disassemble one of the robots. Though, with his current obsession with metal... it’s a real possibility. Remember that night deposit box we saw at the bank, Ethan? He spent a good five minutes trying to pry it open.      Yeah! He was convinced there was treasure inside. The sci-fi event sounds cool. Actually, it reminded me of this book I'm reading -  Horrible History: Savage Science  - it's really graphic. Like, detailing medieval surgeries and stuff. It's a bit gruesome, but fascinating.      Oh, lovely. Just what you need – gruesome details before bed. I’m trying to shield his brother from all that for as long as possible. Too much information too soon. Though, I suppose anything's better than him deciding to become a metallurgist based on his spoon-eating habit.      You wouldn’t believe the biology homework I had to help with the other night. Cells dividing, mitochondria... I swear, I’ve forgotten more than I ever knew.

…and honestly, young Tilly there, she’s grown another inch, hasn’t she? Seems like only yesterday she was scrambling about, wanting a piggyback. Now she’s nearly eye-to-eye with me!      She has, Arthur, she truly has. Time just flies, doesn't it? Lovely to see her so bright-eyed though. How was school today, love? Anything exciting happen?      It was okay. We started doing this new topic in History, about the Tudors. It's a bit boring really, just lots of names and dates. But Miss Davies said we get to do a project later on, maybe make costumes.      Tudors, eh? A good solid grounding in British history. Dates  are  important, Tilly, even if they don't feel like it at the moment. It all connects, you'll find. Though, I remember my own Tudor project… a truly horrendous Henry VIII costume my mum made. Cardboard and a lot of red felt.      Red felt, you say? Sounds a bit itchy, don’t it? Now, speaking of costumes, is everyone sorted for Halloween then? Young Timmy next door’s going as a pirate, apparently. Quite the little scallywag.      We’ve been thinking about it. Tilly wants to be… well, Tilly, what  do  you want to be? You’ve changed your mind about five times!      I  was  going to be a witch, but Chloe’s doing that, and it'll be awkward if we're both the same. And I thought about a zombie, but that’s a bit… icky. Maybe a unicorn?      A unicorn’s lovely! Very magical. Perhaps you could make a horn? We’ve got some craft stuff at school, I could bring some round.      A unicorn, eh? Fancy that. Reminds me of Old Man Hemmings’ mare, Blossom. He always said she was just like a unicorn, all white and graceful. Used to let me stroke her when I were a lad. Lovely animal. He kept her down by the river, did old Hemmings.      You always have a story connected to animals, Arthur, don’t you? It's wonderful. Remember when you tried to teach our Barney to ride a donkey in Great Yarmouth? That was a disaster!      Barney weren't too keen, no. Stubborn as a mule, that one. But the donkey… well, he weren't overly impressed either, I reckon. Still, a good laugh. I do miss Great Yarmouth, mind you. Used to go every summer as a boy.

Honestly, this is ridiculous. We’ve been inching along for… what feels like an hour? Are we  ever  going to get to the Steam Fair? I was hoping to see the showjumping this afternoon.      Patience, love. It's the Dorset Steam Fair, not a Formula One race. Always traffic. Always. Reminds me of trying to get into Brands Hatch back in the day… absolute chaos. Though this is probably worse.      It’s not just the fair, is it? Every road around here is jammed. They’ve probably not planned for the sheer number of people coming. Honestly, it’s a disgrace. It's like they  want  to discourage people from enjoying themselves.      Well, it’s not discouraging  me  from enjoying a good moan about the traffic, that’s for sure. It just makes me think… imagine trying to get around like this if you were, you know, really elderly. Mum would struggle something awful.      Your Mum's alright, she's tougher than she looks. But you’re right, it’s a nightmare for older folks. And finding suitable housing for them… that’s a whole other kettle of fish. They keep building these fancy retirement villages, all gated communities and extortionate fees. Who can afford those?      Exactly! And what about people who haven't got a penny saved? It's all very well saying “look at these lovely places” but it doesn’t help those on a pension, or relying on benefits. They need more council housing, proper council housing, not the stuff they build now - tiny boxes with no gardens! Old Mrs. Higgins down the road, she’s been waiting years for a bungalow. She's got bad knees, can’t manage the stairs anymore.      It’s awful. And then trying to get decent care… it’s a postcode lottery isn’t it? You hear horror stories. Gran used to say, back in the day, the council really looked after people.      They did. I remember. It wasn’t perfect, mind you, but there was a sense of responsibility. Now… it’s all privatisation and cutting corners. They just want to wash their hands of it. I was listening to the radio the other day, talking about the waiting lists for home help. Months and months, some people are waiting!      They expect family to pick up the slack, of course. Which is fine if you  can , but not everyone has that luxury.

…and honestly, the slugs were  brutal  last year. Absolutely decimated the hostas. I'm seriously considering getting ducks this time around. Though, I’m not sure if 0321’s garden is really duck-appropriate, you know? It’s quite contained.      Ducks! That’s…ambitious. Though, effective, I suppose. A natural slug patrol. No, you’re right, this isn’t really duck terrain. It’s lovely, but a bit too manicured for webbed feet. Honestly, I was thinking more along the lines of copper tape for the pots, and maybe some beer traps strategically placed. A slightly less…involved approach.      Beer traps, yes! I’ve tried those. Works for a bit, then they just…seem to get used to it. Like slug happy hour. Copper tape is a good shout, though. I always forget about that. This allotment thing… it just feels like so much more space to protect. My little balcony garden is manageable, but a full plot… it's daunting.      It  is  bigger, definitely. But think of the potential! We can grow so much more than just tomatoes and herbs. I was already daydreaming about a dedicated raspberry patch and maybe even trying my hand at pumpkins. Remember old Mrs. Higgins down the road from my gran? Her pumpkins were legendary.      Ooh, pumpkins! Yes! And proper, carving-size pumpkins, not those little ornamental ones. Although, having said that, a few of those pumpkins  would  look nice dotted around. What are you thinking in terms of layout? I’m completely blank. I’m good at the planting bit, terrible at the planning bit. That’s why you’re here, isn’t it? My brains trust?      Precisely! Brains trust at your service. I've been sketching a few ideas. I was thinking raised beds for most things – easier on the back, and better drainage. We could have a row dedicated to flowers, not just for looks but for attracting pollinators. And then a separate area for the heavier feeders like squashes and brassicas. We definitely need to rotate those crops, mind.      Right, crop rotation. I know I  should  do that, have read about it, but always get muddled. It feels like a botanical version of Sudoku. What goes with what, when?      Basically, you don't want to plant the same family of plants in the same spot year after year. It depletes the soil of specific nutrients and encourages pests and diseases. I printed out a little chart, actually.

Right, so you’re  actually  sticking around 'til next week then? Proper sticking around, not just a fly-by visit?      Proper sticking around. Mum and Dad are having a little… moment. Needed a break from the Cambridge intensity and a sympathetic ear, and honestly? Doncaster felt… grounding. Plus, I missed you, you daft thing.      Grounding? Doncaster? You're taking the mick, aren’t ya? It’s not exactly known for its zen-like qualities. Though, I suppose compared to Cambridge… Still, good to have you. It gets a bit quiet here, even  with  me yammering on. So, what's the plan for the rest of the week? We haven't properly done anything since you got here, just caught up, which is nice, mind, but…      I know, it’s been all 'how are yous' and 'what’s been happening.' Honestly, it's been lovely, but I feel bad imposing. Want to actually  do  something? I was thinking we could check out that new vintage shop on Silver Street. I heard they got a cracking selection.      Ooh, aye, that sounds decent! Old Man Hemmings' place? Always smells a bit of mothballs, but you never know what treasures are hidin’ in there. Reckon I could find a proper 70s jacket. We could go tomorrow? I have a lecture on Thursday, and Friday…well, Friday’s a bit complicated.      Tomorrow sounds perfect. And what’s complicated about Friday? Don’t tell me you’ve finally agreed to go on a date with that lad from your history class – the one who keeps quoting Gibbon at you?      Ugh, no! Definitely not. Though, he did bring up the Punic Wars  again  this morning. It's exhausting. It's just…Liam’s coming back. From uni, I mean. He said he might pop in on Friday night.      Liam? Oh. Right. The… childhood friend Liam? The one you've been deliberately vague about for the last three years?      Well, he’s just… Liam. We’ve known each other forever. It's not a big deal. He's just visitin' his grandma. It’s just, I haven’t seen him properly in ages, and it’s a bit awkward trying to figure out how things are now, y’know? It’s not like we fell out or anything. We just… drifted.      Drifted and you’ve spent the last three years actively avoiding any conversation about him. Come on, Amy. You’re terrible at this.

Nah, seriously, this boss is  unfair . Like, strategically unfair. Not a challenging unfair, just… cheap. He keeps spamming that spin attack, there’s no reading it!      You’ve been saying that for the last hour, Liam. Maybe you just need a different strategy? Or, you know, a break. Your knuckles are white.      Easy for you to say, Chloe. You haven't faced the wrath of Grognak the Destroyer! It’s not about strategy, it’s about…algorithmically-dictated frustration! Honestly, this game is supposed to be fun.      Algorithmically-dictated frustration? Sounds about right for modern gaming. You know, I was talking to my cousin back in Manila about this. He said a lot of the mobile games out there are deliberately designed to be addictive, just to get you to spend money. Feels similar, doesn't it?      Yeah, same principle. Pay-to-win, even if it’s just paying to skip past the frustrating bits. Saw a streamer losing his mind over that new  Call of Duty  skin the other day. He spent, like, a hundred quid trying to get it. Hundred quid! For a digital hat.      A hundred quid?! For a digital hat?! That’s mental. I’d rather just… rage quit and go for a walk. Which, honestly, is looking pretty appealing right now. Grognak, you are the bane of my existence. . See?!  Cheap!       Drama queen. Right, who wants more crisps? Anyone fancy a brew? I’m starting to feel peckish. Uni canteen's been serving dodgy pasta all week, I swear.      I wouldn’t mind a cuppa, thanks. And yeah, the canteen’s been rough. I managed to snag a decent veggie wrap yesterday, but it was a one-off miracle, I think.      Actually, I'm good for now. I was thinking of hitting the library later, got a paper due on Friday that I’ve been putting off. Procrastination is a powerful force, you know? It can rival Grognak’s spin attack, honestly.      Tell me about it. I've got that history essay looming. Victorian industrialisation. Fascinating stuff, truly. But significantly less fascinating than avoiding pixelated annihilation.      Oh, don't even get me started on essays. I’m writing about… wait for it… the semiotics of reality television. It's just layers upon layers of manufactured drama and questionable life choices.      Semiotics of reality TV… wow. That sounds… intense. Does that mean you have to watch  Love Island  for research?

…and honestly, Doreen, I still maintain  The Sound of Music  is vastly overrated. All that singing! It gets right on my nerves after a bit. You’d think after all these years, I’d get used to it.      Oh, Gran! Seriously?  The Sound of Music  is a classic! It makes you  feel  things. It's… wholesome.      Wholesome, yes. Saccharine is more like it. Give me a good, gritty kitchen sink drama any day. Something with a bit of realism. You know, like those Ken Loach films. Now  there's  storytelling. Real people, real problems.      Okay, okay, point taken. You’re not a fan of the musical numbers. Though, I think Julie Andrews is amazing. Have you seen anything good recently? I've been proper busy at work, haven't really had time for films.      Not much, to be fair. Old Mr. Henderson down the road recommended something…  Parasite , was it? All Korean, with subtitles. He said it was a masterpiece. I haven’t gotten around to it yet. Still got a stack of Agatha Christie adaptations I’m working through. Can’t go wrong with a good murder, can you?       Parasite  is brilliant! It's… unsettling. Really makes you think. You should definitely watch it. It’s not all gloom, there's some dark humour in there too. And subtitles aren't so bad, honestly. You get used to reading them.      Hmm. Maybe. I do struggle a bit sometimes, my eyesight isn’t what it was. And all those foreign names… I get muddled. Remember when we tried to watch that French film,  Amélie ? I kept asking “Who’s that again?” every five minutes.      Oh, don't remind me! You were driving us all mad! But yeah,  Amélie  is lovely. I liked the quirkiness of it. Listen, how's Auntie Brenda doing? I haven’t spoken to her in ages.      She's… Brenda. Still complaining about the neighbour’s cat and the price of everything. She sent me a letter last week, three pages long, detailing the audacity of the postman for putting her bills through the letterbox instead of  handing  them to her. Honestly, the drama!      Classic Brenda. She lives for the little things to be outraged about. I really should give her a call. I feel bad. Things get so hectic. Are you and Clive going to the village fete next weekend?      That’s the plan. Clive’s hoping to win the vegetable competition again.

…and honestly, the sheer  volume  of submissions for the phonetics project is astounding. People are so passionate about how they say ‘bath’! It’s quite humbling, actually. I’ve got spreadsheets for days.      Sounds…intense. Though I can believe it. People are fiercely protective of their accents, aren’t they? Especially around here in London. You get Southerners, Northerners, everyone blending and butting heads over vowel sounds. Reminds me of arguing with my Nan about whether ‘scone’ rhymes with ‘gone’ or ‘cone’.      Oh,  god , the scone debate. Don't even get me started! My mum is firmly in the ‘cone’ camp, and it's a hill she'll die on. You’re Welsh, right? Where do  you  land on that one?      Surprisingly, ‘cone’. Growing up, it was just… how it was. But I've lived in England long enough to realise it’s a political statement, apparently. Speaking of statements, have you seen the new issue of  Stylist ? They’ve got an article on ‘self-care Saturdays’ and it’s just… exhausting. All this pressure to have a perfectly curated relaxation day.      Self-care is watching  The Undateables  and eating chocolate biscuits. That’s my self-care.      Honestly, same. That show is both heartbreaking and strangely uplifting. It's just…real. It's a good palate cleanser after all the phonetics. Are you alright, love? You seem a bit quiet.      Just thinking. I had that interview today, you know, the one for the admin job?      Oh, how did it go? You were so nervous about it.      It was… fine. Standard interview stuff. ‘Tell me about a time you showed initiative.’ Blah blah blah. But the woman interviewing me kept talking about how important it was to “be a team player” and I just… froze. I'm terrible in team situations. I work best on my own.      Oh, no. I hate that question. It's so vague! What  is  a team player, really? They’re just fishing for someone who’ll do all the work while they take credit. Did you mention you prefer focused, independent work?      I  tried  to, but then I rambled about needing quiet and how I get overwhelmed easily and I think I scared her off.      Oh, you poor thing. Don’t beat yourself up. Some interviewers just aren’t equipped to deal with honesty. Honestly, half the time they’re just ticking boxes. You’re brilliant at what you do, you just work differently.

Right, so I’ve chucked in a load of garlic and chilli, hoping to salvage this… whatever-it-is curry paste. Honestly, you'd think after living with you for three years, I’d have learned to just  ask  what’s in things before using them. It tasted perfectly fine when you bought it...      Guilty as charged. It's the Madras paste. It  is  quite fiery. You're brave even attempting to adjust it. Speaking of things being fiery… the washing machine is making a noise that suggests it’s about to achieve liftoff. Did you notice?      Liftoff? Dramatic, much? Yeah, I heard it earlier. Sounded like a cement mixer full of rocks. I thought it was just… a particularly enthusiastic spin cycle. Is it one of  your  socks again? You have a habit of leaving them… strategically placed.      Possibly. Though, I maintain that socks seem to develop sentience and actively seek out the dark recesses of appliances. It’s a conspiracy, I tell you. No, seriously though, it sounded genuinely bad. I’ll have a look tomorrow. It’s probably just unbalanced, but if it's worse… we might need to start a collection for a new one. They're extortionate, aren’t they?      They are absolutely daylight robbery. Remember when Mam and Dad finally had to replace theirs? It was a whole family discussion, weighing up the cost against the inconvenience of the launderette. Dad was having none of it. "I built this house, I can certainly fix a washing machine!" he declared. Took him three days and a lot of swearing, but he got it working… until it exploded a week later.      Oh, your Dad. Legend. He truly believes he can fix anything with enough duct tape and determination. Which reminds me, Mum was asking about when we’re coming down for Sunday lunch. She was very specific about needing a headcount. Apparently, she’s attempting a roast with all the trimmings.      Oh good. That means Yorkshire puddings. I’ve been craving a proper Yorkshire pudding. I tried to make them a few weeks ago… let’s just say they resembled something closer to coal briquettes. She’ll need to know I’m definitely in, and yes, I'll bring the wine. What about your brother? Is he managing to escape London for once?      He  says  he is. He’s notoriously unreliable when it comes to firm commitments.

...Honestly, the whole VW emissions scandal still winds me up. Years later, and people are  still  dealing with the fallout, aren't they? Especially those who bought those specific models. It’s just… brazen.      It is, isn’t it? A right mess. You'd think, with all their engineers and testing, someone would have flagged it. Though, given the pressures to meet targets… makes you wonder how much is swept under the rug in every industry, doesn’t it? It’s not just cars, either.      It's a classic case of profit over people, plain and simple. And the politicians letting them get away with it for so long… that’s the infuriating part. They were all scrambling to look like they were doing something  after  it came to light, not proactively preventing it. Reminds me of the planning permissions they give out up here. Always a backroom deal somewhere.      Exactly! It's just the feeling of being taken for a fool. And you know, it makes you think twice about  anything  you buy. Like this house hunting, for example. So many things could be hidden. We’re looking at properties in Hunsonby, but even here, you’re wondering about damp proofing, structural issues... and now I'm adding 'potential emissions scandal equivalent' to the list of worries.      Oh, don’t let it put you off completely, love. Every house has its secrets. This area’s grand, though. A bit quieter than what you're used to, I imagine, coming from down south?      Massively quieter. And cheaper! Though, that’s changing, isn’t it? I was looking at some figures the other day. House prices in Cumbria are creeping up, especially since everyone realised they can work from home and want a bit of the good life.      That’s what we're finding. It’s cheaper than Birkenhead, obviously, but not  drastically  so. I keep reading articles about how the North-South divide is shrinking when it comes to property, and it feels true. It's baffling. You'd think being further from London would equal more affordable living.      It  should  do, shouldn't it? But there's the "quality of life" factor they talk about. People romanticize the countryside, you see. They want the rolling hills, the fresh air… and they're willing to pay for it. Though, fresh air doesn’t pay the heating bills, does it? You're feeling that with the energy prices, I suppose?

Honestly, Marjorie, I’m still feeling quite ruffled about what young David said yesterday. Accusing me of being deliberately obtuse about the computer… obtuse! After  I  spent two hours trying to explain how to reset his password!      Now, now, Arthur, don't let it fester. David’s always been a bit quick to jump to conclusions. Thinks he knows everything, that one does. Probably just stressed about Brenda and the little ones.      He  is  a bit like his father that way, George. Always had to have the last word. And David expecting you to be a tech wizard, Arthur, is a bit rich, isn't it? You still maintain that your mobile phone is strictly for emergencies.      Precisely! And it  is  for emergencies! When the boiler breaks down, that's an emergency. Or if I fall over in the garden. Not for sending pictures of his grandson pulling faces! Honestly, the world’s gone mad. It’s all this instant communication, spoils people.      Well, it’s changed things, that’s for sure. Remember when a letter took a week to arrive? You’d forget what you’d said in it. More thoughtful, in a way. Though, waiting for news was a bit nerve-wracking sometimes, particularly when young Sarah was travelling.      Oh, Sarah’s travels… those were adventures. Still, a quick video call is nice, isn’t it? To see their faces. Though, I do worry about the pension situation. They're talking about raising the age again. At their rate, David will be working 'til he drops.      Don’t even get me started on pensions! Years of contributing, and they keep shifting the goalposts. I was promised a comfortable retirement, building bridges and all that, and now… well, we’re lucky we have this little place. Though even  this  feels precarious these days, with all the new housing developments they're planning.      They're building everywhere, aren’t they? I saw the plans for that monstrosity out near Costessey. Hundreds of houses. Where are they going to put the schools and the doctors? It’ll be chaos. And have you seen the prices? Young people can't afford to buy anymore.      No, they can't. Brenda and David were talking about it recently. They're thinking of staying in a B&B for a few weeks while they save up a deposit. Imagine that, living in a guest house with the tourists.

...Honestly, the physics practical was a disaster. Mr. Davies looked like he was about to have a stroke when Leo nearly set the Bunsen burner alight  again .      Leo? Never change. Though, seriously, why does he think fiddling with the gas is a good idea? It’s literally the first thing they tell you  not  to do.      He’s just…Leo. Remember when he tried to ‘improve’ the school’s sound system by wiring a microphone directly into the PA? That was legendary.      Legendary chaos, more like. Security was not impressed. Anyway, physics aside, has anyone actually  started  the biology essay? The one on evolutionary pressures? I'm completely stuck.      Just skim-reading articles at the moment. It's all so…dense. Like, I get the gist of natural selection, but then you get into things like genetic drift and it just makes my head spin.      I've done a bit. Mrs. Thompson said to focus on the peppered moth example. It's pretty straightforward to explain. Industrial revolution, soot, darker moths survive better... you know the drill.      Yeah, but it feels…simplistic. Like, it doesn’t really explain  everything . What about things like sexual selection? Why are peacocks so ridiculously colourful? It doesn’t help them  hide  from predators.      Exactly! And then you start thinking about humans…and it gets…weird. Like, why are we attracted to certain things? Is everything just down to genes trying to replicate? Is there no romance or anything?      Whoa, slow down, Shakespeare. You’re going deep. Don’t tell me you’re already having an existential crisis about the meaning of love?      No, not an existential crisis! Just…thinking about it. It’s just strange, right? Everything feels so complicated, and then biology tries to boil it down to…survival of the fittest.      It’s just one perspective. I mean, you can’t deny the biological basis of attraction, but there's obviously more to it than just genetic imperative. Culture, personality, shared interests…      It’s funny how quickly people jump to biological explanations though, isn't it? Especially when talking about differences  between  people. Like, if someone’s sexist, someone will be like “Oh, it's just his hormones”.      Oh, absolutely. Or if a guy's not showing emotion, "boys don't cry”. It’s used as an excuse for bad behaviour all the time. My mum’s always going on about how feminism is about fighting against those kinds of predetermined expectations.

Honestly, the whole thing with Mum’s infection has been such a worry. They’re keeping her in for observation, just to be sure it hasn’t spread, but she was really quite poorly yesterday.      Oh, bless her. Poor woman. I popped round to check on your Dad earlier, he seemed…well, he seemed Dad, you know? Trying to be stoic but properly worried sick. He asked if I’d seen you.      Stoic? Arthur? That’s a new one! He was pacing the garden like a caged tiger when I spoke to him on the phone. Kept muttering something about needing a new set of tyres on the car, seemingly as a distraction. Says he needs to get to the hospital quickly if anything happens.      He always did use ‘jobs’ as a way to distract himself. Remember when your Uncle George was ill? He repainted the entire shed, twice! Said it needed doing. Poor man, he’s a worry. This infection…is it the same one she had last year, dear? The one after the operation?      No, thankfully, it’s different. The doctors said it’s a waterborne thing this time, likely picked up at the physiotherapy sessions. They’re running tests to confirm. She’s on antibiotics, which is good, but she's so tired. And getting increasingly frustrated with all the tablets. She keeps saying she feels like a pharmacy!      She’ll be like that, won't she? Always been a stubborn one, your Mum. Reminds me of my Nan. She refused to take her blood pressure medication for months, said it made her dizzy. Nearly ended up back in hospital.      Tablets are the devil, I tell you. Never been one for popping pills myself. Always preferred a good strong brew and a lie-down. Though, come to think of it, lying-down doesn’t help with a bad back these days. How’s your knee doing, Arthur? Still playing silly buggers with that acupuncture?      Oh, don’t start on that acupuncture, dear! It’s a load of nonsense. Waste of money, if you ask me. Though, I suppose if it helps… I did try it once, after I fell in the garden, but all it did was give me a bruise!      Actually, Dad’s been saying it's been helping his knee a surprising amount. He's been going to that new place on Lincoln Road. Says the woman is a miracle worker.

…and so, this picture shows people being transported on a ship, packed in really tightly. It’s a really difficult thing to look at, isn't it?      Why are they all squished, Miss Emily? Are they playing sardines?      No, sweetie, it wasn't a game. It’s…it’s a very sad part of history. They weren’t travelling for fun. They were being taken from their homes in Africa, and brought to America to be forced to work for other people, without pay, and without a choice. It’s called slavery.      Slavery? Like when the dinosaur eats the little people?      Not  quite , Leo. This wasn’t about being eaten, it was about people being treated unfairly, being owned by other people like… like your dinosaur is a toy that  you  own. But these were people, with feelings and families, and they didn’t want to be owned.      But why would anyone  want  to own a person? That’s silly.      It is silly. It’s also incredibly cruel. A long time ago, some people thought it was okay to treat others badly if they looked different, or came from a different place. They wanted the work these people could do, like growing things in fields, and they didn't care about hurting them.      Did they fight back? The people on the boat?      Oh, yes they did. Many tried to escape, or bravely spoke out against it, even though it was very dangerous. And eventually, many people realised that slavery was wrong, and they fought to end it. It took a very long time, and a lot of bravery. It’s similar to what happened during the wars, isn’t it? People fighting for what they believed in.      Like Grandad told us about World War Two? With the aeroplanes and the bombs?      Exactly. People fought in that war to defend their freedom, to stop bad people from controlling others. And the people who fought against slavery, they were fighting for freedom too – for the freedom of those who were being held captive.      So slavery is… like a really, really bad war? But without the cool aeroplanes?      In some ways, yes. It was a long, drawn-out struggle. A war  against  injustice. And it didn’t always have battles with aeroplanes. It was a fight for people’s rights, a fight for their dignity.      Dignity? What’s dignity?      It’s…it’s about being treated with respect.

...Honestly, the sheer  audacity  of that influencer trying to flog detox tea. It’s just… irresponsible. You wouldn’t believe the comments, people actually believing it!      Oh, don’t get me started on influencers. They’re a menace, the lot of ‘em. All filtered photos and dodgy advice. I saw one recommending essential oils for, get this, a serious infection! It just makes my blood boil, knowing people will listen to that instead of, you know,  a doctor .      It’s the power of marketing, isn’t it? People want a quick fix, and they’re easily swayed. Remember when everyone was doing the cabbage soup diet? Utter madness.      Cabbage soup! Oh lord. My ex-wife did that. Smelt the house out for a week. Said she felt amazing. Then promptly ate a whole chocolate cake the minute she stopped.      Aye, quick fixes never work. My Doris – bless her soul – always said a good roast dinner was the best medicine. And a strong cup of tea. She wasn’t wrong, you know.      Your Doris was a wise woman, George. Absolutely. Though I'm not sure a roast dinner would have helped Mrs. Higgins next door. Apparently, she’s convinced the government’s putting microchips in the Covid boosters.      No way! Seriously? That’s…a new level of conspiracy.      Old Mrs. Higgins? I wouldn't put it past her. She's always got a story. Though, truthfully, I'm starting to worry about her. She barely comes out anymore.      She's always been a bit…eccentric. Reminds me of old Mr. Peterson down the lane, used to swear he was communicating with aliens. Built a whole antenna on his roof.      Oh, I remember Mr. Peterson! He used to wave at the sky every evening. Though, honestly, some of the things you hear on the news these days…you start to wonder yourself. It’s all a bit frightening, isn’t it?      Frightening is right. You turn the telly on and it’s just one disaster after another. Give me a good wildlife documentary any day. David Attenborough, now  he’s  a national treasure.      Absolutely. I watched ‘Planet Earth III’ the other night. The footage of the snow leopards was incredible. So majestic.      Have you all seen that new drama on BBC One, ‘The Serpent’? It’s based on a true story, about that conman who preyed on backpackers in Asia. It’s really gripping.

Right, dishwasher’s done. Honestly, this is a never-ending battle. It feels like as soon as I unload it, it needs refilling.      Is it magic, Mummy? Does a house elf do it when we’re asleep?      I wish, darling. No house elves, sadly. Just us being a family who… uses a lot of plates. Though, sometimes  I  feel like a house elf, to be fair. What are you playing with, anyway? Still obsessed with Harry?      He’s flying on his Nimbus 2000! He’s going to win the Quidditch match! And Hermione’s helping him with a spell.      Good for them. Speaking of helping… Leo, love, could you maybe start putting the cutlery away? Please?      But I'm building something  important ! It’s… it’s a railway!      A railway? That’s fantastic! What kind of railway?      A really, really long one! It needs to go all the way to… to… well, a long way! It needs a special engine.      Can you make it fly like a broomstick, Leo?      No! It needs wheels! It’s a  train , silly. It needs someone important to  invent  it.      And who did invent the train, do you know? Or rather, one of the first really good ones?      Um… Thomas the Tank Engine?      He’s a lovely engine, but he’s a fictional one. This was a real person. His name was George Stephenson.      George… Steph-en-son? Sounds like a wizard name!      It doesn’t  quite  roll off the tongue like ‘Albus Dumbledore’, does it? But he was a brilliant man. He lived a long time ago, back when things were very different. No cars, no planes, mostly horses and carts... and it took forever to get anywhere.      So he made the train so people could go faster?      Exactly! He was a miner, you see, and he realised how hard it was to get coal from the mines to the places where people needed it. So he started thinking about how to build a machine that could pull the coal carts much more easily. He built his first locomotive – that’s the engine – called the 'Locomotion No. 1'.      Was it shiny? Did it have smoke?      It was! It was quite basic, and very, very smoky. It wasn’t super-fast, but it worked! And people were amazed. He then built ‘The Rocket’ which  was  fast. It even won a competition! They called it ‘The Rocket’ because it was so speedy for its time.

...Honestly, the sheer audacity of it! He just  assumed  because I decorated a cake with little edible footballs, it was officially endorsing the World Cup. Like, mate, it’s buttercream and sugar, not a political statement.      Blimey, that’s a bit much, innit? Did you actually get a lawyer involved, like you were saying earlier?      A lawyer? For a cake? Honestly, Ella, you’re dramatic. Though, I can see why you’d be annoyed. People are mental. It's a good job you didn't plaster the whole thing in flags, eh?      I  considered  it! It was a kids’ party, they wanted flags. But I was wary, even then. And yeah, I had a quick chat with my cousin, she's doing her articles. Just wanted to know where I stood legally. She said it was… unlikely to hold any water, thankfully. Thankfully! Imagine the paperwork.      Sounds like a right kerfuffle. You Aussies don’t have this kind of… liability stress with cakes, do ya? We just chuck on some fairy floss and call it a day.      Nah, different kettle of fish. Though I was getting grief off my uni tutor last week. Apparently, a blog post I did - just a little review of that new supper club in Shoreditch? - needs a full disclaimer now. Something about influencing and consumer protection. It's mad, isn't it? Everything needs a warning label.      See! It's the same thing. People looking for something to complain about. That supper club  is  good though, isn't it? I’ve been thinking about trying to do something similar, but smaller scale, obviously. Maybe just once a month from the café.      Oh, you should! Your food is amazing, Ash. You could do a proper themed night – Italian, or Moroccan, or… something ridiculously elaborate. I'd volunteer to do the desserts, obviously.      Yeah, that’s a brilliant idea. You could even get me to design the flyers. I’m pretty decent with Photoshop when I'm not drowning in essays. Speaking of which… how's the job hunt going, Ben? Still slogging away at those barista applications?      Yeah, look, it's… competitive. Everyone wants a piece of the coffee pie, huh? I’ve got another interview on Friday, a fancy place in Canary Wharf. Trying to emphasise my latte art skills. It's all a bit superficial, honestly. I miss just, you know, making a decent flat white without having to swirl a fern into the foam.

Honestly, this week has  flown  by. Feels like Monday was yesterday. How are you holding up, Anya? You seem to navigate the printer crises with a zen-like calm I deeply envy.      It’s… a skill, I think. Years of battling Russian bureaucracy prepares you for anything, even a jammed laminator at Bottisham. And yes, it  has  been quick. Though, quick also means the constant stream of cover requests doesn't slow down! Did you manage to get anything interesting planned for the weekend?      Oh, the usual chaos, I suspect. My daughter, Emily, has a netball tournament. She’s… enthusiastic, shall we say. Requires a lot of ferrying around and cheering, mostly. And then attempting to reclaim the house from teenage debris. What about you? Anything fun planned? I remember you mentioning you were getting into pottery?      Yes! The pottery class is going well, actually. It’s… surprisingly therapeutic. Getting my hands dirty, shaping something out of nothing. It's a good break from staring at screens all day, you know? I’m attempting a vaguely bowl-shaped object at the moment. It’s currently leaning rather alarmingly to one side. I’m hoping it won’t collapse before the glazing.      That sounds wonderfully characterful! I’ve always admired people who can create things. I’m strictly a consumer of creations, I’m afraid. I tried knitting once. It ended in a tangled mess of yarn and existential dread. I suppose my ‘craft’ is managing to get a room full of teenagers to do their work for an hour.      That  is  a craft, a very important one! You're basically herding cats. It must be tiring, though? All that supervising.      It has its moments. It’s rewarding when you see a student actually click with something, or when a particularly disruptive one has a slightly better day. But yes, tiring. Especially when you get the ones who claim they’ve 'forgotten' their work  after  you've already started the session. Speaking of tiring… have you tried that new café in the village, The Old Mill? I had a slice of their Victoria sponge last week and it was heavenly.      No, I haven’t! I’ve been meaning to explore a bit more, but work always seems to get in the way. Victoria sponge sounds perfect, though. I’m a sucker for a good cream tea. It reminds me a little of my Babushka’s baking, actually.

Honestly, this traffic is  mental . We’ve barely moved since we left that Next place. Did you actually get everything on the list, Mum? I feel like we've been circling Preston for an hour.      I think so, love. Nappies, wipes, the changing mat… oh, and those little muslin squares you wanted. Though they were  so  expensive for what they are, honestly. Just squares of cloth! Reminds me of the blankets your Nana used to make – she could whip up anything from scraps.      Aye, your Nana was a marvel with a needle and thread. Remember that patchwork quilt she made for Sarah when she was born? Sarah practically lived under that thing as a bairn. Used to drag it everywhere.      I remember! It was covered in little bears. Though, honestly, I’m not sure I want a quilt like that for  my  little one. Too…busy. I was thinking something plain, just a soft, fleecy blanket. Something you can just chuck in the wash.      Sensible girl. Though a bit of handmade love is nice, isn’t it? Speaking of which, did you book that surveyor for the new house again? I need to know if it’s all square before we get too carried away buying stuff for the baby.      Yeah, it's booked for next week. Dad’s already convinced he knows everything that’s wrong with it, though. He’s been pointing out damp patches in houses since before I was born.      It's a gift, lass. A curse, maybe, but a gift nonetheless. I’ve seen enough dodgy wiring and crumbling brickwork in me time to spot trouble a mile off. And this house…it  feels  solid. But a survey’s a survey, and we need to be sure.      Exactly. And we need a plan for the renovation. That kitchen needs a complete overhaul. It’s practically prehistoric. Remember when we were looking at kitchens in IKEA? That grey one…      Ugh, IKEA. Don't even get me started. It’s a  nightmare  getting in and out of there on a weekend. Worse than this traffic, honestly. Though, that grey kitchen was nice… but so expensive! Can we even afford to do everything we want? Like, the bathroom’s going to need doing too, right?      We’ll manage, love. One step at a time. We’ve pulled through worse, haven’t we? Remember when I lost my job at the call centre and we thought we were going to lose the house?

Honestly, this is lovely. Just…lovely. A proper cuppa and a bit of peace. Not like trying to navigate that online match with you two last night. Honestly, the shouting!      It wasn’t  shouting , Mum! It was…strategic communication. And Leo kept trying to rush things! We had a perfectly good plan to flank them, and he just went charging in like a headless chicken.      Hey, I thought I saw an opening. You gotta seize those moments, El. Besides, it's just a game. Though, I’ll admit, the level of vitriol from some of those players is a bit…much. I mean, we lost, and one guy was going on about my grandmother.      Your grandmother?! What on earth did he say? Some people have no manners. It's the internet, though, isn’t it? Makes people braver, or stupider, or both, behind a screen. Makes you wonder about the psychology of it all, doesn't it? Why people feel the need to be so awful.      It’s the anonymity, I think. They don't feel accountable. And it's competitive, obviously. But it's weird, isn't it? I was reading a psychology article about online disinhibition effect…basically, we lose our filters when we're online.      That makes sense. It’s definitely less…inhibiting to type something nasty than to say it to someone’s face. Still doesn't excuse it, though. Speaking of inhibiting… I’m starting to feel a bit stuck, actually. The job hunt is dragging.      Oh, love. Still no bites then? You’ve been sending out applications for months. What about that place your cousin mentioned, the tech start-up in Bristol?      I did apply, but haven’t heard back. It feels like everyone is either overqualified or they want someone with five years experience for an entry-level position. It's frustrating.      Bristol’s nice, though, isn’t it? I liked it when we went for that school trip. Lots of street art. It's a bit further than London, though.      It is a bit of a trek. But maybe if you landed something good, it would be worth it. A change of scenery. Speaking of changes, have you two started thinking about Christmas at all? I was trying to look at flights for Spain, but they are  ridiculous  already.      Christmas? Mum, it's October! I'm still trying to get through my mock exams!

...and honestly, copper is just  so  underrated. Everyone goes straight for diamond, but a full set of copper tools – after the upgrade, of course – is honestly really speedy for early game mining. It’s a good stepping stone.      But diamonds are sparkly! And they last  forever . I made a pickaxe and mined, like, a whole mountain with it!      Did you find any emeralds in the mountain? Because emeralds are the best. You can trade them for, like,  anything .      You did, did you? Good lad. Emeralds  are  valuable. But think about it, even emeralds need to be mined with something! Copper helps you  get  to the emeralds. It’s all about the process. Like… remember Old Man Hemlock’s story about the Ironwood tree?      Oh! The one with the grumpy sprites?      That’s the one! He used to say that the Ironwood tree only grew where a meteor made of iron fell and sunk its roots deep into the earth. That’s why the wood was so strong and… well, iron-y! He said the sprites guarded it because it was a piece of the stars.      That’s a silly story. Iron comes from the ground, doesn't it? Like, in caves?      Technically, yes. But stories are more fun, aren't they? It’s like with fabrics. Everyone wants silk, right? All fancy and smooth. But linen is made from flax, a plant! It’s strong and cooling. Old Man Hemlock used to wear linen all the time, said it kept him cool even when he was arguing with the sheep.      Sheep are silly. They just… baa.      They are rather prone to baaing, yes. But back to materials – did you know that gold is actually a really soft metal? It looks amazing, but it bends easily. That’s why it's usually mixed with other metals to make it stronger. Like, in jewelry.      So, gold tools would be rubbish?      Honestly? Pretty rubbish. They break  so  fast. They’re only really good for enchanting. Though, they  look  awesome. It's all about trade-offs.      Mum, have I had my vitamins? The ones that make me strong like iron?      You had them with your breakfast, sweetie. They don’t  literally  make you like iron, remember. They just help your body grow strong. It's like… copper tools helping  you  get stronger in Minecraft, so you can gather better materials.      Can I have some more toast?

Honestly, I’m just… knackered. Uni’s relentless this term. Essays coming out my ears. And then old Mr. Henderson from down the street… honestly, I saw him talking to little Maisie again. Proper creeping around, he was.      Oi, don’t even  start  on Henderson. That bloke gives me the absolute willies. Saw him myself last week, near the park. Just… lurking. It’s disgusting, innit? Makes your stomach turn. You said something to anyone?      Aye, I told me mam. She said she’d have a word with Mrs. Davies, Maisie's mum. But you know how it is, people don’t want to believe that sort of thing. "He's just a lonely old man," they say. Lonely old men don't stare at bairns like that.      Exactly! They don’t. It’s the worst kind of thing. Makes me proper angry, it does. Anyway, enough about that depressing stuff. How's the guitar coming along? Still trying to learn that Oasis riff?      Slowly! Bloody slowly. ‘Wonderwall’ is deceptively hard, y’know? My fingers are killing me, and I sound like a strangled cat most of the time. But I'm gettin' there. You still playing? I haven’t seen you with yours in ages.      I’ve been a bit… distracted, to be honest. Been busy with prepping for the final exams. I picked it up last night though, did a bit of practicing, mostly just messing about. Thinking about trying to learn some Red Hot Chili Peppers – a bit more challenging, but the sound is wicked. You ever give ‘em a go?      Nah, not really my thing. Too much… funk, I think? I’m more a Britpop girl, through and through. Blur, Pulp, definitely Oasis. It just…  feels  like home, y’know? Reminds me of being fourteen, hanging about in town with everyone else, pretending to be cool.      I get that. Everything old is new again, right? Still, you should give them a listen. John Frusciante's guitar work is something else. Proper genius. Gets right under your skin. What about hobbies apart from torturing yourself with chords? Still painting?      Occasionally. When I've got the headspace for it. It’s hard to switch off from essays and thinking about, well, Henderson and all that. It's a good escape though, when I can manage it. Do you ever feel like… we don’t do enough just for  us  anymore? Like everything's always about needing to be productive?

...Honestly, the EPQ is killing me. Mr. Davies keeps saying "more nuance!" but I  have  nuance! It's about the socio-economic impact of reality TV, what more nuance does a bloke need?      Sounds rough. Mine’s on the history of Wembley Stadium. Relatively straightforward, thankfully. Though, digging through archives is… tedious. You’re doing alright with the juggling though, saw you practicing earlier. Distraction tactic?      It's a  very  effective distraction tactic. And it’s surprisingly calming. Honestly, after listening to Leo moan about reality TV for the last hour, I need calming. Anyway, Wembley Stadium? Bit predictable, isn't it?      Hey! It’s a fascinating subject! And juggling  is  good for focus. Helps me think. Though, admittedly, I mostly drop the balls. Speaking of distracting things…did you guys see that exhibition at the Science Museum? The one on Montenegro?      Montenegro? No, missed that. Is it good? We were supposed to go to that immersive Van Gogh thing last weekend, but my nan needed help with her garden. Classic nan.      Apparently, the Montenegro exhibition’s really focusing on their response to the refugee crisis a few years back. Lots of photography, interviews… quite powerful, according to my older sister. She’s studying international relations, so she’s pretty clued up on that stuff.      See, that sounds way more interesting than my EPQ! It reminds me of that trip your family took there last summer, Maya. You were saying it was beautiful, but…complicated?      Complicated is a good word. Absolutely stunning coastline, honestly breathtaking. But you see the poverty too, you know? Especially away from the tourist hotspots. It's not like…obvious, begging-on-the-street poverty, more like… people really struggling, doing everything they can. Makes you realise how lucky we are, even just having a half-term break in Slough.      True. My mum's always banging on about being grateful for what we have. Which is fair enough, I suppose. Still makes you feel a bit guilty enjoying a takeaway, though. Speaking of which, anyone fancy grabbing some chips from Mario’s? I’m starving.      Chips sound good, but I was actually thinking about trying to make that vegetarian shepherd’s pie my mum made the other day. It was surprisingly amazing. I've been trying to eat less meat.      Oh, you’ve gone vegetarian then, Leo? Good for you! It’s definitely the right thing to do, ethically.

Honestly, this place is robbing us blind. Eight hundred quid a month for a room that's… well, let's just say it’s  cosy . Cosy like a sardine can.      Tell me about it. Eight-fifty for me, and my window looks directly onto a brick wall. A  very  grey brick wall. Back home in Falmouth, I had a sea view for less. Granted, Mum and Dad were subsidising, but still!      You two are lucky you have windows at all. My room feels like a dungeon, honestly. And the heating… it’s either arctic or Sahara. There's no in-between. My mum keeps sending messages asking if I'm eating properly. She thinks I’m just shivering myself to death and living off instant noodles.      Noodles are life, mate. Seriously. Saved me from proper hunger pangs this week. Didn't realise how expensive food was up here. Thought I'd be rolling in it with my student loan, turns out it disappears faster than my motivation on a Sunday evening.      Student loan? Don’t even  mention  that. It's barely enough to cover rent and beans. I’m working at the Sugarhouse two nights a week just to afford nights out… which ironically, are also expensive.      I’m trying to pick up some shifts at that vintage shop in town, but the manager’s a bit… picky. She said my ‘aesthetic’ didn't quite fit. What does that even  mean ? I was wearing a Breton top and jeans! Pretty standard, isn't it?      Maybe she wanted someone more… ostentatious? You know, big hair, brighter colours? Some people have very specific ideas. My dad keeps asking me about internships, and I'm like, ‘Dad, I haven't even finished my first semester!’ He's already planning my career path. Says it’s the ‘family duty’ to go into accountancy.      Family pressure, I know that. My Nan keeps hinting I should be applying for apprenticeships instead. She thinks university is a waste of time. “A good trade is a good trade!” she keeps saying, like I’m living in 1950.      Mine’s just worried I’m going to end up a starving artist. Which, to be fair, isn't entirely unrealistic with my degree choice. English Lit isn’t exactly a gateway to riches, is it?      Tell me about it. My auntie keeps asking when I’m going to "get a real job."

…and honestly, Mrs. Davies from class nearly had a fit when I explained the Boxing Day sales. She just couldn’t grasp the concept of fighting over discounted toasters at 6am. It’s a  cultural  thing, isn’t it? Completely beyond a lot of my students.      Oh, it is. Utterly. Though I suspect even  some  Brits struggle to grasp it! It’s the sheer… frenzy. Reminds me of your Auntie Margaret, actually. Remember her at the garden centre the week before Christmas? For the poinsettias?      Oh,  God  yes! She elbowed old Mr. Henderson out of the way, didn’t she? He was ever so polite about it, but I saw his face. She wanted the biggest, reddest one, naturally. Said it 'made Christmas'. She’s a force of nature, that woman. Are you still sending her a card?      Of course. Always. Despite the poinsettia incident, she’s a dear. And she always remembers to ask about your teaching. Such a genuine interest, even if she doesn’t entirely understand what it  is  you do. “So, you teach… foreigners, dear?” Last time I spoke to her.      That’s her summation of it, yes. It’s more complex than that, but I’ve learned not to argue. It’s less exhausting. How are things with the consultancy work? Still travelling all over the place?      It’s… busy. Just back from a training session in Birmingham, actually. Long days, but rewarding. They were a lovely bunch, genuinely eager to learn. Better than some I've had, I can tell you. Though it's getting harder, the travelling. I miss having a proper routine. And missing Christmas with everyone… last year was awful.      I know, Mum. It wasn't the same without you. Dad was moping about, asking if you were alright every five minutes. Honestly, I think he missed your complaining about the sprouts more than anything!      He's a silly man, your father. But I do enjoy a good grumble about the sprouts, don't I? This year, though, I’m trying to limit the work in December. I’ve told them I’m unavailable after the 18th. Hopefully, they'll respect that. I want a proper Christmas, with all of us.      That sounds lovely. We're having Emily and Ben over this year. And little Leo, of course. It's going to be chaos, but good chaos. Are you still planning on doing the secret Santa?      Absolutely!

...Honestly, Dad, it feels so weird being back in the car. It’s exactly as I remember. Smells faintly of…air freshener and biscuits, I think? Two years is a  long  time.      Biscuits, you say? Your mum always insisted on a tin in the glove compartment “just in case.” Habit, I suppose. It  is  good to have you back, son. Really good. Feels like yesterday you were learning to drive in this thing, panicking about roundabouts.      Don't remind me! I still get a little anxious about roundabouts, actually. And the speed cameras around here are relentless now, aren’t they? They’ve popped up seemingly overnight. Saw three just between Crayford and here. Practically a revenue stream, that's all it is.      They are a pain, that’s true. I get complaints about them  all  day at work, you know. People losing points on their license, fines…It’s the same old story. Thankfully, I’ve managed to keep a clean record, touch wood. Though I swear one nearly caught me last week – thought I was doing 35 in a 30!      Speaking of work, how are things? Still dealing with angry callers all day?      Oh, you know how it is. Always someone unhappy. Though last week was particularly bad. A bloke called, ranting about his broadband for a good half hour. Turns out he hadn’t paid the bill. Honestly. I’m starting to think I need a holiday.      You do! You deserve a break. Mum was saying you were feeling a bit under the weather last month too. Is that still lingering?      Just a nasty bug, thankfully. Knocked me for six for a week but I'm right as rain now. It got me thinking though...about moving.      Moving? Where to? Not…Brighton, are you? You’ve always threatened Brighton.      Well, your sister's been on at me for ages to be closer to them. And it's a nice place, Brighton. Bit…vibrant. Might actually suit me. Got a bit of a sea view place in mind. What do you think?      It's...a big change. But if it's what you want. It’d be good to have you closer to Sarah and the kids. Have you told Mum? She'll be devastated.      I haven't yet. Thought I'd test the waters with you first. She'll come around, eventually. It's not like I'm running off to Tanzania or something!

Honestly, the student feedback today was… a mixed bag. One called my lecture on post-structuralism “illuminating,” which is lovely, naturally. But another said it was “intellectually exhausting” and suggested I “tone down the theory.” Honestly, some days I feel like I’m either speaking to geniuses or… people actively trying to nap. How was  your  day navigating the wonderful world of media ethics?      Sounds about par for the course, doesn't it? You can’t win ‘em all. Mine was… interesting. Had to spend an hour on the phone with the university PR department, dealing with a minor kerfuffle. Apparently, a student journalist accidentally tweeted a rather unflattering quote from the Vice-Chancellor about funding cuts.      Oh,  dear . That sounds like a PR nightmare. Did they manage to contain it? You always seem so good at that sort of thing – smoothing ruffled feathers and crafting the ‘right’ narrative. Is it a skill you honed working at that agency before academia, or just a natural talent for diplomacy?      A bit of both, I think. Mostly damage control. The tweet was swiftly deleted, and they’ve put out a carefully worded statement about ‘ongoing discussions’ regarding resource allocation. Trying to make it sound proactive rather than panicked. It's exhausting though, this constant spin. Sometimes I miss just… thinking. Speaking of avoiding exhaustion, I desperately need new headphones. Mine finally gave up the ghost mid-podcast this morning.      Oh no! The indignity! Which podcast were you listening to? And yes, the spin is draining. It’s why I sometimes retreat into obscure French philosophers. Keeps me safely away from ‘the narrative’. I was thinking of popping to the shops tomorrow - are you after anything specific? Maybe we could even brave the music shop. I’ve been meaning to get that new Florence + The Machine album on vinyl.      Florence! Good taste. Vinyl sounds wonderful. Footwear actually, if you don't mind. My trusty trainers are… well, they're starting to resemble something dredged from the bottom of the sea. And yes, definitely headphones. Noise-cancelling preferably. It's the only way to survive marking essays with the builders next door seemingly determined to renovate their house with power tools.      Trainers and noise-cancelling headphones – noted. We’ll have to brace ourselves for the Saturday crowds though. The city centre is always mayhem. Perhaps we should go early? Say, around ten? Then we can grab lunch somewhere nice afterwards.
