Right, so I’ve definitely put too much garlic in this. It smelled  amazing  when I chopped it, but now… well, it’s asserting itself, isn't it? Asserting itself is putting it mildly, love. It’s practically shouting. But honestly, a bit of garlic never hurt anyone. It’ll be fine with the pasta. How’s the beanbag coming along? Still committed to the multi-coloured yarn explosion? Committed might be too strong a word. Obsessed is probably closer. It’s…progressing. Slowly. I’m on the fifth panel, and honestly, my hands are starting to ache. It's a lot more work than I anticipated. Especially trying to get a consistent tension. You’d think after knitting three scarves and a hat, I’d have that down. You underestimate the sheer  volume  of yarn a beanbag requires. It’s a different beast altogether. Think of it as… large-scale knitting. A textile engineering project, really. You’re avoiding admitting my technique is rubbish, aren’t you? And speaking of large-scale projects…have you given any more thought to the bathroom? I was looking at shower curtains online, and there are some frankly terrifying options. One had lobsters.  Lobsters , Alistair. In a bathroom. Lobsters? Good Lord. No. Definitely no lobsters. I was thinking, maybe something simple? A nautical stripe? Or even just a nice, plain navy? It needs to feel a bit calmer, don't you think? All that bright yellow tile… it’s a bit much. I agree about the tile. It was here when we bought the place, and I'm not dismantling a perfectly functional bathroom just for aesthetics. But a nautical stripe… that could work. It would at least tie in with the little sailboat print I got for the guest towel. Though, I'm also eyeing up these little ceramic succulent pots. They might soften it all a bit. Succulents sound good. Something living in there. Less…marine crustacean. Are you thinking of getting a real plant, or the fake kind? You know my track record with keeping things alive. Oh, you and your ‘black thumb.’ Don’t worry, I was thinking fake. Unless you're feeling particularly ambitious? They do have surprisingly realistic-looking ones these days. Speaking of realistic, the lighting in there is appalling. I keep saying we need to change the bulb, but it never seems to happen. It’s on the list!

Right pleasant this is, isn't it, Margaret? Just sitting a bit. Legs aren't what they were, you know. Feels like a lifetime since I could properly potter about in the garden.      It is lovely, Arthur. Though “pottering” for you always involved more directing than actual doing, if I remember correctly. You were always the supervisor, weren’t you? Telling me exactly where the petunias  should  go.      Now, that’s not entirely fair! I ‘ad a vision, I did. And you’ve got to have a vision for a proper garden. It’s not just chucking a few seeds in and hoping for the best. Speaking of which, David, you alright over there? You've been awfully quiet. Not brooding about the cricket again, are you?      Not at all, Arthur. Though the less said about that last match, the better, frankly. I was just… thinking about the price of everything. Honestly, it's getting ridiculous. Filling the car up felt like a second mortgage payment this week.      Oh, don’t I know it! Everything’s gone up. Tea, biscuits, even the wool for my knitting practically doubled in price. And the heating… well, we're just wrapping up warmer, aren’t we? It's a good job we don't have little ones to worry about keeping warm anymore. Remember when little Emily used to go through clothes like water?      Emily. Good girl, Emily. Always a bright spark. Used to follow me around the garden, asking endless questions. “What’s this, Grandad? Why is that one droopy?” It kept me on me toes, it did. Better than any crossword puzzle.      She did have a knack for asking the difficult questions, didn’t she? It’s no wonder she ended up a lawyer. Speaking of which, I had a rather interesting call from her this morning. She’s working on a pro bono case – a young family facing eviction. It’s just… heartbreaking to hear these stories.      Oh dear, that’s awful. It’s happening all over, isn’t it? People struggling just to keep a roof over their heads. It’s not right, with all the wealth in this country. What's the world coming to, really?      Not right at all. Back in my day, you worked hard, you provided for your family. Things weren't easy, mind you - post-war, rationing and all that - but there  was  a sense of security.

Honestly, darling, you wouldn't  believe  the queue at Sainsbury's yesterday. It was absolutely rammed. Everyone's getting their Christmas bits and bobs already. I felt like I was battling for the last Brussels sprout!      You and your sprouts, love. You’d think it was the end of the world, the way people carry on at Christmas. I still reckon waiting ‘til the week before is the best strategy. Less chaos.      Honestly, it’s already stressful just  thinking  about it. I saw a post online about someone queuing for an hour for a turkey crown. An  hour ! I’m considering a goose this year. A bit different, you know?      Ooh, a goose! That sounds lovely. Though, a bit…traditional, isn't it? My nan used to always have goose. It's a lot of work though, isn’t it, getting all the fat off? We usually just do a chicken. Easier.      A goose is lovely, but you're right, it  is  a lot of faff. We’re doing turkey, as always. My mum would have a fit if we didn't. She’s already planning the menu, bless her heart. Speaking of which, have we decided what we're doing for Boxing Day? Your sister mentioned inviting us over, John?      Hmm, I did hear something about that. Penelope and David are pushing the boat out, apparently. New garden furniture she wants to show off. It’ll be good to see them, though it’s a long drive to Brighton.      Brighton on Boxing Day? That sounds…cold and windy. But it’s nice they're thinking of us. Are we all up for it, though? I was kind of hoping for a quiet one, Netflix and leftovers kind of day.      I wouldn't mind Brighton. A bit of sea air would do me good. I've been cooped up in the hospital all week, it feels like. Honestly, this trainee nurse practitioner course is  exhausting . So much paperwork!      Oh, darling, you're doing so well though! It's a huge commitment. Remember how nervous you were starting it? It’s just brilliant you’re changing your career like that. And, well, Boxing Day is a long way off. We've got plenty of time to decide. What about Christmas Eve? Are we still doing the pub with the Millers?      Definitely the pub with the Millers. That's tradition! We wouldn’t want to disappoint them.

Honestly, this morning is just  gorgeous . You’d never know all the… well, the ‘discussions’ we had yesterday about getting here were even necessary. I still can't believe the state of that roundabout near Ercan airport!      Roundabouts are a national sport here, dear. Strategic chaos, I call it. You get used to it. Though, I admit, that one  was  particularly ambitious. Reminded me of Piccadilly Circus at rush hour. You’re still a bit shaken by the drive, I see.      Shaken isn’t the word. More… perplexed. And slightly terrified. My husband, David, was gripping the dashboard like his life depended on it. He’s normally so placid. It just felt… different to driving in the UK, you know? So much more… assertive.      Assertive is a polite way of putting it. They have a certain… confidence in their driving. Having lived here, on and off, for nearly ten years now, I've adapted. You learn to anticipate. And a constant prayer to whatever deity you favour doesn’t hurt. But tell me, what made you choose Northern Cyprus? It’s not exactly the typical holiday destination, is it?      Well, David’s retired now, and we wanted something… different. We’ve done the Canaries, Spain, Italy - all lovely, of course, but felt a little… predictable. A friend of a friend raved about the history here, the weather, the cost of living. Plus, I'm a history teacher, so the Roman ruins and Byzantine churches were a major draw. Have you been to Salamis?      Salamis? Oh, yes, several times. Wonderful place. Though, it gets dreadfully hot walking around those stones in the summer. I was over there just last week, actually. Was showing old Mrs. Henderson from next door around. She’s only here visiting for a month. She insists on wearing a full sun hat and factor 50, even in the shade. Bless her. It’s a bit of a culture shock for her, she's from a very quiet village in Hertfordshire.      I can imagine! We're trying to be mindful of the cultural differences. I read up on some of the customs before we came. Though, I’m sure I’ll still put my foot in it at some point. Are there any particular things we should be aware of, beyond the roundabout etiquette?      Oh, lots of little things. Don't be surprised if people offer you tea  constantly .

Honestly, this air is just  brutal  today. I swear it's getting worse, even than last week. My throat already feels scratchy.      You're not wrong. It's a thick one, isn’t it? I could practically taste the particulate matter on the walk back from the university. It’s amazing how quickly you get…used to it, and then realise how awful it actually is when you have a relatively clear day.      “Used to it” is a terrifying phrase! It feels really grim when you think about long-term effects. I was explaining to a student today – poor Amelia, she’s just arrived from Devon – about AQI and how it compares to back home. Her face just dropped. She kept saying how she could  see  the stars in Devon.      Oh, Amelia. She's going to have a bit of an adjustment period. It’s a world away from the Devon countryside. Still, she’s a bright spark. She’ll cope. Reminds me a bit of you, actually, when you first came here. Remember how shocked  you  were?      Shocked is an understatement. I felt like I was breathing through cotton wool. And endlessly washing my hair! Still do, to be honest. But it’s… life, isn’t it? At least the university is pretty good. How was your day? Any particularly… challenging students?      Relatively quiet, thankfully. Had a slightly heated debate with Ben about the post-structuralist interpretation of Dickens – he was adamant that it was fundamentally flawed. It became a bit of a circular argument, to be honest. He’s a good student, though, very engaged, just… fiercely opinionated. It’s refreshing, sometimes.      Sounds like a classic Ben moment! He's always been one for intellectual sparring. I miss those old seminar room arguments, actually. Although, a quiet life is nice too. Have you heard anything from David and Sarah lately? I haven't seen their WeChat updates in a couple of days.      They messaged me this morning. They're at that pottery workshop in Jingdezhen. Apparently, Sarah's discovered a hidden talent. She sent a picture of a hideous vase that she’s incredibly proud of.      Oh, Sarah! That sounds perfect. David probably sculpted something perfectly symmetrical and aesthetically pleasing, I bet. They're so sweet though, aren't they? Settled in so well. I still can’t believe they decided to stay permanently.      They said the opportunities for their research are just too good to pass up, and they’ve built a really strong community there.

Honestly, this butternut squash is a nightmare to peel. It’s like wrestling a… well, a very orange, stubborn beast.      You say that every year, love. And every year, you manage to conquer it. Remember that time you nearly took your thumb off, though? That was… dramatic.      Don't remind me. Harold insisted on bandaging it with a tea towel. Said it was "good enough." Honestly, the man.      Speaking of dramatic, have you  seen  the latest season of ‘The Crimson Coast’? It's absolutely bonkers. Lady Beatrice has… well, I won't spoil it, but let’s just say her secret is a doozy.      Oh, I’ve recorded it! Been meaning to start. Everything’s been a bit chaotic at work, I haven’t had a chance to just  sit  yet. How was your day, darling? Still battling corporate jargon for a living?      You know it. Spent three hours refining the phrasing for a banner ad about… paperclips. Paperclips, Mum! The existential dread is real. Found some old photos on my phone though, while procrastinating. Remember that disastrous holiday to Cornwall?      Disastrous? It was character building! The tent nearly blew away, you were convinced a seagull stole your sandwich… good times. Let me see those photos.      Look! Little me, looking windswept and utterly defeated by a pasty. And there's Dad trying to rebuild the tent with one hand and a carrier bag full of biscuits with the other.      Oh, Harold, always prioritising the necessities. Biscuits  are  essential. This soup is going to need seasoning, I think. Are we thinking crusty bread with this, or something else?      Crusty bread is perfect. I can pop to the village shop, get a nice loaf. They’ve got that sourdough one you like. Will I grab anything else while I’m there? Milk? Eggs?      Eggs would be brilliant, thank you. We’re getting low. And maybe some of those little cherry tomatoes? They're good in a salad tomorrow.      Ooh, salad sounds good. I think I need something green after a diet consisting primarily of instant noodles and caffeine today. Being a creative is  exhausting .      You need to look after yourself, love. All that screen time can't be good for you. Have you been for a walk recently?      Not as much as I should, admittedly. It's just…easier to get sucked into work. I promised Chloe I’d meet her for brunch on Saturday, though.

...Honestly, it's just baffling, isn’t it? They’ve rerouted the 2 bus again. Honestly, it's a nightmare now if I want to get to Mum’s from here. Used to be dead easy, straight down Mill Road. Now it does this ridiculous loop through Cherry Hinton.      Seriously? They've messed with the 2 again? That bus is practically a Cambridge institution. What's the reasoning this time? They always have some convoluted explanation. Probably something to do with “optimising flow” or “addressing congestion.”      Aye, some rubbish like that. Something about prioritising access to the Biomedical Campus. As if  that’s  more important than people just getting around town! It's a right pain. I was thinking of popping to Cambridge University Press bookshop later, and now it'll be a mission.      Oh, I was planning on going there myself this weekend. They've got that sale on architectural monographs on, remember? I was hoping to pick up a couple. We could go together, I could drive. Avoid the bus chaos altogether.      Would that be alright? I didn’t want to impose. It’s just… the thought of wrestling with the bus network fills me with dread. And I really wanted to browse.      No imposition at all! I enjoy driving, and honestly, the buses here are… special. They operate on a different plane of existence to anything I experienced at Harpenden. Everything was so… orderly there.      Orderly? Harpenden! Everything’s orderly in somewhere like Harpenden, isn't it? It's practically a postcard village. Cambridge is… a bit more  lived in , shall we say. It’s also just full of students, all protesting about something. I saw one bloke outside Senate House earlier, with a sign about tuition fees. Good on him, but it was blocking the pavement.      Ah yes, the Cambridge student protester. A staple sight. It’s part of the charm. Though I do sometimes wonder if they're actually achieving anything. It’s a different vibe to my university experience, that's for sure. Bristol felt… less performative, somehow.      Performative is a good word for it. Durham was… a bit intense, if I'm honest. All castles and rowing, and a very specific type of student. Plus, you could pretty much walk everywhere. Cambridge, you  need  public transport or a bike, and even then…      Exactly! And the cyclists! Don’t even get me started on the cyclists.

...and honestly, the way he was describing the Lake District to his mum, you'd think he'd  discovered  it! Like nobody had ever visited Cumbria before. It was quite endearing, actually. He’s so excited to come up next weekend.      Oh, men. Always the explorers, even when we’ve been dragging them to these places for years. Is he bringing that fancy camera of his? He was going on about low light settings last time we spoke.      He is, naturally. It's practically an extension of his arm at this point. He's hoping to get some good shots of Derwentwater. You know, moody landscapes and all that. But honestly, I'm just glad he's coming. It feels like ages since we've all had proper time together.      It has! And it’s lovely to be out, isn't it? This little cafe is  so  much nicer than my usual lunchtime sandwich at my desk. Did you see the cake selection, Mum? Honestly, I shouldn’t, but…      Go on, have a slice. You deserve it. You’re working yourself ragged, aren’t you, with all this transcription? It’s a good job, though. Steady income. Something I… well, never mind.      Mum, don’t start. We’ve talked about this. You're perfectly happy pottering about, aren't you? And the garden is looking wonderful. I saw the photos you sent – the roses are spectacular!      It keeps me busy, I suppose. But I miss the structure, the… the mental gymnastics of teaching maths. It wasn't about the  work , you see. It was about making things  click  for someone else. Explaining something until they finally got it. It's a peculiar satisfaction.      I can imagine. Explaining things is… satisfying, even when it’s not algebra. I spend half my day untangling people’s mumbled recordings. Honestly, the things people say! The accents, the background noise… sometimes it feels like I’m deciphering an ancient language.      You’re probably closer than you think! I work with people all day, and the way language is used in HR is… a whole other level of complexity. It's all about what  isn't  said as much as what is. Honestly, sometimes I feel like a translator  between  people, rather than just within the English language.      It’s funny, isn’t it? I taught English grammar for years, the rules, the precision… and then you hear the way people  actually  speak, and it’s a whole different beast.

Honestly, it looks even more… blob-like from this angle. The O2. It still feels so strange it's just  there  now. Remember when they were building it? All the arguments about ruining the skyline?      Vaguely. I was more concerned with the Millennium Dome being a complete white elephant, if I'm honest. And it kind of was, wasn't it? At least the O2 makes money. Though, blob-like is a good description. It’s like a giant metallic… jellyfish.      A jellyfish! That’s brilliant. Though, I still think it’s a shame more people don’t utilise the river for transport. Look at this walk, it’s lovely! We could easily get into central London, or even towards Canary Wharf, and avoid all that tube pushing.      You say that, but then we have to factor in the timing, the potential for drizzle… and frankly, my legs aren’t what they used to be for long walks. Especially not after lugging everything around at work. Speaking of which, the office is pushing this 'team building' exercise – a weekend in the Lake District. With the kids.      Oh,  no . The kids and a work weekend away? That sounds less like team building and more like a logistical nightmare. They’ll be wanting snacks every five minutes, arguing over who gets the window seat…      Exactly! And I'm supposed to be ‘engaging’ with Brenda from accounts while simultaneously refereeing squabbles over Scrabble. It makes me long for the days when holidays were just… us. A small cottage somewhere, no agenda.      Remember that tiny place in Cornwall? The one with the garden overlooking the sea? Simple perfection. And no pressure to network with colleagues. It’s a long way to drive though, isn’t it? Which is why we haven’t been back in ages.      Drive? That’s another thing. Everyone at work keeps talking about road trips, and I just… grimace internally. So grateful we don’t own a car. The cost of it all! Insurance, petrol, parking in London… It’s insane.      It really is. Freedom, though, isn't it? That's what people chase with cars. But freedom from debt and stress is far more appealing, for me at least. It’s funny how different perceptions of freedom are.      Actually, talking about things being appealing… I was trying to follow an American baking recipe last night. It called for ‘one cup of flour.’

Honestly, this rain is  relentless . It’s been chucking it down all morning. Ruined any chance of getting a decent picture for my dissertation, let me tell you. Landscape photography in Kent in November… ambitious, to say the least.      Tell me about it, love. I’ve been soaked through just walking to the bus stop. My cardigan’s still dripping! Makes you appreciate a nice cuppa, doesn’t it? And a warm kitchen. Though speaking of kitchens, my washing machine’s started making this awful noise again. Honestly, it’s on its last legs, I reckon.      Oh, don’t even  start  on appliances! My tumble dryer’s threatening to give up the ghost. And with Leo constantly covering himself in mud…it's a never-ending cycle. Speaking of Leo, did you manage to get tickets for the sports day?      I did! Managed to snag a couple right at the back, but hey, better than nothing. I’m hoping it won’t be  pouring  then. I’m picturing a field of mud and tiny, freezing children.      They don't care, do they? Leo will be loving it, covered head to toe in muck. Remember when your little Emily insisted on wearing her princess dress to the park, and ended up looking like a swamp creature?      Oh my god, yes! She was  furious  when I tried to get her to change. Absolute meltdown. She insisted she was still a princess, just a muddy one. It was hilarious looking back, utterly traumatic at the time!      She was a force of nature, even then. She’s still got that stubborn streak. Actually, she’s been going on about wanting to go to ‘Build-a-Bear’ for weeks. Any idea what I should get her? She's obsessed with pandas right now.      Oh, they’re lovely! A panda sounds perfect. You can get them to put a little heart inside, with a message. Bit pricey, though, aren’t they?      Very. It’s the accessories that get you! Everything is extra. Leo's got a collection of cuddly toys, honestly. He refuses to part with any of them, even the ones that are falling apart. He sleeps with a raggedy old dinosaur called Derek.      That’s sweet. Emily had a similar phase with a bear called Barnaby. Absolutely loved it. It smelled faintly of…well, everything. Speaking of little ones, how’s the potty training going with Alfie?

Right, so, three weeks house-sitting… feels a bit surreal, doesn’t it? Bit of a world away from grey Wellington, even with the sunshine. Still, a good chance to actually  think , I suppose. Which, let’s be honest, we rarely get.      Surreal is a good word. And yes, absolutely. Thinking time is a luxury. I was just reading about this research on the benefits of ‘intentional pauses’… it’s really interesting. But more pressing, have you actually  started  thinking about what you want to do when we get back? Beyond just collapsing in a heap, that is.      Collapsing is definitely on the agenda. But yeah, I have. I’ve been turning over the idea of… well, actually taking the plunge with Liam and Sarah. Their tech startup. They’ve been asking me for ages to come on board, help with the business development side.      Liam and Sarah? Seriously? That's… a big shift, isn't it? From running your own small consulting firm to being a cog – even a vital cog – in something already established?      Not a cog, darling, a  steering wheel ! They specifically want my experience. And frankly, the consulting has been… a little lonely lately. I miss the collaborative atmosphere. And the potential with that company… it’s huge. It’s a bit scary, though. Less control. More risk.      I can see the appeal. It sounds… stimulating. But you've built something really solid with your consulting. And remember how stressed you were last year, trying to land that big contract? This feels… different. Are you sure it's not just the sunshine talking?      No, it's not just the sunshine. It’s… I’m starting to feel a bit restless, and I need something that genuinely excites me. The consulting pays the bills, it’s intellectually challenging sometimes, but it doesn't  fire me up  the way this might. What do  you  think? Be honest.      Honestly? I think it’s a bold move. And I admire that. It's just… it would mean a significant change in our lifestyle, wouldn't it? Probably more hours, possibly more travel. And we’ve been talking about… well, trying for another baby.      That’s what I’ve been wrestling with, too. The timing feels tricky. We both agreed we wanted to wait until things felt a bit… settled. And this is the opposite of settled! But they were asking if I could start in six weeks.

…Honestly, though, I still can't get over how much Mark’s accent has changed since uni. He went down to London for a year, and came back sounding… well, almost Southern. It's bizarre.      Nah, he’s always been a bit of a chameleon, our Mark. Picks things up. Remember when he tried to do an American accent for that drama club thing? Sounded like a dodgy cowboy.      Oh god,  don’t  remind me. It was awful! But yeah, the accent thing is weird. I think it’s just…exposure. You hear something enough, you start to mimic it. Not consciously, but…      It’s not just accents, is it? It's the  words  people use. Down south they say "queue" like "cue". Drives me mental. It's just…wrong. Like they’re not even trying.      You lot are obsessed with accents! It’s just how people sound. It doesn’t make them any less…people. Though I’ll admit, trying to understand a broad Yorkshire accent sometimes feels like learning a new language.      That’s fair, it’s just… Mark. He’s always been proper Northern, you know? Proper Warrington. Now he’s all rounded vowels. Speaking of proper Northern, did anyone else spend yesterday battling Pokémon on their phones?      Was doing, yeah! Had a Charizard appear right outside the Co-op. Nearly walked into a pram trying to catch it.      I spent ages trying to find a decent Pikachu. Gave up in the end. My Fitbit was going mad though. Apparently, I walked three miles purely chasing imaginary monsters.      Three miles! My poor feet. I did a bit, but I’m still recovering from that camping trip last week. Honestly, I think I’ve aged ten years.      Oh, the camping? How did that go? I remember you were dreading it.      Dreaded is an understatement. It rained. Constantly. And there were sheep…  everywhere . Staring. Judgemental sheep. And Alex kept trying to build a fire with damp wood.      Classic Alex. He's got the enthusiasm, but the execution… leaves something to be desired. Remember when he tried to fix his mum's washing machine?      Oh, Christ! The water damage! She didn't speak to him for a week!      Speaking of family, my nan keeps going on about wanting an iPad. Says she needs to “keep up with the times.” It’s sweet, but I can see it ending in disaster. She’ll accidentally order 50 After Eights online or something.

Now, this roast’s lovely, lass. Really lovely. Though not quite like me mother used to make, mind you. She’d always put a touch of mustard in the gravy. Just a touch, see, gave it a bit of…zing. You don’t get that these days. Everything’s bland.      Oh, don’t start on the blandness of modern food, Arthur! You say that  every  time. It's perfectly seasoned, thank you, dear. Besides, you ate three slices of Yorkshire pudding. I think you're enjoying it.      Gran, you’re incorrigible! And it  is  good, honestly. Much better than the canteen at the uni. They tried to do a 'themed night' last week - apparently 'Global Cuisine' meant everything tasted vaguely of curry powder.      Sounds about right. Though, to be fair, catering for that many undergraduates is a logistical nightmare. I volunteered to help, and nearly lost the will to live wrestling with a mountain of naan bread.      Naan bread, eh? Sounds fancy. Reminds me of when Clive – that was me cousin, you know, the one who went to London – he came back one year raving about Indian food. Said it was all the rage. Back then, in Norfolk, the most exotic thing we had was a bit of pineapple upside-down cake.      Oh, Clive! He was a character, wasn’t he? Always trying to be a bit… cosmopolitan. Remember that awful perm he got? It looked like a bird had nested in his hair.      I’ve only heard stories about Clive. Sounds like he was good for a laugh. Speaking of laughs, did anyone see the football on Saturday? What a result! Norwich absolutely smashed ‘em.      Absolutely brilliant! I almost woke the neighbours celebrating the second goal. I still can’t believe how well Sargent is playing these days. A real breakthrough season for him.      Football… hmm. Used to go down to Carrow Road with me dad, years ago. Different game back then. Less… diving, for a start. All a bit silly now, if you ask me. Too much money involved. Spoils the spirit of it.      Arthur, you have an opinion on everything! But I agree, it’s gotten a bit ridiculous. Players earning more in a week than I did in a year. It's just… obscene. They should be grateful, the young whippersnappers.      It's a cultural shift, I think. Sport is now entertainment, a global industry. It's a bit disheartening, but it's the reality.

...Honestly, the thought of another essay on post-structuralism just makes me want to curl up and  disappear . I’m seriously considering just…leaving. Dropping out.      Whoa, hold up. Leaving? Like,  leaving  leaving? You were so excited about uni, especially coming up here to Lancaster. What’s brought this on, El?      I don't know! It’s just…not what I expected. It’s a lot more work than sixth form, obviously, but it’s not the work itself. It's just…pointless. All of it. I feel like I'm jumping through hoops for the sake of it. And I miss…well, I miss home, I miss the sea, I miss just  being  without constantly feeling pressured.      I get that, a bit. It's a massive change, isn't it? Going from a little town like Falmouth to, well,  Lancaster . It’s proper fields here, innit? But you've only been here a term. Give it time! You'll find your feet. Remember when I was panicking about my sociology lectures? Thought I'd signed up for something completely beyond me.      Yeah, but that was a lecture. This is…everything. And I’m just not feeling it, Liv. I thought I wanted to study English Literature, but now I'm wondering if I even  like  English Literature. All those deadlines...and the people! Everyone seems so…intense.      Intense is just a polite way of saying ‘a bit weird’, mostly. Don't take them too seriously. What did your mum say about all this anyway? She always had a good head on her shoulders.      She’s…supportive, in that “I want you to be happy” kind of way. But I know she’s picturing me with a proper job at the end of this, you know? Something sensible. She always wanted me to be a teacher. Like her.      And what about your dad? He's the quiet one, but he always seems to know what you're thinking. Did he grow up near the sea too? You always talk about Falmouth like it's…part of you.      He did! He was a proper little beach bum as a kid. Apparently, he spent all his time building sandcastles and annoying the fishermen. Honestly, sometimes I think that’s where I get my inability to commit to anything. He always said he'd drift, and he sort of did, ended up a marine biologist, which is cool but…not exactly stability, is it?

…and honestly, the spreadsheet nearly defeated me. Three different departments, all needing slightly different data formats, and deadlines looming. It's just  project coordination  isn't it? Sounds fancy, but half the time it's just being a highly organised go-between. How’s marketing treating you, anyway? Still drowning in social media analytics?      Drowning is a good word for it! Though Pearson's slightly different. It’s not  just  about likes and shares. We're trying to demonstrate actual educational impact, which… complicates things. It means less 'viral video' brainstorming and more actual research. It’s definitely keeping me on my toes, though. Though, honestly, sometimes I miss the simple days of uni when ‘research’ meant reading SparkNotes the night before an essay.      Tell me about it. Remember those all-nighters fueled by instant noodles and questionable coffee? God, those were the days. Less responsibility, definitely less spreadsheets. Still, it’s good you're finding it challenging. Better than being bored out of your skull, right?      Absolutely. Though sometimes I wonder if "challenged" is the right word. More like "mildly panicked". How are things with…Liam? Still going strong? I feel like I haven't properly heard about him in ages. Last update I had was something about him attempting to build a shed?      Oh, Liam. The shed…that’s a saga. It’s less ‘building’ and more ‘complicated negotiation with gravity and warped wood’. He’s determined, though. It's actually quite endearing, watching him. We’re good, yeah. Really good. It feels…stable. Which is nice, after all the chaos of our twenties so far. We’ve been talking about maybe looking at places, you know? Somewhere a bit bigger, potentially outside the city.      Wow, seriously? That’s huge! That’s proper grown-up stuff. Congratulations! I’m so happy for you both. I’m still very much in the “fling-to-avoid-commitment” stage, I think. Met someone a couple of weeks ago, lovely guy, really funny. But I already feel the urge to self-sabotage brewing. It's a talent, honestly.      Oh, you’re terrible. You always did have a knack for overthinking things. What’s the worst-case scenario you’ve conjured up so far? He's secretly a taxidermist? He only likes you for your Spotify playlist?      Worse! He's a really dedicated birdwatcher. And don’t get me wrong, I have nothing against birdwatching, but he gets  very  passionate about it.

Honestly, this eBay seller… says ‘lightly used’ but look at this! The box is practically falling apart. I should’ve just gone with Amazon. More expensive, aye, but at least you  know  what you’re getting.      Let me see, Mum. Oh, wow. That  is  rough. Lightly used, eh? More like heavily abused. Are you going to message them?      I probably will. Though I’m not holding out much hope. They’ll just say ‘item as described’ and fob me off. It’s a right pain, isn't it? I just needed a specific size of craft knife blades, and they were a tenner cheaper on here than anywhere else. Should have known there'd be a catch.      You always go for the cheapest option. It's a Yorkshire trait, innit? "Waste not, want not" and all that.      Aye, you’ve got a point there. My mother drilled that into me. Still, it's frustrating. Amazon's delivery is just so reliable. Remember that garden gnome you wanted for your birthday last year? Arrived the next day, perfectly packaged.      Yeah, the one with the fishing rod? Brilliant. And you didn’t have to risk getting a smashed gnome like this craft knife situation. Although, ironically, I've had good luck with eBay for video games. Found a complete, boxed copy of  Chrono Trigger  for a steal.      Oh, aye, you and your retro games. That's a different world, that is. People will pay anything for those. It’s just… sometimes, with everyday things, I rely on the reviews. You read all these glowing reviews on Amazon and you think, ‘right, this must be decent’. But even  those  can be dodgy, can’t they? I saw a program about fake reviews the other day. People getting paid to write positive ones.      That’s mental. So, you can't even trust the reviews?! It's a conspiracy!      Not a conspiracy, lad, just… people being dishonest. Makes you wonder what's real and what's not, doesn't it? Still, I suppose Amazon does have better customer service. If something goes wrong, you can usually get a refund quite easily. eBay's a bit more of a fight.      Have you thought about using that website, Vinted? Sarah at school is always getting clothes from there. She says it's good for branded stuff, like Adidas and Nike.      Vinted… no, I haven't. Is that second-hand clothes, mainly?

Rain again. Honestly, Cambridge seems to get more rain than London these days. Though, Mordern wasn’t exactly known for its sunshine either, mind you. Just…grey. Always grey.      You say that every time, Grandad. It's beautiful here, even when it’s drizzling. And it  is  different from Lewisham, even though it’s still London-adjacent. More…peaceful. Less hustle.      Peaceful is a polite word for it, love. It’s…slow. Everything’s slow. Back in Mordern, even though it wasn't glamorous, there was always something  happening . People talking, shops bustling… Now, it feels like everyone’s hiding inside, avoiding the weather and each other.      Well, people are busy, Grandad. They've got lives. I mean, I'm swamped at work. New system rollout is a nightmare. Production's completely skewed, and everyone is walking on eggshells around Mr. Henderson.      Henderson, is it? Sounds like a right misery. Used to be managers who actually  managed . Now it's all about systems and rollouts and…eggshells. What even  is  a production controller, anyway? Sounds important, but utterly baffling.      It's basically making sure everything gets made on time, and to the right specifications. It’s a lot of spreadsheets, a lot of chasing people, and a lot of having to explain things in multiple ways. Trust me, it's not glamorous. Though the pay is good, which is…necessary. Rent in Cambridge is insane.      Insane is right. Used to be able to get a proper house for a song. Now, it’s a postage stamp for a fortune. You should see what they’re charging for flats in Mordern now, though. Gentrified, they call it. Fancy coffee shops and art galleries where Old Man Hemmings used to sell his dodgy fruit.      Dodgy fruit? Sounds like Mordern was…full of character.      Character? It was rough around the edges, love. But it was  real . Everyone knew everyone. If you needed help, someone would give it. Nowadays…people barely look up from their phones. Even here, in supposedly tranquil Cambridge.      I know what you mean. It feels…disconnected sometimes. Though work is pretty social. We had a team lunch last week. Sarah – she’s in marketing – was telling me about her allotment. She's trying to grow prize-winning pumpkins.      Pumpkins! Goodness me. Fancy that. Allotments are a good thing, though. Gets you out in the fresh air, even when it’s raining. Used to have one myself, back in the day.

Right, so, genuinely, the thought of flying on Christmas Day… it fills me with dread. Absolutely dread. My aunt Carol actually  suggested  it this year. Said it's the only way to guarantee a seat. Guarantee a stress-induced breakdown, more like.      Oh, Carol. She’s always got a ‘practical’ solution that involves maximum inconvenience. I can’t believe she’d even propose that. You'd be stuck in an airport, surrounded by… well, Christmas chaos. Plus, the staff are probably miserable.      Honestly, the whole travel thing at Christmas is just… a mess. Remember last year when Liam got stuck in Manchester for twelve hours? He missed Christmas dinner, the poor lamb. I wouldn't even  think  about suggesting anyone flights.      Twelve hours? Crikey. That's rough. See, this is why I stick to driving. Sure, it's a slog, but at least I’m in control. Though…last Christmas Eve, driving back from my sister’s, nearly hit a deer. Big bloke. Came out of nowhere.      No way! A deer? Here? I thought that was more of a countryside thing.      Nah, mate, they’re wanderin’ further and further in. Rural creep, I reckon. Luckily I slammed on the brakes, avoided it. Bit of a scare though. And the smell…oof. Not pleasant.      Oh, that’s awful! That would be a terrible thing to happen on Christmas Eve. Actually, speaking of smells, I’m thinking about the Christmas food. I’m doing all the baking this year, obviously, but what are we thinking for the main meal? I’m happy to do a full spread, but…      Ooh, excellent! Your mince pies are legendary, you know that. As for dinner, I was thinking a proper roast turkey. I’ve got a good butcher I can get one from. Plenty of sprouts, Yorkshire puddings… the works.      Sounds brilliant. Though, can we  please  negotiate the sprouts? I’m not a huge fan, you know. They’re… intensely green.      Negotiable. Perhaps just a small portion for you then. I’ll do honey-glazed carrots as well.      Honey-glazed carrots? Now you’re talkin’. Although, I gotta say, back home we’d be havin’ a barbie. Seafood, prawns, the whole lot. Hot Christmas with no need for a roaring fire.      A Christmas barbecue sounds… novel. I’d miss the cosy feeling though, wouldn’t you? Lots of blankets, a fire crackling…      Definitely. Speaking of cosy, I saw a fox scavenging around the bins last night.

...Honestly, the satnav’s sending us round the houses. I swear it thinks Mill Road is a mythical beast we need to  avoid  at all costs, not the quickest route.      Mill Road  is  a bit of a beast, innit? Especially on a Saturday. But yeah, it seems determined to take the scenic route, doesn't it? Are you sure you put in the right postcode for Dave’s?      It’s alright, I checked it on my phone earlier. It’s definitely the right one. ANON's satnav is just… questionable. It's like it was designed by someone who’s never  been  to Cambridge.      Exactly! It’s actively fighting against us. It's almost as bad as trying to decipher my Nan's accent when she's on the phone. You know, the one where everything sounds like 'babbledy-goo'?      Oh, God, yeah! Every Nan has that mode. Mine just gets REALLY loud and speaks slower, like I'm a toddler. But yours sounds… advanced.      Mine just blends into a general Midlands mush. You can barely tell what she's saying unless you've known her for about thirty years. It’s evolved, you know? It's a dialectal Frankenstein.      Speaking of dialects, I was listening to the radio earlier and there was this chap on, doing a phone-in about local accents. Apparently, Cambridge has its own little micro-accent, supposedly. All rounded vowels and dropped ‘h’s, mostly.      Really? I hadn’t noticed. I mean, being from Birmingham, I'm pretty attuned to accents, but everyone here just sounds… posh to me. Or students trying to sound posh.      That’s fair. You’re used to something a bit more… robust. I grew up closer to London, so I’ve picked up bits and pieces. Trying to avoid sounding like I’m  putting on  an accent, though, is a constant battle.      It's hard, isn't it? Especially when you move around. I spent a year in Scotland for uni, and I definitely started to pick up a few phrases, even unconsciously. My flatmate kept pointing it out.      It's funny how accents change you, almost like a layer of personality. Keeps things interesting. Although, sometimes I worry I'm losing my Brummie twang. My mum would kill me.      Nah, you’ve still got it. It comes out when you’re explaining something technical, doesn't it? All very precise and…  Birmingham .

...Honestly, the bass in that track was  ridiculous . Like, rattling-your-ribcage ridiculous. Did you guys feel it?      Felt it? Mate, I thought the speakers were gonna blow! It wasn't even a proper club sound system, just the school hall speakers. They really turned it up, didn't they? I was half expecting Mr. Harrison to come storming in.      He would have. Old Harrison hates anything above a conversational volume. Seriously, you can hear him tutting if someone’s chewing gum too loud. But yeah, the bass  was  good. It was that new Headie One track, right? The one everyone's been going on about?      Yeah, 'Public Display of Affection'. It's proper sick. Better than anything that’s been out lately, bruv. Though, I still rate Dave’s last album. That was a masterpiece. Proper storytelling and the production was, like,  layers  you know?      Dave’s alright. A bit… serious though, innit? I prefer something you can actually move to. Like, I’ve been back on a grime kick lately. Getting into some of the older stuff, like Dizzee Rascal’s ‘Boy in da Corner’. That album still hits. It’s just…raw.      Dizzee is legendary. Proper old school. Speaking of old school, my dad was trying to get me into Pink Floyd last week. Said it’s ‘musically important’. I tried, I really did, but it just sounds like… long wailing guitar solos to me.      Pink Floyd?  Seriously ? Your dad's got questionable taste, fam. That stuff’s for, like, philosophy students and people who wear tie-dye. No offence.      Haha, no, I get it. It's a bit... much. My mum's into Fleetwood Mac. She always has it on. It's alright, but not something I'd choose. It feels like background noise, not proper music. It’s just… different.      It’s a generation thing, I reckon. They grew up with it. It's like trying to explain the appeal of, I don’t know, hyperpop to them. They’d just look at you like you’ve grown a second head. Which, y’know, is fair enough.      Hyperpop's a trip, though. It's like someone took all the sounds and just… scrambled them. It’s kinda fun for a laugh. Speaking of weird sounds, did any of you see that documentary about the physics of music? The one we had to watch a bit of in physics class?

...and honestly, Leo, you were absolutely flying on that Balanceability bike today! Mrs. Davies said you were one of the quickest she's seen pick it up. You were a little wobbly at first, but you just  went for it .      It was fun! But my legs hurt a bit now.      Mine too! I kept falling off at the beginning. Old Man Hemmings helped me though. He makes funny faces.      Old Man Hemmings  does  have a talent for funny faces. He's a good egg. It’s brilliant that you both tried it, even when it was tricky. That's what matters, isn’t it? Knowing you can try something new and, even if you wobble, you keep going.      Like learning to swim? I was scared at first.      Exactly like learning to swim! Remember how worried you were about putting your face in? And now you’re zooming up and down the pool like a little fish.      I still need armbands sometimes.      And that’s okay! We all need a little help sometimes. Speaking of swimming... did I tell you about Sarah? She’s finally getting her house renovated.      Sarah? The one with the fluffy cat?      That’s the one! She's having a whole extension built, and… get this… she's putting in an indoor swimming pool!      Woah! With a diving board?      No diving board, thankfully. She’s very sensible. Apparently, there’s going to be a little, manmade waterfall feature. Isn’t that amazing? But she was telling me about how dangerous diving into even seemingly deep water can be. You absolutely  have  to know the depth, even in a proper pool.      Gran always says no running around the pool.      Your Gran is very wise. Always listen to your Gran. What were you two chatting about at school today? Anything interesting?      We talked about dinosaurs. And someone brought in a really cool fossil. It was a tooth!      I told Chloe about National Cat Day in Japan. It’s on the 9th of February because '9' sounds like 'meow' in Japanese!      That’s brilliant! You always pick up the most interesting facts. That's lovely, darling. Did Chloe like that?      She did! She has a cat called Marmalade.      Oh, she does! A very orange, very fluffy cat. Right, speaking of interesting things… I’m thinking pizza for dinner. What do people think?      Pizza! Yes! With pepperoni!      And mushrooms!      Mushrooms for you, pepperoni for you.

Right, honestly, I feel like I’ve aged ten years just  planning  this conference. Honestly, the requests some people come up with… it’s beyond belief. And then trying to find a venue that isn’t charging the earth in peak season? Forget about it.      Sounds stressful. You need to de-stress. Honestly, you look knackered. Have you even been to the gym this week? I swear, you used to live in the place.      Don’t even start on the gym. It’s been… sidelined. Massively. Between the conference and, well, everything else, I just haven’t had the head space. And when I  do  have a spare hour, the thought of battling for a treadmill spot just fills me with dread.      “Everything else”? Is that code for… Liam-related everything else? Last time we spoke, things were still a bit… rocky.      Rocky is putting it mildly. It’s… complicated. He’s just… frustrating. He keeps saying he wants us to spend more time together, and then when I suggest something - like, I dunno, a simple walk - he’s suddenly ‘too busy’. Too busy with what, I’m not entirely sure. Probably strategizing his next FIFA match.      Oh,  honestly . That’s awful. You deserve someone who actually  wants  to spend time with you, not someone who treats you like a last resort. You're brilliant, you're busy, he needs to pull his weight.      Exactly! I told him as much last night. It ended with him saying I was ‘being dramatic’. Dramatic! As if wanting a bit of effort isn’t a perfectly reasonable request.      Men. Honestly. They’re a different species sometimes. My brother was exactly the same with Sarah. Spent the whole time complaining he didn't have enough 'me time' while simultaneously moaning she didn't want to do anything with him. It was head-melting. Eventually, she just called it quits. Best thing she ever did.      It’s just…I keep hoping he’ll change. We’ve been together for two years, and I thought we had something good. But then these things happen and you start to wonder if you were imagining it all.      Two years is a good amount of time, but it’s not a lifetime. And hoping for someone to change constantly is exhausting. Look, maybe you need a break. A proper break. Not just a brief pause, but a proper "me time" period.

This is proper good, Auntie Kath. Best pepperoni I’ve had in ages. Even better than Domino’s, an’ that’s saying summat!      Aye, well, Old Man Hemmings at the deli really knows his stuff, doesn’t he? Takes pride in his ingredients. Glad you’re enjoying it, lad. You demolished that first slice in about three bites! You were hungry after all that concentration at the Domino Drive.      Concentration? He was tryin’ to cheat, Kath, that's what it was! Keepin’ his tiles hidden up his sleeve. Nearly had me fooled, he did.      I was  not  cheating! I was just… strategically concealing my options. It's a valid tactic! And you were just lucky you pulled that double six in the last round, Uncle Arthur. Lucky.      Now, now, both of you. No accusations of cheating, and no sour grapes, Matthew. It was a good game. Arthur did have a bit of a run, didn't he? Though I thought  I  was doing well until your grandad started playing all those doubles.      Ha! Years of practice, Kath, years of practice. Know all the angles, I do. Speaking of practice, you gettin’ yer hair cut this week, Matthew? It’s lookin’ a bit like a haystack.      Mum said I need one, yeah. I’m goin’ on Saturday. I told her I want it shorter at the sides, proper tidy, but still a bit on top. Like… like Erling Haaland.      Erling Haaland, is it? Well, that’s ambitious. The barber will probably just laugh. You’ve got a lot more hair than him, to start with! Remember when you wanted a mohawk? Good grief, that was a phase.      A mohawk! Nearly gave your mother a heart attack, that did. Said you looked like a punk rocker. Though, I secretly thought it suited you. Gave you a bit of edge.      It was just for the school disco! I didn't actually  keep  it. It washed out after a week anyway. What about you, Uncle Arthur? Been gettin’ weighed down with all them sheep lately? You look a bit… substantial.      Substantial? Now look here, young man! A haulier's gotta keep his strength up. Plus, I've been enjoyin’ Kath's baking a bit too much. She makes a cracking rhubarb crumble, y’know. Can't resist it.      He can say that again! I made two this week. One for us, one for Mrs. Peterson next door.

Right, honestly, I’m craving a proper pub roast. Like, the kind where you get a Yorkshire pud the size of your head and enough gravy to swim in. We haven’t had one since…well, since Christmas at your Mam’s, I think. You and your pub roasts. Cambridge is criminally lacking in  good  pub roasts, isn’t it? It’s all gastropubs doing deconstructed this and micro-herbed that. Give me a good, honest, slightly-greasy roast any day. Although, deconstructed Yorkshire puddings… that’s just a crime against humanity. Exactly! And the veg! They always give you, like, three tiny roasted carrots and a sad little floret of broccoli. Back home, you'd get mountains of roast potatoes, parsnips, and proper greens. Remember old Maureen at the Black Cat? Her roasties were legendary. Maureen! Oh, bless her. She’d practically force extra gravy on you, even if you were politely trying to refuse. She was a force of nature. Speaking of forcing things on people…have you seen what happened with that celebrity chef, the one who does all the fancy foams? He tried to claim boiled Brussels sprouts were ‘trendy’ this week. No way! Brussels sprouts? ‘Trendy’? Honestly, some people. They were the enemy for a solid decade, and now suddenly because some posh chef says so, they're fashionable? It's ridiculous. I actually quite like them, but not because they're 'trendy'. My Nana always used to steam them with a bit of butter and nutmeg. Proper comfort food. My Mam used to drown them in cheese sauce. Which, let’s be honest, solves most problems. Though, I’m trying to be better with the cheese sauce these days. PhD life requires a tenuous grip on healthy eating. Speaking of which, I’m attempting to get my five-a-day. Hence the carrot carnage. You and your ‘five-a-day’. You say that while simultaneously eyeing up the biscuit tin. I saw you. I…what biscuit tin? I haven't seen a biscuit tin. It’s a completely separate entity that has no bearing on my nutritional choices. It simply  exists . Oh, you’re hopeless. You know, you’d think someone studying for a doctorate would have more self-control. Though, I suppose endless theoretical physics can really work up an appetite. It does! It really does. It's mentally exhausting. And trying to explain quantum entanglement to my parents is… well, it's an exercise in futility.

Right, okay, let’s just clarify  again . You absolutely cannot  describe  a sound. It has to be an action mimicking the sound, or… something. Rhys, you did it with the ‘buzzing bee’ round. You  said  “it sounds like a bee!” That's a blatant rule break.      Now, hold on a minute, Nia. I was under pressure! It was a difficult card. And besides, Dad was nodding along, wasn’t he? He didn’t say anything.      I was enjoying the spectacle, to be honest. It  did  sound like a bee. Perfectly accurate.      The spirit of the game, boys, the spirit of the game. It's about creative interpretation, not pedantic rule-following. Though Nia is right, technically.      Oh, leave him be, Nia. He gets flustered easily. Remember that time he tried to assemble that flat-pack wardrobe from IKEA? It was… a performance.      That's different, Mam. That was structural integrity at risk. This is a simple board game! And it’s already taking  ages . We need to be efficient. I want to get to the purple cards; those are the really good ones.      Efficient? You’re a teacher, you’re used to wrangling thirty thirty-year-olds, surely a little articulate-related chaos won't phase you?      That's a fair point. They're slightly more…challenging. But still. The rules are the rules. Honestly, growing up in South Africa, we were always very strict on rules. It’s probably ingrained in me. My grandfather was a judge, you know?      A judge? No way! That explains the… meticulousness. So, is that where you get your competitive streak from?      Maybe! I definitely remember being told constantly to ‘play fair’. It's a bit of a family motto, I suppose. Though my uncle… he was a different story. He once tried to convince us that Monopoly money was  real  currency.      Oh, I remember him! He was a character. Always up to mischief. He tried to teach me to gamble with pebbles when I was eight.      Your Uncle Gareth was a rogue. Lived life on his own terms. Ended up running a small cafe in Marbella, didn't he?      Right, my turn then! Okay, it's… "The sound of one hand clapping". Go!      Oh, brilliant. That's deliberately obtuse, isn't it?      Impossible! You can’t physically…      Think Zen koan! It's a philosophical question, not a literal sound.      Hmm… that’s clever, Glenys.

Right, I am  completely  out. Another disastrous hand. Honestly, Gareth, you’re ruthlessly efficient at this Rummy. It’s almost unsettling.      Efficient? Nah, just lucky, Catrin. Pure, unadulterated luck. Though, admittedly, I do enjoy seeing you flustered. It’s endearing.      You’ve said that every round, Gareth. It’s lost its charm.      Oh, leave the girl alone, Gareth. She's a good player, just having a bit of a run of bad cards. Besides, it's not about winning, is it? It’s about spending time together, isn’t it, loves? Especially after dragging ourselves all the way to Hereford.      Mam, you are a saint. And yes, it  is  lovely to be away. Though I did promise my Year 6s I'd be marking their creative writing all weekend... this feels a little…subversive.      Subversive? You're playing cards in a cottage in Hereford. The most subversive thing happening right now is probably the sheep eyeing up Mrs. Higgins’ prize-winning roses next door.      He has a point. And besides, you needed a break, Catrin. You were practically glued to your laptop last week. Burning the candle at both ends, as usual.      I know, I know. It’s just…they’re a lovely class, and they really put effort in. Little Maisie wrote a story about a unicorn who runs a bakery. A bakery! It's adorable.      Ah, Maisie. She’s a sweetheart. She reminds me of you as a little girl, always full of imagination. Remember that time you convinced everyone the garden gnomes were actually tiny Welsh miners?      Oh, please don't remind me! I was  convinced . And I made Gareth dig little tunnels for them!      I did  not ! Well, alright, I dug a couple. You were so insistent! And the look on Mr. Davies’ face when he saw… priceless.      He nearly had a heart attack. Said we were ruining his perfectly manicured lawn.      He was always a grumpy man. But honestly, the gnomes  looked  like they were searching for coal. It made perfect sense at the time. Anyway, back to being thrashed at Rummy. Is anyone else even close to going out?      I’m getting there, slowly but surely. Though Gareth is definitely the one to watch. He’s like a machine. He picked up Rummy from his grandfather, you know. Old Man Rhys? A legend at the village hall.      Legend is a strong word. He was… tenacious. And prone to accusations of cheating.

Honestly, this Christmas is just  needed . Uni’s been… a lot. Like, good, but a lot. All the coursework deadlines hitting at once before the break was brutal.      Tell me about it! I finished a double shift at the care home yesterday, then had to do a massive grocery shop. It’s relentless, isn’t it? Though, at least I'm not writing essays on the French Revolution. What are you studying anyway? Still History?      Yep, still History. Though I'm starting to wonder if a gap year might be sensible. Just to… breathe. Everyone else seems to have it so figured out. Like, Speaker_3, you’re a trainee accountant already, right? That sounds  so  organised.      Organised is a strong word. It’s definitely keeping me busy. It's an apprenticeship, which is good because I get paid while I learn. Sixth form was… fine, but I definitely wasn't cut out for another three years of full-time study. Plus, I'm already earning, which is a huge bonus. What about you, Speaker_4? Still designing fancy bits for ships?      Something along those lines. Navel Combat Systems Engineer, officially. Still can't explain it to my nan without her thinking I fix plumbing on boats. It's good, though. Really challenging. Plus, ironically, it paid for most of my uni fees, so I feel a bit less guilty about the student loans.      Speaking of feeling guilty, I’m feeling guilty for working Boxing Day  again . Retail’s just… crazy this time of year. At least I can earn a bit extra for Christmas presents, but it's not exactly festive. How's everyone's Christmas shopping going?      Stressful! I’ve got Mum a scarf, but Dad is impossible. He always says he doesn't  want  anything and then hints at things for weeks.      Oh, I know that game! My grandad’s the same. I ended up getting him a subscription to a magazine about vintage tractors. He seemed pleased. Mostly because he could tell everyone about vintage tractors.      I'm making things this year. Trying to, anyway. I’m attempting to crochet a blanket for my nan. It’s…slow going. And it looks suspiciously wonky.      Don't worry about wonky! It’s the thought that counts. My strategy is to buy gift cards. Efficient, if not particularly thoughtful. Although, I did get Speaker_5 a really ridiculous novelty mug.      Oh really? Do tell.

Honestly, this shepherd’s pie is lovely, love. Just what I needed after all that… fuss with the car this morning.      Oh, the car again? What happened this time, Gran? Did it refuse to start? You said something about a funny noise yesterday.      Funny noise is an understatement, darling. It sounded like a bag of spanners being thrown around in the engine! Took young Malcolm from next door a good hour to figure it out. Seems the exhaust pipe’s gone… proper rusted through it has.      Sounds expensive. You’re better off getting the bus, Gran. Honest. Less stress, less hassle. You always did hate driving in Cambridge.      Less stress? Easy for  you  to say, dear. You’ve been retired for five minutes and spend your days watching David Attenborough! I need to get to the shops, don't I? I can't exactly cycle with three bags of groceries balanced on the handlebars.      You  could  get a shopping delivery, Gran. They do it now, you know. Sainsbury’s, Tesco... They’ll bring it right to your door.      Delivery? What am I, helpless? I like  choosing  my own vegetables. Feeling the firmness of a tomato, seeing if the lettuce is crisp. You can’t do that online, can you? It’s the whole experience, love. Used to be, I’d walk to the market every week. Lovely it was.      Walk? That market’s ages away now, Gran. Remember when it was just down the road? Before they moved it all to the Grand Arcade? You’d get a right bargain back then, always did.      Oh, those were the days. Mrs. Higgins selling the best plums you ever tasted. And old Mr. Patel with his spices… the smell alone was worth the trip. Now, it’s all fancy cafes and overpriced handbags.      It’s changed a lot, that’s for sure. But you still do a good walk, though, don't you? You were telling me last week about your stroll along the Backs.      I do, when the weather is decent. Though even that’s getting trickier. My knees aren't what they used to be, you know. I used to cycle everywhere as a girl. Down to Southend on a summer’s day, with a picnic. Now  that  was freedom.      Cycling in Southend? That's a long way! Didn’t you used to say your Dad wouldn’t let you go further than Leigh-on-Sea?

...and honestly, the data from the Norfolk dialect recordings is  fascinating . You wouldn’t believe the subtleties in vowel shifts even within a ten-mile radius. It's so much more nuanced than people give it credit for. Though, getting people to  talk  about how they say things is always the tricky bit, isn’t it?      Absolutely! It’s the observer’s paradox, isn’t it? The moment you ask someone to consciously articulate their speech, it changes. I’m mostly dealing with the transcriptions at the moment – a lot of the older interviews. It’s really interesting seeing how language has shifted even in the last fifty years. This Alumni day is quite something though, isn’t it? Feels a bit surreal, being back in the Law Faculty after…well, after  years  of data analysis.      Surreal is a good word, my dear. I feel like I’ve aged a decade just looking at all these bright young faces. Though, it’s good to see the Faculty still attracting a keen bunch. You two are with the Linguistics department, I presume? I’m Arthur Penhaligon, used to lecture here in Constitutional Law.      Hi Arthur, lovely to meet you. I’m Chloe, and this is Daisy. Yes, we’re both working on the dialect project. It’s based out of the Linguistics department. It’s quite a sprawling thing, really. We’ve got recordings from all over the country.      It is. And it's constantly evolving. We're actually having to broaden our scope. It started as a purely UK focus, but we've recently been looking at language contact zones - the impact of immigration, for example. We were actually discussing the Basque country this morning, its linguistic isolation is just remarkable.      Ah, the Basque country. A truly fascinating linguistic enclave. I spent a summer there years ago, wandering through San Sebastián. The food, naturally, was exceptional. But the language… it’s unlike anything else in Europe. Completely unrelated to the Indo-European family, I believe. Did you know my grandfather was a bit of a Hispanophile? He tried to learn Spanish, said it reminded him of… well, Lincolnshire, oddly enough. Said the rolling ‘r’s were similar to the local accents.      Lincolnshire and Spain? That’s a lovely connection! We’ve been dipping into language origins a lot. It’s amazing how much history is contained within just a simple phrase.

...Honestly, Mum's been going on about Uncle Barry’s knee replacement for the last hour. It’s fascinating, truly, but I think I’ve absorbed enough detail about cartilage for one lifetime. How was your journey up, Liam? Dreadful M25, I imagine?      You know it. Solid, bumper-to-bumper. Took nearly three hours from Croydon. Glad to be here though, honestly. It’s been ages. Feels… weirdly normal being back in Mum's, surrounded by all this. And yes, Uncle Barry’s knee. A classic Mum topic.      Oh, don’t even get me started. She cornered me in the kitchen trying to explain the different types of pain medication. I swear she was reciting the leaflet. It’s good to see you both though! Two whole years is a long time. Remember that disastrous ice bucket challenge video Dad made?      Oh god,  that  video! He looked so utterly miserable being drenched. He complained about his hair for a week. And then he tried to donate to the charity  through  Facebook, and got completely scammed. Honestly, Dad and technology are a dangerous mix.      Seriously! I remember seeing screenshots circulating. I think he thought he was donating to ALS research but it was some dodgy account. I had to explain it all to him, carefully, so he didn't feel too silly. It's getting harder, isn't it? Keeping an eye on them as they… well, you know.      It really is. Mum keeps asking when  I’m  going to settle down and give her grandkids. I told her I’m quite happy with my career for now, that Recruitment is stressful enough without tiny humans demanding attention. She didn’t take it well. Keeps sending me links to adoption agencies.      She did the same to me! Before Mark and I even talked about it properly. Just, "Right, darling, have you considered adoption? Such lovely children need homes." It’s lovely she thinks of it, but it's a bit…presumptuous.      It's that generation, isn’t it? They just assume everyone needs to follow the same life path. Speaking of paths, how are things going with work, Sarah? Still battling the recruitment world?      It's... a rollercoaster. Just had a really difficult placement – a marketing manager for a tech firm. The guy had amazing qualifications, did a Masters at Oxford, but completely froze in the interview. No confidence. It's frustrating seeing potential wasted.

Honestly, this coffee machine is driving me round the bend. It makes a noise like a distressed badger every time I try to use it. And half the time it just…doesn’t. You'd think for the price of it, it would at least manage a consistent cup of coffee.      Ah, now don't be blaming the machine, love. You’re just not coaxing it right. It needs a gentle touch. Like everything, really. Though, I will admit it’s a bit temperamental. Reminds me of some of my students, actually. Stubborn as mules.      Speaking of stubborn, have you two looked at those removal and storage quotes yet? They're daylight robbery. Absolutely daylight robbery. I mean, just to put a few boxes into a container for six months? It’s criminal.      I did, briefly. It's worse than I expected. We're looking at nearly £800 for the smallest unit they offer. And that doesn’t even include insurance! Honestly, it’s making me question whether getting rid of some things isn't the better option.      Getting rid of things…that’s always a good idea, isn’t it? Though, your father… he’ll have a fit if you suggest touching any of his ‘precious’ collections.      Don't even start. He's already mourning the loss of having everything  exactly  where he wants it. It's like disrupting a perfectly balanced ecosystem. And if I mention anything practical, like the cost, it’s suddenly all about sentiment and memories.      He’s entitled to his memories, Dad. But sentiment doesn’t pay the bills. It’s just…everything seems so expensive at the moment. You’d think with all the talk about leveling up, things would be a bit easier.      Leveling up. Another empty promise, I’d say. Politicians. They’re all the same, aren’t they? All talk and no action.      It’s the leadership, isn’t it? It always comes down to leadership. Starmer… he’s not a bad man, but he lacks something. That…fire. That ability to really inspire. He’s too cautious, too willing to compromise.      I agree. He's clearly trying to appeal to everyone, but ends up appealing to no one. He needs to take a stand on something, be a bit bolder. But then again, look at the state of the Tories. It's a complete shambles. It’s hard to see anyone capable of steering the ship at the moment.

…and honestly, Mum, the thought of getting everything  done  for Christmas this year is just… overwhelming. It feels like it creeps earlier and earlier each year, doesn’t it? They had Christmas biscuits in Sainsbury’s in October! October!      Oh, they do. The commercialisation of it all is just dreadful, isn’t it? Though, I must confess, I do enjoy a mince pie or two. But you’re right, it's relentless. What's bothering you specifically? Is it the presents? The cooking?      A bit of everything, I suppose. The presents are the usual panic, trying to find something for everyone that isn’t just…stuff. But it’s more the logistics. Dad's wanting the full works again this year, the whole family descending on his. Which is lovely, truly, but coordinating everyone, especially with Uncle George’s mobility now… it’s a headache. And then there's trying to navigate everyone's dietary requirements! Vegan, gluten-free, nut allergies…      Oh, George. Bless him. Yes, getting him comfortable is vital. We’ll need to think about a portable chair, perhaps? And I’ll have a detailed list of everyone's ‘no-gos’ – I’m rather good at that now, after years of practice. Don’t worry, darling, we’ll sort it. You're taking on too much, as usual.      I feel like I have to. You’re so busy with your consultancy work at the moment, and Dad… well, Dad thinks things magically happen. He’ll wave his hand and say “Someone will sort that!” and that 'someone' is always me. How  is  the consultancy going, anyway? You seem to be travelling all over the place.      It's good, surprisingly good. Actually a lot busier than I anticipated, which is a nice problem to have. I was in Manchester last week, and I’ve got a training session in Birmingham next month. It’s tiring, of course, but I enjoy the challenge. Keeps the brain ticking over. And it’s nice to be using all those years of experience for something I find fulfilling. Though I do miss having a bit more downtime.      That sounds exhausting! Do you ever think about… slowing down? Maybe doing less?      I have, dear. I really have. But you know me, I get restless. And honestly, the money's good. It allows me a bit of freedom, helps me with things…and contribute towards things like your niece’s university fund, let’s be honest.

Honestly, I haven't slept properly in days. Liam’s snoring is… a phenomenon. It’s like a foghorn, but rhythmic. A rhythmic foghorn.      Liam? Our Liam? The one who complains if  I  even clear my throat? That’s brilliant. Serves him right, probably.      You're awful, Ben! But yeah, he does go on about the smallest noises. He'd moan if a butterfly farted near his ear. But I can imagine. He's a heavy sleeper, that one. Remember that camping trip? Didn't hear a thing when a badger rooted around our tent.      It's the worst, isn't it? Bad snoring. My housemate back at Uni sounded like a chainsaw. Used to use earplugs, then a white noise machine… eventually just moved rooms.      My grandad used to snore. Proper, earth-shattering stuff. Nan used to poke him with an umbrella. A  proper  golfing umbrella. Said it was the only thing that moved him.      An umbrella! Oh my god. I'm tempted. I've tried the gentle nudge, the "Liam, roll over" whisper... nothing. I'm thinking of investing in some heavy-duty noise-cancelling headphones. Though, I'd probably fall down the stairs.      You need to record it. Honestly. It would be comedy gold. Imagine putting it on TikTok. “Sounds of a Warrington Man Sleeping.” It’d go viral.      You're just trying to exploit his misery for internet points, aren’t you?      Maybe. A little. Anyway, enough about Liam's nocturnal noises. Anyone been to Waterfields lately? They've got those little Eccles cakes in now, individually wrapped. Perfection.      Ooh, good shout. I've not been in ages. I’m usually stuck on campus, fueling myself with instant noodles and regret. I need a proper cake break.      I went on Tuesday. They were rammed, though. Everyone and their mother was after those Eccles cakes. Nearly had to fight a nan for the last one.      You're not kidding! They’re the best Eccles cakes around. Much better than Greggs, definitely. Speaking of fighting over food, remember when we were kids and went mad for those Richmond sausages Waterfields used to do in their rolls?      Oh, don’t even remind me! They were heavenly. Mum used to only let us have one each. One! It was a travesty.      She was just looking out for our waistlines, love. Though, looking at some of us now… maybe she had a point. .

Oh, that was… a weekend. Honestly, I think I need another one just to recover from that one.      Recover? What on earth did you get up to, love? It didn’t sound like there was much planned. Just "a quiet one with the girls," as you put it.      A quiet one  turned  into an attempt to build a flatpack wardrobe in a tiny bedsit with three increasingly frustrated women and a complete lack of the right tools. Turns out, ‘some screws’ isn’t specific enough when ordering online.      Oh, dear. That doesn’t sound very quiet at all! You know, I always say, flatpack furniture is the true test of a friendship. It either bonds you or breaks you. Which was it?      Definitely skirting dangerously close to breaking. Chloe nearly threw a cam lock across the room. Thankfully, I managed to distract her with biscuits. Biscuits are the universal peacemaker, you know.      Wise girl. Reminds me of negotiating with sheep during lambing season – a well-placed bucket of feed can solve most problems. Speaking of which, mine wasn’t exactly relaxing either. Old Man Hemmings’ prize-winning bull decided to take a wander.      No! Not Bartholomew? The one you were telling me about, the one that looks like he’s permanently judging you?      The very same. Escaped right through a wonky fence post. Took me and young Timmy – bless him, tries so hard – nearly four hours to get him back into the field. He was just… strolling down the main road like he owned the place. Caused quite the traffic jam, apparently.      That’s hilarious… and terrifying. Did anyone get hurt?      No, thankfully. Just a lot of annoyed drivers and one very indignant postman. Bartholomew, predictably, was completely unrepentant. Just stood there chewing his cud, looking all majestic.      Honestly, animals. They just don’t care about our carefully laid plans, do they? So, biscuits and a near-wardrobe-related meltdown for me, and rogue bull chases for you. Sounds about right for our weekends.      Pretty much. Though, I did manage to squeeze in a bit of gardening. The tomatoes are coming along nicely, despite the weather being utterly unpredictable, as usual. I was thinking, next weekend, if you're up for it, we could have a barbecue? I’ve got a new marinade I want to try.      Ooh, that sounds lovely! A barbecue is  exactly  what I need after the trauma of the weekend.

...Honestly, the kids were  brilliant  today, but the marking… it’s relentless. I feel like all I do is wade through essays about the subjunctive. It's beautiful when they  get  it, you know? But the getting there…      Oh, tell me about it! My Year 7s are currently wrestling with relative clauses. It's like pulling teeth. Though, I suppose it’s better than phonics with reception all day. That’s a different kind of soul-destroying. How’s the French going, though? Are you still doing your Duolingo streak?      Pathetically, yes. It’s currently at 287 days, and the thought of breaking it fills me with dread. It’s entirely pointless, I know – I teach languages for a living! - but it’s a little…comforting, I guess. Especially when I feel like I’m drowning in teenagers and grammar rules. It reminds me I can  learn  too. You still trying to pick up Spanish?      I’ve stalled, I'll admit. Life got…complicated. Remember when we were talking about maybe doing a weekend immersion course in Barcelona? That feels like a different lifetime now. Speaking of complicated... how are you coping with everything? You always seemed so…prepared. I mean, you always had a plan.      Prepared is a strong word. Strategically anxious, maybe. It's…a lot. Little Leo is wonderful, of course. Truly. But the sleep deprivation is real. And having to relearn everything through the eyes of a tiny human is exhausting. Suddenly, explaining  why  the sky is blue feels like a postgraduate lecture.      Oh, I can imagine! My sister said the same thing. It’s not the actual looking after, it's the constant explaining and answering ‘why?’ that's the killer. It's funny, isn’t it? We spend years teaching kids, and then you have your own and realise how little they actually  retain  from lessons.      Exactly! It’s humbling. And slightly terrifying. Although, he did point at a picture of a croissant this morning and say "pAin." Which, I mean, it’s a start.      That  is  a start! Better than anything my nephew managed at that age. He just mostly grunted and demanded more puree. How’s Mark holding up? He seemed a bit… overwhelmed when we last spoke.      He's good. He’s taking on more of the night feeds now, which is helping. He’s also…embracing the dad-joke aesthetic with alarming enthusiasm.

Right then, what do you reckon to this, Doreen? Bit of a Heath Robinson affair, innit? Though I think the blue tits'll like it. Spent most of yesterday fiddling with it, I did.
