All that fame… doesn’t seem to bring happiness.      It really doesn't. It’s a strange world. Anyway, enough of that gloom. Did you see the geese are back on the village green? A huge flock of them.      Oh, aye! I did, walking back from Mrs. Higgins’ this morning. A right squawking racket they were making! Old Man Hemmings was trying to shoo them away with his stick, bless him. Didn’t stand a chance.      Geese are a nuisance, they are. Absolute menace. They used to come down to our garden when I was a girl, eating all the cabbages. My mother would be furious!      Oh, I can imagine! They’re certainly determined creatures. It’s amazing, isn’t it, how they know when to come back? Such a long journey from… where  do  they go?      Somewhere warmer, I reckon. My Nan used to say they fly all the way to France. Though I don't know how true that is. Seems a long way to flap your wings!      France, Russia, all sorts of places. It’s instinct, dear. Generations of knowing. They follow the same routes, year after year. My husband used to be a keen birdwatcher, you know. He’d spend hours down by the river, binoculars glued to his face. He could tell you every single bird by its call.      That sounds lovely. My father was a bit of a nature enthusiast too, though more with butterflies and wildflowers. He’d take me on long walks through the fens as a child. It’s funny, the things you remember.      Fens, you say? That's right near where I grew up, just outside Peterborough. Used to see all sorts of wildlife there, as a kid. Dragonflies mostly, skimming across the water. Lovely colours. Not much to see on the estates now, though. All concrete.      It's such a shame, isn’t it? Everything's being built over. We had a pair of swallows nesting in the barn at the back last summer.

…and honestly, the nursery rhyme section was the worst part of the interview. They wanted me to  perform  ‘Twinkle Twinkle Little Star’ with puppets. Puppets, Sarah! I teach adults advanced grammar, not… preschool entertainment.      Oh,  no . Seriously? That sounds absolutely mortifying. Which school was it again? St. Jude’s, right? I heard they were a bit… theatrical.      St. Jude’s, you are spot on. The headteacher, Mrs. Hawthorne, has a reputation. Apparently, she believes passion for early years education is best demonstrated through interpretive dance and felt tip pens. I managed a slightly strained rendition, but I think the puppet’s eye fell off midway through.      Ouch. That doesn't bode well. Though, you  are  a natural with languages, you'd think they'd focus on that. Did you at least get to talk about your TEFL experience?      Eventually, yes. But it felt… secondary. Like they were wondering if I could build a miniature farm out of papier-mâché more than if I could explain the subjunctive. I think they’re looking for someone who’s practically Mary Poppins. Honestly, I'm starting to think I’m better off sticking with the adults. Less glitter.      Definitely less glitter. And probably fewer existential crises over missing glue sticks. How did the rest of it go? Aside from the puppet debacle?      It was okay. They asked about differentiation, classroom management… the usual. But I just felt…off. I’m not that person, you know? I'm not overflowing with boundless energy and nursery rhyme enthusiasm. Speaking of overflowing, how’s the bump doing? Any cravings yet?      Oh, it’s getting… noticeable, shall we say. And yes! The cravings are real. I’ve demolished an entire jar of pickle relish in the last week. It’s disgusting, but I  need  it. David’s starting to look concerned. He thinks I'm developing a strange addiction.      Pickle relish? That’s a new one! I always imagined it would be chocolate, or something equally sensible.      Nope. Pickles. It’s just… the brine. It’s perfect. Anyway, enough about my questionable eating habits. How's Mark? Still trying to convince you to move to the countryside?      Don’t even mention it! He sent me a brochure for a converted barn in… Shropshire, I think? With a stable. A  stable , Sarah! He thinks I need to ‘connect with nature’ and ‘learn the simple life’. Coming from a woman who spends most of her time meticulously explaining the difference between ‘affect’ and ‘effect,’ that's a bit rich, isn’t it?

...Honestly, the thought of another spreadsheet detailing material costs for the next shoot is making my soul slowly erode. It’s not  bad , you know? It just feels…small. Like, this is it? This is the peak of my career potential?      Oh, come on, don't be so dramatic! It's a solid job, isn’t it? Good company, decent pay. And you're using your degree, which is more than a lot of people can say. Remember poor Ben from uni? Still delivering pizzas.      Yeah, but Ben seems  happy  delivering pizzas! He's got his photography on the side, actual passion projects. I feel like I'm just…facilitating other people’s creativity. I’m the logistical backbone, the unsung hero of making sure everything  happens , but I’m not… making  anything happen, if that makes sense?      I kind of get it. I mean, I enjoy my role as PA, genuinely, Mrs. Abernathy is lovely, and it keeps me busy. But sometimes I’m scheduling her dog’s grooming appointment and I think… is  this  what all that studying was for? All those late nights in the library?      Exactly! It’s the cognitive dissonance, isn’t it? We’re both capable of so much more. Did you ever think about using your Masters, though? You were brilliant at that environmental policy module.      Briefly. But then I looked at the jobs, and a lot of them required relocation, and honestly, Cambridge is nice. I like being close to family. Plus, the salary wasn’t necessarily  better  than what I have now. And truthfully, the idea of battling bureaucracy to save a patch of woodland…it sounds exhausting.      Right? It’s a trade-off. Comfort versus ambition. My mum keeps saying I should just be grateful I  have  a job in this climate. But grateful doesn’t exactly pay the rent and spark joy, does it?      No. It doesn't. I keep thinking about retraining. Something completely different. Maybe… pottery? I did a weekend workshop ages ago, and it was surprisingly therapeutic.      Pottery! That’s… unexpectedly brilliant. You'd be amazing! You’re always so meticulous. You'd make perfectly symmetrical vases. I'm awful at anything requiring hand-eye coordination. Honestly, I'd probably just end up covered in clay and sobbing.      Maybe we could take a class together? It would be a good distraction. Though knowing you, you'd probably overthink the glaze choices and end up with something incredibly avant-garde and accidentally ugly.

Honestly, I'm proper cheesed off with Liam. He's been acting  weird  all week. Like, distant, and then overly attentive when anyone else is around. It's… taxing, y’know?      Liam? Again? What's he done this time, love? Still talking about that girl from his rugby team? You told me he was going on about her last month.      No, not  her  specifically. It’s just… a vibe. He keeps glancing at his phone when I’m talking, and then when I ask who it is, he clams up. And tonight, at this little bistro? He spent ten minutes chatting up the waitress, complimenting her French! As if  I  don't appreciate a bit of effort. It's just… unnecessary.      Oh, the classic distraction tactic. Cambridge boys are masters of it, believe me. It’s a power play, really. Make you question things, make you feel insecure.      Cambridge boys, eh? You’ve got a wealth of experience there, then?      Let’s just say I’ve documented the species extensively. Though Liam sounds a bit… less sophisticated than the ones I'm used to. More 'bloke down the pub' than ‘intellectual pretender.’      He  is  a bit bloke-down-the-pub, which is normally alright! That’s what I like about him. But this is different. It feels deliberate. I told him how much I was looking forward to this weekend away with you two, thinking it would be nice just the three of us, a bit of girl time, but he's suddenly got to 'help his dad with something' on Saturday. Convenient, innit?      Bloody typical. His dad always needs ‘helping’ whenever something fun comes up. I swear, that man’s a professional at inventing emergencies. You're right to be annoyed, love.      It just makes me feel… stupid. Like I’m being played. And then I feel bad for feeling jealous over a waitress and his dad's imaginary plumbing issues! It’s a whole messy tangle.      Don’t feel stupid. It’s completely natural to feel that way. You’re allowed to feel protective of your relationship. The jealousy bit is just your brain trying to make sense of confusing signals. It's not a failing on your part, it’s his behaviour that's the problem.      He knows you’re amazing, doesn’t he? You’re funny, you’re kind, you actually listen when he rambles on about rugby for an hour.

…Honestly, the shepherd’s pie was lovely, David, but perhaps a  little  heavy on the Worcestershire sauce this time? Not awful, just… assertive.      Assertive is a good word, actually. I was trying to give it a bit of a kick. Bit of umami, you know? I thought, after watching the hockey, everyone would need something robust.      The hockey  was  intense! Did you see that save Miller pulled off in the third period? Unreal.      Yeah! And then old man Henderson nearly took out poor Ben with that shoulder check. Mr. Davies had a right go at him during the break.      Old man Henderson! He’s barely forty, Leo. And Mr. Davies is never one to shy away from a bit of sideline commentary. So, David, speaking of intense… how did that conference call go today? Any movement on the Patel account?      It was… lengthy. Patel’s team are being particularly fussy about the wording on the new campaign. They want everything 'on-brand', which apparently means bland. Lots of back and forth about the subtleties of comma placement. Seriously.      Comma placement determining millions? Sounds about right for marketing. It’s always the details. Still, you’re good at navigating that kind of thing.      Are we still going to Cornwall this summer? Ethan’s mum said they’re looking at booking something in July.      Cornwall would be cool! Can we go surfing again? I actually managed to stand up for, like, a whole two seconds last time.      We absolutely are. I was just looking at cottages last night. I think I found one in St Ives that has a sea view and is dog-friendly, if Auntie Brenda decides to come along.      Brilliant. St Ives is lovely. We could maybe do a day trip to the Eden Project? The boys might enjoy that.      The Eden Project’s alright. It’s just… a lot of plants.      Yeah, it's pretty boring. I’d rather just go to the beach and build a sandcastle. Or find a proper surf school this time.      We can definitely build sandcastles. And maybe look for a good surf school. Though, remember when we tried to teach you, Leo? You ended up swallowing half the Atlantic.      It tasted salty! And I  almost  got the hang of it.      Speaking of salty adventures, I was thinking about taking a long weekend to Barcelona in the Autumn. My colleague, Javier, is from there and keeps raving about it.

Honestly, this is… incredible. I mean, I've seen pictures, of course, but being  under  these trees… it’s just completely different. Remember how Mum always said California was all just Hollywood and beaches? She’d be eating her words right now.      She definitely would. She’s always been a bit skeptical of anything that isn't drizzly and grey, hasn't she? Though, to be fair, I think she secretly enjoys being proven wrong. It feeds her narrative that she’s incredibly insightful. “I  knew  it all along,” she’d say, even if she had no idea.      Precisely! And Dad would just quietly smile and nod, pretending he wasn’t equally surprised. They’re a good team, even when they're subtly undermining each other. Speaking of teams, how’s Leo doing? Has he finally managed to convince his flatmate to, you know,  contribute  to the bills?      Oh, Leo. It’s… a work in progress. Apparently, Ben has discovered the joys of "manifesting abundance" which translates to him believing money will magically appear if he just  visualizes  it enough. Leo's trying to gently introduce the concept of a part-time job, but Ben keeps talking about his ‘energy’ being blocked by mundane tasks.      Oh, good grief. That’s… a level of commitment to avoidance I hadn’t even imagined. Leo deserves a medal. He's a saint putting up with that. Is it impacting Leo much, financially?      A bit. He’s having to pick up more shifts at the office to cover it, which he’s not thrilled about, obviously. He’s started muttering about needing to charge Ben rent for ‘spiritual guidance’. It's quite funny, actually, until you remember he's genuinely stressed. It's the same old story, isn't it? Always someone relying on someone else. Reminds me a bit of my brother and Gran and her endless… “loans.”      Oh, don’t even get me started on Uncle David and Gran! I think she genuinely believed every time he asked for money he was facing some dire emergency involving a broken-down antique car or a rogue tax bill. She’d be knitting furiously, muttering about “helping family.”      Exactly! And David’s justification was always something about “investing in a business venture”. A business venture that clearly involved a lot of pub lunches and questionable purchases from eBay. I remember once I accidentally saw a receipt for a life-sized cardboard cutout of David Hasselhoff.

Now, that Kiev was…alright. Not a patch on what you get in SuperValu back home, mind you. This one was a bit…dry. Nearly needed a pint of water to wash it down.      It was okay. I thought the garlic butter was good. More garlic butter would have been better, though. Can I have another biscuit?      Honestly, you’d think a eleven-year-old could get through a dinner without requesting more biscuits every five minutes. Yes, you can have another biscuit, Leo, but  after  you’ve finished some vegetables. And don’t start with the backchat.      Ah, leave the lad be, Mary. He’s a growing boy. Besides, you’re not exactly radiating energy yourself. Headache again?      You have  no  idea. Thomas, this little one has been bouncing off the walls since lunchtime. It’s exhausting. And then he decided to declare that hedgehogs are ‘silly, spiky Wallies’. Honestly, where does he get this stuff?      They  are  a bit spiky. And they roll up into balls. It's kinda funny.      He has a point, in fairness. Though I wouldn't call 'em Wallies. They're harmless enough, eating slugs in the garden. Speaking of gardens, Granny's been on at me to visit. Says she’s got rose bushes that need pruning.      Good. She gets lonely. You haven't been up to see her properly in ages. I could come with you, maybe next weekend? Though getting her to accept help is like pulling teeth.      That's the truth. She's a proud woman, is your mother. Says I'd be 'interfering' if I started messing with her roses. Still, she always slyly slips me a slice of her apple tart. Worth the ‘interference’, if you ask me.      Did you watch the rugby yesterday? Ireland did really well!      Did I ever! Absolutely brilliant match. That drop goal…pure magic. I was shouting at the telly like a madman. Mary nearly had a heart attack.      You were. I thought the roof was going to come off. It's just a game, Thomas! Though, I’ll admit, it was exciting. Leo, did you see the end?      Yeah! It was awesome. My mate, Ben, was over and we were both jumping up and down. We tried to recreate the drop goal in the garden with a football, but it didn’t quite work.      You'd be surprised how much technique goes into a drop goal, son.

Honestly, this risotto is taking  forever . I thought half an hour was ambitious, but it’s clearly not. Are you sure you don't want a bit of that buckwheat bread while we wait? It’s actually really good toasted with a little butter. Buckwheat? Sounds…healthy. A little piece won’t go amiss, though. It’s been a long day, grappling with Brenda from accounts and her spreadsheet chaos. Though, truthfully, anything’s better than facing another hour of that. Is that the Arborio rice? It always takes a while. Yes, Arborio. I was hoping for a lovely creamy texture. And Brenda sounds… taxing. Still, only a week left until your leaving do, right? Have you finalised the guest list? Almost. Just waiting on confirmation from old man Hemmings. He promised, but you know Hemmings. He’ll probably claim he’s suddenly developed a rare tropical disease to avoid social interaction. It’s at The Red Lion, remember? Seven-thirty. I’ve booked the little room at the back. The Red Lion is good. Cosy. Perfect for a send-off that isn’t…overwhelming. He’ll probably show up. He always does, grumbling about the price of a pint. Speaking of overwhelming, I got completely lost down a rabbit hole on eBay again tonight. Let me guess…vintage cups and saucers? You know you don’t  need  any more. The dresser is groaning under the weight of porcelain. I know, I know! It’s just… there was this set. Royal Albert, Old Country Roses, and it was a proper bargain. A little chipped on one saucer, but honestly, it adds character! I’m bidding on it now. It ends in about an hour. Royal Albert. You and your Royal Albert. You'll have a whole tea room before long. Though, you do have an eye for a good find. Remember that little Shelley cup you got at the community market last month? That was gorgeous. Oh, that  was  a good one! That market is such a gem, isn't it? I have to go next Saturday. Apparently, there's a new stall selling vintage linens, and you know how I feel about a good doily. Have you been meaning to go? I meant to last week, but Brenda's spreadsheet disaster took precedence. It’s good for picking up little bits and pieces. And the coffee van is excellent. Perhaps next Saturday?

...Honestly, the paperwork alone for getting a business loan across borders is a nightmare. And then  proving  the source of funds… they're so strict now, understandably, with everything that’s been going on. It’s not like the old days, is it? Remember old Mr. Henderson down the street? Rumour had it he built his empire on… well, let’s just say non-traditional investment strategies.      Old Henderson. Aye, a shrewd one he was. Everyone  said  it was antiques. Nobody actually  saw  many antiques. Still, he never got caught, did he? Times are different now, though. They're sniffing around everywhere. It’s a wonder anyone can move a penny without a dozen forms.      It sounds stressful, Liv. Especially doing it all while you're actually trying to  run  a business. What sort of business are you even expanding into in France, anyway? You were always so tight-lipped.      It’s a spin-off from the existing online marketing agency. We’re setting up a small content creation hub, mostly video stuff. The French market is huge for that, and the talent pool here is fantastic. But yeah, the banking is a headache. They asked for a complete breakdown of every account transaction for the last six months. Six months! It's...intense scrutiny.      Intense is an understatement. Remember when I got fined for being a quid over on my council tax? They wanted proof of  everything . Bank statements, payslips, even a letter from me explaining why I thought I’d paid it. It's bonkers.      That’s nothing, lad. I had a client once, a builder. He was doing cash-in-hand jobs, perfectly legitimate, all declared through his accountant, but the tax man still suspected something. Went through his account with a fine-tooth comb and nearly bankrupted him with the costs of the investigation. They’re looking for patterns, trying to catch anything that looks like… well, like avoiding tax, or worse.      Worse like...? Don't tell me you've had clients involved in actual money laundering, Liv?      Oh, no! Nothing like that! But you hear stories. And the regulations are designed to prevent it, obviously. You've got to do your due diligence on  everyone . It's terrifying. I actually had a conversation with my solicitor about ‘red flags’ – things that should immediately raise suspicion. Things like unusually large cash deposits, frequent transfers to offshore accounts…      Offshore accounts, eh?

Honestly, this weather is just  determined  to be miserable, isn’t it? One minute it's hinting at sunshine, the next it's chucking it down. Makes planning anything outdoors impossible.      Tell me about it. I was supposed to be doing a sponsored walk for the hospice next Saturday, and they're already talking about postponing. It's a nightmare for fundraising, you know? People are less likely to sponsor when you’re battling sideways rain.      Oh no, Dad, that’s a shame! That walk’s really important for them, isn’t it? Hopefully it’ll just be a delay, not a cancellation. I’m sure people will still sponsor, regardless. You’re a legend for doing it anyway.      Yeah, you always pull in a good amount, Dad. Everyone knows you’re dedicated. I was thinking about volunteering at the summer fete they're having, though. Maybe a bit more sheltered! How’s work going, anyway? Still frantically trying to reach targets?      Always! Targets, targets, targets. It's relentless. But it’s rewarding when you actually manage to make a real difference for the hospice. They do such amazing work. Though, let me tell you, chasing donations in this economy isn’t easy. People are tightening their belts.      It's tough all around, isn’t it? I’m finding it hard to switch off these days. Work's been…intense. It's the new project, mostly. Endless meetings and trying to keep everyone on the same page. It feels like herding cats sometimes.      That sounds exhausting, Mum. You need a break. Remember what the doctor said about stress? Have you thought about finally signing up for that sign language class you were talking about? A bit of a distraction, something  you  enjoy?      I did look at it again actually. The one at the community centre starts next week. It's just… finding the time. And I feel a bit silly even considering it. I mean, what would I even  use  it for?      Silly? It’s brilliant! Imagine being able to communicate with loads more people. And think of the baby, Mum! You could start teaching her early. It's a fantastic skill to have.      That's a good point, love. A very good point. And honestly, anything that gives your wife a bit of ‘me’ time is worth encouraging. She deserves it. It’d be a lovely thing to learn, especially with the little one on the way.      Exactly!

Honestly, this canteen is a lifesaver. I was  starving . All that data analysis this morning… my brain felt like scrambled eggs. Did anyone manage to snag a decent table? It's always a bit of a free-for-all, isn't it?      You’re telling me! I circled for about five minutes before spotting this one near the window. Though, it’s a bit wobbly. I’m Chloe, by the way. I'm a Publishing Assistant… over in the fiction department.      Oh, perfect! Mind if I join? All the other tables seem completely rammed. I’m Anya. Assistant Editor, mostly non-fiction. And yes, this is a popular spot. Especially when the weather is… well, slightly less atrocious than usual.      Hi everyone! I’m Freya. I’m just temping here at the moment, another Publishing Assistant, but covering for someone on maternity leave. Honestly, it’s a whirlwind trying to learn everything.      No, please, do join! I’m Eliza. I’m the Language Research Co-ordinator. So basically, I poke around in language data all day. Sounds more glamorous than it is, trust me. Good to meet you all. Fiction, non-fiction… sounds like you're at the sharp end of the industry then, Chloe and Anya?      Sharp end is one way to put it! It’s exciting, definitely, seeing things come together, from manuscript to finished book. But the deadlines... oh, the deadlines! It's all a bit frantic, sometimes. What kind of language data do you analyze, Eliza? Sounds fascinating.      I used to think editing was frantic, but coordinating all the blurb copy and author bios… that feels like a whole other level of stress! Eliza, your job sounds really interesting though. I was born in Kuala Lumpur originally, but came here for uni and stayed. It's fascinating how quickly you pick up subtle shifts in language just by being  in  a place.      Kuala Lumpur! Wow, that's amazing. I'm Swedish-Chilean, but have lived here in the UK since I was a baby. Sometimes I feel like I’m caught between cultures, linguistically. My Swedish's pretty rusty, and my Spanish… well, let's just say it's not conversational. Do you ever find that impacts your work, Anya, being from somewhere else?      Definitely. It gives you a different perspective, I think. Especially when dealing with translations or even just thinking about who the intended audience is.

Right, so the visa application… it’s a proper headache, innit? I’ve been reading through it three times now and I’m still convinced I’m missing something. They want, like, your mother’s maiden name and the name of your primary school headteacher. Seriously? For a charity rally?      Tell me about it! I was wrestling with the ‘purpose of visit’ section for ages. “Charitable endeavour requiring significant vehicular modifications and potential exposure to challenging terrain”? Didn't quite fit in the box, did it? I just went with ‘tourism’ and hoped for the best. Reckon we can get away with that?      Tourism? You cheeky bugger! I went for ‘cultural exchange with a logistical component.’ Sounds a bit more legit, doesn’t it? Though, I’m still worried about the photos. Mine came out looking like I've just been informed I’m being audited. All squinty and stressed.      Ah, the passport photos. Disaster. I tried doing them myself with my phone, thinking I was being clever saving a few quid, and they were rejected. Apparently, my head was “too close to the background.” So, I had to bite the bullet and go to that booth at the supermarket. Cost me a tenner for two! Daylight robbery.      Tenner? I'll pay you back, I went to that place down by the library, wasn't much cheaper. Speaking of costs…we are seriously behind on donations. I put another post on Facebook, but it’s barely gotten any traction.      Aye, donations are a bit slow, aren't they? I was thinking we could put an ad up on Gumtree, that’s usually good for getting local attention. Maybe something like, “Two lads, one battered van, and a seriously good cause – help us get to Mongolia!” Bit catchy, yeah?      Gumtree's a good shout, actually. We could put up photos of the van looking all…adventure-ready. Before all the duct tape and structural reinforcement, mind. Don’t want to scare people off. What about asking the local pubs? They’re usually good for sponsoring stuff if you promise to put a banner up.      Good thinking! Old Man Hemmings at the Black Bear always has a soft spot for a good adventure. I can swing by tomorrow. And maybe we should try that car wash on London Road? They always need charity drives to boost trade on a weekend.      Yeah, worth a try.

Honestly, Chloe, you look  rough . Like, seriously rough. Did they even give you anything for the pain last night, or were you just… stoic-ing it like a proper Cornish pirate?      Don't call me a pirate. And they gave me paracetamol.  Paracetamol , Liv! For a potentially fractured radius. It felt like someone was slowly sawing my arm off.      Morning, you two. Ooh, are we re-living the hospital drama again? Chloe, you were definitely dramatic last night. All the gasping and the… the clutching.      Dramatic?! I was in agony, Maisie! And Liv was trying to convince the A&E receptionist I’d just tripped over a cat.      I was trying to downplay it! You were screaming about needing morphine and demanding to see a hand surgeon. I figured a little 'tripped over a cat' might speed things up. It clearly didn't.      So, how's the arm feeling now? Still sawing-off worthy? Did they at least confirm it wasn’t broken?      They said it's likely a bad sprain, hairline fracture maybe. Need to get it x-rayed properly tomorrow, but they discharged me at like, 3am. Hence, the zombie look. And the profound exhaustion.      You barely slept, did you? You were shifting all night. Kept mumbling something about “that boy” and “stupid scooters.”      Don’t remind me. That boy, Finn, and his insistence on showing off on a Lime scooter. I told him to slow down, didn’t I? I  told  him! Then I tried to brace myself when he wobbled, and… well, here we are.      Finn sounds like a menace. You need to ditch him. Seriously. Bad boys are only attractive when they’re fictional.      Easier said than done. He's… charming. And apparently, capable of inspiring me to engage in extremely reckless arm-saving maneuvers.      Charming and reckless is a terrible combination. Come on, let’s get you to the kitchen. You’re practically glued to this bed. Maisie, can you grab her cardigan? She’s freezing.           Right, tea, toast, maybe some Lucozade? You need sugar, Chloe. And fluids. It’s the doctor’s orders, probably.      Lucozade sounds amazing, actually. Pink one. I feel like I need all the artificial sweetness I can get. University is draining enough without dislocating joints.      Tell me about it. I'm buried under essays for Professor Davies’ Medieval Lit module. It’s like he  wants  us to suffer. Swear he gets a kick out of it.

Right, well, that was… something, wasn’t it? Your Auntie Brenda really went all out for their fortieth, didn't she? Forty years! Can you believe it? Seems like yesterday they were just starting out.      Yeah, massively. A bit much, though, wasn’t it? All the bunting and the slideshow. Honestly, Mum, some of those photos of Uncle Geoff wearing those Hawaiian shirts… mortifying.      Oh, don't be unkind! He always did have a fondness for bright colours. And Brenda loves a bit of a fuss. It's their style. They  are  a bit showy, I’ll give you that, but they've built a lovely life together, haven't they? And they’re good to everyone.      They are, yeah. Grandad seemed proper happy, though. He was beaming all night. Did you see him trying to dance with Gran during ‘Brown Eyed Girl’? That was quality.      Oh, I did! A little wobbly, bless him, but determined. That's your Grandad all over. He’s got spirit, hasn’t he? I was a bit worried about him being there so late, though. He does tire easily now, doesn't he?      He said he was fine. Loads of energy from all the cake, apparently. He hoovered up a slice of that chocolate one quicker than anyone. I reckon he had three slivers.      Oh, that man. He’ll never change. What did you think of Sarah and Tom bringing young Lily? It was lovely seeing her, but she was a bit of a handful, wasn’t she? Running around, nearly knocking over the buffet…      She’s just full of energy, innit? Like a little whirlwind. I kept an eye on her for a bit, made her a paper aeroplane. She loved that. She kept shouting “Higher, higher!” It was a bit… loud.      Loud is an understatement! Still, it's good to have a bit of life in the room, isn't it? It gets a bit quiet sometimes, with just us old ‘uns. Speaking of loud, your cousin Emily was certainly on form with the stories about her university life.      Oh god, Emily. Always gotta be the centre of attention. I swear, half the stuff she says isn’t even true. All about these wild parties and meeting famous people… I reckon she exaggerates  everything .      Now, now, don’t be too quick to judge. She’s just young and enjoying herself. And she  did  mention meeting that actor from that show you like… the one with the spaceships.

Honestly, Dad, this water bottle is useless. It's like, barely a sip left, and we've only been going for… what, two hours? I knew I should've filled the big one.      Aye, you should’ve, lass. I told you. Always take the big one. You know how thirsty you get when you're staring out the window at endless fields. Though, to be fair, I used most of mine already too. This motorway driving’s thirsty work. Did you grab a pen for the journey? You’ll want one for those crosswords your Gran sent.      Yeah, it’s in my bag. But honestly, crosswords feel… ancient. I’d rather be listening to music. Or, like, planning what Holland & Barrett snacks we’re getting in Newquay. Seriously, they have the  best  protein bars.      Holland & Barrett? Right. Because a holiday needs… protein bars. Well, as long as you’re getting something in you. Your mum worries, you know. About your IBS. Says you don’t always eat properly when we’re away.      Mum  always  worries. And I do eat! It’s just… stressful sometimes, finding places with suitable options. Remember that awful seaside cafe in Blackpool last year? Everything was fried.      Oh, don't remind me. That chippy gave me indigestion for a week. Speaking of stress, remember the chaos when we moved house last September? Felt like we lived in boxes for months. It's a relief to be  going  somewhere rather than  shifting  things.      Ugh, unpacking is the worst. And deciding where furniture goes. It always looks different in your head, doesn’t it? You think ‘Oh, that sofa will  definitely  fit there’ and then it’s just… nope.      Aye, a right mess sometimes. Your mum’s got an eye for that though, she can rearrange a room in her sleep. Are you hungry now? We could stop for lunch somewhere around Birmingham, maybe? Or are you holding out for a proper Cornish pasty when we get there?      Pasties are a  must . Lunch can be… something quick. Though, if they have chocolate brownies, I’m definitely getting one. It's a holiday, right? Rules are looser.      That's my girl. Looser rules. Though your Nan would have something to say about that. She's all about sensible eating. You know, she always said my Grandad had a sweet tooth, and he lived to be ninety-five. She swore it was the liquorice.

...Honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork is getting to me. They keep adding ‘streamlining’ measures which just mean  more  forms, filled out in triplicate, all digital of course, so when the system inevitably crashes… chaos.      Sounds delightfully bureaucratic, doesn’t it? At least my work is… relatively straightforward. Mostly just listening, and trying to make sense of what people  actually  mean, rather than what they  say . It’s surprisingly exhausting. Though, thankfully no triplicate forms.      Exhausting, you say? Try wrangling thirty twelve-year-olds for thirty years. That’s exhausting. Though the paperwork was a beast in those days too, all handwritten reports and carbon copies. Progress, they call it.      Progress usually just means finding new ways to make things more complicated. I’ve been battling a supplier all week about a batch of oak. Promised delivery Tuesday, now they’re saying next Thursday. Says it's a 'logistical difficulty'. What's logistical about forgetting to load a van?      See! Exactly! Logistical difficulties! It’s corporate speak for ‘we messed up’. And you can’t even get a straight answer. It’s always carefully worded, avoiding blame.      It's fascinating, isn't it? The layers of politeness built to avoid direct confrontation. I transcribe a lot of meetings for a marketing firm, and the amount of time spent  talking about  talking is astonishing.      People are afraid of upsetting each other. It’s a rather modern affliction. Back in my day, you told someone precisely what you thought, and if they didn’t like it, well, that was their problem. Though, naturally, there were consequences for being  too  blunt.      I reckon a bit of bluntness is what's needed most times. Saved me a lot of headaches over the years. When a customer tries to haggle me down to a price that doesn't even cover the wood, I just tell 'em straight: "No. That's not going to work." End of story.      You’re brave, Rhys. I’d probably stammer something about market forces and consider offering a discount. I'm terrible at confrontation. It stems from years of being told to ‘be a team player’ and ‘maintain a positive attitude’ even when things are clearly rubbish.      It’s that performance aspect, I think. We’re all acting, to some degree. Presenting a curated version of ourselves. That's why transcription is interesting. You hear  beyond  the performance, the little hesitations, the changes in tone… it’s like glimpsing the real person underneath.

Right, operation Mother’s Day is a go. Any brilliant ideas springing to mind, you two? Because frankly, my brain is currently occupied with preventing this sauce from burning.      Can we make Mummy breakfast in bed? Like, toast and… and sprinkles!      And sausages! Definitely sausages! Mummy  loves  sausages. And a card! A really, REALLY good card. With glitter!      Sprinkles and sausages, a truly sophisticated combination. I approve. Glitter is… a risk. We've all learned from past glitter incidents. But a card is excellent. We can definitely do a card. How about we all make one together? Then it’s extra special.      I want to draw flowers! Mummy likes flowers.      I’m drawing a dinosaur! A  super  dinosaur that gives Mummy hugs.      A hug-giving dinosaur? Wonderful. That sounds magnificent. Right, card making after lunch then. Now, about breakfast… I was thinking croissants? Less messy than toast and sprinkles, and I can get them from the bakery.      Croissants are good. But can we still have a little sprinkle on them? Just a  tiny  sprinkle?      Oh, alright. A tiny sprinkle. But you’re cleaning up afterwards. It wouldn't do to have the house looking like a unicorn exploded. You know what Grandma would say?      What? What would Grandma say?      She’d say, “It’s all fun and games until someone loses an eye!” It’s an idiom, you know? Means things are good now, but could easily go wrong.      Lose an eye? That sounds scary!      It’s just a saying, darling. Grandma loves a good saying. She’s got loads of them. Remember when she said we were ‘burning the candle at both ends’ when we were trying to build that fort and watch a movie at the same time?      That one! That meant we were trying to do too much!      Exactly! You’re quick learners. Now, speaking of doing too much… Forest School on Saturday. Are you both still excited?      YES! Can I wear my wellies? Even if it's not muddy?      Absolutely. Wellies are always a good idea. Especially with you two. Forest School is going to be a bit of an adventure, isn’t it? Making dens, building fires…      And looking for bugs! I want to find a REALLY big spider.      Perhaps a moderately sized spider. We don’t want to frighten anyone. Especially  me . Right, so... Mother's Day breakfast, cards, potentially a sprinkle-related disaster, and Forest School adventures.

...Honestly, the guilt is awful, isn't it? Even knowing it was inevitable, feeling like I  should  have been doing more. Driving her to more appointments, just…being there more. It’s silly, really. She wasn't wanting a fuss.      It’s not silly at all, love. It’s completely normal. You can’t rewrite things, even if you wanted to. Mum’s the same. She keeps saying she understands Dad was tired, that the cancer just…took him. But then she'll burst into tears, blaming herself for not noticing it sooner. It’s a pattern, isn't it? We always look back and think ‘what if?’      Exactly! It's the 'what ifs' that are killing me. And then there’s Leo… he’s pretending to be fine, you know? Just utterly shutting down. He hasn’t even properly  said  her name since…since it happened. Just "Mum" in that formal tone he used when he was little and in trouble.      Oh, bless him. That's his way of coping, though, isn't it? He’s always been one to internalise. Remember when his hamster died? He didn’t cry, just spent the whole day meticulously building a tiny little graveyard in the garden.      I’d forgotten that. Little architect, even then. But this is…different. This is his Nan. They were so close. She used to sneak him biscuits when his mum wouldn't allow it, read him stories with all the silly voices…      She was a brilliant Nan. Always had time for everyone. I used to love going to her house. She always made you feel special, even if it was just with a cup of tea and a biscuit. It’s hitting the kids hard, I think, even the older ones. My Emily's been really moody, snapping at everyone. She says she’s “just tired” but I know it’s more than that.      Teens. Everything’s ‘just tired’ or ‘nothing’ when it’s clearly everything. Have you talked to her properly? Really listened?      Tried. It's like pulling teeth. She just shuts down. I ended up just making her a hot chocolate and leaving it outside her door with a note saying I was there if she wanted to talk. Sometimes, that’s all you can do, isn't it? Just show them you’re present.      It is. It's the being  there  that matters. I keep thinking about the future, about birthdays and Christmases… everything will feel so… empty without her.

...Honestly, the sheer volume of marking I have to do is ridiculous. Twenty essays on the differences between prescriptive and descriptive linguistics – after a long morning teaching pronunciation! It feels like my brain’s going to leak out my ears.      Sounds brutal. You really picked a career that seems to  create  more work than it solves, didn’t you? Though, I suppose that’s teaching in general. At least you’re not having to write the essays, just…judge them. Which, admittedly, can be its own special kind of torment. Smells good in here, by the way. Ginger and garlic, right?      It is, thankfully. And judging is the key word. Some of them…well, let’s just say their understanding of Saussure is… embryonic. Anyway, what’s cooking? Something vaguely edible, I hope? I’m running on fumes and leftover toast.      Vaguely edible is a generous description, but yes. It’s a kind of Korean-inspired stir-fry. I’m trying to use up some of the veg before it goes off. Remember that huge bag of Pak Choi I bought on a whim?      Oh god, yes. The Pak Choi incident. You and your supermarket adventures. It’s a good job you're a student, you practically fund them single-handedly. Speaking of South Korea, you were saying your friend Chloe was talking about studying abroad there?      Yeah! She’s really keen. Apparently, they have amazing linguistics programs, especially focusing on Korean language acquisition for non-native speakers. She's worried about the cultural differences though, especially the societal expectations for women. She read something about it being… quite different to here.      It is. A lot more hierarchical, I think. There’s a very strong emphasis on gender roles, though it is changing, particularly in Seoul. Their concept of 'face' is huge, so behaving in ways that could cause someone to 'lose face' is a real no-no. It can be really subtle, and easy to accidentally offend. I did some reading about it when I was considering teaching English over there a few years ago.      Wow, that’s…intense. No pressure then. She’s a bit of a firebrand, Chloe. Doesn't handle subtlety well. She'd definitely be accidentally causing someone to lose face within the first five minutes. What stopped  you  going?      Tuition fees, largely. And, to be honest, the thought of being so far from family. And… a certain someone convincing me that teaching English to slightly less-travelled students in Sussex wasn't the worst fate imaginable.

Honestly, this pepperoni is  chef’s kiss . Although, I’m starting to regret that third slice. Feel a bit…solid.      You always regret the third slice, Jess. It's a cyclical event, isn’t it? Like Lancaster flooding after a particularly heavy rainfall. Speaking of which, remember last year, when the canal nearly overflowed onto campus? Properly Biblical.      Oh god,  don’t  remind me. I thought my dissertation was a goner! I had it all backed up on a USB, but it was in my bag in the library… Honestly, I was panicking.      It was mental. I was trying to build a makeshift dam with textbooks outside the Sugarhouse. Didn’t exactly work, but it gave us something to do while waiting for the bus. Did anyone actually make it  to  Sugarhouse that night, though?      I think Liam, bless him, attempted it. He was wearing wellies with his Sugarhouse outfit. It was...a look. Remember that time he tried to explain the plot of  Cloud Atlas  after one too many VKs?      Oh, absolutely. It devolved into something about reincarnation and monkeys very quickly. He’s a good lad, but abstract concepts and alcopops are a dangerous mix. Reminds me, did anyone else watch  The Big Fat Quiz  last night? Jack Whitehall was on form.      Saw a bit of it, yeah. I’m more of a  University Challenge  girl myself. Proper brain food. Although, my general knowledge is mostly limited to obscure 80s trivia because of my nan.      My mum’s the same. Her specialist subject is definitely ‘things you’ll never need to know’. I've been trying to catch up on  How I Met Your Mother  – proper comfort TV. Though, it feels weirdly outdated now. Like, no one uses flip phones anymore!      I’m re-watching  The Vampire Diaries . Don’t judge me. It’s pure escapism. Much less stressful than trying to wrap my head around this quantum physics assignment. Honestly, I think I’d rather try to explain the Chaos Walking trilogy to someone who’s never read it.      Ooh, have you started that module assessment yet? Professor Davies is  ruthless  with marking. I’ve been chipping away at it, but I’m pretty sure half of it is complete nonsense.      I'm still trying to decide whether to even bother with the reading list. It's like, a novel in itself. Speaking of reading, anyone else devour thrillers like they’re going out of fashion?

Honestly, this signal is shocking out here. You’d think with all the money they spend on infrastructure, they could get a decent radio wave to reach… well, anywhere outside of a city centre.      You and your radio. It's a wonder you haven’t started building your own transmitter in the garden. Though, knowing you and all that corpus linguistics stuff, it’d probably be optimized for perfect reception of obscure 80s synth-pop.      Don’t even  start  on the synth-pop. It’s a perfectly valid genre! And it's not just a hobby, it's…applied linguistics! Understanding how language evolves through music… it's research, basically. Though admittedly, a lot of it is just enjoying the music. But seriously, it's frustrating. When I was cataloguing that dialect data from Northumberland, half the interviews were crackling messes.      That sounds... intense. Still, I admire your patience. My work is mostly spreadsheets and simulations. Tidier, definitely, but not exactly brimming with cultural insight. This project I’m on, designing a new drainage system for that new housing estate… it’s all just numbers and risk assessment.      Oh, that sounds… practical. Very important, of course. Don’t get me wrong. Someone needs to stop us all flooding away. But it's not exactly  romantic , is it? Like uncovering the linguistic history of a tiny village. Remember Old Man Hemmings in Rothbury? He could tell you the origin of every single phrase used in the village, and it all linked back to the lead miners.      Vaguely. You told me about him. Sounded like a character. You were rabbiting on about isoglosses for a good hour after that visit. I think Mum started actively avoiding you at the dinner table.      She just doesn’t appreciate the nuances of regional vocabulary. She thinks everyone should speak… Mid-Atlantic or something. It’s ridiculous. It’s like she forgets where  she  came from!      Well, she did move down south when she was young. Hertfordshire’s a bit of a linguistic melting pot. It's not exactly a strong dialect area. It's all… softened, blended.      Exactly! It’s bland! No grit, no character. Whereas up North, you get all these wonderfully preserved expressions. Like 'bairn' instead of 'baby'. Or 'canny' meaning good, or clever. Things that completely disappear down here. You wouldn’t understand ‘radgie’ now, would you?      Don’t tempt me. I suspect it’s something to do with being considerably… agitated?

Oh, this wind! It's cuttin’ right through you, isn't it? Feels like winter again, even for Norfolk in October. My joints are complainin' somethin' awful.      You're tellin' me, Arthur. I felt it as soon as I stepped out of the car. Honestly, one minute it's mild, the next you're reachin' for your coat. Doesn’t do your rheumatism any favours, does it? Mine’s playin’ up something chronic today.      It is a bit brisk, Grandad. Though, to be fair, it  is  October. I was saying to Ben, the students are already complaining about the cold in the lecture halls. They’re a hardy bunch usually.      Students will complain about anything, Liv. It's in their nature. Though, you're right, it’s definitely a chill. I forgot my scarf, and I'm regretting it now. How are  you  holding up, Arthur? Still battling with that… what was it, the waterworks?      The prostate, lad. The prostate. It's a nuisance, that's what it is. Keeps me up half the night, it does. Doctor says it’s just age, naturally. Age and a bit of bad luck. I used to be able to sleep through a hurricane, now a little drizzle wakes me up.      Honestly, Arthur, you worry too much. Everything's a 'nuisance' with you! I had a bit of a funny turn myself last week, actually. Just a dizzy spell. Didn’t like that one bit. Made me think, you know?      Oh, Mum, you scared us all half to death when you called! You should really mention these things to Dr. Davies, don't brush it off.      I did, love, I did. He just said it was my blood pressure, and told me to take things easy. Easy for him to say! I’ve got three grandchildren climbin’ all over me most days… well,  used  to. Since I retired from childminding I find I get a bit…off balance, I suppose. It's the quiet, maybe.      It's a big change, isn’t it, going from so much activity to… well, not so much. You were always so busy with the kids. Did you catch the football on Saturday, by the way? Norwich got a lucky draw, I thought.      Lucky draw? They were dreadful! Absolutely dreadful! No passion, no fight. Same old story. I remember when we used to have proper players, lads with grit.

Honestly, this is  exactly  what I needed. Just a proper girl’s night. It feels like ages since we’ve all been together without… well, without distractions.      Tell me about it! Work’s been manic. Trying to push these new software deals… it's draining. And Ben keeps hinting about… you know… the future. A very specific future involving a house with a garden.      Ooh, the pressure! Is he full-on wedding talk yet, or just vague 'settling down' vibes?      It’s edging towards wedding talk. He showed me some Pinterest boards yesterday.  Pinterest ! I nearly choked on my coffee. Lots of bunting and rustic barns. It's a bit… not us, is it?      Rustic barns are lovely! But yeah, Pinterest can be a dangerous place. It creates these unrealistic expectations. Remember Sarah and Mark? Their wedding looked amazing on Instagram, but she was a complete wreck the whole time trying to recreate a photo she'd seen.      Oh god, yes! The flower crown incident was legendary. So, are you panicking about the bunting, or secretly a little bit excited?      I’m… conflicted. Part of me wants the security and the whole ‘life plan’ thing. But another part of me is screaming that I’m way too young to be thinking about mortgages and tiny humans.      You  are  young! We all are. I mean, I’m finally feeling properly settled in my job, but the idea of kids… it feels like a million years away. And finding someone worth having tiny humans with is a whole other saga.      Don’t even get me started on dating apps. It’s just endless scrolling and disappointment. Every other profile is someone holding a fish. What  is  with the fish?      It’s a power move, apparently. Signals they can provide. I've sworn off them. I think I’d rather remain single and slightly eccentric forever. Though Mum keeps setting me up with her German colleagues… it’s mortifying. Being born in Germany doesn't suddenly make me fluent in matchmaking!      Your mum is relentless! Remember when she tried to get you fixed up with the son of the butcher?      Please don’t remind me. Honestly, I think she just wants to brag to the Women’s Institute about having a daughter with a ‘sensible job’. Admin isn't exactly glamorous in their eyes.      It  is  sensible, though! Someone has to keep things running smoothly.

…and little Leo, honestly, he’s obsessed with that tablet. You’d think I’d be pleased, give ‘im a bit o’ peace, but it’s  all  he wants to do. No building blocks, no drawing, just…swipe, swipe, swipe. It’s a different world, innit, Bernard? You and I, we were happy with a skipping rope and a bit o’ chalk.      Chalk! Now there’s a thought. Remember drawing hopscotch on the pavement, Doreen? Used to get right cross when someone stepped on the lines. Different world indeed. This…technology… it’s a bit beyond me, truthfully. My grandson, Mark, tried to show me this 'internet' thing. Said I could see pictures of horses.      Ah, the internet. Gateway to all knowledge…and cat videos, predominantly. I use it all the time for work, researching resources for the kids. It's brilliant, but you're right, it  is  a bit overwhelming sometimes. What did you think when Mark showed you, Bernard?      Thought it was witchcraft, more like. All these little boxes and pictures changing every second. Said I could see horses… well, I’ve  seen  horses, proper horses, down at Old Man Hemmings’ farm. Felt the power of ’em, smelled ‘em. Not the same as a little glowy picture, that's for certain. He showed me a video of a race, though. Said it was at Ascot. Fancy hats and all. Used to go to the races with my dad, years ago, before…well, before everything.      Oh, Ascot  is  lovely. Though a bit pricey, isn’t it? I've always wanted to go. Used to dream about it when I was childminding, picturing myself in a nice dress and a big hat. Mostly I was just covered in sticky fingerprints and building Duplo towers, though!      It’s funny how dreams change, isn’t it? When I started teaching, I imagined I’d be inspiring the next generation of poets and playwrights. Now I spend half my time mediating playground squabbles over who got the red crayon. It pays the bills, though. Just. Things are tight, even with a steady job.      Tight? You’re a teacher! Always thought teachers were alright. Decent pension, weren't you supposed to get? I never had much myself, you see. Never really  worked . Dad provided. Then… well, things changed. Never had the chance, I suppose. Always felt a bit of a burden, if I’m honest.

...Honestly, the sheer variety of accents  within  Birmingham is fascinating. I had a student yesterday, born and bred here, but with a slight lilt I couldn't quite place. Turns out her grandparents were from the Black Country! It's a real melting pot, linguistically.      You're a teacher, ain't ya? Always noticing that sort of thing. I’ve lived here near thirty years now, since retiring, and still pick up little differences. Though, truth be told, I’m more of an Essex boy at heart. You can take the man out of Essex…      Absolutely! And Essex has a very distinct sound. My nan was from near Chelmsford, so I heard a bit growing up. It's funny, isn't it, how much of your identity is tied up in where you're from, even just the way you speak.      It is, it is. Makes a difference, you know. People judge, rightly or wrongly. I remember when I first started working, down in the City, they could spot me a mile off. Didn’t bother me too much, mind. Just meant I had to be a bit sharper, prove I wasn't some country bumpkin. Managing Director, eventually though. Couldn’t have been  that  bad of an accent, eh?      I'm sure it wasn't! And it sounds like you did rather well for yourself. What did you manage, if you don’t mind me asking?      Logistics. Boring as it sounds, keeping things  moving . Used to run distribution for a big pharmaceutical company. Lots of paperwork, lots of responsibility. But good money. Allowed me to travel a bit, which was the best part.      Oh, that sounds interesting! Travel? Where did you go? I’m desperate for a holiday, though realistically, it’ll probably just be a weekend somewhere.      Oh, all over. Europe mostly. Italy, France, Spain… always preferred the warmer climates. Did a bit of the States, too – New York, Florida. But Italy…now there's a place. The food, the history, the people. You haven't truly lived until you've had pasta in Rome. What about you? Any travelling ambition?      Italy is definitely on the list! I did a year abroad in Spain when I was at university, which was fantastic. But since then, it’s been… limited. Little trips to France, mostly. Teaching doesn't exactly lend itself to long, expensive breaks. Although, I'm thinking of doing a language exchange next summer, maybe in Germany.

...Honestly, the whole thing was just a bit  much . Like, balloons everywhere, couples practically glued together. You’d think it was the only day of the year to show someone you care, wouldn't ya?      Tell me about it! My timeline was flooded. Auntie Lourdes was going on about her and Uncle Ben’s fortieth Valentine’s, complete with a throwback photo of them looking about seventeen and deeply awkward. It was… a lot. Did  you  do anything?      Nah, absolutely nothing. I actively avoided anything remotely Valentine’s-y. Went to the library, pretended to revise. It was blissfully quiet, thankfully. And you? I know Liam was trying to figure something out last week…      He tried! He really did. He took me to that new Italian place, "Bella Notte," on Friday. It was… okay. The food was alright, a bit overpriced for what it was, but the atmosphere was horrendous. They were playing the most cheesy love songs, and everything was red.  Everything . Red tablecloths, red roses, even the lighting was tinted red. It felt like being trapped inside a giant Valentine’s card.      Oh,  no . That sounds awful! Cheesy love songs are my nemesis anyway. Red isn’t even my colour! Liam’s a good bloke, though. He tries.      He does. He’s sweet. It’s just… it felt so  forced . We were talking about it afterwards and he was a bit gutted I didn’t seem super impressed. He said he was aiming for 'romantic' and landed on 'slightly terrifying'.      Oh, that’s brilliant! Honestly, at least he’s self-aware. That’s more than you can say for some guys. We were thinking of going to the cinema this weekend. There’s that new horror film everyone’s raving about, “Nightshade”. Fancy joining? A nice antidote to all the romance.      Ooh, yes! I’ve been wanting to see that. Anything to distract myself from remembering all the Valentine’s posts. Actually, speaking of distractions… have you noticed how many people here are trying to do fake accents? I swear I heard someone attempting a… what  was  that? A West Country farmhand?      Oh god, you’re right! They’re terrible. It’s always the people who've barely left London trying to sound all rustic. It's hilarious. My cousin tried a Cockney accent once, visiting from Scotland. It sounded like a pirate impersonating a chimney sweep. Nearly choked on my tea.

...Honestly, the sheer audacity of it all. They’re framing it as ‘firm but fair’ immigration policy, but it’s blatantly targeting specific communities. It feels… visceral, doesn’t it? Like a deliberate attempt to create a hostile environment.      Visceral is  exactly  the word. I was reading a piece this morning about the impact on asylum seekers, particularly those from, well, you know… places they’ve decided are ‘safe’ now. It’s horrifying. And the rhetoric! They’re just dog-whistling non-stop. It’s sickening. This Danegeld policy feels like a direct result of the populist wave.      It is. It’s all about appealing to a base, isn’t it? And it’s so disheartening because, logically, immigration  benefits  society. It's fuelled London for decades. Look at Brick Lane, look at… well, everywhere. It's just blatant scapegoating. Speaking of benefitting society, these noodles are benefitting  me . Did you get the Dan Dan noodles? They’re amazing.      Yeah, I went for the Dan Dan. Good shout. Although, I’m slightly regretting the chilli oil. My mouth is on fire! And you’re right about the benefits. My mum came here in the 70s, and without her resilience and work ethic, I wouldn't be where I am. It’s frustrating to see that contribution minimised, even erased. It's weird because it feels like we're going backwards.      It does. And it’s not just immigration. It's everything, isn't it? The housing crisis, the cost of living… it’s all designed to keep people insecure and fighting amongst themselves. Honestly, even just thinking about trying to buy  anything  in Watford now makes me feel exhausted. My parents keep offering to help with a deposit, but it feels…wrong. Like I'm relying on generational wealth to escape a system created to benefit generational wealth.      Totally. I'm renting in Kensal Rise still and the landlord just put the rent up  again . It’s ridiculous. I’m earning more now freelancing, but it feels like it’s just… absorbed by rising costs. It’s like running on a treadmill. And you’re spot-on with the guilt over help with a deposit. It feels... unfair to those who don’t have that security net. My flatmate’s saving for a deposit, and she’s working two jobs and  still  barely making a dent.      It's not a meritocracy, is it?

Honestly, I'm feeling a bit… overwhelmed thinking about Leo starting nursery next week. It just feels so soon, doesn’t it? Like only yesterday he was a tiny little bundle, and now… well, now he's going to be off making friends and getting glitter everywhere with other children.      It does fly by, doesn’t it? But he  is  ready, Mum. He's so sociable, loves being around other kids at the baby groups. He’ll adore it, honestly. And you need it, too. A few mornings to yourself to get your head straight before going back to work.      That’s true. Work is looming, isn’t it? I've been avoiding looking at my inbox, frankly. It feels like a lifetime ago I was dealing with spreadsheets and meetings. I'm worried about the guilt, you know? Leaving him. Even just for a few hours.      Mum, you  have  to. You're brilliant at your job, and you'll be a much better mum  because  you’re still doing something for yourself. Plus, didn’t you say your boss was really understanding about flexible working?      I did. It’s more… adjusting. And the logistics. Getting him settled, packing everything, the after-school runs. It’s a whole new routine. Speaking of routines, have you thought any more about that holiday we were talking about? Maybe something after I’m back in the swing of things?      I have! I was looking at Cornwall. Proper beach holiday, ice cream, building sandcastles. Leo would  love  that. It's a bit further, but we could drive and take all his stuff - all his toys, his favourite blanket, everything. We could even look at a place that’s dog friendly, so we can take Winston.      Oh, Cornwall sounds lovely! Winston would adore that. He needs a proper holiday too. Though, driving with a toddler… that sounds like a challenge. Remember that trip to Devon last year? The non-stop cries because his dinosaur was "lost"?      Oh god, don’t remind me! But we survived, didn't we? And maybe this time, we'll be better prepared. More snacks. A dedicated dinosaur retrieval team. Anyway, back to the present - how is the weaning going? He seems to be enjoying trying new things.      It's surprisingly messy. Very, very messy. He's discovered the joy of flinging pureed carrots with impressive accuracy. He actually managed to get some on the ceiling yesterday!

...Honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork involved with these legacy gifts is astounding. You wouldn't believe the hoops you have to jump through just to get a simple cheque cashed! And then the reporting requirements… it’s relentless.      Sounds exhausting, David. You always take on so much. How did your meeting with Mrs. Henderson go, the one with the sizable bequest for the hospice? Did she sign everything off?      She did, thankfully. A lovely woman, truly. Lost her husband last year, and he was a regular volunteer at the hospice. She wants to honour his memory. It’s those stories that make the paperwork bearable, you know? Still, I'm wiped. I think I need a full week of doing absolutely nothing.      You and me both! This shift at the shop was  mental . The new promotion started today – buy one get one free on the summer dresses – and it was just a constant stream of people. Trying to keep everything tidy, manage the queues, deal with the inevitable complaints… I’m surprised I haven’t lost my voice.      Tell me about it. Board meeting today was a right slog. We spent three hours debating the Q3 projections. Three hours! As if anyone can accurately predict the market right now. I felt like I was speaking another language half the time. Honestly, I just want to switch off and watch some rubbish telly.      Sounds like everyone’s had a day. I had a… peculiar one. The police were on to me again.      Oh? Still about the incident with Old Man Hemmings and the garden gnome?      Yes! They wanted a formal statement. I thought I’d already given them everything verbally. Apparently not detailed enough. They were asking me, and I quote, "To elucidate on the trajectory of the gnome post-impact." Honestly! It’s a garden gnome, not a ballistic missile!      “Trajectory of the gnome?” That’s brilliant! Honestly, police these days…      You’re kidding. That’s utterly absurd. Did you tell them exactly what you thought of their line of questioning?      I bit my tongue, mostly. I did point out that I was no expert in gnome-based physics. They seemed… unimpressed. It took me a good hour to write the blasted thing. It reads like a crime novel. “The gnome, propelled by an unexpected gust of wind, entered a downward arc…” Honestly.      You're a writer at heart, love.

Right, this is proper good tea, this. Not that builder's brew stuff you get at some places. Though, to be fair, after a morning wrestling with rose bushes, I’d probably drink anything. So, how are things  really  going, now you're properly married? Beyond the, you know, Instagram-perfect photos.      Instagram’s a lie, innit? Looks amazing, feels… well, it feels like a whole new level of logistical nightmare, mostly. But a good one. She's got very strong opinions about… everything. Particularly the arrangement of the spice rack. She’s a whirlwind, honestly. Speaking of which, she’s trying to get me to grow everything from scratch. Herbs, spices, even chickpeas!      Chickpeas? That's ambitious! Though, you've got the gardening skills. I just try to keep my one basil plant alive, and that's a struggle. Remember that time I tried to grow tomatoes and they got some weird blight? Looked like something out of a horror film.      Oh yeah! Orange leaves and all droopy. Like a botanical ghost. She’d be horrified. She’s all about natural remedies and stuff. She was going on about using mortar and pestle the other day to grind some obscure root for… something. I just nodded and smiled. I'm pretty sure I mostly look confused these days.      Sounds about right. My mum gets like that. One minute she's telling me about the healing powers of ginger, the next she's lecturing me on the decline of polite society. It's exhausting. But good exhausting, you know? Keeps you on your toes. Actually, it reminded me - did you ever finish that series,  Spartacus ? We were talking about it last time I saw you.       Spartacus ! God, yeah. I did. Pretty brutal, wasn't it? All that sand and… well, everything. Though, the historical accuracy was questionable at best, I reckon. They glossed over a lot of the… less glamorous bits of Roman life. Like the sheer monotony. And the malarials.      Exactly! It's all sword fights and ambition. No one mentions the sea lice if you were a ship-based auxiliary! Though, I suppose that wouldn't be very dramatic, would it? It's amazing how many historical figures died young. Spartacus himself, Alexander the Great… they barely scratched the surface of old age.      Makes you think, doesn't it? All that striving, all that power… for what? To be a footnote in a history book.

...Honestly, the whole thing was just  stressful . Mrs. Davies kept pacing, and every time someone coughed it felt like a personal attack on her marking scheme. Did you feel like that, Liv?      Ugh, seriously! It was awful. I swear, she was looking right  at  me when old Mr. Henderson started his coughing fit. Like  I  made him do it! I completely blanked on the question about metaphors. Just…gone. What about you? What tripped you up?      The poetry analysis. The poem was about a seagull, can you believe it? A  seagull ! And we had to dissect, like, every single line for symbolism. I wrote about freedom and the sea and all that, but I just had a feeling it wasn't what she wanted. She's so specific.      Oh, a seagull? That  is  rough. Mrs. Davies loves the obscure stuff, doesn't she? Remember that poem about the button last year? No one understood the button! I think I just wrote about how it kept falling off a coat.      Oh my god, you did! I remember! That was brilliant. At least you were honest. Speaking of honesty, I think I accidentally implied Shakespeare was a contemporary of Taylor Swift in the intro to my essay.      No! You didn’t! Oh, you did. That's…amazing, actually. She’ll probably dock you marks, but it’s a story for life. Anyway, English aside, I’m actually slightly excited for art next week. Mrs. Peterson said we’re doing abstract landscapes.      Oh, good! I’m looking forward to that. I’m rubbish at realistic stuff, but I can definitely splatter paint around and call it 'emotional turmoil'. What about French? Still battling with ‘le’ and ‘la’?      Don't even  mention  French. Madame Dubois is convinced I'm deliberately trying to sabotage her lessons. I keep mixing up masculine and feminine nouns. It's not my fault! They just don't  make sense . I’m pretty sure 'la chaise' is just trying to trick me.      It's a conspiracy, I tell you! A linguistic conspiracy. Although, you're better with the pronunciation than I am. I sound like a strangled cat when I try to say 'Bonjour'. Hey, are you still in wind band?      Yeah! Rehearsal is Thursday. We're finally learning that piece from 'Pirates of the Caribbean'. It's surprisingly difficult. All those fast runs on the flute... My fingers are aching already.

Honestly, look at that delivery van. Another one plastered with branding. It's relentless, isn't it? Used to be you just  saw  a van, now you're bombarded with logos and slogans. Makes your head spin.      Mmm? Oh, yeah. I dunno, I kinda ignore 'em. Too busy on TikTok. Did you see that new football challenge Ms. Davies showed us? It's mental.      TikTok, really? When I was your age, we were excited if we got a new Top of the Pops magazine. Times change, eh? Though, I agree about the vans, Margaret. It’s all about image now, isn't it? Everything's a brand. Even people, sadly.      Exactly, Brenda! It's a bit sad, really. Remember when things were... simpler? You just  were  someone, you didn't have to  market  yourself. And speaking of marketing, have you seen the price of petrol lately? Absolutely ridiculous. Filling the car up feels like a small mortgage payment.      My dad’s moaning about petrol all the time. Says it’s the government’s fault. He’s proper wound up. He was saying he might have to cycle everywhere. That’d be a sight, him in Lycra.      Oh, now  that  I'd pay to see! Your dad, on a bicycle… He’d need a flag on the back, proclaiming his outrage! Speaking of flags, I saw one in town the other day, a proper Union Jack, looking rather faded. It reminded me of our holiday to Cornwall back in '88. We had a little one just like it on our campervan.      Cornwall! Oh, that was a lovely holiday. You remember the pasty shop in St Ives? The best pasties I’ve ever had. Mind you, everything tastes better when you’re on holiday and not worrying about marking essays. Though, the state of the students’ writing is worrying me these days. Honestly, they struggle to string a sentence together.      It's 'cause of phones, innit? Everyone just texts and uses loads of abbreviations. My English teacher keeps going on about proper grammar. It’s boring.      He’s got a point, lad. Language is important, even if it feels old-fashioned sometimes. Though, I understand the appeal of a quick text. I'm not exactly tech-savvy myself. My nephew tried to explain crypto to me last Christmas. Nearly gave me a headache. It's all a bit beyond me, to be honest.

Honestly, Arthur, you always take the biggest portion. You’ll be needing a new hip soon at this rate!      Now, now, Brenda. A man deserves a good feed. Besides, these spuds are lovely. Much better than that diet muck your daughter’s always on about, eh, Emily?      It’s not “diet muck”, Dad. It’s about being healthy. Dr. Sharma was quite clear - my cholesterol’s creeping up. And it's not just about weight, it's about longevity. You know, preventative medicine.      She’s right, Arthur. It’s easy to fall into the trap of thinking "I feel fine now", but it catches up with you. Especially with family history. Remember Uncle George?      George smoked like a chimney and drank like a fish. Can’t blame his heart attack on a few roast potatoes, can you? Different times. And different genes, I reckon. My mother lived to ninety, and she ate lard with a spoon!      She did, didn’t she? Always a bit of bacon fat in everything. And she swore by a spoonful of sherry for her indigestion. Times  have  changed. Though, I do miss a proper sherry trifle.      Mum, you know you're allergic to sherry now. Remember the rash last Christmas? It was awful.      Oh, that. Just a little reaction, Emily, don't fuss. I rather think it was the nuts in the trifle too. Everything gives me a reaction these days.      It's probably a cascade of things, Brenda. Allergies seem to be on the rise. Even I've started getting sniffly around cats, which used to be fine.      Cats are trouble. Always have been. Give me a good engine any day. Now  that  I understand. Speaking of which, young Tim down the garage is having trouble with a new fuel injection system on a Beemer. Fancy bit of kit, but needs a specialist. Costs a fortune, of course. Everything does.      It’s frightening how expensive everything is getting. Tuition fees are just spiralling. I have students struggling to afford both food  and  textbooks. It feels… immoral, almost.      It is. And the NHS is creaking at the seams. Mrs. Peterson from next door is waiting months for a hip replacement. Months!      Poor thing. Mine was… well, it was a long time ago, of course. But the surgeon, Mr. Davies, was wonderful. A real gentleman. Told me all about the new techniques they were using. Said my bones were excellent for my age.

…and honestly, the student forum on Moodle is just…a wasteland. Three people posted about assignment one, and two of them were asking if the deadline had changed. It’s like nobody  reads  anything. Sounds about right. It's always the deadline question, isn't it? Even when it’s plastered all over three different pages. Though, to be fair, Moodle isn't exactly intuitive. It’s a beast. A beast is putting it mildly. I spent a solid hour yesterday trying to embed a H5P interactive video. An  hour , Leo! It felt like I was deciphering ancient hieroglyphs. I just wanted them to click on parts of a diagram and get feedback! Is that too much to ask? Oh, the H5P saga. I sympathize. I tried to get a decent quiz working last week and ended up with a tangled mess of multiple-choice, drag-and-drop, and fill-in-the-blanks that barely functioned. Thankfully, Sarah in IT saved my bacon. She’s a Moodle whisperer. You are so lucky you have Sarah as a resource! My department just says “it’s all self-explanatory” and points me at the Help section. Which, predictably, isn’t. It's just a list of links to more unhelpful pages. Honestly, I’m starting to think I should just go back to lecturing and handing out paper worksheets. Don't even joke about that. We'd be buried in marking. Besides, think of the accessibility benefits – screen readers, adjustable font sizes… Moodle, when it  works , is great. It's getting  it  to work that’s the problem. Have you tried the nested activity approach for the video? That sometimes bypasses some of the more…quirky embedding functions. Nested? You mean putting the video inside a Page resource, then linking  that  to the topic? Exactly. It seems ridiculously roundabout, but it sometimes forces Moodle to cooperate. I discovered it by accident, honestly. Pure desperation. I was wrestling with a similar video issue and just…kept clicking until something vaguely resembling functionality appeared. That sounds…very ‘Leo’. Trial and error fuelled by caffeine and frustration. I might give that a go. It can't possibly be  more  frustrating than what I’ve already tried. What about assessment feedback? Are you still struggling with getting meaningful feedback into the Gradebook through Moodle? Ugh, don't even  go  there. It's a nightmare. Rubrics are supposed to streamline things, but they just complicate the process tenfold.

Honestly, I think the jetlag is finally  starting  to lift. Though, honestly, five hours sleep feels like a luxury these days. Not that I’m complaining, of course. Little Leo is worth every lost hour… mostly.      Tell me about it. I swear, I woke up this morning convinced it was lunchtime in New Zealand. And you’re right about Leo – adorable chaos. Though, five hours? You had a  good  night. I think I managed three, broken up by… well, everything.      Oh, don’t even start. The 3 am feed was a particularly vocal affair, wasn’t it? He was having a full-on philosophical debate with himself, I think. Anyway, less about our sleep-deprived states, more about tonight. Did you manage to book those tickets for the theatre? "A Midsummer Night's Dream," right?      I did! Got us seats in the stalls, row G. Apparently, they’re doing a very modern interpretation. Lots of neon and electronic music, according to the reviews. Sounded…interesting. Bit different from the Globe, that's for sure.      Neon and electronic music? Hmm. That  is  different. I'm a bit of a traditionalist when it comes to Shakespeare, but I'm always up for something a little… unexpected. It'll be nice to get out, even if we're practically zombies.      Exactly! A bit of culture, a change of scenery, and hopefully, an hour and a half of relative silence. Although knowing our luck, Leo will decide it's his bedtime  precisely  when Puck starts his mischief.      Don’t even jinx it! Mum and Dad are still on standby, aren't they? They're itching to be grandparent helpers.      They are. Both offering unsolicited advice on everything from swaddling techniques to weaning. Bless them. They're ready to pounce if we even hint at needing a night off. I think Dad's already started researching baby-friendly ear defenders for the theatre, just in case.      Oh, Dad! He's brilliant. You know, I was thinking... maybe we should aim to leave here around seven? That gives us enough time to get there, park, and grab a quick drink before the show starts.      Seven sounds good.
