I’ll make sure I’ve got the changing bag fully stocked – you know, the usual survival kit: nappies, wipes, a spare outfit , a small arsenal of teething toys… We  are  prepared for anything, aren't we?      We certainly are.

...Honestly, it's just a complete bureaucratic nightmare. Old Man Hemmings, you remember him from the faculty Christmas party a few years back? His daughter, Sarah, is trying to get a visa to come and visit from Canada. She's married to a Canadian now, proper settled, but her mum's not well, and she wants to come over for a bit, help out. They’re asking for  so  much paperwork, it's unbelievable. It feels deliberately designed to discourage people.      Aye, I hear you. Visas… that’s my world, in a way. Well, part of it, anyway. The NRPSI work often involves helping people navigate that absolute mess. It's not just the paperwork itself, it's the arbitrary nature of it all. One case officer might approve something, another will reject it for the same reason. It’s infuriating. Where are they trying to go, specifically?      Just here, to Liverpool, to see her mum. And it’s not even a long stay, just a few weeks. You’d think that would make things easier! It's the financial stuff they keep querying. Prove they have enough funds to support themselves, even though her mum is offering to put them up. It's… frustrating. It’s nothing like when my sister wanted to move back from Hamburg. EU rules then, obviously, a totally different ball game. Though even that wasn’t  simple .      Hamburg’s different, definitely. Post-Brexit, everything’s shifted, hasn’t it? Regarding the finances, they're obsessed with proving intent to leave. They don’t trust anyone, do they? It's all part of the wider picture, I think, that tightening up. It’s connected, you know, to the whole… well, the politics of oil, indirectly.      How so? That’s a bit of a leap, isn't it? Visas for visiting relatives and…petroleum?      Not a huge leap, trust me. Look at who  doesn’t  have trouble getting visas. Business people, investors, particularly from certain parts of the world. The focus is on attracting money, not necessarily family reunification. And the money often ultimately leads back to…well, you know. Places reliant on oil. It’s about control, who they want in the country and why. It feeds into the whole security narrative, conveniently.      Hmm. I suppose when you put it like that… It’s cynical, but probably largely true. Makes you think, doesn’t it? It's also about that underlying fear, I guess.

Honestly, David, you  have  to have another slice. It’s perfectly pink, just how you like it. Though I suspect even you can’t eat as much as Buster would, watching him under the table is a performance in itself!      You're right, he's a vacuum cleaner on legs. And yes, please, a small slice. Though it's rich, isn’t it? Mum, you’ve outdone yourself. This is better than any pub roast.      Nonsense, David. I just follow a good recipe. And a generous hand with the rosemary, of course. It’s a comfort, making a proper roast. Reminds me of Sunday dinners with  my  mother. Though we never had a television blaring in the dining room like you two do!      Oh, Mum, don't start on the TV! It's just a bit of background noise. We weren't even watching anything particularly gripping, just news. It’s better than silence, don't you think?      She has a point, though. It does feel a bit…odd, having it on during dinner. Like we’re eating in a waiting room.      Exactly! A dining room should be for conversation, for connecting. Not for absorbing headlines about…well, whatever it is they report these days. Now, has anyone tried this tablet I brought down? Proper Scottish tablet, made by Mrs. MacIntyre from the village. It’s lethal.      Ooh, yes! I had a tiny piece earlier. It's unbelievably sweet. The kind of thing you need a strong cup of tea with, or possibly a lie-down.      I’ll take a piece, thanks. It's been ages since I’ve had proper tablet. Reminds me of childhood holidays in Scotland. Speaking of holidays, are we still thinking about that cruise next spring?      We are. I’ve been looking at brochures, Mediterranean, mostly. Though I’m tempted by one that goes up the Norwegian fjords… it’s just… a bit chilly for an old woman.      The Mediterranean sounds perfect. Lots of sunshine, good food… I could definitely get on board with that. I need to start thinking about getting beach-body ready, though. That lamb isn't helping.      Beach body? You look perfectly fine as you are, darling.      Oh, you always say that. But honestly, I've been trying to get back into some sort of workout routine. Pilates mostly. It's good for the core. Though Buster thinks my downward dog is an invitation to play.

…And honestly, Mam kept going on about getting a job at the Sellafield visitor centre. Like  that’s  my ambition, you know? Explaining nuclear decommissioning to tourists. It'd kill me.      Oh, God, that's awful. She still on about you needing a ‘proper’ job then? You've got a degree, Liam, you’re allowed a bit of…freedom.      Freedom sounds nice. I wish I had more of it. My mum's just…constant. About everything. Especially about me not going to uni straight away. Says I’m ‘wasting’ my potential.      Potential’s a funny word, isn’t it? My Nan thinks my potential peaked when I got the teaching assistant job. "Settled," she calls it. Which basically means “stopped trying for more.” Biscuits, anyone?      Cheers, Ash. Potential, eh? Mine’s probably decaying rapidly at this rate. Honestly, it’s not like I don’t  want  to work, just… nothing feels right. Everything’s either miles away, or…rubbish. I applied for that bar job in Cleator Moor, remember? They said I lacked "enthusiasm." Enthusiasm! For pouring pints!      They probably just wanted someone who could fake it better. Cleator Moor isn’t exactly brimming with exciting opportunities. It's alright though, uni’s keeping me busy. Although… I’m starting to properly worry about next year. Rent's ridiculous in Lancaster, even sharing.      Tell me about it. I was looking at costs for Newcastle, just to compare, and it’s… bleak. My parents are offering to help, obviously, but I feel awful taking it. Especially when I'm not even sure what I  want  to study.      It’s a tricky one. My Mam and Dad were the same with me. Just wanted me to get a qualification no matter what. Luckily, sixth form was enough for what I'm doing, but I get the pressure. You don’t want to be indebted before you’ve even properly started, do you?      Exactly! That’s what scares me about all this uni talk. I should have thought it through more. I took History 'cause...well, I liked books. Didn’t really think about what you actually  do  with a History degree. Now I'm stuck with a pile of debt and…nothing to show for it. Except a lot of knowledge about the Tudors.      Don't say that, Liam! You're brilliant at research. Remember that project we did in school about the Whitehaven harbour?

Right, so, the gingerbread men. Do we think they’ll hold their shape if I add a  tiny  bit more golden syrup? I’m worried they’ll be too crumbly for the kids to decorate. It's for Year 3, you know, they're not exactly… precision bakers.      More sticky then! More sticky makes them stay together. Like in Tomodachi Life, when you make friends, you gotta give them presents, and the stickier the present, the faster they become friends!      Mummy, look! I drew a gingerbread man! He's fighting a dinosaur!      Oh wow, that is  epic . A gingerbread man versus a dinosaur? That’s a story right there. Though, maybe the dinosaur would win. Right, back to the sticky gingerbread question. What do you reckon, is a little more syrup okay?      Yeah! Sticky is good! But not  too  sticky, or they’ll get stuck to the table! Like when I tried to build a castle out of honey… remember?      Oh,  do  I remember. The kitchen looked like a bear had been raiding the pantry. Right, small amount of syrup then. Now, this lesson. I’m trying to explain fractions, using the gingerbread men to demonstrate halves, quarters… it's surprisingly challenging to get seven-year-olds excited about dividing biscuits.      Can  I  divide the biscuits? I’m good at counting!      You are very good at counting, darling. But dividing them equally is the tricky bit. We’ll see if we can manage it in the lesson. It’s also Lily’s half-birthday next week, you know? I was thinking we could maybe do a little celebration at home, just a small one.      A half-birthday! That means presents! Can we have a gingerbread man cake? A  really  big one?      We’ll see. Perhaps a smaller cake, plus gingerbread men. I was at Morrisons yesterday, and I was absolutely ages trying to find that book you wanted, the one about the little bear who loses his hat. Do you remember the name?      Bartholomew Bear! Bartholomew Bear loses his hat and is very sad!      Bartholomew Bear! That's the one. I eventually found it tucked away on a bottom shelf. They really need to organise their children’s section better. I also picked up another book, a really lovely one about a little girl who befriends a lighthouse.      A lighthouse? What does she  do  with a lighthouse? Does she live inside?

Honestly, it’s just… exhausting. Every time I log onto Facebook, it’s another endless scroll of people either bragging or complaining. It’s never  just  sharing, is it?      You sound like my mum. She deleted her account six months ago, said it was turning her into a perpetually irritated person. But yeah, I get it. It’s curated reality, isn’t it? Everyone presenting the best, shiniest version of their life.      Exactly! And then you start comparing. And it’s not even a conscious thing, it just… happens. And then someone posts about their new car – another blooming Range Rover, naturally – and I start questioning why we still trundle around in Betsy.      Betsy’s perfectly good! She gets you from A to B. And reliable, that’s the key, isn't it? Those Range Rovers are just…showy. Status symbols. Remember old Mr. Henderson down the road? Bought a fancy BMW, and then spent half his time worrying about someone scratching it in the village car park.      Oh, God, yes! Pure anxiety on wheels. But it’s still… tempting, isn’t it? Especially when you see all these “life hack” articles online about the ‘best family cars’ and ‘cars that will make your life easier’. It’s all just marketing, of course.      Entirely. The internet is brilliant, but it’s also a master manipulator. It knows exactly what buttons to push. I was reading an article the other day about "essential tech for modern living" and it was all stuff we absolutely  don’t  need. Smart fridges? Voice-activated everything? Just more things to break, more things to update, more things to worry about.      Don't even get me started on smart fridges. What's wrong with a shopping list and a bit of common sense? It all feels designed to make us feel inadequate, doesn't it? Like we're falling behind if we don’t have the latest gadget or the flashiest car.      It's a constant pressure. And it’s amplified by Facebook, Instagram, TikTok… they’re all feeding into the same system. It’s like a feedback loop of consumerism.      It's funny, isn't it? We're both lecturers, we're supposed to be critical thinkers, and yet we get sucked in by it all sometimes. I was actually comparing marking schemes with Sarah online last night. Completely pointless, but I did it anyway. "Is my weighting for the essay correct?"

Honestly, this remote is a nightmare. It’s like they design these things to actively frustrate people. Where’s the volume button… always hiding.      It’s right there, Liam. Next to the one you just pressed. You keep hitting ‘Menu’.      Oh. Right. See? Frustrating. So, how was uni today? Anything actually  happening  or just more lectures about things you’ll probably never use?      It was alright. Had a seminar on feminist art, which was actually really interesting. We were looking at Guerrilla Girls, you know, the ones with the gorilla masks?      Vaguely. Sounds…intense. More intense than meatballs falling from the sky, anyway. This film is ridiculous, isn’t it? I can’t believe we’re watching  Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs  on a Saturday night.      It's comforting! And it's good to switch off. Besides, remember when we were little and this was  the  movie? It’s nostalgic. Plus, little Maisie absolutely loves it.      True, true. Maisie’s practically vibrating with excitement. Still, it's... a weird concept, isn’t it? All the food. Makes you think.      Think about what? Overconsumption? The absurdity of American excess?      Woah, deep thoughts for a cartoon. I was just thinking about how much I fancy a roast dinner now. Work was…a grind today. Had a woman trying to return a toaster she’d had for six months, claiming it didn’t toast properly. Six months!      People are unbelievable. What did you say?      Explained the returns policy, politely, three times. She wasn't having it. Honestly, some people just want a freebie. Makes you question humanity sometimes. Though, admittedly, a never-ending supply of spaghetti and meatballs  does  sound tempting.      It’s a total metaphor for capitalist greed, Liam. Don’t you see? Everything in abundance, until it all comes crashing down. The scientists weren't listening to warnings!      You’re applying a lot of political theory to a children’s movie.      Well, it's there! Plus, it's kinda relevant. We're all being warned about climate change, and nobody seems to be taking it seriously enough. Look at the floods last week.      Yeah, it’s scary stuff. We didn’t even get any proper rain here, but I heard it was bad up north. Speaking of scary, I actually had a really weird conversation with Mrs. Henderson today. She started asking me about my views on…religion. Just out of the blue.

...Honestly, the sheer arrogance of it all still gets to me, even now. Blair thinking he could just  reimagine  Britain with a few focus groups and a spin doctor. It’s laughable, looking back. Though, at the time… at the time, people genuinely believed.      Aye, you’re tellin’ me. I was drivin’ a cab back then, right? And you couldn't swing a cat without hittin’ someone goin’ on about ‘New Labour’ and how things were finally lookin’ up. They believed every word, they did. Even folks who usually wouldn’t give politicians the time of day were gettin’ caught up in the hype.      It was a masterful performance, wasn't it? He had that…that empathetic facade. And the language! He spoke  to  people, not  at  them. It's a skill, manipulating public opinion like that. Though, a deeply unethical one, I always thought. Particularly looking at the aftermath.      Ethical? Ha! You're a lecturer, you worry about words like ‘ethical’. I was worryin’ about keepin’ the meter runnin’ and avoidin’ arguments in the back of the cab! But even  I  could see the cracks start to show. The promises weren’t bein’ kept, were they? The hospitals weren’t gettin’ any better, schools were still stretched… It was all just…paint, wasn't it? Fancy paint on a cracked wall.      Precisely. And that's the tragic irony. The potential was there, really. A genuine opportunity to address some deeply-rooted societal issues. But it got lost in… well, in the pursuit of appearing successful, wouldn’t you say? It’s something I discuss with my students - the power of rhetoric, the dangers of unchecked ambition.      Students, eh? You’re teachin' kids all this now? Good. Someone needs to. My lad, he was just comin’ up then. All excited about things changin’. He got involved in some youth schemes, government funded, of course. Said it was good, gave him somethin' to do. But even he said… it felt like they were tickin' boxes, y’know? No real substance to it.      Exactly. Stakeholder management, they called it. Everything was about perceived value, about appeasing different groups. Real substantive change? That became secondary. It's a fascinating case study in political pragmatism gone wrong. Actually, talking of pragmatism...did Liverpool manage to pull off a decent signing in January? I haven't had a chance to follow the football properly with marking all these essays.

...Honestly, the sheer  volume  of data in these BNC recordings is just… overwhelming. I’ve been trying to isolate instances of specific dialectal features, and it's like finding needles in a haystack made of vowels. I mean, everyone's speaking, overlapping, background noise… it’s a linguistic jungle.      Tell me about it! Editing feels like that sometimes, honestly. Except instead of vowels, it’s badly punctuated sentences and misused semi-colons. It’s surprisingly draining. Have you had any luck with identifying the East Anglian variations you were looking for? That's what really intrigued me about your project.      A little. It’s more noticeable in the longer, spontaneous dialogues, thankfully. The staged interviews are a bit too… curated, you know? Everyone’s trying to sound ‘proper’. It's just not representative. I was scrolling through LinkedIn last night, and saw someone I went to uni with is now living in Dubai. Dubai! Can you  imagine ?      No way! That’s wild. Who was it? I’m always slightly horrified and vaguely jealous when I see people relocating like that. I saw Rhiannon Davies – remember her from Linguistics? – posting pictures from Spain. Gorgeous villa, endless sunshine… Meanwhile, I’m battling damp in my flat and contemplating whether to invest in a dehumidifier.      Sounds lovely, doesn't it? Always seems sunny on social media. Though I do find myself just… scrolling endlessly without actually  seeing  anything. It's a terrible habit.      It is! It’s the vortex. And Rhiannon's photos were completely filtered, I bet. It never looks like real life. Anyway, back to Dubai. Apparently, he’s a data analyst now, which is… fitting. It’s just, it feels so far removed from Aylesbury, doesn’t it? We were complaining about the traffic on the A41 just a few years ago!      Totally. I'm a bit more keen on the idea of shorter-term travel, though. I was looking at flights to the Maldives, actually. Pure escapism, obviously. But the water… it just looks incredible. The only problem is…  flying .      Oh, you and your fear of flying! Honestly, I thought you'd have conquered it by now. Remember that time we flew to Amsterdam and you basically white-knuckled the armrest the entire time?      Don’t remind me! It wasn't pretty. It’s not a logical fear, I know. Statistically, driving is far more dangerous. But the  lack of control  is what gets me.

…and honestly, the plumber said  another  two weeks for the bathroom tiles. Two weeks, Di! It's been six already! I'm starting to think we should just live amongst the rubble and claim it's ‘industrial chic’.      Industrial chic doesn't quite cover the piles of dust, Leo. You’ll be finding tile grout in your tea. Honestly, you need to be firmer with him. They always try it on. Remember old Mr. Henderson with the leaky roof? I had to practically threaten him with a strongly worded letter and a review on Checkatrade.      I  tried  being firm! He just… smiled. A really patronizing smile. It's like he thinks I don't know what's happening. You always handle these things so well. It’s a skill.      Years of dealing with authors, darling. Believe me, a plumber is a walk in the park compared to a temperamental poet. Speaking of which, how's the dissertation coming along? Still wrestling with post-structuralism or have you moved onto something more… cheerful?      Still wrestling. It’s…a beast. I think I’m finally making progress on the chapter about representation in graphic novels, though. Found some really interesting stuff on the visual language of tattooing. Actually, that reminds me… I'm thinking of getting another one.      Oh? Another one? You're rapidly running out of space, Leo. What are you thinking of this time? Something to match the chaos of the bathroom renovation?      Maybe! No, I was thinking… a small sprig of lavender, on my wrist. Simple, you know? A little bit of calm amidst the…everything.           Hello, you two! Apologies for being late, the Central line was a disaster. Smelled suspiciously of wet dog and regret. What’s cooking? Smells amazing, Di.      Amelia! No worries, love. Just getting dinner underway. Leo’s thinking about subjecting his arm to more ink.      Oh, really? Lavender, Leo? That's…unexpected. Very pastoral for someone who lives in a building site.      Hey! It’s symbolic! And it's less shouty than a dragon. Though, a dragon  would  be quite apt for the current situation.      True. So, how are things with the interns at the magazine? Any promising young talents, or are you mostly fielding requests for biscuit runs?      Surprisingly good, actually. We’ve got a girl, Clara, who’s just brilliant with research. She spotted a factual error in a manuscript that I'd missed – a historical detail about Victorian mourning rituals.

Right, I  think  this is almost ready. Honestly, I’m still not entirely sure about adding the harissa. It smelled so fragrant at the market, but you never know, do you? Might blow our heads off.      You and your adventurous cooking, Chloe! It’ll be fine. A little spice never hurt anyone. Besides, I'm starving. This smells amazing already, even  potentially  fiery amazing. How was your pilates class this morning? You were looking rather…determined when I dropped you off.      Determined is one word for it. Tortured is another! Honestly, Sarah – the instructor – is a demon. She’s convinced we can all achieve peak physical condition by the end of the month. I think my core is actively protesting. Definitely needed a comfort cook after that. Did your run go okay? You seemed to be gearing up for a long one yesterday.      It was…productive. I managed about eight miles, which is good, but I think I pushed it a little too hard. My left knee is having a bit of a moan now. Old age setting in, I guess. I’m thinking of trying one of those yoga for runners classes. Less…impactful.      Oh, the one at the community centre? I’ve heard good things. Mrs. Patel runs it - apparently, she’s absolutely brilliant, and very calming. You need calming after an eight-mile run! Speaking of which, are you still planning that trip to Morocco later this year? I was remembering that time we went to Marrakech… absolute chaos, but so much fun.      I am, yes! Though, to be honest, the thought of all the navigating is slightly daunting. I'd love to get properly lost in the souks again, but last time, we nearly ended up in a tile factory. And your French… let’s just say it wasn’t helping!      Hey! My French is  rusty , not non-existent! And they didn’t speak French in the tile factory anyway, it was Arabic! Honestly, the memory is a little blurry. Too much mint tea. But seriously, Morocco is amazing. Have you booked anything yet? I can send you the details of that lovely riad we stayed in. It had such a beautiful courtyard.      That would be fantastic, thank you. I've been looking at flights, trying to find something reasonable. It’s just… work’s been a bit frantic lately. The editor is determined to launch this new digital platform before the end of the quarter, and it's consuming everyone's lives.

Honestly, that was a  day . Three essays flagged for potential plagiarism, and then young Li Wei asking if existentialism applies to choosing a flavour of bubble tea. It’s…a lot.      Bubble tea existentialism? That’s a new one, even for a Chinese university. You’re a saint, you know that? I just had the usual spreadsheet battle with attendance figures. Apparently, Ms. Chen has decided Tuesdays are optional.      Optional! The audacity. Though, part of me understands. Honestly, sometimes I just feel… drained. I need a holiday. A proper holiday, not just shuffling papers in a different country.      Agreed. Somewhere with no students, no essays, and definitely no philosophical bubble tea debates. Remember Sarah and Mark's trip to Thailand last year? They looked genuinely  relaxed  in the photos.      Oh, yes! They were raving about it. Although, knowing Sarah, she probably spent the entire time analysing the socio-political implications of longtail boats.      Probably. She has a gift for that. Speaking of friends, have you heard anything from Ben lately? I haven't seen a message in weeks. He usually bombards me with terrible puns about linguistics.      That’s what I was wondering about too! I tried texting him last week, just a quick “how’s it going?”, but nothing back. I’m starting to worry a little. He was sounding a bit stressed when we last spoke, everything with his mum and the house sale.      Right, yeah. It’s been dragging on for ages that house sale. And his mum's health is… well, it's not great. He hides it well, but I know he's carrying a lot. Maybe he’s just completely overwhelmed and switched off for a bit.      Maybe. It’s just… not like him to vanish like this. He always answers, even if it’s just to send me a picture of a particularly unfortunate toe nail. Remember that time?      Oh god, how could I forget? That was a truly horrifying photographic offering. He was so proud of the…texture. "An anthropological study in keratin," he called it.      Exactly! That was classic Ben. So, a missing message from him is immediately suspicious. Honestly, sometimes I think his toenails are more reliable than he is.      Okay, stop stressing. We’ll try calling him tonight. Maybe a phone call will get through. If not, I'll drop an email to Emily. She's probably heard something. Emily always has the inside scoop.

...Honestly, the whole thing just feels a bit manufactured, doesn’t it? All this relentless positivity. Like, it's good to be optimistic, sure, but pretending everything's sunshine and roses when people are really struggling... it feels disingenuous. Especially on those morning TV shows.      You mean the relentless ‘good vibes only’ brigade? Yeah, I get what you mean. It’s exhausting. I saw Lorraine Kelly practically bounce off the walls this morning talking about ‘summer optimism’. It’s February, Lorraine! People are battling the bills and the grey. It’s a bit out of touch.      Exactly! And it's not just Lorraine. It’s everywhere. And then they have these 'wellness gurus' peddling this idea that if you’re not feeling amazing, you’re  doing  wellness wrong. It's infuriating. I mean, I teach language for a living, and even  I  have days when I just want to hide under my duvet.      I can imagine. Teenagers are… a unique demographic. My own kids are driving me mad at the moment. Leo's decided he’s a musician, and it involves a lot of very loud electric guitar practice at all hours.      Oh dear. A budding rock star, huh? Is he any good?      That’s… debatable. He’s got enthusiasm, which is something. My wife’s threatening to invest in soundproofing. Which, frankly, seems like a sensible idea. It reminded me of a documentary I watched the other night. About Elvis. It was fascinating, the pressures he was under. Fame, money, the control… or lack thereof.      Oh, I love a good documentary. There was that one about Britney Spears recently, which was just heartbreaking. It’s terrifying how easily people can be exploited when they’re young and famous.      Absolutely. It’s the whole ‘system’ isn't it? The managers, the record labels… they just see dollar signs. Speaking of systems and exploitation, have you gotten down the rabbit hole of that whole Jeffrey Epstein thing lately? I was reading something online… it's wild.      Oh, don't even get me started. That’s a can of worms I try to avoid. It's all so deeply disturbing. It feels like there's always another layer of… well, you know. Conspiracy theories abound. Sometimes, I feel like the truth is almost impossible to find.      It is. Makes you question everything, doesn’t it? It’s why I mostly stick to football these days.

Dad, honestly, all this green is… a lot. It’s just fields and hedges and more fields. It's like someone set the colour palette to ‘British countryside’ and just  kept  pressing repeat.      Aye, well, that's England for ya, lass. You wanted a proper holiday, didn’t you? Away from the city. Can’t get much more ‘away from the city’ than this. Though I grant you, it’s not exactly vibrant, is it? Makes you appreciate a good splash of colour, like the purple heather we’ll see down in Cornwall.      I suppose. It just feels…monochrome. It reminds me of that scene in  The Wizard of Oz  when they get to Oz and suddenly everything bursts into colour. Before that it’s all grey and… well, like this.      Good comparison, that. Your grandma used to love  The Wizard of Oz . She’d always say life was a bit monochrome before she met grandad. Always a romantic, your grandma. Remember that little china Dorothy she had?      Vaguely. Was she the one who used to tell us fairy tales? The really spooky ones?      She was indeed. Proper Brothers Grimm stuff, none of this modern, sanitised rubbish. She believed a good fairy tale needed to have a bit of bite. Now, are you keeping an eye on the sat nav? Just checking we’re still heading southwest. This M5 can be a bit of a beast.      Yeah, it says we're on track. Though why do they call it a ‘sat nav’ when it’s doing so much more than navigating? It’s basically a tiny computer telling us everything. It's not like the old days with maps and… telegrams!      Telegrams! Now  there's  a throwback. Your great-grandad used to send telegrams when he was at sea. Short, sharp messages. “All well.” “Arriving Tuesday.” That was it. Though he knew Morse code, apparently. Said it was vital for ship-to-shore communications.      Morse code! That’s amazing. It’s like a secret language. Is Braille like that? A whole language based on touch?      It is. Very clever, actually. Entirely different way of understanding letters and words. It made me think, you know, how many different ways humans have devised to communicate. From smoke signals to texts on your phone.      It is a bit mind-blowing. Speaking of texts, I haven’t had a signal for ages. Typical. I was hoping to read that new Sherlock Holmes story everyone’s been talking about.

…and this is Blackpool Tower, Grandad. Remember when we went when I was little? I was convinced it was  actually  in the clouds.      Blackpool, aye. Good times, good times. More sticks of rock than a body could shake a stick at. Though, I’ve never understood why folk buy ‘em. They taste of nowt after the first bite. Just…hard sugar.      Seems a bit like modern cinema, doesn’t it? Overpriced and ultimately underwhelming. Went to see that new superhero film last week. Fifteen quid a ticket! Fifteen! For a two-hour bombardment of CGI.      Honestly! It's daylight robbery. You could get a proper meal for that. Speaking of which, Nana’s roast was amazing yesterday. Though, you didn’t eat much, Grandad. Feeling alright?      Aye, lass, I’m fine. Just… not the appetite I once had. When I were a lad, we used to get a proper beating for leaving food on our plates. Different world. Everything was different then. We didn’t have all these fancy petrol stations with convenience stores selling everything under the sun. Just a pump and a bloke who wiped your windscreen.      Funny you say that. I was driving back from a site visit yesterday, and I needed petrol. Ended up spending another tenner on snacks and a coffee. It’s a trap! They design everything to encourage impulse buys. It’s the clever psychology of retail.      It is. I’m trying to avoid it. Costs are insane as it is. Rent’s going up again, apparently. Another fifty quid a month. It’s ridiculous! How did you manage when you were starting out, Grandad? I imagine things were cheaper back then?      Cheaper? Lass, you wouldn’t believe it. I started with BT straight after the war. Didn’t earn much, of course, but you could live on it. A house cost a fraction of what it does now. And work… it was  work . Proper graft, climbing poles in all weathers. Built character, that did. None of this desk work you youngsters do.      It’s all evolving, isn’t it? My job's mostly modelling stress on structures using computers. Not exactly scaling pylons. Though, I do a lot of site visits. And yes, it’s a lot less physically demanding.      Oh, look! This is my primary school photo. I’ve got that awful bob haircut Mum insisted on. And I was obsessed with geography.

Honestly, Mum, this tea is  exactly  how I remember it. Strong, a good biscuit on the side… it’s proper revitalising after that flight. I think the jet lag is finally starting to lift. Though, trying to recall what day it is still feels a bit… hazy.      That’s the age, love. It starts creeping up on you. I used to remember every detail, every birthday, every anniversary. Now… well, let’s just say I have a very detailed calendar. You look knackered though, even with the tea. Did you manage any sleep on the plane?      A couple of hours, on and off. Mostly just weird dreams about accidentally teaching a class full of weaver fish. Honestly, it was bizarre. They kept trying to… well, weave nets, I guess. It felt deeply symbolic, but I can’t remember  what  it symbolized.      Weaver fish, you say? That’s a new one. Sounds like your brain's sorting through all the new information. Anyway, we should really get cracking on that list for the flat. You said Sarah’s helping you move everything next weekend?      Yeah, she is. Absolute lifesaver. She’s already compiled a spreadsheet, naturally. She's wonderfully…organised. Which is good, because I’m already overwhelmed thinking about it all. Did you keep that old chest of drawers from the attic? I was hoping to snag it for the bedroom.      The oak one? Yes, still up there. Bit dusty, mind you. Your Grandad made that, you know. Lovely piece of furniture. It’s just been… accumulating things over the years. Speaking of accumulating things, have you finalized the guest list for the wedding?      Not quite. It's proving tougher than I thought. Trying to balance family expectations with…well, trying to keep it relatively small. Auntie Brenda keeps suggesting we invite everyone she’s ever met.      Brenda. Always Brenda. Tell her it's a 'small, intimate gathering' and hope for the best. She’ll get the hint… eventually. More tea? You need to keep your strength up. All this planning is exhausting even  watching  you do it.      Please. This is genuinely perfect. It’s just… good to be here. Talking through all this with you. It feels more real, somehow. And… not just the moving and the wedding, but… everything.      Everything? What do you mean, love?      I don’t know… just… settling down. With Sarah. It feels right, but it’s also a bit daunting, you know?

Honestly, look at that Venus flytrap. It's brutal, isn't it? Just…  snap . And people keep them as pets. It's a bit dark, even for me.      Dark, but fascinating. It's pure efficiency. No messing about. Reminds me a bit of Ms. Davies, my A-Level Biology teacher. Zero sentimentality. Just facts. Speaking of A-Levels, did you see the latest proposals? They’re messing about with the content  again .      Oh, aye, I skimmed something about it. More modular, right? Less in-depth study? Honestly, it feels like they're actively trying to de-skill a generation. When I did mine, it felt… proper. Like you had a solid base to build on. Though, I  did  spend half my summer holidays revising physics. Wouldn’t fancy that again.      Exactly! It's like they're aiming for breadth over depth. Which is fine for some, but for anything research-focused, you need that grounding. It's a bit worrying, especially given everything else that’s going on. Like the state of the NHS. I had to call 111 last week, just to ask about a persistent cough, and it took forty minutes to get through. Forty minutes!      Aw, that’s rubbish, isn’t it? My mum’s been saying the same. She’s a nurse, you know, and she's absolutely knackered. Apparently, they’re short-staffed  everywhere . And the waiting lists… It’s scandalous, honestly. They talk about funding, but it never seems to reach the frontline.      It's a systemic issue, isn't it? And it's not helped by constant restructuring. Just when people get settled, they change things again. It’s all a bit… chaotic. Hey, random thought - have you seen what Lisa’s done with her hair?      Lisa? Oh, the bright pink pixie cut? I saw a picture online. Bold move. Suits her, though. She's always been a bit of a trendsetter. Reminds me, I need to actually  book  a haircut. Mine’s getting seriously unruly. It’s getting to the stage where it's actively defying gravity.      You should. You've been saying that for weeks! There’s that little place on Mill Road, the one with the really good reviews. You know, the one where they  actually  listen to what you want?      Aye, I’ve seen it. I just… procrastinate. It's a skill, really. Like, Olympic-level procrastination. Anyway, back to slightly more important things… have you been following the petrol situation?

…and honestly, the reading list for Medieval History is  intense . Like, week three is entirely dedicated to the Black Death. Entirely. It’s just…death, death, death. I get it was important, but after a while you just need a bit of cheery stuff, y’know?      Oh god, that sounds grim. My American History course is bad enough with all the, like, colonialism and slavery details. At least there’s some progress narratives in there, sometimes. All death and disease sounds…depressing. Are you coping alright?      Depressing is an understatement. I’m doing a module on public health and we touched on outbreaks. It’s just…thinking about the sheer panic. No antibiotics, no real understanding, just watching people die. And the smells! Apparently, the smells were horrific.      Aye, I read something about that. They didn’t know about germs, obviously, so they blamed everything – miasma, the stars, Jewish people… awful things. It’s just a completely different mindset. It makes you appreciate modern medicine, doesn't it? Though, talking about appreciating things… anyone got a job sorted for summer? I'm currently staring into the abyss of my bank account.      Don’t even  mention  money. I applied for everything going. Bar work, retail, leaflet dropping – nothing. Mum keeps saying I should just get a ‘proper’ job, like working at the garden centre. Honestly, the indignity. I’d rather re-read all about bubonic plague.      My parents are the same. They want me to intern at my uncle’s law firm. It’s… soul-destroying just thinking about it. I’m hoping to snag something at the museum, but competition is fierce. It's all well and good being a feminist and wanting equality, but it doesn't pay the rent, does it?      Preach. My dad keeps going on about me 'building a career' which translates to 'getting a posh office job and earning loads of money'. Like, I want to  help  people, not shuffle papers for some corporation. I’m thinking of just working at that music festival again. Low pay, awful toilets, but at least it's fun.      Ach, festivals are good. I worked at one last year, near Middlesborough. Paid alright, and the atmosphere was brilliant. But then I spent the next month smelling of cider and regret. . It’s just…everything’s so expensive. Even a basic student life feels luxurious these days.      Tell me about it. I swear, rent in Leeds is going up every week.

...Honestly, it's just exhausting, isn’t it? Pretending you're thrilled to hear from someone when you really…aren’t.      You mean like, having to mentally brace yourself when their name pops up on your phone? Oh, God, yes. I've been  there . It’s the worst kind of social obligation, isn’t it? It feels so unkind to just…stop replying, but prolonging it feels worse.      Exactly! It’s the prolonging that kills me. I’ve got this friend, Sarah, we’ve known each other since uni, and…I just don't  enjoy  her company anymore. It’s not like she’s done anything wrong, she hasn’t. She’s just…changed. And I think I have too. But every time she messages, I feel guilty for even considering ignoring it.      It's a classic. People grow apart. It's totally normal. But we’re so conditioned to think friendship is forever, commitment and all that. My cousin, Chloe, went through this with her best friend from primary school. They’d been inseparable, then suddenly Chloe realised she felt completely drained after any interaction.      Drained is a good word. That’s exactly how it feels. It's not a dramatic falling out, it’s just… an emotional tax. What did Chloe do? Did she just ghost her friend? I’m terrified of confrontation.      No, she didn't ghost. Chloe did the slow fade. It took months, but she gradually responded less and less, made fewer suggestions for meeting up. Eventually, the friend kind of got the message. It wasn't pretty, there was a bit of hurt feelings involved, but ultimately, Chloe was honest - gently honest - about needing space. She said something about needing to focus on different things, needing energy for other relationships.      “Needing space” sounds less harsh than “I find you utterly exhausting now.” Which, let’s be real, is closer to the truth.      Precisely! It’s diplomatic. It’s about framing it around  your  needs, not  her  failings. It's easier for the other person to absorb that way. Though, honestly, with Sarah, has she ever been…demanding of your time? If she's always the one initiating things, it might be easier.      She is, actually. She’s always suggesting things, always wanting to hear every detail of my life. It's not that I don’t want to share, it’s just… constantly being  asked  feels…suffocating.

…Honestly, Nan, this shepherd’s pie is exactly what I needed. Uni food just doesn’t hit the same, you know? It's all microwave meals and questionable pasta sauces.      Oh, darling, I  know . That’s why you come home for a proper meal, isn't it? And don’t talk with your mouth full! It’s dreadful manners. Though, I understand the student life. It’s hardly gourmet, is it? Even when  I  was at the Academy, we lived on strong tea and sheer willpower.      The Academy? Right, the art school in Florence. You always told me stories. Was it as… chaotic as you make it sound? All berets and impassioned arguments about perspective?      Oh, far more chaotic. Berets were optional, naturally – though very popular. It was the arguments that were compulsory! Everyone had an  opinion , especially about the Renaissance masters. And the professors? Eccentrics, every single one. Old Professor Bellini would lecture on Michelangelo whilst balancing an orange on his head.      No way! Seriously? That's amazing. You never told me that bit. Speaking of amazing, I think I’m finally starting to get my head around my dissertation. It's on post-war British sculpture, specifically the influence of constructivism. It’s… dense.      Constructivism, you say? Interesting. Very angular, isn’t it? All that metal and geometric shapes? Reminds me a bit of some things I saw in Moscow, back in… oh, must have been the early seventies. Travelled with your grandfather, you know. He was fascinated.      I didn’t know that! Grandad? In Moscow? He never mentioned it. He mostly just talked about his stamp collection.      He loved his stamps, yes. But he had a thirst for knowledge, your grandfather. And a hidden adventurous streak. We saw some incredible things. The Bolshoi Ballet, of course, but also these tiny, underground galleries showcasing artists who were working  around  the restrictions. It was… exhilarating. It makes me wonder if I should go back, actually. There's a big Malevich retrospective at the Tretyakov Gallery.      Woah, seriously? You should! It sounds incredible. I could actually help you plan it. I'm pretty good with logistics now, all that managing deadlines and budgetting for essays… Actually, travelling with you would be way better research for my dissertation than reading dusty books. Think of the inspiration!      You’re a flatterer, darling. But a tempting offer, nonetheless. Although, I'm not sure my knees are up to navigating the Moscow metro these days.

Right, that little pierogi place was  exactly  what I needed. Honestly, I was starting to feel a bit…wobbly. Not driving wobbly, just…energy low. Perhaps shouldn’t have skipped breakfast, even knowing the gym was looming.      You and your pre-gym rituals! You've told me about this a million times. It's always a debate – fuel up and feel sluggish, or push through on fumes and risk collapsing mid-squat? Honestly, I just grab a banana. Simple. Less to think about.      A banana? Oh, darling, that’s barely a starting pistol. I need something substantial. A proper carb load. It's a Cambridge thing, I think. We overthink everything. Or maybe it's just an age thing. You wouldn't understand at twenty-something.      Oh, here we go. Ageism already? We’ve barely left Tarnow! And honestly, I think it’s more of a 'never having held a proper job' thing. You’ve had the luxury of perfecting your pre-exercise routine for decades. I have to fit a workout  around  marking essays and prepping lessons.      That’s…a little harsh, don’t you think? I  have  done things. TEFL, remember? Trying to earn a living, supporting myself... in a small way, admittedly. It's just… different, isn't it? It’s not the same trajectory as climbing the career ladder. And it’s not like having a consistent income makes you immune to appreciating a good pre-workout meal.      Okay, okay, fair point. It wasn't meant to be  that  cutting. It’s just…seeing you talk about ‘Cambridge things’ and needing specific fuel… it feels very… privileged? Look, I’m not trying to start a fight, just pointing out a contrast. It’s interesting to see how different our experiences are, even though we’re both… well, English.      That's the funny thing, isn't it? “English.” Such a broad term. You sound so Northern, so distinctly…Lancashire. I get labelled ‘posh’ or ‘southern’ the moment I open my mouth further south. It's ridiculous. You wouldn’t get that in Poland, would you? They probably just hear ‘foreigner’.      Probably. Honestly, it's a relief sometimes. Easier to blend in. Though, being a woman travelling alone…even here, you get a different sort of attention. It’s infuriating. The stares, the unsolicited advice…      Oh, don't even get me started on the casual sexism. It's exhausting. I remember once, trying to fix a flat tyre years ago, and this man just  took over .

Oh, this is lovely, isn’t it? Proper coffee. Not that instant stuff Doreen keeps trying to foist on us. And this mug…it just feels right in your hand, doesn’t it? I remember when we got these, down at that pottery workshop near Haworth.      Aye, it does. Feels…substantial. A good weight. Not like these flimsy things they sell you now. And Haworth... that was a good day. You were determined to make yours perfectly symmetrical, weren’t you? I remember you fretting over it, turning it and turning it. Mine’s a bit wonky, as you can see. Adds character, I think.      Wonky is a polite way of putting it, love. It leans! But you were more interested in decorating it, weren’t you? All those little bluebells. Did they survive the firing, I wonder?      Most of ‘em. A few faded, but they’re still there, if you look close. Just like some memories, eh? Faded but still present. Speaking of present…have you put milk in? It seems a bit…strong.      Oh, sorry! Got distracted. Here you go. . Dreadful weather we’re having though, isn't it? Rain one minute, then that weak sun trying to break through. Barely enough for the tomatoes to appreciate it.      It’s Yorkshire weather, lass. You can’t expect anything else. I remember summers when it rained for a month solid. Old Man Hemmings used to say it was the spiders’ holiday. He swore they held meetings to decide when it should drizzle.      Old Man Hemmings! He was a character. Always had a story. I was out in the garden earlier, trying to deadhead the roses, and a huge spider dropped right onto my hand. Nearly jumped out of my skin!      Oh, I hate that. I leave them to it, generally. They’re good for the garden, apparently. Keeps the greenfly at bay. Though I did have a fright last week. Went to get a biscuit and there was one hiding  in  the biscuit tin!      Oh, no! That’s awful! It’s just… they’re so  sudden . We really need to get the ivy cut back from the house, though. It’s bringing them in. I've been meaning to do it for ages, but… well, you know how it is.      Always something else needing doing. It’s like that with the decorating, isn’t it? You start one room, then realize three others need a lick of paint.

Honestly, this is  so  stressful. Too many beaches, too many historical ruins… how are we supposed to choose? And Mum, you said Uncle Barry and Auntie Sheila might come with us?      Well, they’ve expressed interest, haven't they, darling? It would be lovely to have them join us for at least part of it. They haven’t had a proper holiday in ages, and Hastings is…well, Hastings is lovely, but a bit quiet for them all the time. Somewhere with a bit more going on might do them good.      Aye, Sheila’s been badgering me about a bit of sun for months. Keeps saying her joints are seizing up. A bit of Mediterranean weather might loosen ‘em, eh? Though I’m happy enough just pottering about with me guitar, wherever we end up.      But…Uncle Barry? Remember what happened last time we all went away together? The incident with the inflatable flamingo and the…well, everything? It was chaos! And he insists on bringing his karaoke machine  everywhere .      Oh, don’t be so dramatic, love. It wasn’t  that  bad. A little bit of harmless fun. They may bring the karaoke, yes, but we can always strategically position ourselves far, far away. Plus, it would be nice for them to see you enjoying yourself, you’ve been cooped up studying for ages.      She's got a point, you know. Barry means well, even if he is a bit… enthusiastic. And honestly, a bit of bad singing never hurt anyone. Reminds me of some of the gigs I used to play back in the day! Though granted, they weren't  always  well-received.      Easy for you to say, you  are  a musician. You’re supposed to make noise. Uncle Barry just…amplifies it and adds questionable song choices. What about Corfu, though? That looks…decent. Lots of water sports, not too many museums.      Corfu is a good shout. I remember your friend, Chloe, going there last year and she raved about it. She said the beaches were beautiful. And they have lovely tavernas. We could try to find one with live music, your Dad would like that.      Live music, you say? Now you're talking. Though, if it's anything like some of the tourist traps I've seen, it’ll probably be someone butchering a Beatles song on a keyboard. Still, it’s the thought that counts.      Chloe also said it was full of British tourists.

...and honestly, Kat, I’m still reeling from Patrick Verona. Like, Heath Ledger in  10 Things I Hate About You ? Peak. Just… peak. It's unfair to the rest of us men, really.      Oh,  please . You’re obsessed. It’s a good film, yeah, but ‘unfair to the rest of us men’? You barely even  have  a crush on anyone at the moment! Besides, it’s a classic teen rom-com. Predictable, but enjoyable. Though I did feel a bit bad for Joey Donner, he really thought he was  it .      Predictable? It’s about challenging preconceptions! And the poetry scene? Iconic! Don't underestimate Joey Donner though, he was a model. A  model , Kat! That's a whole thing. Anyway, shifting gears… Ugh, History is just… killing me. Mr. Harrison is convinced we all want to write essays on the socio-economic impact of the Industrial Revolution.      Tell me about it. I spent three hours last night trying to understand the Corn Laws. Three hours! My brain felt like mush by the end. And he  loves  asking about primary sources. Like, who actually  remembers  what some bloke wrote in 1842?      Exactly! It’s just…stuffing our heads with dates and names. And then he wonders why we can't remember them for the test! I'm pretty sure I dreamt about spinning jennys last night. It was a weird dream.      Spinning jennys? Oh, no. See, you  are  obsessed! But seriously, we need to study together for the test. Maybe next week? My mum’s making me do extra piano practice this week, so I'm already miserable.      Definitely. Next week is good. We could do it at my place? My mum's out at a conference all week, so we’d have the house to ourselves. We could order pizza and make it a proper study session… with a  10 Things I Hate About You  break halfway through, obviously.      Ooh, sold! Your mum makes the  best  cookies, too. Remember those chocolate chip ones she made last Christmas? Divine. Speaking of leaving the house though… are you still excited about London? We're practically counting down the days now.      So excited! I’ve been making a list of all the things I want to see. The British Museum, obviously. And I really want to go to a West End show. There’s one about Matilda that looks amazing.      Matilda is brilliant! I’ve heard the music is really good.

Now, you say this… Facebook… it’s all pictures of what people 'ad for their tea, is it? Seems a right waste o’ time, if you ask me. Back in my day, if you wanted to know what someone was up to, you just popped round for a chat, didn't ya? None of this digital nonsense.      Oh, Arthur, don’t be so dismissive. It's how we keep up with everyone, especially the ones who’ve moved away. I see pictures of little Emily, my granddaughter, all the time. And Sarah posts lovely photos of her garden. It's nice. Though I confess, I don't understand half of it. All the ‘shares’ and ‘likes’…      It's more than just pictures of food, Mum. It’s about connection, sharing information. I use it a lot for my students – sharing articles, setting assignments. But it can be… overwhelming. I was reading about how it can exasperate certain conditions, like OCD. Obsessive Compulsive Disorder.      Absolutely. The constant stream of information, the need to curate a perfect online persona… it’s a breeding ground for anxiety. People get stuck in cycles of checking and re-checking, comparing themselves to others. It’s a big topic in psychology at the moment.      OCD, you say? Sounds a bit…fancy. My sister, bless ‘er soul, she was a bit particular, always ‘avin’ things  just so . Doors locked three times, that sort o' thing. But they didn’t ‘ave names for it back then. Just said she was a bit…eccentric.      That sounds a bit like my Aunt Millie, actually. She’d wash her hands raw, even after just touching something clean. We used to think she was just a bit of a nervous wreck. Poor thing. It's interesting how we understand these things better now. Makes you wonder how many people suffered in silence.      It does. And it's not just about cleanliness. It can manifest in all sorts of ways – intrusive thoughts, compulsive behaviours, a need for symmetry. It can be incredibly debilitating. I had a student last year who was struggling with it badly. Luckily, the university has good support services.      Speaking of struggling… anyone remember when young Thomas – your nephew, Sarah? – had chicken pox? That was a nightmare. He was covered head to toe. Little red spots everywhere.      Oh, don't remind me! He was miserable. And constantly scratching. Had to keep his nails clipped short, didn’t we?

Honestly, this is lovely. Just having everyone together like this. It feels…proper. Like the old days, doesn’t it? Before everyone was glued to their phones.      Proper is a good word, Sarah. It is. Remember when a holiday meant a week in Bognor Regis, battling for a deckchair? No Instagramming the sunset, just…being there.      Oh, Bognor Regis! Gran used to drag us there every year. The arcades were the only redeeming feature. Though, looking back, it  was  nice to just switch off. Unlike trying to have a holiday now, where you feel obligated to document every single crumb you eat.      Tell me about it! I spent half my last holiday editing photos for TikTok. Honestly, it's exhausting. I’d rather just…  be  on the beach, ya know?      You lot sound like old fogeys! Though, I get it. I’m planning a little trip to Germany soon, finally. Been meaning to for ages. Got a silver exhibition over there, showcasing some new pieces. Want to practice my German too. It’s… rusty, to say the least.      Germany, eh? Good luck with the German, Mark. They don’t take kindly to butchered attempts, that’s for sure. I did a bit of business travel over there years ago - needed to be pretty slick with the language to get a decent deal.      Oh, languages! My German is atrocious. I remember trying to order a coffee on a school trip and somehow asking for a live chicken. The waitress looked at me like I’d lost my marbles.      A live chicken! Gran, you’re brilliant!      She’s always been a bit of a disaster with languages, our Sarah. Though, she’s a miracle worker with a syringe, wouldn’t you say?      Hey! I managed to decipher enough French to get through a couple of holidays. And I certainly haven’t ordered any poultry in… well, a long time. Speaking of holidays though, are we still thinking about that cottage in Cornwall this summer?      Cornwall sounds lovely! Especially if the weather holds. Remember that camping trip we took as kids, Gran? The one where it rained for a week straight?      Oh, don't remind me! That was a disaster. Your mum swore she’d never go camping again. Spent the entire time huddled in the car trying to stay dry. I had to drive to Ashford just to get another tent pole.      Mum always did have a knack for attracting bad weather.

...Honestly, the sound at that festival was atrocious. Like, genuinely awful. You could barely hear Leo’s fills over the bass. Which, considering how good a drummer he is, is a crime against music.      Leo? Right, yeah, you went to “Coastal Chaos” then? I saw a few snaps on Insta. Thought you were meant to be buried in dissertations.      I  am  buried in dissertations! It was a strategic escape. A mental health day, if you will. And yes, Leo was playing with “Static Bloom”. They were… underwhelming, mostly due to the sound guy clearly having never mixed anything before. How’s work been? Still slinging amazing food at The Salty Siren?      Still slinging. It’s non-stop, especially with the tourists. Had a bloke complain his scallops were 'too sea-like' yesterday. You can’t win. But yeah, it pays the bills, and Chef Davies is actually letting me take on a bit more responsibility with the specials board, which is good.      “Too sea-like”? Seriously? People… Anyway, that’s brilliant about the specials board! You’re a way better cook than half the people I know who went to uni. Speaking of which, any thoughts on the internship hunt? Still eyeing up that place in Bristol?      Nah, Bristol fell through. Turns out ‘experience with high-volume service’ doesn't count when your experience is mostly seaside pubs. I’m looking at something closer to home now, a gastropub near Dartmoor. It's less glamorous, but the hours would be better, and the guy seems decent. What about  you  then? Dissertation going okay amidst the festival escapes?      It’s…progressing. Slowly. It’s on the semiotics of post-punk album art, which sounds way cooler than it is in practice. Mostly it's staring at Joy Division sleeves for eight hours a day. I’ve applied for that research assistant role at the university, though. That's the dream. More staring at things, admittedly, but  paid  staring.      Paid staring sounds significantly better than unpaid suffering. Hey, remember Mark from sixth form? The one who was obsessed with The Strokes?      Vaguely? The skinny one with the perpetually ironic t-shirts? What about him?      He’s a tour manager now! Apparently, he’s with this up-and-coming band, “Crimson Static”. They’re doing really well. Saw something about them playing the O2 Academy in Birmingham.      No way! Mark? That's mental. He always seemed…directionless, bless him.

Och, it’s proper noisy in here, isn’t it? I can barely hear mesel think. Still, at least the coffee’s decent. You alright, lad? You haven't touched yours.      It’s alright, Mam. Just…thinking. About the summer, mostly. And whether I’ll actually be able to sleep with Uncle Derek snoring like a cement mixer at your sister’s.      Oh, Derek. He’s a force of nature, that one. We’ll get you a quiet room, love. Or maybe earmuffs! Seriously though, have you been giving any thought to what  you  want to do this summer? Beyond avoiding Uncle Derek’s nocturnal symphony, that is.      I dunno. Ben wants to go camping, up near Durham. Said there’s a massive field where loads of us can pitch tents. But, like, tents? Sleeping bags? All that effort…      Durham's lovely, aye. I used to take school trips there. The cathedral’s magnificent. And camping… well, it’s not so bad. Bit of fresh air does you good. We’ve got some old sleeping bags in the attic, I think. And maybe even a spare two-man tent. We'd need to check it for spiders, mind.      Spiders?! No way. I’m not sharing a tent with eight-legged freaks. Plus, getting there… it’s a pain, isn’t it? Train to Durham then a bus… or trying to convince Dad to drive us.      Your Dad’s busy with that new “business venture” of his. Honestly, all these online things… he thinks he’s the next Richard Branson selling fancy dog collars. Still, it keeps him occupied. Look, we’ll figure out the transport. Maybe I could drive you and Ben? Though, I swear, the roads are getting busier every year. Especially around the Metrocentre when people try and do their shopping.      The Metrocentre's a nightmare. Remember last Christmas? It took us an hour just to find a parking space. And then Grandma got stuck in the lift!      Don't remind me. That was a day. She was convinced she was going to be trapped forever, and kept shouting at the control panel. Speaking of lists, I need to write one for the shop. Milk, bread, biscuits… and that loyalty card thing for this coffee shop. They’ve got some offer on, apparently.      Oh, I saw that. You need to collect seven stamps to get a free cake. You’re already on three.

...Honestly, the whole thing was a disaster. Trying to get a decent recording of Mrs. Higgins attempting a West Midlands dialect – a complete train wreck. She kept slipping into Received Pronunciation! It was supposed to be for my phonetics project, but it's more comedy gold at this point.      No way! Mrs. Higgins? The lady who runs the village shop? That  is  rich. You’d think living in Bronsgrove her whole life, the accent would be ingrained. Though, I suppose even we lose bits of it when we’re trying to be…professional, or whatever. It’s funny, isn’t it, how conscious you become of  how  you speak when someone’s actively listening.      Massively. I was trying to explain the difference between a glottal stop and a T-deletion, and she just looked at me like I’d grown a second head. Then she started talking about her granddaughter, Chloe, who's expecting. Completely sidestepped the question.      Chloe? No way! Is that Mark’s girlfriend? Brilliant! I haven't seen them both in ages. Last time was… graduation, wasn't it? Feels like a lifetime ago. Are they excited?      Very. She’s about six months along, apparently. It's a bit surreal, isn’t it? Us getting to ‘adult’ stuff like babies and… mortgages and all the rest. Remember when our biggest worry was finishing that dreadful comparative literature essay?      Oh god, don’t remind me. Professor Davies and his obsession with Borges. I swear, he single-handedly ruined my enjoyment of short stories. Speaking of ‘adult’ stuff... have you had a chance to look at that form for the council tax? It's a bloody nightmare. All those boxes, and they expect you to know what a ‘collective household’ even means!      Not yet, it's lurking on the kitchen table, a monument to bureaucratic ineptitude. I’ve been trying to avoid it. I’m still trying to get my head around the cost of everything here in Sussex. It's noticeably more expensive than Bedford, even for just groceries.      Tell me about it! Everything's gone up. It's mental. I’m actually starting to budget properly now. Never thought I’d be  me  of all people budgeting, considering what I earn. Still, need to think about the future, you know? Thinking about maybe getting a place with Sarah.      Oh, really? That’s brilliant! How’s that going?      Good, good.

...Honestly, the guilt is awful, isn't it? Even knowing it was Dad's decision, even knowing he was in pain… it doesn’t make it easier. Especially with Mum, she's just…lost. Completely.      Oh, love, I can only imagine. Losing Dad so quickly, after everything… it’s a shock to the system, even for those of us who weren’t  directly  caring for him day to day. And your Mum, bless her. They were always such a unit. It’s almost like a part of her has gone with him. Have you been able to get her to eat anything? She barely touched her dinner when I popped round yesterday.      No, not really. A few bites of toast, a sip of tea. Mostly just staring out the window. I’ve been trying to coax her, bring round her favourite biscuits, but she just pushes them around the plate. She keeps saying she feels like she should be  doing  something, like she failed somehow because she couldn't fix it. It’s heartbreaking.      That’s Mum, isn't it? Always needing to be the one in control, the one looking after everyone else. It’s what she does. She'll feel completely adrift if she can’t. You know, it might be worth seeing if Dr. Davies will come out for a house call? Just to check she’s not getting dehydrated, and maybe…maybe suggest something for her anxiety. She’s always been resistant to medication, but even just talking to a professional might help.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to call him, I just… keep putting it off. It feels like admitting defeat, that Mum needs help. But you're right. She  does . It's all just so raw, isn’t it? And then, on top of that, Liam’s been off school for a week now with this persistent cough. Not COVID, thankfully, but the doctor suspects a chest infection. He's miserable.      Oh, poor Liam! Another worry on top of everything else. Kids pick up everything, don’t they? How’s Sophie coping? She's usually so resilient.      She's…better than I expected, actually. She’s being really supportive of Mum, running around making her tea, trying to distract her with stories about school. But I caught her crying in her room last night. She’s pretending to be strong, but I think she's really frightened.

Honestly, Leo, you’ve barely touched your dinner. You need your energy for tennis tomorrow. Old Mr. Henderson will have you running around like a blue-arsed fly if you're not fuelled up.      It's alright, Mum. I’m just…thinking about the history essay. It's due on Friday and I haven't even started researching the Suffragettes yet. It’s  so  boring.      The Suffragettes were anything but boring, Thomas. Quite radical, actually. Perhaps approach it from that angle? The sheer audacity of what they did…breaking windows, disrupting meetings…      Disrupting meetings sounds…fun. Though probably gets you in trouble now, doesn’t it?      It did then, too, Leo! Definitely not something to try at school. Speaking of trouble, how  was  football practice today? Did you manage to score?      Not really. Sam hogged the ball the entire time. It's so frustrating. I think I’m better off sticking to tennis. At least Mr. Henderson spreads the coaching around a bit. He’s actually really good, you know. He used to be proper good, played at Wimbledon qualifying, I think Dad said.      That’s right. He was. A nasty wrist injury, though, ended his playing career. That’s why he's so keen on technique, making sure his students avoid the same pitfalls. It’s a good investment, really, these lessons. You’re building discipline, skills…      And fitness! You’re never too young to think about that. It’s interesting, isn’t it, how people often turn a disappointment into something positive? Like that whole Brexit referendum - people thinking they were taking back control, but it ending up a bit of a mess for a lot of folks.      Don’t get me started on that. A very short-sighted decision, in my opinion. It's created so much uncertainty for businesses. We’re still navigating the fallout, even now.      Is it like when my computer game gets an update and then everything breaks?      That’s a surprisingly accurate analogy, actually. A bit less consequential, admittedly. Thomas, you’re getting to that age where you need to start thinking seriously about what you want to do after school. Have you given any more thought to apprenticeships?      Dad keeps going on about them. He thinks I should look at something in engineering. But I don’t  want  to be an engineer. I was thinking maybe something to do with…I don’t know…media?

Honestly, this is a blessed relief. Getting out of London, even for a few days… it’s just  needed . Though Lancaster wasn’t exactly top of my list of ‘escape to’ destinations, was it?      No, definitely not. It was more… convenient. You needing to visit your aunt, and me needing to scope out Lancaster Uni for potential Masters programmes. Kill two birds, and all that. Though, I’m genuinely starting to feel a bit excited. Have you been before?      Oh, ages ago. When I was little. I remember a castle, obviously. And a really… grey sky. Auntie Brenda's house is lovely, all rambling and cosy, but the town itself… I don’t have much recollection. She keeps going on about Morecambe, though. Apparently, the promenade is ‘absolutely delightful’.      Morecambe? Right. I did a tiny bit of research. Saw something about a big, slightly sad-looking pier. And… a cockle disaster? What was that about?      Oh god, don’t even  start  me on the cockle disaster. It’s a local legend. Back in 2004, a bunch of cockle pickers, mostly Chinese migrant workers, were trapped by the tide. It was… awful. Twenty-three people died. It really put Morecambe on the map for all the wrong reasons. It's grim, but it's part of the area’s history, I suppose.      Wow. That's… horrific. I had no idea. Right, maybe we’ll skip the cockle-picking then. Focus on the fish and chips, yeah? I’ve read they do a proper Lancashire fish and chips.      Absolutely. Fish and chips are non-negotiable. Auntie Brenda promised to take us to her favourite place. It’s reputedly the best for miles. Speaking of miles, how’s the uni hunt going? Have you narrowed down your options at all?      Sort of. Lancaster seems… nice. Very campus-based, which I like. It's a bit intimidating though, thinking about going back to full-time study. It's been a few years since my undergrad. And a Masters… yikes. That means a dissertation!      Oh, the dreaded dissertation. I remember those days. It feels like an Everest you have to climb. What are you thinking of doing, anyway? Still leaning towards something linguistics-based?      Yeah, hopefully. I'm toying with the idea of a sociolinguistics project – maybe looking at dialect levelling in younger generations. It’s something I’ve been noticing more and more in my role at the research centre.

...Honestly, I still can’t believe Old Man Hemmings actually  liked  that band. The Voidwalkers? Sounded like a cat fightin’ a washing machine, didn’t they?      Aye, a right racket. Though, to be fair, Hemmings likes anything loud enough to drown out his own thoughts, doesn't he? Reminds me of Dad, actually. Anything with a good bassline and he’s hooked, regardless of what else is goin’ on.      True enough. Still, you’d think a history lecturer would appreciate a bit more… nuance. Speaking of which, how's your dissertation comin’ on? Still wrestlin’ with the Norman Conquest?      Don't even  mention  it. I'm officially lost in a sea of primary sources. Apparently, every farmer in 1066 had a detailed account of William the Conqueror's breakfast habits. Or somethin’ like that. It’s relentless. I'm half tempted to just write about the impact of Norman fashion on peasant footwear.      Now  that  I’d read. Seriously though, are you alright? You seem a bit stressed. Need a break? We could ditch this and go for a walk down by the canal. It’s a lovely evening.      I appreciate it, I do. Just… the deadline’s looming, and I feel like I’m makin’ zero progress. Plus, I promised I’d help Liam with his photography project tomorrow. He's trying to get some shots of the old railway bridge, but reckons the light's always wrong.      Oh, Liam's still at it with the photography, is he? Good for him, though. He's got a real eye, that lad. Remember when he tried to photograph Mrs. Higgins’ cat? Ended up covered in scratches.      How could I forget? That cat was a demon. But yeah, he's proper dedicated. He’s talkin' about applying to art school after college. Seems serious about it.      Good on him. It’s good to have something you’re passionate about, isn’t it? What about you, with music? Still playin’ the guitar?      On and off. Life just gets in the way, y’know? Lectures, essays, tryin’ to have a social life… it's all a bit much sometimes. I did jam with Ben and Sarah last week though. We tried to cover some Arctic Monkeys. It sounded… rough.      Rough, you say? I bet you were brilliant. You always were the best guitarist in the band, even when we were fifteen and sounded like a swarm of wasps.

Right, okay. This is officially stressful. Rhys, you’ve just cured yellow  again ? Honestly, you're suspiciously good at this. Are you secretly a virologist in disguise?      Now, now, Angharad. A bit of strategic thinking is all it is. Though, I  did  consider a career in medical research once. My Nan always said I had a knack for spotting patterns. And let’s be honest, you were distracted by trying to build a research station in Atlanta when we  clearly  needed one in Cairo.      Strategic thinking? He's just a ruthless efficiency machine. Like a Welsh badger on a mission. No offense, mate.      He  is  good. It's… unnerving. He makes it look easy.      Easy? Nothing’s easy when saving the world, my boy! Reminds me of my time volunteering in disaster relief in Indonesia. You think you've got a handle on things, then BAM! Another outbreak. Different continent, same panic. Though, thankfully, no colour-coded disease cubes.      That’s the truth, Dai. It's always something. Always. I deal with enough 'outbreaks' at work, I don’t need them on a board game! Though, it  is  a good distraction from the rain hammering down outside.      Distraction? I'm bordering on a full-blown anxiety attack. We’re one epidemic away from losing, and Ben, you haven’t even used your special ability yet! You're supposed to be moving between cities to share knowledge, not admiring the scenery.      Look, I was scouting for potential hot spots! Bristol’s a vibrant place, you know. Needed to get a feel for the geography. Plus, I was thinking about what we're having for dinner if we actually  win  this thing. Roast lamb? I'm feeling a roast.      You and your roast lamb! Priorities, mate, priorities. Angharad's right, though, Ben. Use your dispatch. We need to get the cures spread around.      I… I don't want to mess things up. What if I move to the wrong place and it makes it worse? I always feel like I’m hindering everyone.      Oh, come on, Huw. That's rubbish. You’re excellent at containing outbreaks. Remember last time we played? You single-handedly saved Europe. Don’t underestimate yourself. Rhodes, explain it to him again, slowly. You’re the patient one.      Right you are. Huw, think of it like this. You  are  the transport network. If I find a cure for blue in Paris, you can get it to Rome in a single turn.

Honestly, this whole CBeebies pantomime thing… it’s a bit much, isn't it? They’re  everywhere  promoting it.      But Mummy, it's gonna be  amazing ! Mr Tumble is gonna be in it! And the Octonauts!      Yeah! And Captain Barnacle! He’s the best. Do you think he'll have his goggles?      I’m sure Captain Barnacle will have his goggles, darling. But it's… the timing. It’s right before your birthdays. It feels a bit chaotic trying to organise everything.      My birthday is  first ! Remember? March the 15th! It's a good day, because it's almost spring.      Mine's in June. That’s proper summer. We can have a bouncy castle then! A really BIG one.      A big bouncy castle sounds good. We’ll see. We haven’t even decided what you each want to  do  for your birthdays yet. Last year was the zoo, wasn't it?      And the pizza afterwards! That was the best part!      I wanted the dinosaur nuggets! They didn’t have enough dinosaur nuggets.      Okay, okay, we'll make sure there are  plenty  of dinosaur nuggets this year. Now, CBeebies... have you been watching that new story about the little bear who lost his roar?      Oh! The one where he tries to find it in all the silly places? It's funny! He looked in a teapot!      And a shoe! He looked in a really big Wellington boot.      Exactly! It’s a lovely little story, isn't it? It reminded me of something my Nan used to say, “Lost your roar, have you? Well, look under the cushions!” She always had a saying for everything.      Nana's sayings are good! She always said, "Don't count your chickens before they hatch." What does  that  mean?      Mmm, that means don't get excited about something happening until it's actually happened. It's a bit grown-up, really.      Like, don't get excited about the bouncy castle until we've actually  booked  it?      Precisely! You’re a clever one. Right, back to birthdays. We also have World Book Day coming up, and then Mother’s Day… it's a busy few weeks. I'm thinking we can tie World Book Day into a little trip to the library. You both love picking out books.      Can I choose a book about a princess? A really sparkly princess!      I want a dinosaur book! With lots of pictures of T-Rexes!

…Honestly, the sourdough is  amazing . Did you two get this from that new place on Bellenden Road?      I did. It’s ridiculously good, isn't it? Worth the extra couple of quid. Though, you’ve already practically demolished half the loaf, so clearly you agree!      It is lovely. Though, it makes me think about moving back to Hitchin. My mum keeps sending me photos of the village bakery – proper bread, proper everything. It's tempting, you know? After… well, after everything with Ben.      Hitchin? Really? I thought you were pretty settled here, teaching and all. And the… vibrancy, as you always call it.      I  am  settled, mostly. I love my job at the language centre. But…it's quiet here, isn't it? Particularly in the evenings. And Mum’s right, it just feels…easier there. Less pressure. Fewer dating app disasters.      Oh, still on the apps then? I thought you’d sworn them off after… the artist who claimed to be a ‘spiritual alchemist’?      Don’t remind me. He tried to read my aura over Zoom. Honestly. No, I dipped out for a month, then I gave it another go. Old habits, I suppose. It’s just… lonely sometimes. And London dating feels so… transactional.      I can imagine. It’s mostly people looking for a ‘project’ or something to fill their Instagram feed. It's mental. I tried it briefly after moving back from Germany, but it felt so… manufactured.      You and your manufactured experiences! You spent three years living in a castle, practically! That's hardly 'real life', is it?
