Though, I suppose being an engineer rebuilding historical structures  is  a bit niche on Tinder.      Hey! There are plenty of people who appreciate a well-preserved medieval turret. It’s just they weren’t on Tinder. And it wasn't a castle, it was a  schloss . There’s a difference. Anyway, it’s not the dating I miss about Germany so much as the… the feeling of being somewhere new. Here, everything feels so… defined. Like everyone already has their place.      That’s a good way to put it. It's hard to break into established friend groups, isn’t it? Even after years.      It is. But you’ve got us! And Lizzie and Mark, and… a few others. We  are  your established friend group, aren’t we? We just need to socialise more. Honestly, the weather’s been dreadful lately, it's been an excuse for everyone to hibernate.

...Honestly, the whole thing just triggered a memory. My Gran used to make a treacle tart  exactly  like that – right down to the slightly burnt edges. She’d always say it was the secret to the flavour. Do you two remember Gran's treacle tart?      Oh,  absolutely . It was legendary! Though, thinking about it, I mostly remember trying to steal bits of the pastry before it went in the oven. She always knew, didn’t she? And would give me a little slap on the hand, but then sneak me a tiny piece anyway. It’s funny the things you remember. Did she ever try to teach you, Sarah? You're a good cook, aren’t you?      I wouldn’t say  good , more…competent. And no, not the treacle tart. She tried to get me to learn her Yorkshire pudding recipe once, but I just couldn't grasp the timing. It always ended up flat. She was a brilliant cook, your Mum, Helen. Completely self-taught, wasn’t she?      Completely. Left school at fourteen, I think, and just picked it all up from her mother. It's amazing, really. She never wrote anything down either. Everything was ‘a pinch of this’ and ‘a handful of that’. I’ve tried recreating some of her dishes and it’s so frustrating. It’s never  quite  right. It feels like a little piece of her is missing when it doesn't taste exactly as it should.      I know what you mean. It’s the same with my Nan’s shortbread. She used to make it every Christmas. It wasn't fancy, just simple, buttery goodness. And it tasted… like Christmas. I’ve tried so many recipes, and they're all okay, but they just lack that… something. It makes you wonder about language, doesn’t it? We can write down recipes, but can we really translate  feeling  into instructions?      That’s a really good point, actually. It’s like dialects, isn't it? You can try to phonetically write out how someone speaks, but it never really captures the rhythm and…the essence of it. I noticed when I was in France last year, no matter how fluent I became, the French always knew I wasn't  from  there. It was something in my pronunciation, my intonation.      It's completely true! I was on a conference call with some Americans last week, and they kept asking where in England

...and honestly, the buffet breakfast was a  disaster . Not a full English in sight! Just croissants and this weird German bread. Which, considering where  you  were born, love, doesn’t seem right, does it?      Oh, Mum! You and a full English. It’s a love story. And yes, slightly ironic, isn’t it? Germany doesn’t need to be reminded of its bread, thank you very much. Did you at least find some decent coffee? That's the most important thing.      Aye, the coffee was alright. Not Yorkshire tea, mind you, nothing ever is. But strong enough to keep us going during those… enthusiastic… line dancing lessons.      Line dancing?! Seriously? Dad, you? I’m picturing something… magnificent.      Magnificent is a strong word, lad. More… determined. There was a woman, Brenda, ran the whole thing. Very energetic. Kept telling me I needed to “dig deeper with me heels!” Nearly took out poor Mrs. Higgins next to me.      He nearly did! She shrieked, poor thing. Honestly, it was all a bit much. The hotel  itself  was lovely though. Right on the coast, beautiful views. We took a little boat trip, saw some seals. That was nice and peaceful, compared to Brenda.      Seals! Oh, that sounds lovely. Was the weather okay? I was worried about you two going with all that rain we’d been having.      Actually, it was surprisingly good. A bit breezy, but mostly sunshine. We had one day where it poured, absolutely  poured , so we spent it in a little antique shop. I found a rather charming teapot – a little chipped, but perfect for my collection.      A chipped teapot? Knowing you, Mum, it’ll be the most treasured one. You always find the character in things.      It does have a certain…je ne sais quoi. Your father wasn’t so impressed. Said it looked like something the cat dragged in.      I just said it wasn't… pristine. Practicality, you see. A chipped teapot is a recipe for disaster.      Oh, Dad. You're such a romantic. Did you have any good food, apart from the breakfast debacle?      We had some wonderful fish and chips one evening, proper seaside fish and chips. And there was a little pub that did a lovely Sunday roast. Your father nearly ate them out of house and home.      I was hungry! All that line dancing wears a man out, you know. Serious business, that. Although, I did manage to trip over my own feet during the 'Electric Slide'.

Right, okay. So, this is…an attempt at shakshuka. It’s either going to be amazing or a complete disaster. Honestly, I'm not sure which.      Ooh, ambitious for a Saturday morning, isn’t it? Smells…interesting. A bit spicy? You know I’m a wimp with chili.      Just a  touch  of harissa. I saw Gordon Ramsay do it on YouTube and made it look so effortless. It never is, is it? Everything looks easier on YouTube. Like learning to fix a boiler. Which, incidentally, is still on my list.      Morning, you two. Boiler still on the list, eh? You’d think with your engineering brain, a bit of plumbing wouldn’t scare you.      It’s not the plumbing, it’s the  gas . Honestly, I don’t want to blow the house up. Plus, finding the time. This week has been…intense at work. They're pushing this new bridge design through and the simulations are… temperamental.      A bridge? Goodness, that sounds important. And stressful. What’s temperamental about them?      Well, the load distribution isn’t quite behaving as predicted, especially with extreme weather scenarios. It’s likely just a modelling issue, but it needs triple-checking. Every decimal place is crucial when you're talking about tonnes of steel and potentially hundreds of cars.      Sounds proper grown-up stuff. I’m currently dissecting the fallout from that pop star’s latest Instagram post. Slightly less weighty, admittedly. Though the comments section is a battlefield.      Oh, who? The one who dyed her hair bright orange?      The very one. Apparently, it’s a political statement. Or…perhaps just a bad hair day. The internet is convinced it’s both. Honestly, the lengths people go to for a reaction.      It's baffling. I saw something about a celebrity apology video last night. Seemed to take more effort than designing a perfectly stable arch.      Speaking of effort… have you two made any plans for the weekend besides near-disaster shakshuka and online outrage? I was thinking of going to that new artisan market in Digbeth. Thought you might like it, Sarah, for research for your articles.      Oh, that sounds good! Actually, I'm supposed to be interviewing a local ceramicist next week, something a bit different from the usual showbiz fluff. It might be there. I’ll check. What about you, Alex? Still escaping into the world of bridges and boilers?      Probably. I promised myself I’d get back to that woodworking project, but… the bridge is looming.

...Honestly, the satnav just completely lost it on the A1. Kept telling me to turn left into a field. A  field , Reg!      Ah, those things. Bless ‘em. They’re good for a laugh, aren’t they? Mines tried to take me down a cycle lane a few times. Google Maps is usually alright, though. Can’t beat it for knowing where you are, even if it does tell you to take the scenic route when you just want to get there.      Google Maps is a lifesaver, definitely. Though even  it  struggles sometimes when you’re trying to navigate these tiny German villages. My mum's been on at me to visit more, says I’m forgetting my roots, being born over there and all. It's just…getting time off is impossible.      Your mum's a good woman, Ella. Mine’s always moaning I don’t call enough. Says I’m too busy 'swinging a hammer' as if that’s a crime. Still, beats being stuck in an office all day, right? Speaking of beating things, anyone else reckon this steak is fantastic?      It is good, isn’t it? Best pub grub in Peterborough, easily. Listen, Reg, we were talking about you heading off... Saudi Arabia, that's a long way. You'll be needing a proper satnav over there, I reckon. Not one of those cheap ones.      Saudi? Cor, that's a different kettle of fish altogether. It'll be hot, that's for sure. And different rules, different everything. You’ll have to keep your wits about you, lad. Make sure you’ve got someone reliable to look after things here, too.      How long are you going for, Reg? And what will you actually  be  doing? You’ve been a bit vague.      Six months, to start. Training the local chaps, mostly. Part of the military assistance program. It's… well, it's a job. Pays well. And honestly, it's a bit of a change. I’m getting too old for all this running around in the UK, you know? Back acting up again, knees are creaking…      Six months... that's a good chunk of time. Will you be able to get internet access, keep in touch?      Oh, aye. They’ve got everything over there now, surprisingly. Satellite internet, the works. Though I doubt I’ll be spending much time online. Too much to see, too much to learn.

Honestly, seeing gardens like this does wonders for the soul, doesn’t it? It’s a far cry from the, uh, slightly overgrown patch I call a ‘lawn’ back home. Though, to be fair, I  have  been meaning to get on top of it. Just… life keeps happening.      It really does. Though, don’t beat yourself up about the garden, Alistair. You’ve been incredibly busy launching that new tech venture. I remember you practically living on coffee and spreadsheets for months. How  are  you feeling, actually? You looked a bit… drawn when we bumped into each other at the hotel this morning.      She’s got you there, Alistair. You were a shade of pale that even the Swedish light couldn't brighten. You need looking after, you do. Have you been sleeping? And properly  eating ? Not just grabbing whatever’s easiest when you’re coding at 3 AM.      You two are terrible. Enabling each other in worrying about me, the lot of you. I’m fine, honestly. Just a bit… run down. The launch was enormous, more successful than we anticipated, which is brilliant, but it came at a cost. Sleep definitely suffered. And yes, my diet has consisted largely of takeaways and energy drinks. Urgent adjustments are needed.      “Fine” is a very subjective word, Alistair. It doesn’t sound particularly convincing coming from someone who looks like they’ve been wrestling a badger. Honestly, you need to think about boosting your immune system. All that stress and poor nutrition is a recipe for disaster. I’ve got a friend who swears by elderberry syrup.      Elderberry is good, but you need more than just a syrup, Kate. He needs a consistent routine. Maybe we can drag him for a walk every morning? And I’ve been reading about the benefits of forest bathing –  Shinrin-yoku , they call it. We’re practically in a forest here! Apparently, the phytoncides released by the trees are amazing for stress and immunity.      Forest bathing? Sounds…New Age-y. But frankly, I’m open to anything. My vitality is currently hovering around that of a wilted lettuce. You're right, I need a proper kickstart. I was thinking maybe a detox retreat when things settle down, but that feels so… drastic.      A retreat is lovely, but it's often the follow-through that's hard. Small, consistent changes are far more sustainable. And honestly, Alistair, have you been regular with, well… with  everything ?

...Honestly, the way your dad’s voice has changed, it’s startling. It’s gotten  so  gravelly. I nearly jumped when he answered the door earlier. It’s not just age, is it? I mean, it's more…worn.      You're not wrong, Carol. It’s the years, definitely. And… well, you know. He still enjoys a pint or three. Doesn’t help the vocal cords, does it? Mum keeps saying he needs to see a doctor, but he just waves her off. Stubborn as an old mule, he is.      Stubborn is an understatement. Remember when he tried to convince us the roundabout at Hempstead Valley wasn’t actually a roundabout, but a “continuous flow intersection”? He argued for a solid ten minutes.      Ah, good times. Though, young lady,  your  accent’s changed a bit too. Less Kentish, more…London, almost? Being at uni in the city does things to a person.      Dad! Don’t start. It’s not a  change , it’s…refined. And it’s not London, it’s just less…pronounced. People can actually understand me now! Back home, I felt like I had to translate myself sometimes. Everyone round here still sounds like they've swallowed a gravel pit. No offence, Carol, you're lovely, but...      None taken, dear. I’ve heard worse. Your brother, for a start. He sounds like he's permanently got a cold. And it's funny, isn’t it, how accents can change? My nan, bless her, used to say Harlow sounded completely different when she was growing up. All fields and farmhands, not council estates.      Speaking of changes, has anyone else noticed how much weight Mum’s put on? I’m worried about her. She’s barely leaving the house since…well, since everything with Geoff happened. It’s all biscuits and daytime TV now.      It’s awful. I tried bringing it up last week, gently, but she just got defensive. Said I was being critical. It’s like she's self-sabotaging. I think she's really struggling with being alone, y’know? Geoff always used to walk with her, even just around the garden. Now she just sits.      Geoff was a rotter. Always had a shifty look about him. Glad she finally got rid. Though, the custody thing is a mess. Little Alfie deserves better than being bounced between two households neither of which seem particularly stable.      Tell me about it.

Honestly, Leo, you’d think grating cheese wouldn’t be such a monumental task. It's not rocket science, you know. Just…hold it firmly and  go . Not…little tentative scrapes.      It's harder than it looks! And it's…slippery. Plus, I don’t want to grate my knuckles. Remember Uncle David and the nutmeg?      Oh,  that  Christmas. Poor David. He was sporting bandages for weeks. But yes, a firm grip is key. You’re making enough for the Baked Alaska, you know. We need a mountain of grated cheese for the meringue. Speaking of which, are you excited about Halloween? Mrs. Henderson is going all out this year, apparently.      Yeah! Old Man Henderson’s always pretty good. Last year’s graveyard was amazing. I’m going as…well, it’s a surprise. Still working on the costume. You and Dad are doing…what?      We’ve decided on a themed couple's costume – Morticia and Gomez Addams. Very sophisticated. Your father is already practicing his dramatic finger-snapping. It's rather alarming.      That  does  sound like Dad. Hey, did you finish looking at those recruiting materials for the youth programme?      Almost. It’s…challenging. Finding people with the right blend of experience and, frankly, the right  attitude . It feels like everyone’s either overqualified and bored or enthusiastic but completely lacking the skills. It reminds me of trying to find volunteers for the school fete back when you were little.      You were  always  in charge of the fete. You organized everything! Remember Mrs. Peterson trying to sell those dodgy knitted owls?      Oh, goodness, yes. And she insisted they were ‘rustic chic.’ Honestly! It's funny the things you remember. Though, it's also unsettling how easily some people justify…portraying difference as something negative. I was thinking about that incident with young Jamie at school last year…      Jamie? The kid with the purple hair? People were being awful to him.      Exactly. It made me really angry. The casual discrimination, the assumptions…It’s things like that that make me question whether things have  really  changed as much as we think. It’s… disheartening.      It’s rubbish. It's like, why do people have to be mean just because someone is different?      Precisely. It’s something we need to actively tackle. And it’s not just with children, either. I had a very frustrating conversation with a senior colleague last week who…well, let's just say his views on certain things were antiquated and rather concerning.

Aye, this is proper good toast, lass. You’ve outdone yourself, you have. Not like that pale stuff they try to pass off in the university canteen.      Glad you like it, Bronwyn. It’s just a sourdough from the local bakery, nothing fancy. Though, honestly, after dealing with student essays all week, fancy is the last thing I need. Are you having another cuppa?      Don’t mind if I do. Strong, mind, strong as an ox. Thinking about New York… honestly, I still feel jet-lagged. It was fantastic, mind, absolutely fantastic. Seeing the lights… but flying, even in a big plane, does nothing for my nerves.      New York sounds incredible! I’ve always wanted to go. Though, the idea of  being  in a plane… well, let’s just say I prefer solid ground. You wouldn’t catch me doing those flying lessons Matthew’s been going on about.      Flying lessons! That man’s daft as a brush. He keeps sending me videos on Facebook, him wobbling about in a little Cessna. "Look at this, Bronwyn! Look at me, flying!" Honestly, it looks terrifying. He's going to end up as a news headline, I reckon. And that reminds me, have you seen what Susan posted on Instagram? Another picture of her prize-winning roses.      Oh, goodness, Susan and her roses. It’s a constant barrage, isn’t it? I saw it, yes. Beautiful, I suppose, but I try to limit my social media exposure these days. It's rather… draining. Remember when we first met in Japan? None of this nonsense. Just, you know,  life . Actual conversations.      Ay, Japan. Now  there  was a time. Proper clean it was, wasn't it? And the manners! You could set your watch by the bin collection. Everything had its place. Speaking of which, I need to remember to put my recycling out today. They're on a different schedule this week, apparently. A note landed on the door.      That’s the Swansea council for you. Always changing things around just to confuse everyone. I’ll remind you later, if you like. It's a bit of a nightmare if you miss it; they just leave it there for ages. What are your plans for today, once you’ve recovered from the jet lag and the sight of Matthew grinning from a cockpit?      Well, I thought I’d wander into town. Maybe browse the shops, have a look at the market.

Right… Q…U…A…K… Yes! On a triple word score. Take  that , Suffolk. Though honestly, the way you’ve blocked me with ‘Zebra’ is just… cruel.      Cruel but effective, darling. It’s called strategy. You should try it sometime instead of relying on lucky double-letter scores. Besides, you were the one who was rambling on about being late for everything this morning. Perhaps a bit of punctuality would free up brain space for Scrabble domination.      It wasn’t ‘rambling’! I was recounting a formative experience! Honestly, the bus in Cardiff is perpetually delayed. It’s a defining feature of living here. And it’s not my fault if Professor Davies is always starting seminars precisely on the hour, even though his office door clearly states ‘flexible timings’.      Flexible timings just means he’s perpetually late himself, doesn’t it? My old Head Chef used to say that about the suppliers. “Flexible delivery” just meant they’d rock up whenever they felt like it. Speaking of which, anyone fancy a refill? I’m heading up.      I’m good, thanks. Still trying to figure out how to use these vowels. Honestly, ‘queue’ is just…unfair. All those vowels jammed together. Where did that even  come  from?      It’s French, actually. From ‘coüe’. Then it got all anglicised and messed about with. It’s a classic example of how ridiculous English spelling is. I had to write an essay on etymology for my linguistics module. Honestly, it’s a wonder anyone can spell anything.      You and your linguistics! It's fascinating to you, I know, but I just want to win at Scrabble. Though, thinking about it, my grandma always used to say ‘que’ was derived from the sound a raven makes. Which, admittedly, is also slightly unhinged.      Your grandma sounds… colourful. Linguistics aside, how are the dissertations going, you two? Still wrestling with post-structuralism, Leo?      Wrestling is a polite word. I’m actively losing the fight. It feels like trying to hold smoke. It’s just…abstract. I miss A-Levels, honestly. At least with history, there were dates and facts. This is all just…interpretation.      Tell me about it. I’m doing a literature dissertation and I’m analysing picture books!  Picture books ! My parents keep asking when I’m going to get a “real” job.      Oh, don’t listen to them! Picture books are brilliant. What are you looking at?

Right comfortable this is, isn't it, Doreen? Rain batterin’ against the window, good brew… can't ask for much more, can ya?      Not a bit, Arthur. Absolutely lovely. Makes a change from that blasted sunshine we had all last week. Positively  scorching , it was. You’d think we were in Spain, not Norfolk.      Spain! Aye, I remember Spain. Blackpool it weren’t. Though, mind you, I’ve never been to Spain. Just see it on the telly. They all seem to be sunburnt and drinkin’ sangria. Looks a right carry-on.      It’s not all sangria and sunburn, Arthur. Though, I did see a programme once about a little village… looked very peaceful. Much too hot for me, though. I prefer a bit of a breeze. Reminds me of Harrow, actually, hills and everything. Not flat like… well, like here.      Harrow, eh? Didn’t you grow up near those fancy schools, up there? The ones where they teach the posh kids?      Oh, that Harrow School. Yes, just around the corner. Never went  near  it, mind. Couldn’t afford to. My dad, he worked at the biscuit factory. Lovely smell when the wind was right, though. Digestives, mostly.      A biscuit factory! Now that’s a proper job. Something you can  smell . Better than… well, better than nothin’, I suppose. My old man, he was a bit of a wanderer. Never stayed anywhere long enough to build up a proper trade, he didn't.      That's a shame, Arthur. Still, he kept a roof over your head, didn’t he? That’s the main thing. Though, I do worry about young Thomas. He’s been lookin’ a bit peaky lately. Said he's got a cough.      Thomas? Oh, that lad's always coughin’. Drama queen, that one. A bit of damp, that's all. Gets it from his mum, I reckon. Always fussin'. I tell ya what though, he can build a Lego castle like nobody's business.      Don’t be like that, Arthur! He is your grandson, after all. And he's a sensitive boy. He takes after his father, that way. Always thinking, always feeling.      Sensitive, eh? Sounds like a trouble waitin’ to happen. Still, good lad, I don’t doubt it. He’s been helpin’ me with the garden, bless ‘im. Though, he keeps tryin’ to plant those… what are they, those foreign things?      Sunflowers, Arthur. He wants to grow sunflowers.

Honestly, Dad, you've outdone yourself with this roast. The gravy is… heavenly. What's your secret? It doesn’t taste like anything from a packet.      Well, dear, there's no secret, really. Just good stock, a long, slow reduction, and a generous splash of Madeira. Something I learned from your grandmother, you know. She wouldn’t  dream  of using anything pre-made. Though, I’ll admit, it takes time. Something I've got a bit more of these days, thankfully.      Absolutely gorgeous. And the vegetables are perfectly al dente. You haven't lost your touch, despite retiring from… well, everything, basically. Are you keeping active though? You mentioned trying that new fitness app?      The app… it's… an experience. It’s called ‘StrideRight,’ apparently. Keeps telling me I need to hit 10,000 steps a day. 10,000! I barely manage 5,000 shuffling between the kitchen and the telly. It’s relentlessly cheerful, even when I’m failing miserably. Keeps sending me motivational quotes.      Oh, Dad! That sounds… intense. Maybe dial back the goal a bit? Small steps, literally?      Easier said than done, love. It’s having a detrimental effect on my biscuit consumption, I tell you. Speaking of detrimental things, have you two seen the latest on the Exmouth station? Another delay. Apparently, they've found unforeseen… geological issues.      Seriously? That’s the third delay now, isn't it? They promised it would be open by the summer. It’s going to be so disruptive to everyone. I rely on that line to get to Exeter for training.      It’s ridiculous. It’s just a short stretch of track, you’d think they could manage it. Old Man Hemmings at the shop was saying it's down to cost-cutting. They’re using cheaper materials and it’s causing problems.      I wouldn’t be surprised. Everything's about cutting corners these days. It’s a disgrace. Remember when they built the line out to Paignton? That was done properly, took a bit longer, yes, but it  lasted . These modern projects… built on sand, I tell you.      Still, it'll be good when it finally opens. It will really open up the area. It’s just… frustrating. I’m starting to think I’ll be retired before I can reliably commute by train from Exmouth.      Don't say that, Mum. It'll happen eventually. On a brighter note, did you two see that new Italian deli opened in town?

...Honestly, the seminar today was  painful . Professor Davies just kept circling back to Foucault without actually  saying  anything useful about the play. It was all abstract theory and no practical application. You’d think, studying Shakespeare, we'd actually  look  at Shakespeare, you know?      Tell me about it. Mine wasn't much better, thankfully not as… ethereal as Foucault, but it was all about post-colonial readings of  The Tempest . Which, fine, it's a valid angle, but when it's  all  you talk about for ninety minutes it feels a bit… forced. Did you catch that new Shakespeare adaptation on the BBC last week? The one with the modern setting?      The one with the hoodies and grime music? Yeah, I flicked through it. Looked a bit… much. I appreciate trying to make it accessible, but it felt like they were trying too hard to be ‘relevant.’ Like they didn’t trust the source material to stand on its own.      Exactly! It felt like they were screaming, “LOOK HOW MODERN AND IMPORTANT SHAKESPEARE IS!” rather than just letting the story speak for itself. Speaking of screaming, did you see the football on Saturday? Arsenal absolutely battered Bournemouth. 4-0.      Oh, I missed it. I was stuck revising. Heard it was a good game though. Saka was on fire, yeah? Honestly, I need to get back into watching more consistently. It's just… with uni work, it’s hard to find the time. Thinking about a stag do next month, though. Ben’s getting married, finally.      No way! Ben’s finally biting the bullet? Good on him. Where’s it going to be? Some kind of crazy weekend in Amsterdam, knowing him?      Worse. Bristol. Apparently, he wants ‘sophisticated fun.’ Which, knowing Ben, translates to a fancy cocktail bar, an escape room, and potentially a questionable amount of karaoke.      Oh, Bristol. That’s… surprisingly tame. Though, I've heard the bars down by the harbour are decent. I went once with a mate after a gaming convention. We were arguing about  Elden Ring  builds for hours.       Elden Ring ! Still addicted? I tried it, got absolutely destroyed by Margit, the Fell Omen, and threw the controller at the wall. It's not for me, too much frustration. I’m more of a  Civilisation  guy. Give me world domination through careful planning any day.      Haha, fair enough. Margit  is  a brick wall. You gotta respec your build, man.

...Honestly, the amount of passive-aggressive emails I’ve had to decipher this week is  criminal . Old Mr. Henderson thinks CC'ing the entire department on a request for a stapler is a productive management technique.      Oh, bless him. Sounds… delightful. You’re back in Cambridge full-time now, then? I feel like all I’ve seen of you for the last six months is fleeting glimpses at Christmas and then a rushed coffee when I was down visiting Mum.      Yep, officially Cambridge-based. Finished the project in London, thankfully. It was a good experience, but the commute was slowly eating my soul. It’s so much nicer being closer to everyone here. How was Mum's? Did your brother bring his… acquaintance?      Ugh, don't even. Liam brought  Chloe . The one who spends the entire time talking about her 'wellness journey' and trying to get everyone to drink kale smoothies. Mum was politely stifled, let's just say. I think she secretly wants to disown him sometimes. But yeah, it was good, got to see everyone, stuffed my face with Mum’s roast – worth braving Chloe for, honestly. How are your grandparents doing? Last I heard your nan was having trouble with her hip?      They’re… hanging in there. Nan’s hip is a saga. She's refusing to have the operation, says she's ‘too old for messing about’ which is classic Nan. Grandad’s trying to be all supportive, but I think he secretly just wants her to stop moaning about it! It's getting harder for them to manage, though. I've been trying to pop in more often.      That’s really sweet of you. It's hard watching them get older, isn’t it? My grandma's started forgetting things, little things, but it's scary. Speaking of scary, how's… well, how's Ben? Haven't heard anything since the… drama.      Oh, Ben. Don’t. Just… don’t. He's “finding himself” in Thailand, apparently. Posted a picture last week looking suspiciously zen next to a monkey. Turns out, ‘needing space’ meant ‘needing to backpack across Southeast Asia with a girl he met on Bumble’.      You are kidding?! Honestly, the audacity! I always thought he was a bit… flaky. Zen with a monkey, seriously? That’s a new level of cliché.      Right? I saw the girl's profile. Yoga instructor. It's like he actively tried to find the most Ben-compatible person possible.

Right, milk first for me, always. It's a North East thing, apparently. My gran would have a fit if I did it any other way. She’d say it 'spoils the flavour' if you put the tea in after. Honestly, the drama! Gran’s are always right, aren’t they? Even when they’re demonstrably…opinionated. Milk last for me, a staunch Midlands rebel. Though, to be fair, my mum never really had strong feelings about tea-making. She was more into getting a decent roast going. Speaking of which, how's your mum doing? Haven’t spoken to her properly in ages. She’s good, she’s good. Bit obsessed with her new orchids, actually. Keeps sending me pictures. They're…impressive, I’ll give her that. She's turned the conservatory into a miniature jungle. Says it's 'therapeutic'. I suspect it's just a good excuse to avoid doing the gardening. Remember her battle with the bindweed last summer? Nearly lost a finger. Oh,  that  bindweed! Yes! She was waging war. And didn’t she try to enlist  you  to help whilst you were visiting? I think you strategically developed a sudden allergy to pollen. A very convenient allergy, yes. Look, I’m a Research Manager, not a horticulturalist! Besides, I’m trying to keep my own little green corner alive here. See? It's…hanging in there. It's looking a bit peaky, to be honest. Like it’s contemplating an existential crisis. Are you even  watering  it? I am! Sort of. Okay, maybe not consistently enough. It's embarrassing, I can grow complex statistical models, but a herb?! It’s beyond me. How’s your chilli plant doing? You were so proud of that thing last autumn. Oh, the habanero? It's thriving, actually. A bit  too  thriving. I've got a mountain of chillies. I've made chilli oil, chilli jam, frozen them… I’m basically a chilli baron at this point. I might start blackmailing people with them. "Nice life you've got there, shame if something...spicy...were to happen to it." You're terrifying. You really are. You’re supposed to be a PhD student focusing on ancient history, not a supervillain with horticultural weaponry. Have you tried making that fermented chilli paste your mum likes? The gochujang-y one? I have! Tried and utterly failed. It was…a disaster. It smelled like something died.

…and honestly, Gareth, the marking is just relentless this year. It’s not the volume, it’s the sheer… lack of engagement with the material. They clearly just summarise Wikipedia articles. It's disheartening, really. How was your weekend, at least? Hopefully, a bit more stimulating than engaging with undergraduate essays?      You’re telling me! Similar story here, Alistair. Endless paraphrasing, zero original thought. My weekend  was  better, thank you. Managed to get out in the garden. Spent a good few hours wrestling with the roses. They’re being particularly stubborn this year, refusing to climb where I want them. A bit like some of my students, actually.      Roses, eh? I tried a vegetable patch a few years back. Utter disaster. Ended up with more slugs than produce. I stick to the odd potted geranium now. Low maintenance. Speaking of stubborn, did you see that young Rashford lad’s son getting into trouble again? The papers were full of it. Honestly, you'd think with the opportunities they have, these children would stay out of mischief.      Aye, saw something about that. It’s a shame, isn’t it? They’re growing up under such scrutiny. Still, it’s easy to judge. They’re just kids, after all. Reminds me a bit of when Ronnie O'Sullivan’s daughter was causing a bit of a stir. Public school and a famous father won't shield you from life's bumps, eh? It's a different world to how we were brought up, growing up in Tredegar.      Absolutely. My own upbringing in Cairo was, shall we say, considerably less… sheltered. My father expected a certain level of resilience, let’s put it that way. Though, even he’d be shocked by some of the entitlement I see now. It’s all a bit soft, I think. Though, it got me thinking… the recruitment standards for the police and the armed forces must be incredibly high these days. They need individuals with a degree of… grit.      They do, indeed. My nephew, Rhys, was toying with the idea of joining the Royal Marines. Bright lad, very fit. But the process... it's brutal. He said they're looking for mental fortitude as much as physical capability. Apparently, they’re seeing fewer and fewer applicants who can actually handle it. They're competing with university offers and easier career paths.      It's a tragedy if we lose that pool of potential.

Honestly, this week has been… something. Mr. Henderson is driving me round the bend at work. He keeps changing his mind about the presentation, wants it  completely  different every time I finish a draft. It’s exhausting.      Is Mr. Henderson a dinosaur? Because dinosaurs are  very  changeable. They went extinct, didn’t they? Ms. Davies told us at school.      Sounds more like a T-Rex with a project management issue, honestly. You need to learn to just… manage  him , Mum. Set boundaries.      Boundaries? With Henderson? That’s a laugh. He  is  the boundary. It’s all “urgent” and “vital” and then he ignores it for three days! Anyway, let’s not talk about work. It’s depressing. We need to focus on something nicer. Like Poppy’s Christening. Are we still good for the 12th?      Yep, I’ve booked the train ticket. Bit pricey, but I wouldn’t miss it. Manchester to Lichfield is a killer on the bank account though. Are you sure the church is definitely confirmed?      Absolutely. Reverend Thompson is booked. And I've tentatively booked The Plough for after, for a little buffet. Nothing too fancy, just sandwiches and cake mostly. Your Dad’s already volunteered to tackle the sausage rolls, God help us all.      Sausage rolls are the BEST! Can I help make them? I can put the sausages inside!      You can absolutely help. You’re a very good sausage-roller-inner, my love. Though maybe not  all  of them, eh? We don’t want a pastry-based disaster.      Speaking of disasters, have we finalised the guest list? Grandma wants to invite half of Birmingham, and I'm pretty sure Uncle Barry and Auntie Carol are still feuding. That'll be cheerful.      Oh, don’t even start me on the family dynamics. I’ve had a quiet word with your Grandma. She’s agreed to be… selective. As for Barry and Carol… I’m hoping enough cake will distract them. It's Poppy's special day; we need to keep things civil.      Can we have a rainbow cake? Poppy loves rainbows! And sprinkles! LOTS of sprinkles!      A rainbow cake it is! With a mountain of sprinkles. I've already ordered it from that lovely bakery in town. They do amazing work. We also need to think about her outfit. I found a beautiful little lace dress, but I’m not sure if it’s warm enough.

Honestly, this week has just  flown  by. It feels like Monday was yesterday. How are things at the shop, love? Still battling the Black Friday early birds?      You have no idea. It's been…intense. People are already trying to ‘scope out’ the deals, marking things they want. I spent half of yesterday untangling a display someone had completely dismantled looking for discounted fairy lights. Fairy lights in  October !      Fairy lights! Can we put fairy lights up in my room, please? Pretty, sparkly ones?      We’ll see, sweetheart. Perhaps a little closer to Christmas. Right now, we're trying to plan something a bit more…ambitious. Remember we were talking about New York?      Oh, New York! Yes! I was looking at flights last night, actually. It's going to be pricey, isn’t it? Especially around Christmas. I found a few that weren't  terrible , but even with those, accommodation is…ouch.      Exactly. That’s what I’m worried about. I was thinking maybe spring? Avoid the worst of the cold and the Christmas rush, potentially find slightly better deals? Although, New York at Christmas  does  sound magical… Remember that trip to Venice we did over New Year’s?      Oh, Venice! That was… chaos, but amazing chaos. All those tiny bridges, getting completely lost, eating pasta for every meal.      Was Venice full of gondolas? I want to ride in a gondola!      It was, darling. Lots and lots of gondolas. We'll have to add that to the list. But back to New York. I’d really like to see a Broadway show. And we  have  to go to Central Park. I saw a photo online of it covered in snow and it was breathtaking.      A show sounds good. And maybe one of those fancy afternoon teas? I saw a video of one with tiered stands full of tiny sandwiches and cakes… It looked incredible. Though, knowing us, we’d probably spend most of the time trying to figure out how to get around on the subway.      Probably! We’re notoriously bad with public transport. Remember getting completely turned around in Paris trying to find the Eiffel Tower? We walked for miles!      Was the Eiffel Tower sparkly?      Very sparkly, poppet! It lights up at night. We took a boat trip on the Seine. It was lovely.      It was, wasn’t it? Speaking of lovely, your wedding photos look amazing framed, by the way.

Right, so this… this is the catastrophe. Honestly, I think my methodology section is actively trying to sabotage my chances of graduating.      Catastrophe seems a bit strong, doesn’t it? It's just a bit of paperwork, innit? What’s the issue? I thought you were pretty confident with the quantitative side of things.      Confident is a strong word. Competent, maybe. But  explaining  it to someone who isn't neck-deep in statistical modelling… that's a different beast entirely. See, I’ve run the regressions, I’ve got the significance levels, the R-squared is… well, it’s alright. But when I try to  write  it up, it sounds like I’m making it up as I go along. And I  swear  I'm not.      Okay, okay. Deep breaths. Let's just pick it apart. What specifically feels clumsy? Is it the jargon? You know, sometimes we get so used to the terminology, we forget not everyone speaks fluent ‘stats’ as a second language.      That's a huge part of it, yeah. I’ve already toned down some of the more… ambitious phrasing, but it still feels dense. Like, look at this sentence . “Utilising a multivariate regression framework, exogenous variables were assessed for their influence on the dependent variable, controlling for potential confounding factors.” It sounds like a robot wrote it!      Okay, that  is  a bit robotic. Try… “I used a regression model to see how different factors affected the results, while taking into account other things that could have influenced them.” See? Totally different vibe. More… human.      Huh. Yeah, that’s… considerably better. It doesn’t sound like I’m trying to impress anyone with my vocabulary. But then it feels… dumbed down? Is it still academically rigorous if I say things like that?      Rigorous doesn’t equal impenetrable, mate. Honestly, a marker wants to see you understand the  concept , not how many polysyllabic words you can string together. Plus, clarity shows understanding. Think about it—if you can explain it simply, you clearly  get  it.      That’s a good point. It’s just… Professor Davies is notoriously picky. He once marked down someone for using the word ‘very’. Apparently, it lacks precision.      Oh,  that's  ridiculous. Sounds like someone who enjoys power a bit too much. Anyway, back to your methodology. What are the biggest things you're worried about explaining? Beyond the language, is there anything technically shaky?

...Honestly, the weirdest bit was the spreadsheets. Giant, floating spreadsheets, chasing me through a garden made of biscuits. Biscuits, of all things! And I  had  to balance them, apparently, or the whole thing would collapse.      That  is  properly bizarre, Ben. You and your work brain, even when you’re asleep. Though, a biscuit garden…that sounds oddly appealing. At least it smells nice.      Can we  have  a biscuit garden?      No, silly! Biscuits get all crumbly and sticky. It'd be a mess!      Probably. Though a spreadsheet collapse sounds messier. Anyway, what about you, Chloe? Any colourful adventures in dreamland last night?      Actually, yes. Not as chaotic as yours, thankfully. I was giving a lesson… but to a class full of puppies. Tiny little golden retrievers, all trying to write essays. It was incredibly stressful trying to keep them focused. And one kept eating the pens.      Puppies! We  need  a puppy!      We’ve been over this, Leo. Your mother and I have discussed it. It's a big responsibility.      But a puppy would be  so  good! It could sleep at the end of my bed!      They are awfully sweet, aren't they? I keep scrolling through rescue websites. It's just… finding the right one, with the right temperament for the kids. And with both of us working…      Exactly. Logistics are a nightmare. Although, if I won the lottery… that'd solve a lot of problems, wouldn't it? We could hire someone to look after a dog, buy a bigger house with a proper garden…      Always back to the lottery, Ben? You've been buying tickets religiously since that big rollover last month.      Well, a man can dream, can’t he? And imagine! No more chasing spreadsheets, I could finally learn to properly play the guitar. You could take a sabbatical and write that children’s book you've always talked about. We could finally get a Labrador!      A Labrador! A big, bouncy one!      With floppy ears!      Okay, stop. You’re both getting carried away. The chances of winning are astronomically small.      You never know! My grandad always said, "You have to be in it to win it." And he was a very wise man. Although he also believed in leprechauns…      That’s reassuring. Still, realistically, a puppy is a long way off. Maybe when they’re a bit older, more self-sufficient.      But I’m  almost  self-sufficient! I can tie my shoes! .

...Honestly, the waiting room was  packed . You wouldn’t believe it. And the smell. Like disinfectant and despair, all mixed together.      Ugh, A&E. Never a pleasant experience, is it? Even just visiting someone. What happened, anyway? You were pretty quiet on the drive over, just saying you’d “had a mishap.” A mishap sounds…understated for needing a hospital visit.      Mishap was being generous, to be fair. I was trying to be stoic. It was the shelf, you see. The one in the utility room. I was reaching for the bleach…and it just…came away from the wall. Took the whole lot with it. Bleach, cleaning supplies, and me, under a cascade of particleboard and tins of polish.      Right. Okay. So…you weren’t, like, trying to dismantle a shelf with your bare hands? Because that would be a slightly different story.      No, absolutely not! Just trying to clean! Honestly, it was like something out of a cartoon. Everything just… crashed. Landed right on my foot.      Ouch. That sounds awful. Did they x-ray it? Is it broken? You’re limping a bit even now.      X-rayed it, yep. They said it’s not  broken  broken, thankfully. Just badly sprained, and a bit bruised. They gave me a support to wear, and told me to elevate it and ice it. The doctor said I was lucky it wasn’t worse. Honestly, looking at the size of the shelf, I think I  was  lucky. It could’ve been my head!      Good lord. You’re right, that could have been…much worse. Seriously, you need to be more careful. You always were a bit of a klutz. Remember that time you tried to hang fairy lights and ended up tangled in them, looking like a Christmas tree yourself?      Don’t remind me! That was mortifying. But this was different, it was a proper structural failure! The shelf was clearly dodgy. I'd been meaning to get your dad to look at it for ages. Said he was good with that kind of thing.      He is. He'd have seen that coming a mile off. He's obsessed with load-bearing capacity. We’ll get him over on Sunday, he’ll have a good look and reinforce everything. Though he'll probably give you a lecture about DIY safety.      I deserve it, honestly. And the worst part? After all  that , the A&E doctor just kept asking me if I was up to date with my tetanus jab.

...Honestly, Harold, the price of tomatoes these days! It’s criminal. Used to be able to get a decent punnet for a pound, now it's nearly three. Makes you think twice about a salad, doesn’t it?      Tell me about it, Arthur. Everything’s gone up. Fuel, electricity… it's a right squeeze, even for me, and I own the blasted shop! Though, thankfully, the bakery’s doing alright. People  always  need bread, eh? Though even flour prices fluctuated something fierce there for a bit.      Always the practical one, you are. Bakery’s a good solid business. Speaking of businesses though… I’ve been rattling around with an idea. A rather silly one, probably.      Oh? Don't be shy, let's hear it. After all these years, I'm used to your ‘silly’ ideas. Half the time they turn out to be surprisingly sensible. Remember the birdhouse venture?      That  was  a bit of a disaster, wasn't it? Too many blue tits, not enough demand. This is… different. It's about tutoring, but not the usual GCSE stuff. Language exchange. Online, mostly.      Language exchange? You mean, pairing up people who want to learn each other’s languages? That's… actually quite clever. There's a lot of that going on already, isn't there, with apps and websites?      There is, but a lot of it feels… impersonal. I was thinking of a curated experience, small groups, focusing on conversational skills, cultural nuances. I've got a few contacts from my teaching days. Germans, French, even a chap from Japan. I could build a network. And, crucially, offer some actual  teaching  alongside the exchange. Correcting grammar, helping with pronunciation…      Hmm. Interesting. You’d need to think about marketing, of course. And insurance, all that. Running a business isn’t just about the idea, Arthur, it’s the admin. You know me, I’ve learned that the hard way with the bakery. Council regulations alone!      I’m aware of the paperwork, Harold. It’s the initial setup that’s daunting. I wouldn't want to sink a lot of money into it before knowing if there’s a market. I was thinking of starting small, running a couple of pilot sessions, free of charge to friends and their friends. See how it goes.      That’s sensible. Very sensible. You wouldn’t need a fancy website to start. Social media, a simple landing page…

...Honestly, the floral wallpaper in here is a bit… much, isn’t it? It's like my Nan's living room. Though, it  is  warmer than I expected, considering it's a Guardhouse. I thought it'd be all dark wood and stern looks.      You’re never one for floral, are you? No, it’s a bit much. Bit oppressive. But it’s Woolwich, not Hampstead. Expect a certain… robustness. Besides, it’s a nice change from the sterile environments we usually find ourselves in, eh? What are you thinking food-wise? They do a decent-looking pie menu.      A pie does sound good, actually. I’m starving. Though, remembering that slightly dodgy steak and ale pie from The Crown last month is putting me off a bit. Maybe something simpler? Sausage and mash? Or a jacket potato?      Sausage and mash is a solid choice. Can’t go wrong with that. I’m leaning towards the pie too, though. Going to be brave and risk it. Speaking of risks, have you seen the latest  Happy Valley ? Absolutely gripping. Sarah Lancashire is phenomenal.      Oh my god,  Happy Valley ! Yes! I’m only two episodes behind, I’ve been meaning to catch up. Everyone at work is talking about it. Apparently, it gets  really  dark. I’m bracing myself. Though, honestly, after transcribing medical legal reports all day, ‘dark’ is pretty much my baseline.      Fair point. You're immune to darkness! It's just so well-written, though. And the setting, those bleak Yorkshire landscapes… it just adds to the atmosphere. Reminds me a bit of when we went to visit your aunt in the Dales, all those windswept hills.      Oh, don’t remind me. And your coat! You insisted on wearing that ridiculously bright orange one. It was like a beacon for sheep.      Hey! It was practical. Waterproof! And it kept me warm. Besides, you were the one who packed the luminous pink walking boots. We were a stylish pair, attracting all the local wildlife.      Touché. Still, I maintain it was a fashion disaster. Remember university? The outfits we wore... questionable decisions all round.      Oh god, don't even go there. My paisley shirts... truly awful. And your phase with the ridiculously oversized jumpers. It was the 90s, we can't be held accountable. What are they playing now? Some sort of indie thing, isn’t it?      It is. Quite loud, actually.

Ach, look at that. Typical. Thought we might get a wee break today, but naw. Makes ye miss bein’ somewhere… warmer, aye?      You and everyone else, Hamish. Though, to be fair, even  I’m  starting to feel the pull of somewhere with consistent sunshine. You were saying the other day about that trip you took to Iceland? How was the photography up there?      Aye, Iceland. Different planet entirely. Photos don’t even  do  it justice, honestly. The light…it’s just… ethereal. I spent a full day tryin' to capture the Northern Lights, standin’ oot in freezin’ temperatures, fingers numb. Worth every second, though. Got a shot I’m really proud of – a green swirl over the Kirkjufell mountain.      Kirkjufell… beautiful spot. I’ve seen some stunning images from there. You’ve really become quite the photographer, you know. Remember when you were usin’ that wee point-and-shoot on holiday and complainin' about blurry pictures of scenery?      Dinnae remind me! That was a disaster. My Aunt Maggie still has a framed one of that blurry Loch Ness monster picture. Says it's ‘atmospheric’. Honestly, it's embarrassment embodied. I started takin’ it a bit more seriously after that, though. Started watchin’ some online tutorials, investin’ in proper gear. Then, well, it just sort of took off. It's a good escape, aye? Beats watchin' the telly.      It’s more than just an escape, Hamish, it’s a genuine talent. You have an eye for composition, for light. It’s quite impressive, especially given you’re self-taught. I’ve always admired people who can pick up a skill like that. My attempts at watercolour painting ended in… well, let’s just say they resemble abstract messes.      Ah, ye’re too kind. It’s just pointin’ and clickin’, mostly. Although, the amount of time spent editin' the photos on the computer… that’s a different story. It's a rabbit hole, honestly. You start adjustin’ one thing, then another, then another… hours disappear.      I can imagine. It's the same with research, really. You start looking into one small aspect of a topic and six hours later you’ve uncovered a completely unrelated but fascinating piece of information. Speaking of travel, you mentioned Iceland - any other places on the list currently? Anywhere callin’ to ye?      Been lookin’ at Patagonia. The landscapes look incredible. Rugged mountains, glaciers… another photographer’s paradise, I reckon.

Honestly, this week is already feeling…full. It's just one thing after another, isn’t it? How are things at school, love? Any particularly delightful five-year-olds causing chaos?      You know it! Little Leo decided today that painting wasn't about  on  the paper, but  with  the paper. Covered himself, covered Millie, nearly covered me. It was…an experience. But yes, school’s good. Exhausting, but good. How about you? Anything beyond the usual whirlwind?      The usual, yes. Trying to juggle everything. I finally got a call back about the nursery places, though. They’ve offered us a spot at Little Acorns, but it's…three days a week. Three! I was hoping for five, especially with me potentially starting that freelance project.      Oh, mum! That  is  a pain. Little Acorns is lovely, apparently, Mrs. Davies raves about it, but three days isn’t ideal, is it? Especially if you're thinking about taking on extra work. So, what are you going to do?      I don’t know. I’ve put my name down for the waiting list for five days, naturally, but they said it could be months. And honestly, the thought of trying to manage work  and  a baby full-time… it’s daunting. Your Dad keeps saying I need to slow down, but that's easier said than done, isn't it?      Dad always says that! He worries, that’s all. You thrive on being busy, that’s just you. But honestly, he’s right to an extent. You do take on too much sometimes. Perhaps you could put the project on hold for a bit?      I'd like to, I really would. It’s a good opportunity, a chance to get back into…well,  something  that's just for me. But the money would really help. The nursery fees alone are frightening.      They are. Have you looked at the new government scheme for childcare costs? I read something about it online, could be worth checking. It might help offset some of it.      I’ve skimmed something about it, yes. I need to properly look into the details. It probably involves filling out approximately seventeen forms in triplicate, knowing my luck. Speaking of which, what have  you  got planned for the week? Just surviving Leo’s artistic outbursts?      Mostly! I'm meeting Chloe on Wednesday for a coffee, trying to reclaim some semblance of a social life.

This is proper good, ANON. Seriously, you’ve outdone yourself. Reminds me a bit of my nan’s lasagne, but with, like, actual finesse.      Yeah, it’s miles better than what I usually get. Usually it’s a pot noodle if I’m being honest. Work's been… hectic. Long hours, you know? Least I can afford a decent takeaway now and then.      Oh, don't we all love a good pot noodle emergency. Though, ANON's cooking is a definite upgrade. So, Liam, how  is  work? Still building sites in the freezing cold?      Pretty much. Just finished up a new block of flats over by Milton. Brutal weather last week, wind was nearly blowing the scaffolding over. Then it was back to a house extension, all muddy boots and grumpy homeowners.      Ooh, sounds… fun? Not exactly glamorous, is it? I mean, I'm at a conference centre, so it's  slightly  less physical. Though dealing with delegates who think they’re royalty can be a workout in itself.      Tell me about it! I had a supplier last week who insisted his presentation needed a specific shade of purple lighting. Specific shade! Like I'm a lighting technician and not a production controller managing a million other things. Honestly, the entitlement…      Exactly! It's exhausting. It’s not even the work itself, it’s the  people . At least you're building things, Liam. Something tangible at the end of the day. I'm just moving chairs and making sure the biscuits are replenished.      Don't sell yourself short, Elsie. Organising things properly is a skill, innit? It’s more than just biscuits. And someone's gotta do it. Besides, you get to wear nice clothes for work, don’t you? I’m stuck in hi-vis and steel toe caps. Glamorous.      It’s not  always  glam, believe me. This dress is from Primark, so not exactly designer. Though I did splash out on some decent boots last month, 'cause I’m on my feet all day. Found 'em in a sale. You should see the state of 'em now though... covered in conference hall carpet fluff.      Oh, I know the struggle. I have a 'work' wardrobe and a 'life' wardrobe, and they rarely intersect. Though, speaking of clothes, I've been trying to find a decent winter coat. Everything is either ridiculously expensive or completely shapeless.      You should check out the market in town, Ella.

Now, this is… alright. Not quite like Mabel used to make it, mind you. She always had a knack for getting the strength just right. Not too weak, not too strong. Just… perfect.      Oh, Arthur, you always say that about everyone’s tea! You've a right picky palate, you 'ave. It’s perfectly good tea, isn’t it, Harold? Don’t listen to him, dear. He’d complain if it was served to him on a silver platter.      I think there’s a little truth in both of you. It  is  a decent cuppa, Margaret, but Arthur does have a point about Mabel’s. It was…remarkable. She always insisted on using loose leaf, remember? Said the bags just didn't have the flavour.      Loose leaf is definitely superior. I always encouraged my students to appreciate the ritual of it, even if they were just having a quick brew in the staffroom. There’s something… calming about watching the leaves unfurl. Although, frankly, these days I’m happy with a quick bag myself. Less washing up!      Washing up! That’s what Mabel always said. "Arthur," she’d say, “You wash, I brew.” A simple arrangement, that was. Kept the peace. I used to grumble, o'course, but I didn’t mind that much. She knew I wouldn't do it right anyway. Always leave streaks on the glasses, I do.      You and your streaks, Arthur! It's a family legend. My Nan was the same, wouldn’t let anyone near her china, said they’d ruin it. Though she was more worried about chips than streaks, I suppose. This reminds me, I had Mrs. Peterson round yesterday, for a little chat. She was going on about her grandson, off to university… wants to study… what was it… astrophysics?      Astrophysics! Goodness me. That’s a far cry from when I started teaching. Mostly it was aspiring accountants and teachers. A few shopkeepers. Not many aiming for the stars, so to speak. Though I did have a student who went on to do quite well in… I can’t quite recall the field now. Something to do with computers, I think. Before my time, really.      It's amazing how things have changed, isn't it? When I started teaching, we were still using overhead projectors! Now they’ve all got interactive whiteboards and tablets. My granddaughter, bless her, teaches coding to seven-year-olds.

Honestly, these are  divine , Mum. You’ve outdone yourself. Honestly, I think these are better than even The White Hart’s roasties, and that’s saying something!      Oh, you always say that, Lizzie! It's just good Norfolk spuds, that’s all. Though, I did parboil them in slightly salted water this time, makes all the difference. Speaking of The White Hart, did you hear they’re having that live band on Friday? Might be worth a trip.      Mmm, good spuds. And yeah, I saw that on their Facebook. Bit loud for me, probably. I’m more of a quiet pint kind of guy these days. Especially after… well, you know. That protest in London last weekend was  loud .      Don’t remind me. The news was full of it. Honestly, the sheer volume of people… did you manage to avoid getting caught in the worst of it, Rhys?      Oh, I wasn’t  in  it, thankfully. My sister, Nia, she’s a bit of an activist, she was down there. She said it was…intense. Apparently, a lot of police presence. She sent me photos, looked like something out of a film.      Intense is an understatement, from what I saw online. It's just... exhausting, isn’t it? All the constant everything happening. Trying to explain it all to the students is a challenge. I had one ask me yesterday why people protest. Like, genuinely didn’t understand.      Good luck with that one! It’s a complex issue. Though, I’ve got a simpler battle on my hands at work. Trying to get everyone’s CRB checks sorted for the new training programme. Such a palaver. People dragging their heels, forgetting forms… It’s like herding cats.      CRB checks… brings back memories. Remember when we were discussing them for little Leo’s nursery? Suddenly everyone had an opinion on everything…       Oh god , don’t. That ended up being a whole thing with Uncle George and his… views. Specifically on whether or not Leo should be… y’know.      Right, let’s not go there. That was a very sensitive discussion, and frankly, I'm still recovering. It's not something we need to revisit over Sunday roast.      Yeah, let’s keep it light. Talking of sensitive… I was chatting to a mate, Dave, down the pub last week, and he was telling me about this hotel he stayed in. Apparently, the décor was all… abstract art.

Oh, you're back! Didn’t hear you come in. How was the flight? Did you manage to snag any duty-free chocolate? Because honestly, I’m running dangerously low.      Ugh, the flight was…a flight. Packed, delayed an hour, and the guy next to me kept talking about his prize-winning begonias. No chocolate, sadly. I was too exhausted to navigate the duty-free chaos. But I  did  bring you back something. It’s in my bag, a little something from Cornwall.      Begonias?! Oh, the horror. Still, a Cornish something sounds amazing. I’ve missed having someone to properly moan to about work with. It's been absolute mayhem since you left. Old Mr. Henderson decided  now  was the time to ‘restructure’ everything, which basically means more work for everyone.      Oh, Henderson. Predictable. Still at it then? Sounds like you've been holding the fort admirably. How bad is ‘mayhem’ on a scale of one to needing a full-body detox?      Solid eight, I’d say. And on top of that, I ran into Liam at the supermarket yesterday.      Liam?  The  Liam? Oh god. That’s…a lot to process before even having caffeine. How did  that  go? Please tell me you weren’t forced to make small talk about beige wallpaper and his dad’s garden gnomes.      You know me too well. It was exactly that. And he asked about…you. Asked if we were still friends. Honestly, the audacity! I just mumbled something about needing to find organic kale and practically ran away. He's dating Bethany from accounts now, apparently. Bethany! The one who wears those aggressively bright pink suits.      Oh, bless Bethany. Bold choices. Good on you for escaping. Liam always did have questionable taste. Anyway, enough about him. Tell me about…everything. Did you go out with anyone while I was gone? Did you finally manage to finish that book?      Aside from surviving Henderson, not much excitement. I did binge-watch that ridiculous baking show everyone’s talking about, and I attempted a sourdough starter. Key word: attempted. It currently resembles something closer to cement than bread. And no dates. Honestly, the thought of swiping right on anyone feels exhausting.      Sourdough is a commitment, you’re right. It's basically another child. And I get the dating fatigue. It’s brutal out there. Work has been…intense. We had a really difficult case last week, a teenager who...

...Honestly, the way she talked about the new immunotherapy trial, it sounded… hopeful, but also exhausting. Like it’s a massive undertaking, even  if  it works. She’s always been so pragmatic, you know? Never one for false optimism. That makes it even harder to gauge how she’s genuinely feeling.      She is. And she’ll downplay everything, won’t she? Always has. Remember when she broke her arm skiing and insisted it was “just a bit of a tweak”? She was in a cast for three months! I think we need to just… listen for what  isn’t  being said, as much as what is. Did she mention how John is coping? He seems like he’s taking it so hard, the poor bloke.      He is. She said he’s been utterly useless around the house, completely frozen. Apparently, he just sits and watches documentaries about space. She was trying to be funny about it, but you could hear the frustration. It’s like he’s retreated to another planet to avoid dealing with it. Poor things. It just puts everything into perspective, doesn't it? All this fussing about house prices...      Absolutely. Which brings me back to the village. I had another look at that cottage on Mill Lane. The one we talked about, with the overgrown garden. Still listed, surprisingly. They’ve dropped the price a little, too.      Oh really? That’s… interesting. I thought it would have gone quickly. It’s a sweet little thing, wouldn’t you agree? Very ‘chocolate box’ as they say. But I still worry about the garden. Remember what Mrs. Higgins said about the flooding in the winter?      I did. And that is a concern, definitely. But the estate agent said the current owners have put in some drainage, apparently. It might not be a perfect fix, but it’s something. Plus, think about it – a proper project for you! You’d absolutely transform that garden.      Don't tempt me. I’m already picturing climbing roses and a vegetable patch. It’s just… it feels like a big step. Especially when everything feels so uncertain with Sarah. Moving further away could make it harder to pop in and help.      We wouldn't be  that  far. It's still only a twenty-minute drive, and the train link is decent. And honestly, I think a bit of a change of scenery would do us good.

Right, I need a vent. Honestly, this job… it's alright, pays the bills, but some students… Honestly, Sarah, some students.      Oh? Lay it on me, Mark. Long day? I’ve had a couple of noise complaints already and it’s barely past two. A “rave” in 203, apparently.      Raves? Aye, that’s classic. No, well, it's not even the parties, though they’re a pain. It's the  entitlement . They treat this place like a hotel, innit? “My heating's not warm enough,” “My shower’s only lukewarm,” “Can you get Deliveroo to bring my food  to  my room?” Like, seriously? I'm a security officer, not a concierge.      Tell me about it. I had one lad last week demanding I write a letter to his lecturer explaining why he was late to a seminar because his avocado toast wasn’t “Instagrammable.” An actual request.      You’re joking! Avocado toast? That’s a new level, even for Salford Uni students. It’s just… they've never had to fend for themselves, have they? Mum and Dad have always sorted everything. They think life just  works  like that.      It’s the helicopter parenting, I reckon. They've been shielded from any kind of inconvenience their whole lives. It makes even minor issues feel catastrophic to them. I spent an hour yesterday helping a girl find her lost phone charger. She was practically in tears.      An hour! I had a bloke complain the vending machine ate his pound coin. A  pound coin . I told him to contact the vending machine company, and he looked at me like I'd suggested he climb Mount Everest. I swear, the level of basic life skills is dwindling. What do they teach them at school these days?      Rhetorical question, I assume? I’ve noticed it too. It's not just the practical stuff, it's the common courtesy. No "please" or "thank you," leaving the communal kitchen looking like a bomb site… I spend half my week reminding people to wash up their dishes.      Oh, the kitchens! Don’t get me started on the kitchens. It’s a biohazard most days. They leave mouldy food festering, dirty pots piled up… It’s disgusting. And then they complain about the smell! It's like, look at what  you've  created.      It's exhausting trying to enforce basic cleanliness. I’ve sent out so many emails about kitchen etiquette, I’m starting to feel like a nag.

…and honestly, the sheer  number  of Brits in Barcelona was just… startling. Like a takeover. You couldn't move for someone asking for a full English breakfast. It wasn’t even peak season!      Oh, you get that everywhere, love. Always have. Used to be Majorca, then the Costa Brava… now it’s all Barcelona and Prague. It’s the package tour boom, isn’t it? Makes it easy for people. No fuss.      Easy, but… a bit sad, isn't it? I mean, you go to experience a different culture, not just hang out with people from Basildon. Remember Mrs. Higgins telling us about her Christmas market tour? She said it was full of people complaining the sausages weren’t like Tesco’s!      Oh,  god . Typical. Though, I do get the appeal of a Christmas market. I was thinking about Antwerp this year. They’re supposed to be amazing. Bit further afield, though.      Antwerp, eh? Sounds expensive. Not for me, that’s for sure. Retired life isn’t all it’s cracked up to be when it comes to funds, you know. Though, it’s definitely better than battling the London traffic every morning. Used to take me an hour just to get into the city centre, and for what? Stress.      You’re lucky you didn’t have to drive, Dad. At least you could read or something on the tube. I’m stuck in and out of Essex all day, and the A12 is a nightmare. Honestly, sometimes I think I spend half my life in stationary traffic.      It's awful. Mum, you’ve got the best of both worlds now, though. You can pop into Herne Bay whenever you fancy for a bit of shopping.      That’s true, bits and pieces. But even Herne Bay is getting overrun with tourists now! It's not the quiet seaside town it used to be. I was trying to get some Christmas presents last week and it was rammed. It’s all those Londoners escaping the city, I reckon.      It’s the world shrinking, isn’t it? Used to feel like going abroad was a real  event . Now it’s like popping to the shops. Speaking of Christmas, have you started your shopping yet, Poppy?      Not really. I’m trying to not think about it. It feels so soon. Also, my uni cohort are all doing Secret Santa, and finding something decent for £10 is… challenging.

...Honestly, Mum, I still don’t  get  it. Why is everyone making such a fuss about this equality vote? Like, isn't everyone already equal? It feels a bit… pointlessly complicated. Mr. Davies in History tried to explain it, but honestly, it just went over my head. Something about amending the constitution?      Oh, love. It’s…it’s not about whether everyone  is  equal, it’s about making sure the law  says  everyone is equal. Right now, the constitution doesn't properly recognise care work, or work traditionally done by women, as valuable work that deserves the same protections as, say, paid employment. And it impacts things like divorce settlements, access to social welfare… all sorts of things.      Divorce settlements? That's a bit heavy for a school debate, isn't it? I thought we were just talking about…rights.      It  is  heavy. But it all connects. Think about it – for ages, women were just expected to look after the home and kids, and that wasn’t seen as earning a living. This vote is about finally recognising that  that  work is important too. It's about making sure if someone dedicates their life to caring for family, they aren’t left with nothing if things go wrong.      Right. Okay. So, like, if Grandma had stayed with Grandad, and he’d… you know… messed things up, she’d be better protected now?      Possibly. Though, honestly, knowing your Grandma, she'd have sorted Grandad out regardless. She was a force of nature. Remember that time she told Mrs. Higgins her prize-winning roses looked a bit peaky?      Oh God, yeah! Mrs. Higgins didn’t speak to her for a month! Grandma had no filter. She was brilliant. But still… it sounds like a really complicated change for something that should just…  be .      It is. Irish politics is…peculiar. They're amending the constitution twice, actually, one about care and one about family. It’s all a bit messy, and there are people campaigning against it, saying it’s too broad, or will create other problems.      People are always finding something to moan about. Speaking of things to moan about, have you booked Old Man Hemmings’ hall for my birthday party yet? I want to make sure it’s free. It's the only place big enough for  everyone  I want to invite.      "Everyone" being the entire year group plus half the rugby team?

There you go, Arthur. Egg mayo, just how you like it. Though honestly, looking at you, I’m surprised you’ve still got an appetite after that story you were telling. A hamster…in the microwave?!      Well, don't look at me like that, Margaret. Wasn’t  me  put ‘im in there, mind. Old Mr. Henderson’s grandson, little Timmy. A right handful, that boy. Always fiddling. Anyway, he thought it’d be a good idea to give Hammy a ‘warm-up’ on a cold day. Honestly, the things children get up to. Poor Hammy didn't stand a chance, bless 'im.      Good Lord. That is…disturbing, Arthur. Absolutely disturbing. You'd think common sense would prevail, even with a six-year-old. Though knowing Timmy, common sense wasn’t exactly his strong suit. Remember the time he tried to paint the cat blue?      Oh, don't  start  on that again, David! Poor Clementine was traumatized for weeks. And the smell! Turquoise cat, honestly. Still, a hamster in the microwave…that takes the biscuit. I'm just picturing the poor little thing.      It were awful. Mr. Henderson was distraught. Said Hammy was a particularly good hamster, knew ‘is name and everything. Anyway, it got me thinking about tools, strangely enough. Precision. You need precision with tools, don't you? Like with my lathe tools.      Precision is everything, Arthur. Absolutely. In my line of work reviewing curriculum, it's all about precise assessment, clear objectives. It’s not unlike turning a piece of wood, really. One wrong move and you’ve ruined the whole thing. Speaking of which, how's that birdhouse coming along? You were working on it last week.      Slow, David, slow. I’m having trouble with the parting tool. Keep nicking it, and then the whole thing goes skew-whiff. I think I need a different steel. Something a bit harder. Got to get one from that fella down in Norwich, old man Withers. Knows his stuff, he does. Though his prices are a bit…sharp, let's say.      You and your lathe, Arthur. It's a lovely hobby, but you fuss over it so much. Honestly, it's more trouble than it's worth sometimes. I'd rather be knitting. Though I'm running low on yarn again…and the price of wool is going up, you know. It's scandalous.      Everything is going up, Margaret.

...Honestly, the sheer audacity of it! Charging for plastic bags  again ? As if everything isn’t expensive enough already. It's just another little pinch, isn't it? They say it's for the environment, but it feels more like a revenue grab.      You know, you’re probably right. It’s the principle, really. They’ve been doing it on and off for years now. I remember the first time they introduced it, everyone was furious. Then we got used to it, and now they’re bringing it back up again. It’s exhausting keeping up with it all. Did you see that article about the cat rescued from the tree in Birmingham? Extraordinary!      Oh, the cat! Yes, a truly remarkable rescue. Apparently, it was up there for three days. Three days! And only came down for a tin of tuna, the cheeky thing. Reminds me of Tibbles, when he was a kitten, getting stuck in Mrs. Henderson’s prize-winning hydrangeas. A right nuisance he was.      Three days! That's incredible. They must have been so relieved when it finally came down. Reminds me, I need to check on the patio furniture before it rains again. Speaking of relief, I’m still trying to decipher this cryptic crossword. It’s brutal. “Ancient city, initially hidden by regal ecstasy” – honestly, what does  that  even mean?      Sounds…intense. I gave up on those years ago. My brain just isn’t wired for that kind of lateral thinking. I’m more of a Sudoku man, myself. Simpler pleasures. Though, I  did  see something fascinating online about mirror writing. Apparently, Leonardo da Vinci was a prolific mirror writer.      Mirror writing? Fascinating! A defense mechanism, some believe, to keep his ideas private. Though, I always wondered if it was simply a quirk. You wouldn't catch  me  trying that. My handwriting is bad enough going the right way. It's getting harder to read my own shopping lists these days!      It is rather bizarre, isn’t it? The idea of writing backwards… It makes me think of all the documents I transcribe. You wouldn't  believe  some of the handwriting I have to decipher. Occasionally, I get medical notes that look like advanced hieroglyphics.      That must be stressful! Speaking of stressful, have you two been keeping up with the American political scene? It’s…well, it's something. Absolutely bonkers. The constant mud-slinging… I switch off, frankly.

Right, team. Operation ‘Less Screen Time, More Book Time’ is officially…under review. Honestly, it’s been Ninjago  and  Minecraft all weekend. I feel like I haven’t heard a proper sentence that wasn’t about a creeper or a spinner weapon in about 48 hours.      But Mummy! Kai just unlocked a new elemental blade! It’s  amazing ! It shoots fire and… and… everything!      And I nearly finished building the Destiny’s Bounty! Just need to add the sails. It's going to be huge! Bigger than the kitchen table, almost!      That’s…impressive, actually. You’re very dedicated builders, both of you. But remember we talked about reading a chapter of your books before any more screen time or Lego?      But Minecraft is just…it’s a whole world! I’m building a castle for my unicorn and a secret underground base! You can’t do that in a book.      You can  imagine  a whole world in a book, sweetheart. And you can imagine unicorns and castles, and secret bases, and everything else. Books let your imagination do all the work, which is even cooler. It’s like… building the world  yourself  inside your head.      But in Minecraft, I  am  building the world. I made a working farm, and a redstone contraption that opens a secret door…      That  is  clever. Honestly, it is. You’re both really good at the technical stuff. It’s just…I worry that you’re missing out on other things. When I was your age, I used to disappear into books for hours.
