It felt like I was travelling to different places, meeting amazing people…      What kind of books did you read? Were there dragons?      Oh, lots of dragons! And witches, and knights, and even…time-travelling adventures! I read everything I could get my hands on. It’s not that these games and Lego are bad, not at all. They’re fun! But reading helps you with so many things. It helps you learn new words, understand different ideas, and it just… expands your world.      Does it help you build better Minecraft worlds?      Hmm… that’s a good question. Not directly, perhaps. But it helps you come up with cooler storylines and more interesting characters. And think about describing your builds to your friends – reading helps you do that too. You can tell a really good story about your Destiny’s Bounty if you’ve read lots of stories yourself.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of people at the Roman Forum was just  ridiculous . You couldn’t move for selfie sticks. It completely ruined the atmosphere, didn’t it? Though, Rome itself… breathtaking. Absolutely breathtaking.      Oh, Mum, you always say that about historical sights! I bet you said it about Stonehenge too. You’re such a romantic. Was the food good though? That’s what  I  want to know. Did you at least get loads of pasta?      Yeah, Mum, spill the foodie details. You went to Italy, it's practically illegal to come back without gaining at least half a stone in pasta and gelato!      Don't be so cynical, you two! It  was  romantic. And yes, the food was divine. I had this little trattoria near the Trevi Fountain, absolutely tiny, family run… the carbonara was… well, just perfect. Rich, creamy, proper guanciale. I’m already craving it. But honestly, the crowds. I’m starting to think I prefer quieter holidays now. Maybe the Lake District next year?      The Lake District sounds lovely, actually. A bit more our speed. Less… overwhelming. I’ve been meaning to go for ages. Though, honestly, after the chaos of the shop this week,  anywhere  quiet sounds good. We had a delivery go missing, a burst pipe in the stockroom, and Mrs. Higgins complaining her loyalty points weren’t working  again . It's been a nightmare.      Oh no, that sounds stressful, Liv. Seriously. People can be relentless. How did you sort the delivery?      Still trying to! It’s with the courier, they’re ‘investigating’. Which usually means it’s vanished into the ether. It was a big order, too. A garden gnome collection, of all things. Who orders a  collection  of garden gnomes?      People are peculiar. That's the best way to describe them. Anyway, enough about work troubles and missing gnomes. It’s Saturday! We need to make the most of it. I was thinking, after this, we could potter around Lichfield market? They’ve got that new artisan bakery stall everyone’s raving about.      Ooh, yes! I’m in. I need to find a birthday present for Ben anyway. His is next week and I’ve left it ridiculously late, as usual. Are they doing those sourdough loaves with the olives and rosemary?      I believe they are! And a lovely selection of cheeses too. We could even make an evening of it. Have a nice early dinner, watch a film… I’ve got that new period drama everyone’s talking about, the one set in Cornwall.

Right, anyone fancy a quick game of Exploding Kittens while we finish these sandwiches? Honestly, this egg mayo is… questionable. My mum makes  way  better ones.      Mmmph. Questionable is putting it mildly. It tastes like they used mayo from a jar that’s been open since the war. But yeah, Exploding Kittens sounds good. Beats staring at the slightly sticky floor of this food court.      It's not  that  bad. Just… bland. And seriously, why is everything in this shopping centre so expensive? I swear, a bottle of water costs a fiver. Exploding Kittens is a good shout though. I’m still reeling from Mr. Henderson’s history lesson. He went on a tangent about the Crimean War and then started talking about modern geopolitical tensions. My brain hurt.      Henderson’s a bit intense, isn’t he? He always tries to make everything sound like the start of World War Three. Remember when he was going on about Brexit like it was the Schlieffen Plan all over again?      Oh god, yes! He was practically prepping us for rationing. And then he gave us that look, you know the one, like he was judging us for not knowing the intricacies of the Eastern Question. Honestly, some teachers.      It’s just… frustrating. He seems to think anyone who isn't obsessed with history is actively malicious. And then old Mrs. Davies cornered me after maths, asking if I'd considered applying to be a prefect. A  prefect ! Like I want to spend my free periods policing the corridors.      Prefects? Seriously? They spend more time strutting around like they're in the army than actually helping anyone. I saw Ben Carter giving someone grief for having their hood up yesterday. Total power trip.      It’s all about the badge, innit? Speaking of armies and power trips… Did you see that documentary on Channel 4 last night about the Russian invasion? Absolutely terrifying stuff. Makes Henderson's rambling seem… almost sensible.      I did! It was awful. It makes you feel so helpless, you know? Like what can  we  even do? It's just… yikes. Changed the mood for watching  Heartstopper  afterwards, that's for sure. Needed something fluffy to balance it out.       Heartstopper  is genuinely good though. I'm not ashamed to admit I'm hooked. Although my little sister keeps teasing me about it. She thinks it's "cringey". She’s obsessed with that new dystopian thing on Netflix,  The Fracture .

...and honestly, Mrs. Davies’ explanation of quantum entanglement just went  right  over my head. It was like she was speaking another language, and not even a helpful one like French! Did you understand any of it, Chloe?      Oh, don’t even  start  me on Mrs. Davies. It’s always so… abstract. Like she expects us to just  feel  the subatomic particles being linked across vast distances. I got as far as ‘spooky action at a distance’ and then my brain just short-circuited. Did she even check if anyone was following?      Nope. She breezed through it like we were all Einstein. And then the question at the end! “Explain quantum entanglement to me as if I were five.” Seriously? Like  that’s  helpful. I just mumbled something about connected things and hoped for the best.      I think I said something about magic. Or maybe ghosts. Honestly, I was just trying to avoid eye contact. It’s bad enough trying to understand it, let alone  explain  it. It's completely different to Mr. Harrison. He actually  tries  to make it make sense.      Totally! Mr. Harrison is brilliant. He breaks everything down. Remember when he used the analogy of the two gloves in boxes to explain superposition? That actually clicked. Mrs. Davies just waves her hands and talks about wave functions.      Oh yeah! The glove one! That was good. It's amazing how he can make physics… approachable. Speaking of teachers, did you hear what happened with Mr. Peterson, our form tutor, today?      No! What? Don’t tell me he’s left! I actually quite like him, even if he does constantly ask if we've ‘considered a career in accountancy’.      No, no, he’s still here. Apparently, someone changed his ringtone to the theme tune from '17 Again'. During assembly! He was mortified. Apparently, Leo Matthews was the culprit.       No way!  Leo! That's… brilliant. Poor Mr. Peterson though. That must have been awful. I can just picture his face. He's always so proper!      It was gold. Complete and utter gold. Everyone was trying not to laugh. Even Miss Andrews was struggling. It's made him even more determined to find out who did it though, so Leo's probably in for a stern talking-to.      Worth it. Absolutely worth it. Hey, did you finish the English reading assignment? The one on character development in  Pride and Prejudice ? It’s so long!

...Honestly, the sourdough starter is being a right drama queen this week. It either explodes, or it just… sits there, sulking. Like a teenager.      Sounds about right for a starter, doesn’t it? They’re temperamental little blighters. So, are we still on for Transylvania, then? You haven't backed out, have you? Thinking about the sourdough, or, you know, Dracula?      Oh, don’t even  start  with the Dracula jokes, Leo. It's a really beautiful part of Romania, honestly. I did some research for a potential themed night at the café – okay,  fine , it was partially Dracula-inspired – and the castles are stunning. Real history, not just spooky stories. And yes, I'm still in! I’ve finally booked a week off.      Transylvania, eh? Crikey. Sounds a bit fancy for us, doesn’t it? I’m more of a beach and a bar kinda guy. Still, I’m up for it. A bit of history never hurt anyone. Though, honestly, the thought of all those castles… gives me the heebie-jeebies.      It'll be amazing, Ben! Imagine all the spooky photos. Plus, I need a break. I've been up to my elbows in flour for months. It'll be good to just… wander around old towns and not think about proving times.      Exactly. It's a proper adventure. And we're going in September, right? So hopefully, the peak tourist rush will be over. I’ve been looking at flights, and they’re looking fairly reasonable. I can send you all the links later, Chloe?      Cheers, Leo. That’d be brilliant. Speaking of flights, have you heard from Finn lately? He mentioned something about a possible trip to Australia.      Finn? No way! He didn’t tell  me  anything. Though, to be fair, Finn and I aren't exactly… super close. He's a good bloke, just... a bit out there, you know? What's he planning? A gap yah at 28?      He was talking about visiting his aunt in Perth. Said she's got a vineyard. Fancy, huh? He was on about “chucking a shrimp on the barbie” or something equally stereotypical.      Oh, Finn. Always with the stereotypes. He probably thinks we all wander around in Akubra hats and wrestle crocodiles. It's endearing, really. He  did  mention needing to save up some money, which is why he was asking about extra shifts at the pub.      That sounds like Finn.

Honestly, Leo,  please  stop drumming on the counter. It’s driving me round the bend. And Maisie, darling, is that really necessary to sing the chorus of ‘Baby Shark’ while I'm trying to make dinner?      But Mummy, it’s a  good  song! And Leo's drumming is the beat! We need a beat for the party!      Yeah, Mummy! It’s a party beat! Like when we did that muddy obstacle course and everyone was cheering!      The obstacle course was… an experience. A very muddy experience. And we’re not quite at the ‘party’ stage yet. We've still got to sort photos, remember? Auntie Carol wants those for her slideshow.      Photos? Oh, like the  Alice in Wonderland  ones? I was the Queen of Hearts! I shouted "Off with their heads!" really loud.      You did indeed. Perhaps not  quite  so loud for Auntie Carol. She's a bit sensitive. We also need some normal family photos. You know, not everyone in fancy dress? Though, to be fair, Leo’s knight outfit was rather impressive.      I could fight dragons! I was the bravest knight  ever .      Absolutely. The bravest. Right, I was thinking we could try and get some nice ones tomorrow afternoon, maybe in the garden? If the weather holds. I was hoping to get a few of you two with the aerial hoop too. I’ve got that new backdrop.      The sparkly one? Ooh, yes! Can I wear my fairy wings?      Of course you can wear your fairy wings. But promise me, no attempting aerial acrobatics  with  fairy wings.      Can I be a pirate? I can do a pirate voice! "Arrr, shiver me timbers!"      We can discuss pirate costumes later. I’m trying to get a plan sorted. Speaking of which, I need to ask - did you two tell Grandad anything about the party theme? I specifically said  no  mentioning it.      Maybe… a little? I told him we were having a 'magical' party.      And I said there might be dragons! And a bouncy castle!      Oh, brilliant. He’ll be trying to rent a fire-breathing dragon  now , won't he? Honestly, sometimes I think I need a course in damage control. And a filter for anything you two tell the grandparents.      But Grandad’s fun! He said he used to listen to really loud music when  he  was little. He called it… rock 'n' roll?      He did, didn’t he? He’s got a surprisingly rebellious streak.

Right, so you’re telling me young Maisie here almost took out old Mr. Henderson's prize-winning roses with that parallel park attempt?       Almost . It was a near miss, honestly. He came storming out, waving his secateurs. I thought I was going to die of embarrassment.      Roses, eh? Always trouble, roses. My mother used to grow ‘em. Prickly things. Reminds me of your Aunt Mildred really, always a thorn in everyone’s side.      Oh, Harold, you and your stories! Mildred wasn’t  that  bad. Just…particular. And Maisie, you'll get there with the parking. It takes practice. Remember when  I  first started driving? Ended up in a hedge, I did.      A hedge? Seriously, Gran?      Honestly! A lovely hawthorn hedge. Didn't do much damage, thankfully. Your grandfather wasn’t best pleased though. He had to fetch me out with the tractor.      A tractor rescue? That’s a story! Speaking of stories, I had parents' evening last night. You wouldn’t believe the drama. One parent was practically accusing me of deliberately failing their child. The pressure on these kids is ridiculous.      It  is  stressful. Everyone's talking about their results. Chloe got all 9s, apparently. All of them! It's insane.      Nines? What in the world is a nine? Back in my day, you just got a pass or a fail. Simple as that. No fuss.      It's the highest grade now, Harold. The new system. It means she basically aced everything. It’s a lot of pressure on them, though. Everyone expecting perfection.      I think it’s a bit much. I'm happy if I just pass. It’s not like my career depends on it…yet. I’m thinking about maybe being a vet.      Oh, that’s lovely, dear. A wonderful profession. You've always been good with animals. Remember that stray kitten you brought home? We spent weeks nursing it back to health.      And then it scratched you, Gran! You were furious.      Well, it  did  draw blood! But it was worth it in the end. It found a lovely home with Mrs. Peterson down the road.      It’s all these gadgets nowadays causing the problem. Everyone glued to their phones, tweeting pictures of their dinners. What’s the world coming to? I saw young William posting a picture of his…his roulade, was it? With some ridiculous filter on it.      Social media, Harold. It’s just how they communicate now.

Honestly, Liam, you need to eat something. You’ve barely touched a thing since you arrived yesterday. All that driving from London… you must be flagging.      Thanks, Margaret. I am a bit knackered, actually. Just…thinking, I suppose. It’s good to be here, though. Lovely to see you both. And Dad, still crushing me at Chinese chess, I see.      Just applying a little strategic thinking, son. You're still thinking about grammar when you should be thinking about cannons and horses. Though, I must say, you're getting better. Much better than when you first tried learning, years ago. Remember when you thought a 'cannon' just moved like a… well, like a cannon?      Oh, don’t remind me. My understanding of the rules was… rudimentary, to say the least. It’s a bit like trying to explain the perfect subjunctive to a class of fifteen-year-olds, really. You  think  they get it, but…      Speaking of explaining things, I was telling Doreen about your job the other day, Liam. She still hasn’t quite grasped what an ‘English Language Instructor’ actually  does . She said, “Does he just…correct people’s grammar?”      That’s pretty much the core of it, isn't it? Though there’s a lot more to it than red-penning essays. It’s about culture, communication, helping people navigate a new language and a new country. I actually had a student from South Korea last term, incredibly bright kid. Struggled with the idioms, though. Kept asking me what "raining cats and dogs" meant!      Now  that's  a good one. Imagine trying to explain  that  logically. You’d need a linguistic PhD for that. Still, better than trying to understand what’s going on with Scottish independence. Seems to be dragging on forever and a day.      Oh, don’t get me started on politics, George. It'll ruin breakfast. I’ve been meaning to ask you, Liam, how's work been? Still battling with student loan repayments? It’s outrageous what they charge these days. When  I  left sixth form, tuition was practically non-existent!      Honestly, it's a constant worry. The interest is brutal. I’m contributing what I can, but it feels like I’m barely making a dent. I keep thinking about going back for a Masters to boost my earning potential, but then…more debt. It's a vicious cycle.      My nephew’s going through the same thing.

…and honestly, the level of basic grammar some of these students expect to just  know  is astounding. I had one yesterday who genuinely thought ‘affect’ and ‘effect’ were interchangeable. Affect! He was writing a piece about the effect of climate change!      Oh, bless him. You’re back in teaching mode, aren’t you? I get it, though. It’s amazing how much assumptions students make. My lot in Vietnam were convinced I’d automatically understand their cultural references. Try explaining the nuances of a traditional water puppet show to someone who’s only ever seen TikTok.      Exactly! And it's not just the grammar. It's a sort of… entitlement, maybe? Expecting everything to be spoon-fed. It's probably the education system, isn't it? Though, to be fair, my generation wasn't exactly taught to  think  critically. More to memorise facts for exams. Which, incidentally, is why I ended up with a perfectly good English degree and absolutely no idea what to  do  with it.      Hmm, fair point. Access to information is so much easier now, but the skills to process it… not so much. I think universities are starting to grapple with that. Which brings me to my current existential dread: student loans. Trying to pay them off while living on a teacher's salary, even abroad, is… a challenge.      Oh, don’t even  start  me on debt. I’ve been spectacularly avoiding it my entire life. My parents, thankfully, paid for everything. Which meant I didn’t have the financial pressure to “get a proper job” and ended up… well, here. Semi-retired in Poland, teaching the occasional reluctant TEFL student. Though, frankly, seeing what’s happening with pensions now, even  that  feels precarious.      Seriously! I read an article the other day saying people my age will likely be working until they’re 70 just to scrape by. It’s terrifying. Makes you wonder what the point of all the sacrifice is. Speaking of sacrifice, I really need to get my car MOT’d when I get back. Completely forgot.      Oh no! Don’t leave it too long. It’s such a faff, but essential. You're driving back to Bury, right? Are you happy to take the more direct route, even though it's mostly motorway? I was thinking maybe we could loop through the Peak District, but it'll add hours.      Motorway’s good for me.

...Honestly, the Human Sciences open day at Oxford was…intense. Like, beautiful buildings, obviously, but everyone there already seemed to have a five-year plan mapped out in calligraphy. And they were all talking about A-Level Further Maths.  Further Maths , Kai! I barely scraped a B in the normal stuff.      Calm down, Liam. Oxford attracts the…ambitious, let's say. It doesn’t mean you’re not good enough. Human Sciences is brilliant though. I still reckon you’d be perfect for it. All that social stuff, history, psychology… you’re way better at understanding people than I am. I’m a numbers guy, through and through.      Yeah, but is it…practical? You're going straight for Maths at Imperial, right? That feels  solid . Like, a guaranteed job at the end of it. My Uncle Barry keeps saying I need something 'employable'. He thinks Human Sciences is just 'thinking about feelings all day'.      Uncle Barry also thinks a pint of bitter and a packet of crisps is a balanced meal. Don't listen to him too much. Look, Maths is practical, sure, but it's also brutal. The workload is insane, and honestly, if you don’t  love  it, you’ll burn out fast. Human Sciences lets you do stuff with that, you know? Policy, research, even social work. Plenty of options. Plus, thinking about feelings  is  important, even if Barry doesn't realise it.      Fair point about Uncle Barry. He does have questionable dietary habits. Still, I'm stressed. What if I get offers from both, and I pick the wrong one?      You won’t pick the wrong one. You’ll pick the one that feels right. Look, we’ve got time. We’ve got UCAS deadlines looming, but we’ve still got time. Speaking of feeling right… are you coming to watch the Harlequins on Saturday? They’re playing Saracens. Should be a good game.      Definitely! I wouldn't miss it. It’s a good distraction from the university panic. Actually, I promised to bring snacks. I was thinking of attempting some of Mum's sausage rolls. Remember how good they were last Christmas?      Attempting? Your Mum’s sausage rolls are legendary! You’d have to actively  try  to mess those up. Maybe just don't get distracted by doom-scrolling university prospectuses while you're making them.      Okay, fair enough. No multitasking culinary disasters. I might rope my little sister in to help.

…and that’s why, even now, after all these years, I still think National Insurance contributions are fundamentally a bit of a con. People think it's  just  for pensions, bless 'em. It’s not. It funds the NHS, unemployment benefits, all sorts. They dress it up nicely, of course, but it's still a tax. A compulsory tax.      Right, so it's not a separate pot of money specifically  for  your retirement, it's just… blended in with everything else? I always thought there was a ring-fence.      A ring-fence! That’s a good one. Politicians  like  ring-fences. Makes it sound responsible, doesn't it? But the reality is, they can move things around. Say the NHS needs a boost, they can effectively ‘borrow’ from the National Insurance fund. Officially, it's all accounted for, of course. Lots of spreadsheets. I used to  make  those spreadsheets.      Of course you did. You’d see right through it. It’s just… it feels so complicated. Especially with all the changes now. Self-assessment, universal credit, tax-free allowances shifting… It’s a full-time job just understanding what you owe!      It  is  designed to be complicated, you know. Keeps people from questioning things too closely. If it was simple, everyone would be auditing the government’s books. Which, frankly, they should be doing more of. This current lot... spending like there's no tomorrow.      It feels like that, doesn't it? I was reading about the proposed cuts to adult social care, and then there's the increased spending on… well, everything else. It’s a difficult balance, I suppose. But where does the money  actually  go?      That’s the million-dollar question, isn’t it? A good chunk goes on interest payments, for starters. Debt’s gone through the roof. Then you’ve got the consultants, the outsourced contracts… all massively inflated prices. And frankly, a good deal just vanishes. Mismanagement, waste, plain old corruption. Don't tell me governments are squeaky clean, I've seen too much.      It's disheartening. We pay so much in tax, and you’re right, it's not always obvious what we're getting for it. I try to tell my students about civic responsibility, about understanding the political system… but sometimes I wonder what the point is if it feels so opaque.      You keep telling them, love. It's important. Even if they don’t see immediate results.

...Honestly, Mum, I just feel like I’m constantly putting out fires. It's not even  creative  fires, it's just…admin fires. Spreadsheets that haven’t been updated, people not replying to emails, the printer refusing to cooperate… you wouldn't  believe  the drama over the printer.      Oh, darling. Sounds like a typical Tuesday, doesn’t it? Though, I thought printers were pretty reliable these days. The one at school is a beast, honestly. It’s got a mind of its own. Still, “admin fires” – that’s a good way to put it. Better than ‘soul-crushing monotony’, I suppose.      Soul-crushing monotony is a  very  accurate description sometimes. It’s just… I had this image of being a Project Coordinator, you know? Leading teams, strategizing, actual  projects . Instead, I’m glorified office management. Mrs. Henderson actually asked me to order more staplers yesterday.  Staplers.       Well, someone has to keep the office running! And a good stapler is a vital piece of equipment, you know. Seriously though, it’s only been a few months in the role hasn’t it? Give it time. It always takes a while to carve out what you want to do, to move beyond the essentials. Remember when I first started at the school? I was basically a human filing cabinet for the first year.      That's true, I suppose. It just feels… disappointing. All those university courses, all the late nights studying, and I'm ordering stationery. How was Auntie Carol doing, by the way? I haven't spoken to her in ages.      She’s good, she’s good. A little creaky, naturally, but her garden is blooming apparently. She’s proper proud of her roses. She was telling me she’s finally mastered that climbing rose she’s been battling with for years. It’s a stubborn one, apparently, just like her! She sends her love. She was asking about your boyfriend, Liam. Is he still playing football?      Yeah, he is. He’s actually doing really well, got scouted by a team a bit further afield. He’s really excited, but also stressed about the travelling. It's a bit of a commitment. We’re trying to figure out logistics. It’s… complicated.      Oh, that’s lovely to hear about the football. But complicated is right. Long distance is hard. Still, if he’s serious about it, you’ll find a way. You always do.

Right, so you’re saying this new recycling scheme… they want us to separate  everything  now? Even the plastic film off the yogurts? Honestly, it's getting ridiculous. Back in my day, it was just paper and glass. Simple.      Aye, Dad. It's a nightmare. They sent the leaflet last week, and it’s a whole new level of detail. Apparently, the plastic film contaminates the whole batch if it gets mixed in. It's all about the quality of the recycling, they say. Makes you wonder if it’s worth the bother, though, doesn’t it?      It's not  that  bad. You just need to get a system. I’ve got a dedicated bin for soft plastics now. It's all part of being responsible, isn’t it? Plus, they're threatening fines if you don't comply.      Fines! Now they're threatening fines. That’s what I mean, it’s too much. They're treating us like children. Remember when we used to just chuck everything in the same bin and not think twice? Simpler times…      You  always  say that, Dad. But honestly, things have changed. The planet’s in a bit of a state. Speaking of states, have you heard from Auntie Brenda? She was supposed to call about Christmas arrangements.      No, not yet. I sent her a text yesterday, but nothing. She’s probably busy with her bridge club. She lives for that bridge, you know. Keeps her mind sharp, apparently. Though sometimes I wonder if it just sharpens her competitive edge.      I saw a picture on Facebook of her winning a tournament last month. She looked utterly triumphant. Maybe she's strategizing her Christmas gift offensive. She's always got a plan.      That's her all over! I’m thinking of suggesting we do a games night this year instead of the usual big Christmas dinner at her place. It could be more relaxed.      A games night? What kind of games? I'm not much for all those modern board games with hundreds of tiny pieces. Give me a good old-fashioned game of cards any day.      I've got that new strategy game, 'Terraforming Mars'. It’s quite involved, but it’s really good. We could play that. Or maybe something simpler, like Codenames?      Codenames sounds good. And we could put some music on. I've just downloaded a load of old stuff onto my iPod, reminding me of uni days.

...Honestly, the sheer  volume  of new digital resources they were pushing at the conference was overwhelming. It’s like everyone’s suddenly decided lesson planning isn’t about pedagogy anymore, it’s about which app has the coolest filter.      Tell me about it! I was at that one in Bristol last month, remember? Same thing. Every other stand was selling some sort of interactive whiteboard software or AI-powered grammar checker. It felt less like a professional development opportunity and more like a sales pitch convention. Did you go to the one in Birmingham?      No, not this year. Too expensive, to be honest. And after the last few, I'm starting to wonder if it’s even worth it. I mean, I learn a fair bit from chatting with other teachers, definitely, but the actual keynotes… they’re usually just repackaged ideas. Especially the ones promising a ‘revolution’ in language learning. I swear, I've heard ‘gamification’ touted as the future for five years running.      Exactly! It’s all buzzwords. My head was spinning. And then you get the ones who’ve clearly had a grant to develop some groundbreaking new method… and it’s immediately apparent it’s completely impractical for a classroom of thirty teenagers with varying levels of motivation.      Oh god, yes. The ‘blended learning’ sessions always get me. They show these idyllic setups with individual tablets and personalized learning pathways… and you think, ‘Right, and where am I supposed to find the budget for thirty iPads,  and  the time to create a unique lesson plan for every single student?’ It's just… unrealistic. How are you finding it at the grammar school? It must be different than my college, right?      It is, but not always in a good way. More paperwork, for starters. Endless assessment grids and tracking data. It's suffocating. They're obsessed with progress eight scores and value-added measures– I spend more time  proving  I'm teaching than actually teaching, if that makes sense. It’s all very… target driven. And the kids…they just see through it. They know it's all about the numbers.      Ugh, that sounds awful. At least my students are a little more forgiving. Although, trying to get them to use full stops is a constant battle! Honestly, I spend half my week correcting punctuation. Remember old Mr. Henderson at sixth form? He’d have a field day.

Honestly, this is the life, isn’t it? Just gliding along, Polish countryside whizzing by. Though my back is starting to complain about all the bumpy roads. I really need to get back into some sort of…movement.      It  is  lovely. Though, if I’m being honest, I'm starting to feel a bit guilty. I promised myself I’d be running at least three times a week when I had a bit of a break between contracts. And here I am, fueled by pierogi and enjoying the scenery.      Oh, don’t feel bad! You’re working hard all year round, teaching those eager students. A bit of a holiday is  deserved . Besides, you look fantastic. Seriously, you’re glowing. Must be all that fresh air, even if it's only through a campervan window.      You’re sweet, but you always say that! I think it’s good lighting. And possibly a filter on my Instagram stories. You, on the other hand, look wonderfully relaxed. Have you been reading much? I saw you with a book earlier.      I have! Finally finished Hilary Mantel’s  Wolf Hall . It’s…dense. Absolutely brilliant, but dense. Took me ages. Now I’ve started something lighter, a detective novel set in Scotland. Needed a bit of a palate cleanser after all that Tudor intrigue. Are you reading anything on this trip?      Not yet, I downloaded a couple of ebooks, but I keep getting distracted by…well, everything. Trying to plan the next leg, figuring out where we're going to park this beast in Rzeszow. It's apparently a nightmare. I was on a forum last night, people were complaining about tiny spaces and aggressive parking attendants.      Oh, lovely. Sounds…fun. Maybe we should just embrace the wild camping life? Though I’m not sure my nerves could handle being woken up by a Polish farmer with a shotgun.      Probably not the best idea. I think I found a campsite on the outskirts, hopefully it’s decent. It seems finding a decent campsite these days is almost as hard as finding a good man!      Oh, here we go. Still on that subject, are we? What’s the latest verdict on the male of the species?      It’s just… frustrating, isn’t it? You meet someone who  seems  lovely, intelligent, funny… and then they reveal they collect porcelain dolls or are obsessed with conspiracy theories. It’s always something.

...and honestly, the way they’re talking about telomere lengthening now, it's not science fiction anymore, is it? It's edging closer to being a genuine possibility. Though, personally, I'm not entirely sure I  want  to live forever. Sounds exhausting. Imagine all the tech support issues you’d accrue over centuries!      Oh, you and your tech. But you’re right, it’s a bit daunting to think about. It’s not just the practicalities, it’s… what’s the point of a life without end? Wouldn’t everything eventually lose its flavour? Though, thinking about my Gran, maybe a bit more time  would  have been good. She was always saying she hadn't seen enough of the world.      Aye, that's the rub, isn't it? My own grandfather, he’d a fascination with the pyramids. Said they weren't just tombs, that they were some kind of…energy accumulators. Sounded a bit mad at the time, but then you read about the alignment with Orion’s belt, the precision of the construction… it makes you wonder. And then you factor in what we know about plate tectonics and how the land shifts over millennia… the things they’d have known, watched happen.      It's incredible, isn’t it? They had such a deep understanding of the natural world, even without our modern science. It makes you wonder about all those lost civilizations too. And speaking of long-lasting structures, Vikings! They were prolific travellers, weren’t they? I was reading about their influence on Ireland, how much of the early settlements around Cork were actually Viking in origin.      Ah, the Norsemen. They certainly left their mark. Old Head of Kinsale has stories attached to it, you know - a Danish princess apparently threw herself off it rather than marry an English lord. A bit romantic, a bit tragic. It’s funny, though, considering their reputation, they weren't just raiders. Skilled traders, shipbuilders… incredibly adaptable. It’s like risk was built into their DNA. They just  went  for it.      That’s true. And it’s a good thing they did, in a way. They pushed boundaries. It makes me think about what we’re doing now with energy resources. We're taking so many risks with the planet just to maintain our current way of life. Comets used to be seen as omens of doom, now we're trying to figure out how to mine them for resources.

Honestly, this coffee maker is driving me  mad . It’s like a science experiment every morning. First it gurgles, then it spits, then it just… stops. And half the time it tastes burnt. You’d think for the money Dad spent on it, it’d at least make a decent cuppa!      Oh, darling, you know your dad and his gadgets. He always goes for the bells and whistles, doesn’t he? Functionality is often an afterthought. I told him a simple drip machine would do, really. Did you try descaling it again? It might just be lime scale build-up.      Aye, he’s a magpie for those things, our Keith. Saw a self-stirring mug online yesterday, nearly ordered it straight away. Said it’d save his arm. Honestly! Descaling’s a good shout, love. I’ve had trouble with mine sometimes. Though, to be fair, a proper brew needs a bit of effort. None of this instant nonsense.      I've descaled it three times this week! I'm starting to think it secretly hates me. Speaking of spending money... did you two decide where we're going for dinner on Saturday? I’ve got that voucher for La Piazza, the Italian place, but I’ve heard mixed reviews.      La Piazza… hmm. I’ve heard the service can be a bit slow. But the pasta is good, apparently. Or, we could try that new tapas place, ‘Sol y Sombra’? I saw a picture online and it looked lovely. Bit pricier, though, without a voucher.      Tapas sounds good! Long as there’s plenty of garlic prawns. La Piazza’s alright, but it's always so busy. You're crammed in like sardines. And they tried to charge me extra for relish last time! Daylight robbery, I tell you.      Garlic prawns sound amazing, actually. Okay, tapas it is! Right. Onto more pressing matters… the baby chair. It’s arrived, hasn’t it? Has anyone worked out how to assemble the thing? It looks like something out of IKEA, with about a million pieces.      It's in the hall, still in the box. I glanced at the instructions, and they're… pictorial, to say the least. We'll probably need your dad's engineering skills for that one. Though, knowing him, he'll probably watch a YouTube tutorial instead.      YouTube tutorials. The bane of my existence. Last time I let him ‘help’ with a plumbing issue, we had a flood!

Honestly, darling, I think the fairy lights are trying to escape. It’s leaning like the Tower of Pisa over here. Did you even  try  to centre it this year?      Mum, it’s charmingly imperfect! Besides, I was distracted. Chloe messaged, wanting to know what we’re doing for pre-Christmas drinks. And honestly, trying to get the tree straight felt like a metaphor for my life right now - utterly futile.      Chloe, eh? Good girl. You’ve kept in touch with her since uni, which is lovely. You need good friends. It’s just… everything feels a bit hectic this year, doesn’t it? Mrs. Higgins next door started putting her decorations up in November! November! It’s madness.      Oh, Mrs. Higgins. She’s always been a bit… enthusiastic. Probably compensates for Kevin, the perpetually grumpy husband. Still, she did offer me a mince pie last week, which was nice. How's Winston doing, by the way? He seemed a bit off his food yesterday.      He’s being a drama queen, that cat. He ate perfectly well this morning, demolished most of my salmon pate actually - the cheek! I think he just wanted extra fuss. Honestly, he knows exactly how to manipulate me. Speaking of fuss, have you booked that nail appointment? Your birthday’s only a couple of weeks away.      Ugh, don’t remind me. It’s creeping up so fast. No, I haven’t booked it yet. I keep meaning to, but work is just… relentless. The new client is asking for constant revisions. It's just copy for a website about, get this, luxury dog beds. Apparently, “fluffy comfort” isn’t conveying the  right  image.      Luxury dog beds? Good grief. That sounds soul-destroying. Still, it's a job. And it pays the bills. Remember when you were obsessed with German history at school? All those hours researching the Rhineland… did you ever think you'd be writing about dog beds?      It’s a far cry from the Holy Roman Empire, that's for sure! I did love learning about Germany though. It's so complex, you know? All that cultural heritage… I was thinking about taking Ben to Heidelberg next year, maybe for his birthday. He's been really into learning German.      Heidelberg! Oh, that's lovely! It’s beautiful there. Very romantic. Is he still talking about that motorbike trip he was planning?      He is. He keeps showing me YouTube videos of winding roads through the Black Forest.

Right, so… it’s officially a flat. Still feels a bit…echoey, doesn’t it? Like shouting into a cavern. I swear I heard my voice bounce back three times just now.      It  does  echo. But it's a good echo! A 'potential' echo. Think of all the furniture we’ll fill it with. And honestly, after Mum’s place, anything feels spacious. Though, I do miss her biscuit tin…      Fair point about the biscuit tin. Speaking of necessities, we need to tackle the internet. I’ve been on the phone to ‘ConnectSussex’ for seemingly an eternity. Apparently, “engineer availability” is a mythical beast. They’ve booked someone for… next Thursday.      Next  Thursday ?! Seriously? How are we supposed to binge-watch terrible reality TV without internet? That's a priority, Ben. A fundamental human right, practically. Have you checked BT? Sometimes they’re quicker.      I did, but they're saying the same thing - a week out. Honestly, I'm tempted to tether everything to my phone, but my data allowance wouldn't last five minutes with your Netflix habit.      Hey! My Netflix habit is  cultured  viewing. And yes, okay, I might watch a lot of ‘Selling Sunset’. But it’s research! Research into… aspirational interior design. Anyway, we can cope for a few days. More pressing: food. I’m starving. Did you manage to grab anything on the way?      I got some bread, cheese, and ham. And a truly questionable-looking banana. It’s… brown. But it's fruit! We can make sandwiches. It’s not exactly a gourmet feast, but it’ll do for now. We need a proper shop tomorrow. There’s a farmer’s market in Lewes, apparently. Loads of seasonal stuff.      Ooh, a farmer’s market sounds lovely. We should definitely go. I've been craving some decent tomatoes. The ones from the supermarket just taste…watery. And we need to figure out the rubbish situation. I saw a confusing array of bins outside. Black, blue, green… It’s a recycling riddle.      I think I downloaded a leaflet from the council website. Let me have a look… Right, okay. Black is general waste, blue is recycling – glass, plastic, paper – and green is garden waste. Apparently, they’re quite strict. Massive fines if you put the wrong thing in the wrong bin.      Oh great. More rules. I’m starting to feel very…adult. Have you had a chance to check out the nursery next door?

...Honestly, the carbonara was  huge . I thought I’d be delicately picking at it, but I genuinely had to stop myself from scraping the bowl. How was your halloumi and roasted veg? You looked pretty content.      Oh, it was amazing! So much flavour, and perfectly cooked. Bills does a good veggie option, which is a win, right? It’s massively better than trying to find something decent in the uni cafeteria. It feels like ages since we were subjecting ourselves to that, doesn’t it?      Ages! It feels like another lifetime. I’m still having flashbacks to that…grey stew they called ‘beef’. Remember Sarah trying to convince everyone it tasted like gravy?      Oh my god, Sarah! She was always the optimist. Bless her. It’s so good to actually  see  you, by the way. Proper see, not just a blurry face on a video call. How’s everything going with the project co-ordinating? Still wrangling spreadsheets and keeping people on track?      Wrangling is the perfect word. It’s…a lot. It’s good experience, definitely, learning how to manage deadlines and stakeholders, but honestly, sometimes I feel more like a glorified messenger. How’s the placement going for you? Are you actually getting to  do  things, or are you just making coffee and filing?      It's thankfully more than coffee and filing. I’m mostly doing market research, which is pretty cool. It’s a bit overwhelming trying to get my head around the industry, but everyone’s been really supportive. It’s funny, though, I keep accidentally slipping into university speak when I’m explaining things to people. Like using ‘parameter’ when ‘thing’ would do just fine.      Oh, absolutely. We’re all guilty of that. It takes a while to un-learn the academic jargon. You’ll get there. And how’s home? Are your parents driving you mad, now you're back for the placement?      You know my mum. She’s already started asking about my ‘long-term prospects’ and subtly hinting at potential eligible bachelors in the neighbourhood. Dad’s just happy to have me home and making use of my driving skills. He's outsourced all the grocery shopping to me. How about your folks? Did they have a good Christmas?      Christmas was… chaotic. My little brother decided to re-enact the nativity scene with the dog as the donkey. It was surprisingly realistic, and not at all peaceful.

...Honestly, the sheer  volume  of beige in this place is depressing. It's Cambridge, not a retirement home. You'd think they could inject a bit of colour, wouldn’t ya? Like, a nice splash of crimson or something. Reminds me of Gran's living room.      You and your aversion to neutral tones. It's calming, isn't it? A bit of peace amongst the academic frenzy. Though I admit, it  is  a bit… bland. Speaking of bland, how’s the research going? Still wrestling with those data sets?      Wrestling is putting it mildly. It's more like being slowly strangled by them. Honestly, quantitative analysis feels a million miles away from anything actually  real . I miss the qualitative stuff, you know? Talking to people, getting proper stories. This feels…sterile. Though, the funding is good, which is the only reason I’m not handing in my notice and opening a vintage shop.      A vintage shop? That...actually suits you. All those amazing outfits you put together. I always admire your style. It's so much more…intentional than mine. I just throw on whatever's clean-ish.      Oh, stop it! You clean your clothes, that's half the battle. And it’s a running joke, isn’t it? Me, the research manager, dreaming of selling old clothes. Though, imagine, a little place full of proper 60s dresses and Dr Martens. I'd call it "Wayward Threads" or something dramatic. It would be  fully  stocked with stuff I can't afford to wear myself.      “Wayward Threads”, I like it. Very evocative. You could totally pull that off. It'd be a haven for students looking to avoid the beige. So, how far off are you from finishing this research anyway?      Months, unfortunately. It’s a big project, mapping social mobility trends. Fascinating in theory, soul-crushing in practice. It also makes me think about home. About Sunderland, you know? It’s a stark contrast to Cambridge, obviously.      I can imagine. I've only been up North a handful of times. Mostly through Leeds, never actually  in  Sunderland. What’s it really like? People have this… image, y’know? Of bleakness and shipyards.      That’s… not entirely inaccurate, historically. But it’s changed. It’s got a really vibrant arts scene now, loads of brilliant musicians coming through. And the people are just… different. More down to earth, more brutally honest. Less pretending, if you know what I mean?

Right, Gran, you said you wanted to talk about… everything that’s going on? Feels a bit heavy for a Tuesday afternoon, doesn’t it? I’ve got history homework looming, you know.      Aye, well, history's important, lad. But knowing what  is  history in the making is important too. It's all this Rishi Sunak fella, isn't it? Honestly, another one. They come and go like buses, don’t they? Seems like yesterday it was Truss, making a right mess of things.      It  was  only yesterday, practically! And yeah, it's a bit… chaotic. At school, everyone's talking about it. Old Mr. Henderson, our politics teacher, was going on about U-turns and the economy. I just glazed over after a bit, to be honest. It's all numbers and graphs.      Numbers and graphs! That's all they ever talk about these days. Back in  my  day, politics was about principles, about what you believed in. Not chasing figures on a spreadsheet. My dad – your great-grandad – he was a staunch Labour man. Worked down the railway, he did. Never had a bad word said about Clement Attlee, he didn’t. Said he gave the working man a bit of dignity.      I think Mr. Henderson mentioned Attlee. He said something about the NHS being his big thing. Which, you know, is still going, so…      Still going, aye, barely. They’re letting it crumble, they are. It's scandalous. I remember when you could see a doctor without waiting six months. And free prescriptions! Now they want you paying for everything. It's just… disheartening. It feels like they're trying to make it harder for folks.      Well, they say the population's bigger now, and older, so there's more demand. But yeah, I’ve heard stories. My mate's mum was waiting ages for a hip replacement. It's not fair. Do you think… do you think it’s all just a big mess because nobody agrees on anything anymore?      Partly, lad, partly. It's the divisions, see. Everyone shouting at each other instead of listening. And this whole Brexit business… Oh, don't get me started on Brexit. It's caused nothing but trouble. Darlington voted Leave, you know. I didn’t. Never understood it. We were alright with Europe.      Dad said Brexit was supposed to mean more money for the NHS. Seems like that didn’t happen, did it?

Right then, absolutely brilliant stew, Mary. Though young Thomas here seems to think it’s perfectly acceptable to eat with his mouth open. A fine Irish tradition, is it?      ‘Snot fair! I  am  eating quietly! And it’s really good, Dad. Seriously.      Now, now, Thomas. Your father’s right, darling. It’s just polite to close your mouth when you chew. Think of Granny Moira. You wouldn’t want to spray her, would you?      Och, don’t mind me. A bit of spray never hurt anyone. Seen worse in the playground, I have! Though a bit of etiquette never goes amiss, mind you. Used to have to drum it into wee bairns for forty years. Honestly, the things they thought were acceptable...      Forty years of shaping young minds, Moira. That's a lifetime of wiping gravy off chins. Speaking of lifetimes, did anyone see that blood moon last night? Absolutely spectacular. Kept me up late, I confess.      Oh yeah! It was red! Mum made me come inside though, said it was getting late. Was it… spooky?      It was beautiful, sweetheart. Not spooky, just… a little magical. They say it happens when the Earth lines up just right with the sun and the moon.      Aye, it’s an old omen, that one. Some say it foretells grand changes. Though usually, it just means the weather's about to turn. Speaking of changes, I was thinking about maybe coming over for a few days next week. Would that be alright with you, Mary? I could give you a hand with the wee one.      Oh, Granny, that would be  amazing . Honestly, I’m starting to feel like a permanent fixture on the sofa. Just getting out for a coffee is a military operation these days.      You’re more than welcome, Moira. It’d be lovely to have you. Though you’ll be on babysitting duty, you know that? Thomas is a bundle of energy. We might even take him down to Fitzgeralds Park. He loves the playground there.      Yeah! And the ducks! I like feeding the ducks. But sometimes they chase me!      Ah, those ducks are cheeky, alright. Used to take my classes there on field trips. Always had to keep a close eye on them, little scamps pinching sandwiches!      It’s such a nice park, isn't it? It's good to get a bit of fresh air, even if it's just for an hour.

...Honestly, the whole thing with the interview just has me rattled, Arthur. It wasn't the questions, not exactly. It was…him. Old Man Hemmings. Still there, still clinging on to the History department like a barnacle.      Hemmings? Blimey. Still breathing, is he? Thought he’d have retired years ago. What’s he doing interviewing people now? Last I heard he was threatening to report students for using coloured pens.      You’re not far wrong. Turns out, the Head of Department decided Hemmings’ “institutional knowledge” was vital to the selection process. Institutional knowledge meaning he remembers everyone who ever annoyed him and dismisses anyone remotely similar. He kept asking me about my approach to… “modern interpretations” of the Tudors. Sounded like a veiled criticism of anything post-1950, frankly.      Good Lord. Sounds like a dinosaur judging the future. You’d think they’d want someone with fresh ideas, especially with the curriculum changes. Still, you’ve taught history for years, David. You know your stuff. Don't let the old grump get you down.      It’s not just that, Arthur. It reminded me… well, it reminded me of everything. The politics within the school, the endless meetings, the marking… I used to thrive on it. Now… I’m just tired.      Tired is an understatement, I reckon. Especially after everything with Sarah. How  is  she doing, by the way? Haven't seen her in a few weeks. Still enjoying the life in Edinburgh?      She’s good. Actually, she’s very good. She’s really settled. She’s working with a charity helping refugees, which suits her down to the ground. Still, she called last week – apparently there’s a proper buzz about another Scottish referendum. She's fully on board with independence, naturally. Says it's a different Scotland now, more confident.      Always was a headstrong one, your daughter. Smart as a whip, too. A Scottish referendum, eh? Here we go again. Seems like they're forever debating it up there. Honestly, I can’t understand the appeal. It all seemed to work perfectly well as part of the United Kingdom to me. I remember when they first started talking about it, back in the seventies. A lot of noise for not much gain in the end.      She argues it’s about self-determination, Arthur. Being able to chart their own course. And she says the current government in Westminster is ignoring the needs of Scotland.

Right, so, are we talking about needing a whole new set of baking trays then, Mum? Because seriously, the ones we had were…questionable. Like, permanently coated in something.      Oh, don’t even  start  on those baking trays, Aaron. Your dad insisted they were “perfectly serviceable” right up until the non-stick coating decided to migrate into the Victoria sponge. It was a disaster. And yes, we  do  need new ones. I’ve added it to the list. Honestly, moving is bringing up all sorts of kitchen-related anxieties.      It’s amazing what you accumulate, isn't it? You don’t realise how much stuff defines a space until you’re dismantling it. It's like, each chipped mug holds a memory.      Chipped mugs and questionable baking trays. Sounds about right for this family. Remember that time your Auntie Maureen brought that fruitcake? The one that could have doubled as a doorstop?      Oh god, yes! It featured prominently in every family photo for a good six months after that. She was so proud. Did anyone actually  eat  it?      A polite nibble here and there. Mostly it became a conversation piece. Speaking of conversations… did you manage to sort out those tuition fee queries, Liam? You were chasing up a form or something?      Yeah, sorted it. It was just a bit of a bureaucratic maze, as always. They wanted proof of… well, everything, basically. Birth certificate, bank statements, a blood sample, I’m not sure. It’s all done now though. Still feels incredibly daunting, though, doesn't it? All that debt looming.      It does. It's a different world now compared to when we were going through it. Though, I'm not sure  my  student days were much better financially. I worked every weekend at the supermarket just to keep my head above water.      Supermarkets… oh, the memories. That’s where I perfected the art of the strategically placed banana to look busy when I should have been stacking shelves.      You were always a charmer, Aaron. But seriously, have you been thinking about what you'll do with all your art supplies when we're settled? I was thinking you could maybe set up a little studio space in the spare room?      That’d be amazing, Mum! Actually having a dedicated space would be… transformative. I'm currently operating out of a corner of the living room, which isn’t ideal with Dad doing his… computer things.

Right, honestly, this is a lovely drive. Proper countryside. Beats staring at a spreadsheet all day, doesn’t it? Though honestly, even spreadsheets are looking appealing after that last data clean…      Aye, a good stretch of road. Reminds me of drives we used to take when I was courting your grandmother. Different cars, of course. None of this fancy automatic gear. Everything was manual back then, and you  earned  your journey. This is almost too easy, isn’t it?      It  is  pretty relaxing. Though, I’m still trying to figure out the logic of navigating these tiny lanes. Google Maps is having a field day. Are we nearly there yet? My internal engineer is screaming about road camber on some of these bends.      Nearly! Just another few minutes. And Dad, you always say everything was harder back then. It's your default setting.      It’s just the truth, lass! You young ‘uns have it easy. Everything handed to you on a plate. Still, look at that field over there. What are those, do you think? Look like fluffy clouds landed in a field.      Sheep. Definitely sheep. Probably Dorsets, judging by the… …never mind. Just observing. Sometimes I over-engineer things, even pastoral scenes.      You always do. Honestly, you could analyse the structural integrity of a haystack. They  are  lovely sheep though, aren't they? Reminds me of visiting your Auntie May’s farm when I was little. She had a prize-winning ram, apparently. Called him Bartholomew.      Bartholomew! Aye, a grand animal. Nearly took old Mr. Henderson’s hat right off his head one year at the county show. Ram decided his tweed was a rival. Shepherds have stories for days, you know. You learn a lot listening to them.      I imagine. My experience with farm animals is pretty limited to… seeing them in fields. Didn’t even get to go to a petting zoo as a kid, apparently. My parents were very focused on academic enrichment.      Oh, bless you. That's a bit sad! I spent half my childhood covered in mud and chasing chickens. It builds character, you know. And a good immune system.      It does, it does. Though, I remember your mother being less thrilled about the character-building aspect. Always muttering about the washing. Speaking of which, did you remember to bring a spare jumper, lass? It can get a bit nippy up at the farm.      I did, thankfully.

...Honestly, the shepherd’s pie was lovely, Mum. Really lovely. Though maybe a  little  heavy on the potato, just a tiny bit.      Oh, now don’t be starting on the potatoes, love. It wouldn't be shepherd’s pie without a proper topping, would it? Besides, your father always liked a generous portion. I’m just keeping traditions alive. How's the transcription work going, anyway? Still mountains of audio to conquer?      Aye, it  was  good, Mary. Proper comfort food. And it’s true, you always did make a good mash. Reminds me of my mother’s, actually. Speaking of work, Sarah, have you heard anything back about that grant application for the community garden?      Not yet, Dad. They said they’d be in touch by the end of the week, which is… tomorrow. I’m trying not to get my hopes up too much. It’s a lot of money, and there are so many worthy projects. It would just be amazing to get it off the ground and give the village something nice.      It’s a wonderful idea, Sarah. A really worthwhile cause. You’ve always had a good head for that sort of thing, helping others. It’s a gift. I’ve been thinking, though, about volunteering somewhere myself now that I’m properly retired. Perhaps helping with reading at the primary school. Missed being around young minds, I think.      The school’s a good shout, Mary. They always need extra hands. Though, remember Mr. Henderson, your maths teacher? The one who used to make you stand in the corner for chewing gum?      Oh,  don’t  remind me! Henderson was a tyrant! Though, surprisingly, a very effective one. I’d never have gotten through calculus if it wasn't for his relentless drilling. He wasn't pleasant, mind you, but he knew his stuff. I often wonder what happened to him. Probably retired on a tropical island, funded by years of confiscated gum.      Sounds about right! Actually, speaking of school… little Leo’s started getting a bit fussy about his homework. He says it’s ‘boring.’ Any advice from the expert? Aside from telling him to just  do  it?      Oh, Leo. He gets that from your side of the family! No, you have to make it…relatable. Find ways to connect it to things he enjoys. If it’s maths, build something with Lego. If it's writing, invent a story about his favourite dinosaur.

Right, peas and carrots are almost done. Honestly, this has been… a long evening. Parent’s evening is always a bit draining, isn't it?      Was Mrs. Davies nice? Did she say I was good at drawing?      Mrs. Davies  did  say your drawings are fantastic, sweetheart. Absolutely brimming with imagination. It was Mr. Harrison I was… dissecting feedback from.      Dissecting? Like in science? Do they dissect people?      No, darling. Not like  that  dissecting. Just…talking about how you’re doing. And, well, Mr. Harrison says you're struggling a bit with your times tables.      Times tables are  boring . They're just numbers going round and round.      I’m good at the two times! Two, four, six, eight, ten…      That's brilliant, Lily! You  are  good at your twos. But it's the seven and eight times that are giving him pause. We need to work on those a bit. Maybe we can make it a game?      Can we have dessert if we do times tables?      We can certainly talk about dessert. Now, eat your dinner. It’s chicken and, you know, perfectly normal chicken.      Mummy, at school today, Leo said people used to eat people! Is that true?      Oh, Lily… that’s a… complicated question. There were times, a long, long time ago, where people  did  things that weren’t very nice. But we don’t do that now. It’s not something to think about.      What does it  smell  like? If you ate a person?      Oh, good heavens, Thomas! Don’t be morbid! That’s… frankly a disgusting thought. I haven't a clue! And honestly, I don't  want  to know. Let’s talk about something nice! Like World Book Day! Have you decided who you're going as?      I’m going as Hermione Granger! I have the robes and everything. I’m learning spells!      I'm going as… Captain Underpants! He’s really funny. He flies around in his underwear!      Excellent choices, both of you! It’s going to be a lovely day. Right, after school tomorrow, I need to pop into town to get some fabric for Lily's costume. Thomas, your grandma called. She wants to know if you’d like to go to the circus with her on Saturday.      The circus?! Yes! With the elephants and lions?      She said there are acrobats and clowns and… well, she thinks you’d love it. It's a matinee performance, so we’ll get you back in plenty of time for bath time.

Ah, now listen to this, Mary. Young Finn down at O’Connell’s curtains is offering young lads work during the school holidays. Apparently, he’s desperate. I half expected him to offer  Oisin  a job, the wee chatterbox.      Oh, really? That  is  desperate. Finn’s usually pretty sorted. Though, honestly, Oisin with a measuring tape…I can just picture the chaos. He'd probably tell the customers the curtains were made of dragon scales.      Dagon scales! Shiny!      He gets that from your side of the family, dear. A vivid imagination is a blessing, even if it does make for interesting shopping trips. Remember young Hamish trying to convince the butcher he needed a whole sheep for a school project?      Oh, good lord, that I do. A whole sheep! But seriously, it’s good he’s talkative, isn’t it? Though, sometimes when he's explaining something...it's like he's inventing a whole new language. All these little made-up words.      He’s experimenting with language, that's all. Perfectly normal at his age. Though, I admit, deciphering "Flummox-gobble" yesterday took a solid ten minutes. It apparently meant 'hungry teddy bear'.      Flummox-gobble. Right. Speaking of the little fella, have we sorted anything concrete for his birthday? It's creeping up, isn't it?      Not entirely. I was thinking a small party here, maybe just a few of his friends from creche. I’m a bit overwhelmed by the thought of a bouncy castle in the back garden, to be honest. And your brother offered to organize something big, but…well, you know Declan. It always ends up being a  production .      Ah, Declan and his productions. A lovely man, but one must manage expectations. A small gathering sounds nice, personal.      That’s what I was thinking. We can get a cake from that bakery in the village, the one with the amazing chocolate. And maybe some balloons. I could take him and your Da to the rugby next weekend as a pre-birthday treat? Munster are playing Leinster, it’ll be a good match.      That sounds lovely, Oisin would adore that! Though, knowing him, he'll spend most of the game explaining the rules to everyone around him.      You're probably right. He was trying to explain the offside rule to the postman last week. Poor fella looked utterly baffled. Now, speaking of baffling things, I nominated myself as treasurer for the garages last month… and the paperwork!

Right, so I was thinking about it after you two were going on about obscure Scrabble strategies last week… and I reckon I’ve got a game that's even  better . It's not about points, it’s about… connections.      Oh? Better than Scrabble? That's a bold claim, Liv. I’ve spent years perfecting my two-letter word game. What have you got up your sleeve?      Yeah, you are a bit of a Scrabble fiend, aren't you, Ben? Liv, lay it on us. Is it one of those weird word association things?      Sort of! It's called "Chain Reaction." Basically, one person says a word. The next person has to say a word that's linked to it – not necessarily a synonym, could be anything related. And then the next person links to  that  word, and so on. The catch is, you have to explain  how  you've linked it. Keeps it interesting, you know? No just shouting random nouns.      Hmm, sounds… potentially chaotic. But I see the appeal. It’s less about vocabulary and more about lateral thinking. Okay, I’m game. Who starts?      I'll go! Alright, let’s start with… “Brick”.      Ooh, good one! Right, "Brick"... okay, I’m going to go with “Wall”. Obviously, bricks are used to  build  walls. Simple enough. Your turn, Ben.      Wall... right. This is trickier than I anticipated. Okay, I’ll go with “Berlin”. Because of, well, the Berlin Wall. A historically significant wall! Bit obvious, maybe?      Not at all, a perfectly valid link! Alright, Berlin… hmm… Okay, I’m going with “Techno”. Berlin is famously known for its techno music scene. It’s a huge part of the city’s identity now.      Ooh, nice one, Liam! I wouldn’t have got that connection. Right, “Techno”… that makes me think of… “Pulse”. The pulse of the music y’know? The beat.      Very clever. “Pulse”... Alright, I'm going to push this towards something slightly academic... “Cardiology.” Because a pulse is obviously vital for cardiology, the study of the heart. Show-off, I know.      You  are  a show-off! Using your engineering brain to hijack the game. Cardiology… that gets me thinking of… “Hospital”. A pretty straightforward link, I suppose.      That’s a really solid one. “Hospital”… this is where it gets tricky. Right… okay… “Waiting Room”. Because, honestly, who  likes  waiting rooms in hospitals? They’re the worst.      Accurate. “Waiting Room”... this is good.

Oh my god, look at this one! Remember this? Graduation day. You looked terrified. Absolutely  terrified .      Hey! I wasn’t terrified, I was… contemplating the vast, uncaring void of post-university life. Big difference. And you were trying to sneak a chip butty into the hall. Don't pretend you weren’t.      Slander! Pure, unadulterated slander! I merely assessed the structural integrity of my handbag in relation to potential snack containment. Besides, that ceremony was  ages  long. I needed sustenance. I nearly fell asleep, honestly. I could have napped right there, under my mortarboard.      You would have. You can fall asleep anywhere. Remember that lecture on post-structuralism in second year? You were out cold, drooling slightly, for a good twenty minutes. Professor Davies nearly had a conniption fit.      Don’t remind me. That man. Honestly. Anyway, what have  you  been up to? Aside from meticulously planning your descent into existential dread on graduation day, obviously. Anything interesting happen this week?      Not much, to be fair. Still wrestling with this dissertation. It’s like… the more I write, the less I understand. It's about the impact of regional music scenes - specifically, the early 90s Madchester scene - and I'm starting to think it was all just a really good marketing ploy.      Ooh, controversial! But I kinda see what you mean. Happy Mondays, The Stone Roses... brilliant, yeah, but did they  create  something new, or did they just package up existing vibes really well?      Exactly! And everyone’s acting like it’s some huge, vital cultural movement. I need to find a more critical angle. I’ve been listening to loads of stuff trying to get inspired. Found some obscure indie bands from Liverpool at the time. Surprisingly good.      Oh yeah, Liverpool had some gems back then. Remember Jamie? Jamie Williams? He was obsessed with The La's. Drove everyone mad. Speaking of which, have you heard from him recently? I saw he posted something on Facebook about a new job...      Yeah, he’s working down in London now, apparently. Something in finance. Can you believe it? Jamie Williams, the king of scruffy indie fashion, in finance. The world’s gone mad. He sounded… resigned on the phone last time I spoke to him.      That's a shame. He always swore he'd be a musician. Though, knowing Jamie, he probably still plays guitar in a smoky pub somewhere on weekends.

Right, so I’ve gone over the plans  again . And I'm still convinced Old Man Hemmings is going to try and derail everything at the planning committee meeting. He just doesn’t want  anyone  changing the streetscape, does he? It’s ridiculous.      Hemmings is… Hemmings. A force of nature dedicated to preserving the aesthetic of 1950s semi-detached suburbia. It’s his life’s work, apparently. But you’ve prepped brilliantly, haven’t you? The report’s solid, the neighbours we’ve spoken to are supportive…      Supportive, yes, but will their support translate to actually  speaking  at the meeting? That’s the question. Half of them just nodded politely and said, “Oh, very nice,” then scurried back inside. They're terrified of him.      People are. He's got that booming voice and that…that unwavering conviction. Remember when he tried to get Mrs. Peterson fined for having a pink garden gnome?      How could I forget? Absolute carnage. Anyway, back to the house. I’m worried about how I’ve structured my presentation. Is it too… technical? I wanted to emphasise the sustainability aspects, the use of reclaimed materials, the solar panel integration, but I’m worried it'll just go over their heads.      It's good to include that stuff, absolutely. Shows you’ve thought it through. But maybe lead with the benefit to the community? Highlight how the extra space will allow you to run the workshops you’ve been talking about for ages - the pottery classes, the local history group… That’s what will get their attention. They’re a council committee, they care about community engagement.      You’re right. I keep getting bogged down in the specifics. Focusing on the ‘why’ rather than the ‘how’. Okay, community benefit first. Then the details. And  then  maybe a quick mention of the reclaimed materials and solar panels. Don't want to sound like a zealot.      Precisely. And don’t get drawn into arguments with Hemmings. Just politely but firmly reiterate your points. Let him rant, then smoothly steer the conversation back to the agenda. Think of it like… herding cats.      That is a remarkably apt description. It's just… selling the house was relatively straightforward. Estate agents, viewings, offers. This is a completely different beast. Dealing with bureaucracy and…and Hemmings! It feels so much more exposing.      It is. Selling the house was transactional. This is about getting permission to  build  something, to change something.

Honestly, this Bolognese is taking  forever . I thought I’d be a culinary whiz by now, living away from Mum and all, but it's just… sauce. How hard can sauce be?      Harder than you think, apparently. You’ve been battling that sauce for a good hour now. Is it the onions? You always struggle with the onions.      No, the onions are fine! I actually managed to dice them without crying this time, which is a win. It’s just… it’s not thickening up. It’s like tomato soup pretending to be Bolognese. And I promised a proper comfort meal after the week I’ve had.      Rough week, then? Still dealing with Mr. Henderson and his insistence that the marketing report needed  another  colour-coded spreadsheet?      You know him! And yes. He actually asked me to justify the font choice. The  font ! I swear, I'm starting to understand why people have stress-related breakdowns. How’s work been? Any drama on the ward?      Relatively quiet, thankfully. We had a new patient admitted yesterday, really sweet older gentleman. A bit confused, but mostly just lonely. It's… grounding, you know? Reminds you what the actual important things are. Though, Mrs. Gable is convinced Mr. Peterson is stealing her biscuits again. It’s a whole saga.      Oh, bless her. She lives for drama, doesn’t she? Speaking of drama, did you see old Chloe Davies posted pictures from her hen do? It looked insane. Vegas, apparently.      No way! Chloe Davies? Vegas? That’s… a bit much, isn’t it? Last I heard, she was saving up for a deposit on a house.      I know, right? Her fiancé’s parents are paying, I think. Apparently, he’s doing  very  well in tech. It just feels… different. Remember when we all just went to that dodgy karaoke bar in town for her 18th?      And someone spilled a whole pint of cider over Sarah Jenkins’ new dress. Good times. It's weird how people change though. Makes you wonder what we'll all be like in ten years.      Honestly, don't even. I'm still trying to figure out what I'm going to be having for dinner, let alone the next decade. This sauce... It needs something. Maybe a dash of red wine?      Definitely red wine. And maybe a side of gossip about old Mrs. Higgins? I swear she's been watching us through the window all afternoon.

Right, honestly, David Attenborough could narrate a washing machine instruction manual and I’d be hooked. It’s just… the  tone , innit?      Absolutely. He makes everything sound epic. Though, I am slightly distracted by this online ad that keeps popping up. "Lose 10lbs in a week!" Honestly, the audacity. It’s always the same rubbish, isn't it?      Tell me about it. They prey on people, those ads. Makes you wonder who actually falls for that stuff. Though, I suppose if you're feeling a bit… wobbly… after a weekend of takeaway, it might  seem  appealing. Speaking of wobbly, I was thinking we should actually  do  something about the state of the kitchen.      Oh, here we go. The kitchen critique. It's not  that  bad. Just…lived in. And I was working late yesterday, remember? Sorting out that case file with the young lad showing signs of dyslexia. It's fascinating, the brain, really, how differently people process information.      Yeah, you were saying about it. It's awful, though, isn't it? Kids getting left behind. Makes you feel helpless. But still, the dishes are piling up. I was thinking, Saturday morning, car boot sale? We could clear out some of this stuff, make a bit of dosh, and then treat ourselves to a proper cleaning spree later?      Ooh, that’s a good shout! I’ve got that old printer I need to get rid of, and a stack of books I’ll never read again. You could take some of your old band gear, maybe? You've got that amp gathering dust in the spare room.      Now you’re talkin'! Though, knowing my luck, someone will try and haggle me down to a fiver for it. Remember that time I tried to sell my guitar at a car boot sale and someone offered me a packet of biscuits?      Oh my god, yes! And you were so outraged! You gave them a lecture on the value of musical instruments! It was brilliant. Seriously though, car boot sales are a goldmine for weird and wonderful things. Like that time I found that vintage film camera...      Ah, that was a good find. You’re always unearthing treasures. Did you catch that documentary about NLP last week? Neuro-Linguistic Programming? It was on Channel 4, I think. All about how your language shapes your thinking. Pretty mind-blowing.      I meant to, but I got stuck dealing with a crisis at work.

…Honestly, I’m starting to think this whole house hunting thing is a complete waste of time. Every place either needs a full gutting or is already massively overpriced. It's just… demoralising.      Tell me about it! We’ve been looking for months. London’s obviously insane, but even looking a bit further out, it’s ridiculous. You get a tiny box for an absolute fortune. Are you still aiming for Solihull, then?      Yeah, still the goal. Good schools are the priority, obviously, with little Leo starting soon. But I just feel… pressured. Like we  have  to buy now, but the numbers just aren’t making sense.      It’s a horrible feeling, that pressure. Don't feel you  have  to. Especially with interest rates where they are. We rented for ages, and honestly, it gave us breathing room to actually save, and be sure of what we wanted.      Yeah, renting isn’t the enemy, you know? People act like it's a sign of failure. I’m pretty content renting in Birmingham for now. Access to the city centre is great, and avoids the commute nightmare. Speaking of which, did anyone see that article about the clean air zone expanding? Absolute chaos.      Oh, don't even get me started on the clean air zone! It's a nightmare for anyone with an older car. I was talking to a taxi driver the other day…he was fuming. But back to houses, Liam, have you tried looking at new builds at all? They're often offering incentives.      A couple. They look… soulless. And often they’re built on former industrial estates. I worry about what’s  under  the foundations, if you know what I mean. Plus, the Help to Buy scheme stuff feels a bit… dodgy, doesn’t it?      It does, a bit. And the quality isn’t always amazing. Speaking of dodgy, I’ve been trying this new AI writing app for work. It’s supposed to help with drafting articles, but frankly, it just churns out bland, repetitive drivel. It needs so much editing it’s not worth the effort.      Oh, I've heard about those! The ethical side of things worries me too. Are journalists even going to  have  jobs in five years? I’m trying to embrace technology in the classroom, but it's a double-edged sword. My students are relying on spellcheck way too much – their actual spelling is getting worse!

...and honestly, the landlord looked like he hadn’t updated a single thing since Queen Victoria was a girl. Damp patches everywhere, floral wallpaper peeling… but it was all we could afford, you see. A dentist starting out, even with a qualification, doesn’t exactly walk into a fortune.      Oh, you’re telling me! Though, I think my first place was marginally better. A little terraced house near the school. The kitchen sink leaked constantly, but the garden was decent. I remember spending every weekend battling bindweed. It was almost a full-time job on top of marking essays!      It was the same for us, wasn’t it, David? We were lucky to get anything at all. Almondsbury was…well, a village then, really.
