Oh, Harold, you haven't changed a bit! Always noticing the biscuits. And yes, it  is  a new armchair. My back's been playing up, you see, and this one just… swallows you whole. Blissful. Though I can’t see half of what's on the telly from  in  it. David, dear, are you still fiddling with that globe?      Just thinking, actually. You were talking about holidays, and it got me pondering places we haven't been. Thinking maybe a bit of Yorkshire, actually. I've got a colleague who raves about the Dales.      Yorkshire, eh? Hmm. Never been a huge fan, to be honest. Too… flat for my liking. Give me Norfolk any day, all those little hills and the coast. Though getting  to  the coast’s become a bit of a mission these days, with this leg.      Oh, Harold, don't start on that leg again. It's a bit frustrating for everyone. Yorkshire’s lovely! Remember young Thomas’s school project, David? The one on the industrial revolution? He spent weeks researching all the mills and things in Yorkshire. Fascinating, really. He even wanted us to go, but… well, school projects.      I remember Thomas’s project. He was a bright lad. Actually, the Dales have some incredible underground systems - old mining tunnels, naturally formed caves. Might be interesting. We could even look at doing it via youth hostels, keep the costs down. Remember those, Doreen?      Oh, my goodness, youth hostels! That takes me back. Rough as anything, most of them! Remember that one in the Lake District, David? Shared a room with… well, let's just say a very enthusiastic German walking club. Harold would  not  have approved.      Enthusiastic Germans? Sounds like a nightmare! No, thank you very much. Give me a proper hotel, or even better, staying put. Keeps things simple. Although, I will admit, that trip to London with your mum, Doreen… now  that  was a proper adventure. Even if getting around on the Underground was a bit of a struggle.      The Underground is a beast, isn’t it? I commute into Birmingham sometimes, and even  that’s  a challenge. Speaking of challenges, how’s the garden coming along, Harold?

Right, so I’ve been lookin’ at flights again. Honestly, this is a nightmare. Every time I refresh, the price jumps up another tenner. It's like they  want  you to pay more, innit?      Tell me about it. I swear, algorithms are specifically designed to stress us out. Have you tried incognito mode? Sometimes that helps. Though honestly, I think it’s a myth.      Aye, I did. Didn’t make a jot of difference. I ended up checkin’ Skyscanner, Kayak, even bloody British Airways direct. It’s all the same. I’m starting to think February in Barcelona is just a pipe dream.      No, don't say that! We  need  February in Barcelona. I've already mentally prepped my wardrobe. What are we lookin' at price-wise now, roughly?      Best I’ve seen is, like, £180 return. But that's with a connection in… Luton. Luton! I’d rather swim the channel.      Oh god, Luton. You’re right to be wary of that. It’s essentially another universe. Plus, think about the travel time. We want to actually  be  in Barcelona, not spend the entire holiday getting there. My uni friend went through Luton once. Said it was an experience she’d rather forget. Involving questionable sandwiches and a very long wait.      See? Even you think it's bad! I was hoping for something direct from Stansted, but they’re all sky high. It's just... I’m tryin’ to be sensible with money, y’know? This new role, it’s good, but not ‘splash-the-cash-on-luxury-holidays’ good, not yet anyway.      I get it. I'm the same. Being a Production Controller sounds fancy, but it mostly involves spreadsheets and apologising to people when things inevitably go wrong. Though, the pay  is  decent, so maybe we should just bite the bullet? It's ages since we’ve had a proper girls’ trip.      True. Last time was Edinburgh, ages ago. And that was… rainy. Very, very rainy. Barcelona's sunnier, at least. It’s just… my mum keeps goin’ on about how I need to save for a deposit on a house.      Your mum. Always with the house talk. She started on me about it at Christmas. “Stable investment, dear, stable investment…” Honestly, sometimes I think she just wants grandkids so she has an excuse to buy miniature furniture.      Exactly! She’s convinced I’ll be living in her spare room forever if I don’t get on the property ladder.

…and honestly, the price of a loaf of bread these days. It’s criminal, isn’t it? Used to be you could get a decent white sliced for… well, less than half what they're charging now. It's all these fancy sourdoughs and artisan whatever-you-calls-it that've driven the price up, I reckon. Nobody  needs  sourdough every day.      Dad, you always say that! But it's not just the bread, is it? Everything’s gone up. I was at the supermarket yesterday, and a bag of apples… seriously? Nearly four pounds! I nearly put them back. I'm trying to budget, obviously, with the mortgage and everything, but it feels like I’m constantly playing catch-up.      Tell me about it, love. I’m on a fixed income, and every little helps. Though, to be fair, I get a bit of a discount at Tesco now, being a senior citizen. Makes a difference, even if it’s just a few pennies. Still, it’s the energy bills that worry me most. They’ve skyrocketed, haven't they?      Skyrocketed is putting it mildly, Margaret. It’s daylight robbery. Remember when British Gas used to be… well, British? Now it’s all foreign companies, and they don’t care a jot about the average punter. I’ve been with them for donkey’s years, loyal as they come, and what do I get? Price hikes! I considered switching, but then you read all these stories about the smaller companies going bust… it's a minefield.      It is. I’ve been looking at Octopus Energy, apparently they’re quite good, and their customer service is better. I’m still with Bulb - or, rather, Octopus  through  Bulb, and it’s been a nightmare trying to get a sensible bill. They keep sending me estimates, and they're always wrong. It's infuriating. I spend half my life on hold with them.      Oh, customer service… don’t get me started. I had an issue with my mobile phone provider last month. Took me three hours on the phone, being passed from pillar to post, before someone finally understood what I was saying! And then they tried to sell me an upgrade. Honestly, the cheek!      Mobile phones. Another money pit. I have a simple one, just for emergencies. Can't be doing with all those apps and gadgets. Just give me a phone that rings and lets me make calls.

…and honestly, the sunsets in Cape Town are just  unreal . Like, photos don’t even do them justice. You just…feel small, y'know? I keep meaning to get all the photos printed, but uni's just swallowed me whole.      Oh, I  know  that feeling. I spent ages sorting through photos from last summer in Greece, then just…didn't bother printing them. Too much faff. Cape Town though… that sounds incredible. Was it really different to being here? I’ve never been further south than Cornwall, to be honest.      Cornwall’s lovely! Though not exactly the same vibe, is it? I always fancied a holiday in South Africa, just for the wildlife. Imagine seeing a proper lion in the wild! We've got deer back home, but it's not quite the same, is it?      Deer are lovely, mind you. We get loads around my mam's place in Penarth. But lions... definitely a step up in the majestic stakes. I'm more of a small, fluffy animal person myself. Give me a Welsh Corgi any day. They’re the best. Have you seen the ones with the ridiculously short legs?      Ooh, corgis  are  cute! My nana used to have one. Little terror, but so sweet. I'm a sucker for a good dog, honestly. Speaking of sweet, anyone fancy a slice of that carrot cake I made yesterday? It’s in there.      Carrot cake? Yes, please! You’re a lifesaver, Ella. Uni food is… an experience. It’s mostly beige. Cape Town was  so  different. Everything felt a bit…brighter. The colours, the people. And the food! Bobotie, have you ever heard of it? It's like a spiced minced meat dish, baked with an egg custard topping. Honestly, I'm craving it now.      Bobotie? No, I haven't! Sounds… interesting. I'm quite boring with food, I admit. Give me a good roast dinner, or a proper Sunday lunch, and I’m happy. It's comfort food, innit? We had a good one at my parents' last weekend, but it's not the same trying to recreate it in a student flat.      Roast dinners are  grand . Though, you can't beat a good Irish stew when you’re missing home. My mam makes the best one – seriously, it's a family legend. Full of lamb and potatoes and everything. I tried to make it once in halls, and it was… questionable.

...Honestly, the sheer  volume  of reading for this Art History essay is ridiculous. It’s not even about analysing a piece, it’s about the socio-political context of Victorian landscape painting. Like, who  cares  that much? Old men with beards, probably.      Sounds… stimulating. You alright though? You've been muttering about Ruskin for the last half hour. Need a distraction? I’m about to demolish someone on Apex.      Distraction would be lovely, actually. But I really should… I’m just feeling so overwhelmed. And it’s making me think about, like, the point of all this. Is this what I’ll be doing when I’m eighty? Analysing landscapes? I picture myself just… knitting. Or yelling at grandchildren.      Eighty? Blimey, that's a lifetime away. You’ll probably be a famous art curator, jetting around the world, discovering the next big thing. Or, yeah, maybe knitting. Depends how much you like yarn. Grandchildren are optional, obviously.      Easy for you to say, you're conquering virtual worlds. You're a digital warrior! I’m wrestling with the past. Still, it’s making me think about time, you know? Like, my nan, she always used to say she felt like she blinked and her life just… went.      That’s proper bleak, Sal. Don't let that get you down. Nan's are good at dramatic pronouncements. Mine used to tell me ginger people don't have souls. Which, obviously, is nonsense. But the point is, they embellish!      True. She  was  a bit of a character. But still, thinking about ending up old and… forgetting things, feeling useless. It’s a bit scary. Do you ever think about that?      Sometimes. Mostly when my lecturers start rambling about post-structuralism or something. Makes you feel ancient just  listening  to it. But I think focusing on enjoying things now is… useful. Like, you  like  art, right? Even Victorian landscape painting, deep down?      I do! I genuinely do. It's just...the academic dissection of it sometimes sucks the joy out. It feels like you’re meant to be critical, to deconstruct everything. Which is fine, but sometimes I just want to look at a pretty picture and think “that's nice”.      Exactly! You’re allowed to just  feel  things. And honestly, maybe old age isn’t so bad. Think of all the art you’ll have had time to appreciate. You could become the expert, the one who actually  does  care about those Victorian landscapes.

Honestly, this butternut squash is a  nightmare  to peel. It feels like I'm wrestling a small, orange boulder.      Tell me about it. I tried one last week and nearly took a finger off. You alright though? You're looking a bit… stressed. Long day at work?      You have no idea. Old Mr. Henderson decided  today  was the day to completely re-scope the marketing campaign. Three weeks before launch. Three weeks! It's just… constant firefighting. And then Sarah emailed saying she needs me to cover her presentation on Friday because her nan is poorly.      Oh, no, poor Sarah’s nan. That’s awful. But seriously, Mr. Henderson sounds like a menace. You need a raise, just for surviving him. Is that why you’re making this ridiculously healthy butternut squash soup? Self-soothing through vegetables?      Something like that. It’s supposed to be good for stress, apparently. Though right now, I'm mostly stressed about ending up in A&E with a squash-related injury. How was your day? Anything more calming than rogue marketing briefs and elderly relatives?      Surprisingly, yes. Relatively. It was… emotionally draining, as always, but no major crises. Mostly supporting a new patient settling in, getting to know her story. It’s just… hearing everything people go through, you know? It stays with you. It makes Mr. Henderson sound like a mildly irritating toddler.      Definitely. It puts things into perspective, doesn’t it? You’re proper amazing, doing that job. I don’t know how you manage. I’d be a complete mess.      It’s rewarding, when it is. Though sometimes I just need to switch off. Speaking of switching off, are we still on for drinks with Liam and Chloe on Saturday?      Oh, yes! Absolutely. I texted Chloe earlier, she was saying Liam's trying to learn how to make cocktails, so prepare for some… experimental beverages.      Oh, God. That sounds terrifying and hilarious all at once. He's got the enthusiasm, that's for sure. Remember that attempt at paella last year? It was basically just rice flavoured with despair.      Don’t remind me! It took a week to get the burnt smell out of the flat. So, are you still seeing Ben? I haven’t seen him around much lately.      We… we’re taking a break.      Oh. Right. A break. That sounds… complicated. Everything alright? You don’t have to tell me if you don’t want to, obviously.

Right, so I’ve had a proper look at this consent form for the seminar attendees. It’s… thorough, isn’t it? A bit  too  thorough, maybe? I'm thinking folk might be put off filling it in if it looks like a legal document.      You’re not wrong, Brenda. It’s covering all the bases, I’ll grant it that – GDPR and all the rest – but it feels a bit intimidating. Especially for undergrads. They’ll just glaze over and tick ‘yes’ to everything without reading it.      And that defeats the object entirely, doesn’t it, Fiona? We need informed consent. I was hoping for something… simpler. A paragraph explaining what data we’ll collect – email addresses for follow-up materials mostly, and maybe a quick feedback form – and how we'll use it. And a clear opt-out.      Aye, exactly! Simpler is better. I mean, we're not asking for their medical histories, are we? It feels like we are with some of this wording. “Potential for data to be anonymized and used in future published research…” Good grief. We’re running a workshop on negotiating with Japanese clients, not conducting a study on the neurological effects of intercultural communication!      You’re right. It’s a bit overblown. I think Legal just blanket-applies this to everything. I’ll drop them an email, point out the context, and see if they have a shorter version or can at least tailor it.      Good shout, Fiona. While you’re doing that, shall we have another run-through of the seminar structure? I’ve been thinking about how we divide up the ‘high-context vs. low-context’ section. It's crucial for understanding the differences, but can be a bit dry if not presented well.      I reckon I can handle that one, lass. I've spent years dealing with European companies - Germans, especially - who are right at the low-context end of the scale. I can illustrate it with some funny anecdotes about directness versus politeness. Gets people engaged.      Excellent. That’s much better than me just lecturing on Hall’s theory. Anecdotes always land better. I was thinking I could take the section on non-verbal communication. Building rapport, appropriate gestures, that sort of thing. I recently spent a month in Brazil with a project team, and the cultural differences in body language were… eye-opening.      Perfect. I'll take the negotiation strategies then.

Honestly, the feedback on those essays was  exhausting  today. Three hours straight of dissecting undergraduate attempts at post-structuralism. Three hours! You wouldn’t believe some of the things they try to pass off as original thought.      Sounds brutal. Worse than your usual Friday essay mountain? I had a particularly…enthusiastic debate with a student about the merits of Marxist film theory. He seemed convinced  Transformers  was a profound critique of late-stage capitalism.      Oh, goodness. That’s… dedicated. Though, I suppose you could  stretch  it. Mine were mostly complaining that Baudrillard is ‘too confusing’. As if it’s his fault they haven’t done the reading! It makes you question everything, doesn't it? Like, am  I  even explaining it well enough?      You're a brilliant lecturer, Elara. Don’t let a few confused undergrads get you down. You always make it accessible. It’s me who struggles with the relentless optimism of some of my students. Everything is going to be fixed by renewable energy and collective action! Sweet, but… realistically?      It’s good to have hope, though, isn’t it? A little naive optimism is preferable to the bleakness I sometimes feel after marking. Speaking of bleakness…did you manage to speak to the estate agent again about that little courtyard house?      I did. And it’s… complicated. They’ve had another offer. Apparently, a family are moving from Shanghai, wanting something ‘authentic’. Which, apparently, trumps our perfectly reasonable offer.      ‘Authentic’. Ugh. That’s code for ‘Westerners willing to pay over the odds’. Honestly, this house hunt is driving me insane. I just want a garden! A tiny, postage-stamp-sized garden where I can grow herbs and not feel like I’m living in a concrete box.      I know, love. It’s frustrating. It feels like every place remotely decent is either ridiculously expensive or needs a full renovation. That one in the French Concession looked promising, but the plumbing was… questionable. Remember the photos?      Don’t remind me. It looked like something out of a horror film. We’d have been wading through damp for the first year. And honestly, I'm starting to wonder if we should just accept that we'll be renting indefinitely.      No. We won't. We’ve been saving for too long. We just need to be patient, and maybe adjust our expectations slightly. Perhaps aim for something a little further out, where the prices haven’t quite reached London levels yet.

Honestly, I made way too much. Gran would have a fit if she saw this. She  never  wasted a crumb. Remember how she’d save the pasta water for the soup stock?      Oh god, yes. The pasta water was sacred. And every leftover roast chicken bone became the base for something new. It's a world away from people chucking perfectly good food now, isn’t it? I saw a student at uni the other day binning a half-eaten sandwich. Just… binning it.      Unbelievable! It drives me mental. I try to drill it into my Year 8s at school – the environmental impact, the ethical issues, the fact people are  hungry  – but it's like talking to a wall sometimes. They’re so wrapped up in… well, everything else.      It’s tough. They haven’t had that ingrained upbringing, like we did. Seeing Gran scraping every last bit of jam from the jar. Still, maybe some of it sinks in. You're doing good work. So, how's teaching going generally? Still battling the system?      Battling is putting it mildly. They’re talking about further curriculum changes, more focus on “employability skills”. Which is fine, I guess, but it feels like we're churning out kids for specific jobs and not actually  educating  them. They need to be able to  think , not just code or fit pipes! What about you? How’s the engineering world treating you? Still designing robots to take everyone's jobs?      Not quite world domination yet. Though, the automation side of things is definitely ramping up. We’re working on advanced robotics for manufacturing, mostly. It's… a bit unsettling, to be honest. The potential for job displacement is huge. It feels less like progress and more like accelerating towards a future where lots of people are redundant.      Exactly! And what are schools supposed to  do  with that? "Right, Timmy, your future involves competing with a highly efficient machine." It's not exactly inspiring careers advice, is it? It's all "STEM this, STEM that," but nobody’s talking about the broader implications.      It reminds me a bit of what Dad said about his old firm. Remember him talking about how it used to be a ‘closed shop’? You had a job for life basically, and entry was pretty much through knowing someone. It’s completely different now. No security, constant retraining…      Completely different. And Dad always used to say it was the unions that secured that stability, even if it wasn't perfect.

Honestly, this risotto is taking  forever . I thought I was good in the kitchen, but this creamy texture…it’s proving elusive. It's a labour of love, darling. And you  are  good in the kitchen, you just get impatient. Remember that time you tried to make macarons? Now  that  was a disaster. Okay, point taken. The macaron incident is best left buried. But seriously, work’s been… draining. I’m starting to question everything. All the long hours, the grant applications… is it actually  making  a difference? Oh, the existential postdoc crisis, is it? I thought we’d avoided that one for a while. What’s specifically got you down? It’s not the study on stress in new mothers again, is it? That was heavy. It’s not  just  that. That’s always… weighing on me, you know? Seeing those data, knowing the pressures they’re under. But it's also the constant feeling of needing to justify everything. Like I have to  prove  that understanding the psychological impact of long-term illness is worthwhile. Some of the senior academics just seem to want hard numbers, measurable outcomes… it feels like the nuance gets lost. Ugh. Sounds infuriatingly familiar. It's similar in education, honestly. Everything’s about ‘raising attainment’, ‘closing the gap’… but it’s all framed around test scores. They want quick fixes, demonstrable progress in spreadsheets. They forget about the whole child, the context, the  why  behind the data. I spend half my time explaining to people that assessing a kid isn’t just about giving them a number; it’s about understanding their individual needs. Exactly! And it's exhausting trying to convey that. I was talking to Professor Davies today, and he just kept going on about 'impact factors' and 'publications in high-ranking journals.' I just wanted to scream, "But what about the people the research is  about ?!" He sounds… delightful. It’s the academic equivalent of box-ticking, isn't it? And it stifles creativity. You're doing genuinely good work, Liam. Helping people understand their health, their behaviours… that  is  impactful. Sometimes you just need to step away from the metrics and remember that. It's easy to get lost in it. And then there's Mum constantly asking when I’m going to get a ‘proper job’. Oh, Mum. She'll never understand the intricacies of a postdoctoral research position.

…and honestly, Harold, seeing those little blue tits nesting in Mrs. Higgins’ garden just brightened my whole week. Such a tiny, vibrant blue. You wouldn’t believe it. Reminded me of… well, never mind. Just a nice little thing.      Blue tits, eh? Aye, they are a cheerful little spark, aren’t they? Used to get 'em nesting in the ivy on our shed, back in Costessey. Mother used to put out crumbs for 'em. Wouldn’t get many now, not with all the new builds. Everything’s concrete and straight lines now, isn't it? No room for a bit of wildness.      It's sad, isn't it? That loss of habitat. It's the same with the kids at school. They’ve no concept of just letting things  be . Everything’s got to be structured, scheduled… They don’t appreciate the simple pleasures, like watching birds.      That’s terribly true, Peter. It’s like they’re rushing through life already. Though, I suppose  we  didn’t always slow down enough either, did we, Harold? Always chasing something. A bigger house, a better car…      Houses. Always houses. Seems to be all anyone ever talks about, doesn't it? Always wanting a bigger, better one. We never did have much in that department, me and your mother. This little place in Norwich was… comfortable. Enough. But folk always want more, don't they? Even when more brings more worry.      It’s the societal pressure, I think. The constant comparison. You see what others have, and you feel like you’re falling behind. I’ve got a mortgage still, even after all these years teaching. Trying to help the kids get a foot on the ladder, and it feels…impossible sometimes.      Oh, Peter, don’t I know that. Foot on the ladder… It’s a joke, isn’t it? They’re practically asking for a wing and a prayer these days. It’s just… worrying. Worrying about them, worrying about the future. It gets you down, doesn't it?      It does. It really does. I haven’t been… myself, lately. Not since… well, you know. Since Margaret went. It's not just the missing her, although God, I miss her dreadfully. It's the… the emptiness. The silence. Used to moan about her talking, now I’d give anything to hear her ramble on about the price of tomatoes.      I can only imagine, Harold.

Honestly, I don’t know  what  I’d do without this hand cream. My skin gets so dry teaching, constantly washing my hands after helping the kids with their art. It’s like sandpaper otherwise. Have you tried anything new lately? You always seem to be on top of the beauty front.      Oh, that’s awful! Teachers’ hands  must  get wrecked. No, not massively new, actually. I’ve been really into perfecting my gel nails at home, that’s been my obsession. Less money than going to the salon, and I can experiment. Did a really lovely dusky rose colour last week.      Ooh, nice! I’ve always been a bit intimidated by gel nails. I always worry I’ll mess it up and end up with peeling, half-done disasters. I usually just go for a regular polish, or sometimes just…nothing. I'm a bit rubbish at keeping on top of it.      It takes a bit of practice, definitely. The key is a really good base coat and  thin  layers. Don’t try to get it perfect in one go, you know? And a good topcoat is essential. I watched loads of YouTube tutorials, honestly. There’s a girl, Sam’s Nails, she’s brilliant. I could send you the link.      That would be amazing, actually! I’m perpetually stuck in a beauty rut. It’s always the same - mascara, a bit of blush, and that hand cream. Speaking of ruts, have you seen Sarah lately? She’s completely changed her hair!      No! What’s she done? Last I saw her she was still rocking that long, blonde, slightly frizzy style.      She’s gone for a bob! A proper, sharp bob. And she's dyed it a proper fiery red. I barely recognised her at the supermarket yesterday. She looked… fantastic, actually. Really suits her.      Wow! Sarah always played it safe. Good for her! I sometimes wish  I  was brave enough to do something drastic. I’ve been thinking about getting some layers cut in, but I’m scared of ending up looking like a poodle.      Oh, you wouldn’t! Your hair’s naturally quite thick. Layers would look lovely, give it some movement. It can get a bit…flat, can’t it?      It does, doesn't it? That's why I keep thinking about it. And I saw this advert for a hair mask, one with argan oil, supposed to be amazing for shine.

…and honestly, the parking situation 'round the World Museum is a nightmare now, isn't it? Remember when you could just pull up on William Brown Street? Forget about it. It's all pay-by-app, and half the time, the signal’s rubbish.      Tell me about it. Tried to take Ms. Doherty, one of the families I work with, there last month. Ended up parking near the Catholic Cathedral and walking. By the time we got  to  the dinosaurs, she was knackered! Little Mia was buzzing though, bless her. It’s just… frustrating when you're trying to do something nice and it’s immediately complicated by a fiver for an hour of parking.      Exactly! It's like they  want  you to stay away. Speaking of complicated, how's work been? Still battling the council for resources, I imagine?      You know it. It's perpetually a fire-fighting exercise. Had a really tough case this week, a teenager, been sofa surfing for months. Trying to get him stable housing feels… impossible some days. But, you know, little wins. Got him an appointment with the youth mental health team, at least. What about you? Still molding young minds into linguistic geniuses?      Trying to! It’s… exhausting. Year 11s are preparing for their mocks, so it’s just red pens and endless essay marking. But I’m actually starting to think about doing a Masters.      No way! Really? Doing what?      Applied Linguistics. I had an interview last week, actually. At the uni.      You clever sausage! How did it go? Was it awful? You always look like you're about to be sick before interviews.      It wasn’t  awful . More…intense. They grilled me on my research ideas. I'm thinking of looking at dialect levelling in Liverpool. How much Scouse is actually changing with younger generations… it’s fascinating. But it's expensive, isn’t it? Even with the loan…      It is a chunk of change, definitely. But think of the career boost! And honestly, the research sounds brilliant. You’d be perfect for it. You practically  speak  the history of the city in your accent. Speaking of expensive, have you even started thinking about Christmas presents yet?      Don't even go there! My nan's already sending me links to catalogues. She wants to know what I want for  her  present, which is just… baffling. I told her a quiet night in, but she won’t have any of it.

…and honestly, the whole thing just feels  exhausting . It’s not even about Mark being a bad dad – he’s not, he really isn’t. It's just… the constant negotiation. The “my mum said…” or “at my house, we…” It's like I'm permanently mediating a tiny UN summit.      Oh, I can imagine. It’s a different dynamic, isn’t it? You're trying to build a family unit, but there are these pre-existing rules and loyalties. It’s not like starting fresh. And trying to navigate that  and  the emotional landscape of a kid adjusting to… well, to everything.      Exactly! And it’s Leo, bless him, he’s a good kid. But he's fourteen! He’s already, you know, testing boundaries. And I feel like I'm instantly the bad guy if I try to reinforce anything that differs from what his mum allows. She’s…well, she’s lovely, but she definitely prioritises being ‘the fun one’.      Oh, the ‘fun mum’. A classic. It’s hard when you feel like you're always the one laying down the law. Though, to be fair, being the ‘fun one’ sounds pretty appealing after a year and a half of toddlerhood. Honestly, sometimes I feel like all I do is wipe noses and break up battles over Duplo bricks. Speaking of which, I think I found a blue one wedged in my hair earlier…      Oh, Hazel. The glamorous life! But seriously, it must be isolating sometimes, not having… well, you know, a professional outlet. Apart from being a super-mum, of course.      It is. It’s… a strange shift. I always thought I’d be doing something ‘important’, something with my degree. And then, bam. Tiny human demands all your time and brain space. I miss the intellectual challenge, the feeling of…contributing in a different way. I'm thankful I have you to talk to, though. It’s easy to get lost inside four walls and a mountain of laundry.      Any time, honestly. And don't sell yourself short, being a mum  is  important. Crucially so. But I get it. That need for something…  yours . Something that's just about  you . It's the same with Mark and me, sometimes. He gets so focused on his work and Leo that I feel like I’m just… managing things. He means well, he truly does, but it’s easy to lose sight of what  I  want.

…and honestly, I spent  hours  scrolling through Pinterest last night. It's a total time sink, isn't it? Specifically, I was trying to get ideas for Mum’s birthday. Sixty, you know? It feels…big.      Big is an understatement. Sixty. Blimey. Pinterest, though? That’s…dedicated. I mostly end up looking at ridiculously expensive kitchens I’ll never have. What were you thinking? A themed party? A weekend away?      No, no parties. She’s not really a ‘big fuss’ person. I was thinking more along the lines of a really lovely, personalised gift. I saw some ideas for photo albums, but not just a  normal  photo album, like, one with little captions explaining the stories behind the photos. Proper sentimental stuff. It's just…finding the photos is the hard bit. Dad’s hoarding is legendary.      Oh, your Dad. He’d keep receipts from 1987, wouldn’t he? Remember that time he tried to explain the historical significance of a bus ticket?      Don't even! He genuinely thought it was important. It was from the day he met Mum, apparently. Anyway, Pinterest also led me down a rabbit hole of ‘experience gifts’… hot air balloon rides, pottery classes. Mum attempting pottery…now  that  would be a sight.      Definitely. I'm terrible at gifts, honestly. I usually end up getting people socks or a book. Safe options. Have you spoken to Liam about it at all? He’s usually good at the thoughtful stuff.      Yeah, I texted him earlier. He suggested a spa day. Predictable Liam. But actually, not a bad shout. Mum deserves a bit of pampering. Actually, speaking of people, have you heard anything from Sarah lately? I haven't seen her since…well, ages.      Not much, no. I think she’s been really busy with work. She mentioned a big project, something to do with historical linguistics, actually. Sounds fascinating, but demanding. She did post something on Facebook about binge-watching that new crime drama, 'The Shadow Line'. Have you seen it?      Oh, aye, I started it! It's proper gripping, isn’t it? Really dark. Actually, it reminded me a bit of that series we all got into a few years back – 'Happy Valley'. Remember how obsessed we were?      Obsessed is an understatement. We were quoting Sarah Lancashire for weeks! Good shout on ‘The Shadow Line’ though, I might give it another go. I started it, got distracted by reading for my thesis, then completely forgot about it.

Oh, look at this one, David. Isn’t it  gorgeous ? It’s a proper Art Deco fitting, and the glass looks like it’s in really good condition. Only £85 with bidding still open. Hmm. It  is  nice. Bit…fussy for the hallway, though, don’t you think? Remember what happened with that chandelier your Aunt Mildred gave us? Dust trap extraordinaire. That was different! That was full-on rococo. This is…refined fussiness. And the hallway needs  something . It feels so…empty. Honestly, looking at these light fittings is far more productive than looking at houses, I think. Rightmove is just depressing. Everything is either a shoebox or requires a second mortgage and structural surveys. You say that now, but we agreed we need to get serious about the house search. We can’t keep putting it off. Little Timmy’s growing like a weed, and honestly, this place… it just doesn't  fit  anymore. One bathroom for a family of three is bordering on inhumane. I know, I know. You're right. It’s just… overwhelming. Every listing is “quirky” or “in need of modernisation,” which translates to damp and dodgy wiring. Did you see that one near Sevenoaks? "Charming cottage with original features." The photos showed wallpaper peeling off and a garden full of nettles. Oh, you've seen it. That's the one! They're very hopeful estate agents, aren't they? I was looking at a few around Guildford earlier. Slightly more…realistic. There’s a semi-detached with a decent garden, needs a kitchen update, asking for around £550k. £550k! Right. And then you add on stamp duty, solicitor’s fees, the inevitable repairs…we’d be utterly cleaned out. Honestly, sometimes I think we’re better off just extending. Extending is a nightmare, though. Planning permission, builders, living in a building site for six months… I'm not sure I'm strong enough for that again. Remember the kitchen remodel? I still have flashbacks. Oh, don't remind me. That was a dark time. Still, at least if we extended, we could get a proper ensuite. Think of the luxury! And maybe a bigger utility room. This space is perpetually chaotic. A utility room would be a  godsend . Okay, okay. Let's focus on Guildford for now. I'll filter Rightmove to show only properties with at least three bedrooms and two bathrooms, within a reasonable commute for me.

Honestly, this week at the hospital has been  mental . You wouldn't believe the state of Ward B. Staffing is down, again, and everyone is just…running on fumes. Old Mrs. Higgins tried to feed her biscuits to the oxygen tank again. Honestly, you could write a comedy, if it wasn't so heartbreaking.      Oh, bless her. She’s a character, isn’t she? Remember when she tried to elope with the delivery driver last year? It’s dreadful about the staffing though. Is it still that agency relying on last-minute bookings? They’re the worst. They never seem to send anyone who actually knows what they’re doing.      Yeah, I heard a rumour they lost a big contract. That's probably why. It's the same with the agency I'm signed up with for my bits and pieces. They promised me shifts at Bluebell House, you know, the fancy residential home? Then just…nothing. Ghosted, basically.      That's awful, darling. Still looking for something more permanent then? Tidying up after Mr. Peterson isn’t exactly a career move, is it? Though, to be fair, he  does  make a lovely cup of tea.      He does, you’ve got a point there. But no, still looking. I've applied for that admin job at the vets, ironically enough. Animals are less…demanding than some of my clients, let's just say.      Oh, the vet’s! Good thinking. It's a lovely practice. Old Mr. Davies is retiring though, isn’t he? I heard his daughter’s taking over. She seemed nice when I took Daisy for her boosters.      Daisy? How’s the little fluffball doing? Still shredding every single piece of post? I swear, she has a vendetta against Royal Mail.      Oh, she’s a menace! But a sweet menace. We had to hide the Christmas cards this year. Honestly, it looked like a blizzard had hit the living room. She thinks anything paper-based is a personal challenge. And she’s started barking at the vacuum cleaner again!      Classic Daisy. Animals are hilarious. Speaking of hilarious, Mum’s cat, Winston, tried to steal my roast chicken when I was visiting last weekend. He actually  jumped  onto the table. She wasn't impressed.      Winston! That cat is pure chaos. Your mum spoils him rotten. So, you’re still staying with her while you job hunt? It must be nice to have a home-cooked meal every now and then.

…Honestly, it’s remarkable what they’re finding out about sleep these days. I was reading an article this morning, apparently blue light isn’t the  whole  story. It’s more about the timing, and crucially, maintaining a consistent sleep schedule even on weekends. Apparently, that throws everything off.      Oh, really? You’d think after all this time, we’d have cracked the sleep code. I feel like I’ve tried everything. Cutting caffeine, lavender oil, blackout curtains… the whole shebang. Consistency? That’s a tough one with school holidays. They’re lovely, but utterly disruptive to any routine.      Exactly! The article highlighted that specifically. The body clock is brutal, isn't it? It's like a toddler - needs the same bedtimes, the same everything. Reminds me a bit of trying to navigate London with your insistence on 'shortcuts'.      Hey! Those weren’t  shortcuts , they were…alternative routes. And they usually added character! Remember that time in Rome? We were trying to get to the Trevi Fountain and ended up three streets back, staring at a rather aggressive pigeon?      Aggressive is an understatement. It practically dive-bombed you for a chip! And the map…oh, the map. You were convinced your internal compass was superior to the paper one. Honestly, you'd get lost in a phone box. It's a talent.      I maintain that the map was badly drawn! And at least the wandering led us to that amazing little trattoria. Sometimes getting lost is the best way to find the good stuff. Speaking of journeys, are you still planning that camping trip to the Lake District?      Definitely. Booked the site last week. Though, knowing my luck, and my inherent inability to read a compass – which I blame on growing up in Wellington and relying on landmarks – we’ll probably end up in Scotland.      You and navigation… it's a running joke. Remember when we tried to drive into Cambridge the first time? You insisted on bypassing the A14, and we ended up in a tiny village with no through road and a very confused farmer.      I thought I was being clever! Avoiding the traffic! The farmer was lovely, actually. Offered us tea. It was a valuable lesson in humility. And road planning. Anyway, that's nothing compared to some of the stories I've heard from pilots.      Oh? Pilots? What kind of stories?      An old contact of mine, Captain Davies, a commercial pilot for years, was telling me about a young co-pilot he had.

…and honestly, I still can’t believe Brenda thinks hamsters are ‘low maintenance’. Low maintenance?! They’re tiny, fluffy escape artists! She was complaining about cleaning the cage, like, it's a weekly thing, Bren!      She  is  a bit…optimistic about pet ownership. Remember when she got that goldfish and named it Captain? Captain lasted, what, three days? She said it “didn’t seem happy.”      Three days is generous. And she blamed the  water  for being sad. Said it lacked…personality. Honestly. It’s a fish, Brenda!      Ay, she's one of a kind, that one. But back to the hamsters, are you still worried about Winston? You were saying he’s been a bit off his food?      Yeah, just a little. He usually hoards everything like a tiny, furry dragon, but he left a sunflower seed untouched yesterday.  Untouched!  It’s a sign of the apocalypse, I’m telling you. I've been watching him like a hawk.      Don’t stress too much, love. Hamsters are notoriously dramatic. They probably just had a particularly good nap and aren’t feeling peckish.      Aye, they’re wee bundles of fluff and anxiety. Is he still running on his wheel like a maniac?      He is, thankfully. That’s the one thing that hasn’t changed. He runs for  hours . It’s like he’s training for the Hamster Olympics. It’s just… he seems a bit quieter overall. Less enthusiastic about stuffing his cheeks.      Maybe he’s just judging all our life choices. They’re secretly very discerning, you know.      You’re probably right. They’re little philosophers trapped in furry bodies. Speaking of discerning…have you seen the dating profile of that lad, Alex? He specifically said “no gingers apply.”      WHAT?! Seriously? In this day and age? That’s… unbelievable.      No way! That’s absolutely ridiculous. Is his profile still up? I need to screenshot that and send it to Twitter. The absolute cheek!      It was up last night. I saw it on Liam's phone. He was trying not to laugh, but he was failing miserably. He said it was under "Dealbreakers".      Honestly, people. It’s a hair colour. It’s genetic! It’s not a character flaw. I mean, I'm not a ginger, but that's just… prejudiced, isn’t it?      Proper daft, that is. I know loads of amazing gingers. It’s a beautiful colour, actually. Makes you stand out.

Honestly, this is brutal. You two are just systematically dismantling my entire South American continent. It's… it's a massacre.      Tactical brilliance, Geoff. Pure tactical brilliance. You left Australia completely undefended, remember? A cardinal sin in Risk, that.      Don't worry, Geoff. It’s just a game. Though, I  am  rather enjoying seeing you squirm. Reminds me of Aaron trying to assemble that flatpack bookshelf last Christmas. Utter chaos.      Aaron and flatpack furniture… a tragic pairing. He'd be better off conquering South America, honestly. At least  that  would give him a sense of control. Speaking of which, is anyone else utterly baffled by the new version of this game? The cards are different, the territories seem… shifted.      They did a minor update last year. Supposedly 'balancing' things. I think they just made it more confusing. Remember the old days? You could reliably hold Kamchatka and basically win. Now, everyone's swarming everywhere.      They always ‘balance’ things and it always makes it worse. It’s like they think we’re all Genghis Khan, planning world domination. Though, I did hear someone mispronounce ‘Kamchatka’ the other day. Called it ‘Kam-chat-kee’.      Oh, brilliant! Kam-chat-kee! I’ll be using that. Reminds me of that time I tried to order something in Mandarin on a business trip to China... disastrous. Completely butchered the tones.      China… That reminds me, Mum was talking about trying acupuncture for her back again. Says Western medicine just masks the pain, but Chinese medicine gets to the root cause.      Oh, she and that. She’s always going through phases. Last month it was essential oils, before that, crystals. Still, anything’s worth a go, I suppose. Though I have complete faith in Dr. Sharma, personally.      Faith in doctors is a good thing. Honestly, some of the things people try… you read these stories online. It's frightening. Remember that case a few years back about that couple who decided not to get a pregnancy test and just… waited?      Yeah, I remember. Actually, talking about that… Sarah – you remember Sarah from Uni? – she just messaged me. She’s… facing a difficult decision. Unexpected pregnancy.      Oh dear. That must be awful for her. Has she talked to anyone? Is she leaning towards keeping it?      It’s a really personal thing, isn't it? Morally, legally, ethically… there are so many layers. It’s not like the old days.

...Honestly, I'm starting to think I made a complete mess of picking my course. Marine Biology sounded  so  idyllic, you know? All Jacques Cousteau and dolphin research. Turns out it's mostly… staring at plankton under a microscope and writing essays about the mating habits of sea slugs. Not quite the adventure I signed up for.      You’re telling me! I thought Law would be all dramatic courtroom scenes like in  Suits . It's mostly reading. Just… endless reading. Mountains of it. And it’s really dry stuff, like property law. Property! Who gets excited about property law?      Exactly! It's the romanticising, isn’t it? We all get sold these amazing narratives, and the reality is… significantly less glamorous. Remember when we were obsessed with Millie Bobby Brown and thought being a child actor was the  dream ?      Oh god, don’t remind me. Now we know the horrifying stories about what that industry does to people. No, thanks. I’d rather wrestle with tort law. Still, at least Law feels like it  leads  somewhere, right? Like, you can actually  do  something with it. What about you? Is there anything in Marine Bio you actually enjoy?      The field trips are alright, I suppose. Being out on the boat is good. But even then, half the time I'm seasick. And everyone keeps asking what I’m going to  do  with it. “Oh, you want to save the whales?” Yeah, great. How about I get a job first? My mum's already dropping hints about teacher training. "Steady income, darling, think of the pension!"      The pension talk. The ultimate parental weapon. My nan’s been on about me becoming a solicitor since Year Seven. She thinks it’s the height of sophistication. “Think of the houses, love!” She’s got a point, I guess, but… I don't know if I can face another three years of this.      It's just… scary, isn't it? Thinking about the rest of our lives. Everyone else seems to have it figured out. Posting careers on Instagram. Like, "Just landed my dream job at Google!" with a picture of their fancy office.      Instagram is a lie! My cousin’s ‘dream job’ involves making tea for people who  actually  work at Google. She's miserable. Honestly, I’m starting to think just… not having kids and travelling sounds pretty appealing.      Ooh, now  that’s  a thought.

...Honestly, Mr. Davies is  obsessed  with consumerism for this project. Like, everything has to be framed around advertising and planned obsolescence. It's exhausting. We’re supposed to be looking at societal issues, not just how much rubbish companies churn out.      Tell me about it. He practically had a meltdown when I suggested we focus on, like, the impact of food banks. He said it was “too sensitive” and “lacked analytical distance.” Analytical distance? Seriously? It's people being hungry, mate.      Exactly! It’s Slough, Raj! We  see  it. It’s not some abstract concept. My nan relies on the food bank sometimes, you know? She's too proud to admit it, but I know. It's proper stressful for her.      Wow, I didn’t know that. That’s rough. My uncle lost his job last year, things were tight for a while. It makes you think, doesn’t it? All this talk about the economy 'improving', but who is it improving  for ? We're learning about GDP in economics, but it feels disconnected from what’s actually happening to people.      Totally. And Davies is going on about how advertising ‘drives innovation’ and ‘creates jobs’. It's like he's swallowed a marketing brochure whole. I tried to bring up the ethical implications, the mental health aspect, how it makes people feel inadequate… he just waved his hand and said I was being “melodramatic.”      Classic Davies. He loves a good dismissal. Did you tell him about that documentary we watched, the one about planned obsolescence in tech? The one where they showed how phones are deliberately designed to slow down after a couple of years?      Yeah! I mentioned it. He said it was “conspiracy theorising” and that companies are just “responding to market demands.” It's infuriating! It's not a conspiracy if it’s, like, demonstrably happening. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if he even  believes  what he's teaching.      Maybe he just doesn’t want to rock the boat? Teachers get a lot of… pressure. Still, it’s a bit rubbish. What are you thinking of doing for the presentation anyway? Can you at least steer it towards a slightly more meaningful angle?      I'm trying. I was thinking we could focus on how advertising targets vulnerable groups – kids, low-income families… show how it perpetuates inequality. But I'm worried he’ll shoot it down.      Worth a shot. We could even link it back to poverty, explain how it makes people feel like they  need  stuff they can’t afford.

...Honestly, the whole recording process was a nightmare. Trying to get a decent vocal take when Mrs. Higgins next door decided  that  was the moment to practice her tuba? It was beyond frustrating. I nearly lost it.      Oh, Mrs. Higgins and that tuba. Right. She’s… dedicated, isn’t she? I heard it through the walls the other day. Sounded like a dying walrus. What were you recording anyway? Still the Shakespearean sonnets?      Yes, still the sonnets. For that little online course I’m doing. It's supposed to be relaxing, a creative outlet. Relaxing until the brass section of Higgins’ orchestra decides to rehearse. I’m starting to think I need soundproofing, which is utterly ridiculous. Though, come to think of it, that might actually help with other things… like the creaking in my knees when I get up.      Tell me about it. I tried to do some gardening yesterday - just weeding, honestly - and I was practically crawling back inside. My back’s been playing up something awful. I really need to book a physiotherapy appointment. Remember how good that was last year?      Oh, yes! Old Mr. Davies. He worked wonders on my hip. It’s just… getting myself  to  the appointments. And then finding the energy for the exercises he gives you. It’s all these bad joints, isn’t it? It's like living in a constantly protesting machine.      It is. It makes you feel… old, doesn't it? Even  thinking  about exercise. I used to be able to run around all day with no problem. Now, even just walking to the shops feels like a marathon.      Don’t beat yourself up about it, dear. It happens. We're not getting any younger, are we? Speaking of feeling less than energetic, I tried on that new dress I bought for Aunt Mildred's birthday… it’s… snug.      Snug is a kind word. I haven't even bothered trying to find anything remotely presentable for ages. Everything feels too tight, or just… wrong. I ended up just grabbing the first thing I found that wasn’t covered in cat hair.      Cat hair is a constant battle! Honestly, I’ve considered shaving Winston. But he’d never forgive me. Anyway, regarding the dress… I'm thinking a diet is in order. Again. I've tried them all, haven't I? Keto, Paleo, juice cleanses…      You and a million other people.

Right, this sauce needs a good whizzin’ – honestly, ANON’s kitchen is lovely but their utensils are… lacking. No proper wooden spoons, just a load of silicone things. Feels wrong, doesn't it? Like tryin’ to build a dry stone wall with bubble wrap.      You and your Yorkshire traditions! It’ll taste the same, won’t it? Though, I do see your point about the spoons. Silicone’s a bit…slippery. Are you sure you’ve added enough chilli flakes? ANON’s a bit of a wimp when it comes to spice.      Aye, I put a good pinch in. Enough to give it a bit of a kick, but not enough to set their hair on fire. Though, honestly, they were complaining the last time I made a curry it was  too  mild. You can’t win, can you? It’s all relative, innit?      It is. They're just…particular. How’s the job going, anyway? Still drowning in conference proposals and dietary requirements? Last I heard you were battling a vegan, gluten-free, nut-allergy crisis for the textile convention.      Don't even  start  me on the textile convention. Honestly, that was a nightmare. Turns out “vegan” for some people means “I’ll only eat things grown within a five-mile radius and blessed by a shaman.” I spent three days cross-referencing farm locations and spiritual practices. It was… intense. This week's better, thankfully. It's a smaller tech summit, mostly just working out logistics and chasing speakers for their presentation slides.      Sounds marginally less stressful. Although, tech people can be just as demanding, just in a different way. All about the AV setup and the perfect lighting for their Zoom backgrounds.      You’re spot on there. Honestly. It's always  something . What about you? Still wrestling with production schedules and supply chain chaos? You made it sound pretty hairy last time we spoke.      It… it’s stabilised  slightly . Things are still delayed, and the prices of everything are ridiculous, but we've managed to secure alternative suppliers for some of the key components. It involved a lot of late nights and a frankly terrifying spreadsheet, but we’re getting there. Keeps me busy, though, which I suppose is a good thing. Trying to remember to actually  live  outside of work is the hard part.      Tell me about it. I feel like all I do is email and coordinate.

Right, okay, so we  have  to settle this. Everyone’s been dropping hints all evening - what’s the best film of the last, like, five years? No historical dramas, no black and white classics, modern stuff only.      Ooh, good shout! Five years… that’s narrowing it down. I'm gonna throw  Everything Everywhere All at Once  into the ring immediately. Honestly, mind-blowing.      Aye, that was… a lot. Visually fantastic, definitely, but a bit much for me, if I'm honest. Too frantic. I reckon  The Banshees of Inisherin  was better. Darkly funny, beautifully shot, Colin Farrell was superb. Proper acting, that.      Ooh,  Banshees  is a good one. Really good performances. But I think you're both forgetting  Parasite . It came out just before the five-year mark, maybe, but it had such a massive impact. And it’s a brilliant social commentary, isn’t it? Plus, the twists!       Parasite  is amazing! My media class did a whole unit on it. But… I'm gonna go for something a bit different.  Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse . Animation that's genuinely groundbreaking. And it’s just…fun! Sometimes you need a bit of fun.      Oooh, biscuits have arrived. And a film debate!  Spider-Verse  is solid, I’ll give you that. But for sheer emotional impact, I’m going with  Past Lives . It absolutely wrecked me. The subtlety, the unspoken feelings… it was just beautiful.      Okay, we’re getting somewhere. Right, so we’ve got  Everything Everywhere ,  Banshees ,  Parasite ,  Spider-Verse  and  Past Lives . Quite a diverse bunch, actually. I think… I liked  Everything Everywhere  a lot. It was just so creative and heartwarming, despite all the chaos. Michelle Yeoh deserved every award she got.      Totally agree about Michelle Yeoh! And it was just such a unique story. It tackled so many big themes, but in a really accessible way. It didn't feel preachy.      See, I just found it overwhelming. Like they threw everything at the wall and hoped some of it stuck.  Banshees  had a focus, a clear story. Pádraic and Colm's ridiculous feud… it was brilliant commentary on loneliness and pride. Plus, the landscapes of Ireland are stunning.      But  Parasite  was just so clever. The way they built up the tension, the symbolism… and the rain! The rain was  essential  to the story.      I just think animation gets overlooked sometimes.  Spider-Verse  wasn’t just visually stunning; the story was really strong too.

Honestly, I think my feet are  still  recovering. Paris is beautiful, don’t get me wrong, but so much walking!      Oh darling, you look exhausted! Was it good though? Tell me everything. And careful with that bag, you’ll knock over the fruit bowl.      Paris sounds amazing! I was stuck on the ward all weekend – a particularly… lively set of patients. How was it, Chloe? Did you manage to get to the Eiffel Tower?      It was…an experience. The Eiffel Tower was, predictably, swarming. We did go up, though. And yes, Mum, everything’s relatively intact. The fruit bowl is safe. It was mostly the cobbled streets that murdered my feet. I swear, I walked about ten miles each day.      Cobblestones. Nasty things, those. I remember twisting my ankle on those in Rome years ago. Ended up hobbling around for the rest of the holiday. Did you at least get some decent pastries? That’s what Paris is  for , really.      Oh, the pastries were phenomenal. Seriously, I think I gained about five pounds just in croissants and pain au chocolat. And we had this amazing little bistro near the hotel… But, honestly, there was one slight disaster.      Disaster? What happened? Don’t tell me you lost your passport!      No, worse, in a way. I managed to trip… over absolutely nothing, on the Metro. Just completely lost my balance and went flying.      Oh, Chloe! Are you alright? Did you hurt yourself?      I'm fine now, honestly. Just bruised my ego, mostly. But I scraped my knee pretty badly. It looked like something out of a horror film. Luckily, Lucy – you remember Lucy, from uni? She came with me – Lucy is a  whizz  with first aid. She’s training to be a paramedic, so she had antiseptic wipes and bandages in her bag.      Lucy, right! The one who’s always rescuing stray animals? Good on her for being prepared. I always carry plasters, being around patients and all, but antiseptic wipes never crossed my mind.      That Lucy sounds a treasure. It’s good to have someone like that with you when you're gallivanting about in foreign cities. I’m glad you're okay though, dear. Tripping on the Metro sounds…undignified, to say the least.      Undignified is an understatement. There were people staring! But Lucy was brilliant. She patched me up and then made me promise to walk slower. Speaking of promises, promise me you’ll never let me near a cobbled street again?

Morning, Chloe! You look… relatively awake for a Monday. Which is a feat in itself.      Liam! You have  no  idea. Fireworks last night kept me up until, honestly, ridiculous o'clock. Some local display, apparently. Sounded like a warzone. How was your weekend? Anything more peaceful than explosions?      Significantly. Went back to Bedford to see my mum and dad. Standard stuff – roast dinner, complaints about the weather, the usual. It was nice, though. They’re already asking about Christmas plans. It’s October! You going anywhere for half-term?      Probably not. I’m trying to be sensible, actually. Save up. Pay day is… well, it feels like ages away. Supervisor life doesn’t exactly come with a huge salary, you know? Especially with looming tuition fees from my Master’s. How’s the TEFL life? Still battling passive voice with the international students?      Oh,  always  battling the passive voice. It’s a constant struggle. Honestly, sometimes I wonder if the British National Corpus was secretly designed to torment English language instructors. I’m trying to get them to understand the nuances, but… it’s hard. I'm grading a pile of essays on creative writing too, which is a nice change, but oh, the referencing. It’s a disaster!      Ugh, referencing. Don’t even get me started. I was helping my little brother with his undergraduate degree essay last week, and it was a nightmare. He’s doing history, and the sheer volume of sources... I felt a migraine coming on. He’s thinking of doing a novel, actually. Big ambitions!      That's brilliant! Has he always been into writing? My sister tried a novel once, got about fifty pages in, then decided divorce lawyers were more fascinating. Speaking of which, how are things with… oh, shoot, did I just put my foot in it?      It’s… complicated. Ex-boyfriend’s getting married. Found out through Facebook, naturally. Very theatrical proposal, apparently. He's always been a bit of a showman. Likes musicals. You wouldn’t believe.      Oh, yikes. That  is  complicated. I’m so sorry. Facebook is the worst for things like that. Look, distraction time. Have you ever been to Chichester?      Chichester? Briefly. Just passing through on a coach trip years ago. Why?      There’s a fantastic theatre there. I was thinking about going to see something next weekend. I’m desperate for some culture that  doesn’t  involve student essays or the complexities of Malaysian dialects.

Right, so  this  is why Mum always insists on doing the rice. It's not just about having time, it's about…not ending up with glue. Honestly, it’s a skill.      Glue, you say? Dramatic, aren't you? I managed rice perfectly well once, ages ago. Before Leo came along and my brain turned to mush.      Once? That’s… optimistic. Remember Auntie Carol’s curry night? The rice was…structural. You could have built a small house with it.      Oh, don't remind me! She was mortified. Still, the curry was amazing. Speaking of, what are we having with this…potentially glue-like rice? Is it the leftover chicken curry?      Yeah, the curry. Found the voucher for “Spice Paradise” in Mum’s purse, actually. Thought we could use it next week, but saving it for when Leo's not teething seems sensible. Honestly, the screaming when we tried to eat out last time… it wasn't a vibe.      No, definitely not. A quiet night in is bliss. And that Spice Paradise voucher is a lifesaver. It’s practically extortionate eating out these days. Everything's so…fancy. And full of salt. I’ve been trying to be better about checking labels, you know, for Leo.      Salt is the enemy. Hidden salt is the  real  enemy. I read an article about how much salt is in ready-made curry paste. It’s insane. And fat. And sometimes, inexplicably, jalapenos. I don’t understand the jalapeno obsession.      Right? Like, why put a fiery surprise in something that’s supposed to be comforting? Speaking of things that are a bit off-putting… did you see that documentary about people with facial deformities? Awful. Really brought it home how lucky we are and…      Yeah, I did. It was… intense. Makes you think, doesn't it? About what 'normal' even  is . It reminded me a bit of that time we were on holiday in Cornwall and saw that jellyfish washed up on the beach. All… translucent and strange.      Oh,  that  one! It looked like a ghostly handbag. Poor thing. Leo would've been fascinated. He's obsessed with anything remotely watery. Though probably not if it stung him.      Probably not. Right, rice check. Looking…slightly less alarming. It’s the timing that gets me. Mum always says it’s a ‘feel’ thing, which is incredibly unhelpful.      A ‘feel’ thing? Mothers and their feelings! Honestly. Is the chicken still alright, by the way?

...Honestly, the amount of coursework they’re piling on this year is ridiculous. I feel like I’m just  living  in the library. It's all essays and readings, and barely any actual…doing.      Aye, tell me about it. Sounds proper draining. Though, t’be fair, at least ye’re  doing  summat. I've spent most of today attemptin' to get owt on Indeed. Same old story, though. “Experience required.” Experience  how  am I supposed to get experience if nobody’ll give me a chance?      It’s a catch-22, isn’t it? But you've got a good degree, Liam. Don’t get disheartened. Have you tried tailoring your CV to each job, highlighting transferable skills? Sometimes that makes a difference.      Tried, Jen, tried. They all want summat specific. "Proficient in data analysis." Like I've just been sat at 'ome, analysin' data for fun. I did a bit volunteerin' at the food bank last year, put that on, but…doesn't seem to cut it.      Food bank is good! Shows initiative. Maybe you’re aiming too high straight away? Have you thought about applying for entry-level roles, even if they aren't exactly what you want to do long-term? Just to get a foot in the door?      Aye, I've seen a couple of those. Retail stuff mostly. Doesn't exactly scream "utilise my psychology degree," does it? And the pay… well, you know. It's not like I can move out anytime soon at that rate.      Don't be too proud, Liam. A job's a job, right? And proper retail experience can be useful, even if it’s just for learning how to deal with people. Plus, it wouldn't hurt to have some money of your own. Mum and Dad aren't getting any younger, you know.      That's a fair point, Chloe. But I think Liam’s worried about being…stuck. Feeling like he’s wasted his time at uni.      That’s a big part of it, aye. All that student debt for what? To be stackin' shelves? I was hopin' for summat a bit…more. I saw an advert for a support worker role, somethin' with mental health. Thought that might be a good fit, but it required a driving license. Mine expired ages ago, and retakin’ the test… well, it costs a fortune, doesn’t it?      Oof, yeah, it does. I’m still learning with my auntie.

This is proper good, this. Your shepherd’s pie’s always been a winner, ANON. Proper comforting. It's a world away from conference centre buffet food, that’s for sure.      Glad you like it, lass. It's a bit of a family recipe, passed down. Though, I haven’t made it for a good while now, to be honest. Not much point cookin’ for just one, is there? Makes a change havin’ someone else ‘round to enjoy it.      Aye, it does. It’s nice to… just  be  somewhere that doesn't smell faintly of disinfectant and stale coffee. How are you keepin' busy, though? Since… well, you know. Since you packed it all in.      Busy? That’s a laugh. Not particularly. Days bleed into each other, truth be told. I potter about a bit. Used to enjoy a bit of gardening, but my back isn’t what it was. Tried Tai Chi, down at the village hall, but it wasn’t really for me. Too much… floatin' about. Not enough get-up-and-go.      Oh, Tai Chi! That sounds a bit… peaceful? I’m already knackered just thinkin’ about it. I’ve been tryin’ to get back into running, since that half marathon last year. But work's been a right slog lately, and I just can't seem to find the energy after a twelve-hour shift.      A half marathon? Blimey, you’re a fit one! I used to walk a lot, years ago. Little rambles around the South Downs. But even  that  feels like a monumental effort now. What's got you so tied up at work? Still doin’ all the conferences and weddings and whatnot?      More or less. It’s the  organising  that’s killin' me, though. We had that tech conference last week… honestly, the demands! Everyone wants somethin' different. Vegan options, gluten-free options, specific brand of mineral water… and then someone complained the Wi-Fi wasn't fast enough for their livestream. Honestly! It's all a bit much.      Sounds stressful. People are so particular these days, aren't they? Back when I was y’know,  workin’  - which wasn't that long ago, relatively - things were simpler. You did a job, you got paid. No one bothered you with all this fuss.      Definitely a different world. It’s alright when it's a nice wedding, and you see everyone havin’ a good time, then you think ‘yeah, I helped make that happen.’

Right, that was…substantial. Honestly, I think I ate my weight in roast potatoes. Anyone want help with these, or are you all strategically positioned for maximum sofa access?      I’m good, thanks Mum. Just… finishing something.      I’ll grab the plates, love. Though I might need a lie down after that. It was delicious, honestly. You outdid yourself.      Yeah, really good. Did you see that Federer match earlier? Incredible comeback.      Oh, Federer! Yes, I caught the last set. He's still got it, doesn't he? Such elegance. It’s a shame he’s retiring, though. It feels like the end of an era. Speaking of eras... did either of you finish that history homework about the 1930s?      Ugh,  Hitler . Why do we have to learn about  him ? It’s just… depressing.      It’s important to understand how these things happen, son. How someone like that can rise to power. It’s not just about memorizing dates, it’s about learning from the past.      Mr. Henderson said it’s about recognizing the signs. Propaganda, scapegoating… stuff like that.      Exactly. It’s terrifyingly relevant, even now. Though, switching to slightly less terrifying topics… David, your facial hair is looking… ambitious.      Ambitious is one word for it. Your father is going through a mid-life crisis manifested as a beard, apparently.      It’s not a mid-life crisis! It’s… a stylistic choice. And it’s itching terribly.      It looks like a badger tried to build a nest on your face, Dad. No offense.      Harsh, but accurate.      Very funny. Anyway, I noticed you’ve been spending a lot of time on Instagram, Leo. Everything alright? I saw a  lot  of pictures of… Chloe.      Mum!      Chloe, eh? Is that the girl from school? The one with the… excellent taste in music?      She likes the same bands as me. So yeah.      That’s lovely, dear. But remember to be careful online. It's easy to get carried away, and you don't want to say or do anything you’ll regret. And please, for the love of all that is holy, don't send her pictures of… well, anything questionable.      Mum's got you sussed, Leo.      I didn’t even  send  her anything! I just… liked her post. It was a picture of a cat.      A very discerning cat, I presume?      Just be sensible. And Leo, make sure you’re still getting your schoolwork done.

Right, nearly there then. Honestly, that traffic getting  out  of High Lane was a nightmare. Worth it though, to get a proper look at that sofa at Barker & Stonehouse. You think it’ll fit, don't you, love? I’m starting to have doubts.      Mum, you worry too much. You measured, didn’t you? Twice? It'll be fine. Though, honestly, if we ended up having to take the legs off… that's a faff. More faff than a trip to the tip, and you  know  how I feel about the tip.      Oh, don't start on the tip, lass. Your grandma used to say the tip was a reflection of your soul. A messy tip, a messy life. Though looking at her spare room… she wasn’t one to talk.      Your grandma, bless her, saw meaning in everything. Remember when she thought Mr. Henderson from next door was deliberately mowing his lawn to annoy her?      Oh god, yes! The lawn wars. That was legendary. Speaking of legendary… how’s Sarah doing? I haven't spoken to her since… well, since she told me about Mark. It’s awful, isn’t it?      Poor love. He’s really not well at all, is he? She's holding it together, but you can tell it's exhausting. She said he had another… episode last week. Forgetting things, getting confused. It’s frightening.      It is. My sister, Margaret, her husband… started just like that. A little forgetting at first. Then… well, then it became something else entirely. Dementia's a cruel thing, a truly cruel thing.      It's just… it feels so quick. They only got married a few years ago. She’s utterly devoted to him. I offered to help with bits and pieces, picking up groceries, things like that. But she’s so fiercely independent.      She is. Remember when she wouldn't let anyone wash her clothes? Said only she knew how to get the whites  properly  white?      Oh, goodness, yes! She was convinced everyone else ruined everything. And remember her mum, always offering unsolicited advice?      Ah, Brenda. A force of nature, that woman. Always had an opinion, and wasn't afraid to share it. Though she did make a cracking trifle. Still, she was a bit… intense about family gatherings. “Are you  sure  you’ve eaten enough, love?”      They’re all a bit… intense, our family, aren’t they? Even Uncle George, seemingly placid as he is, has his moments.

...Honestly, Mum, the whole thing’s just felt so… precarious lately. Like walking on eggshells. They’ve been ‘restructuring’ for months, but this morning, old Mr. Henderson called me into his office.      Oh, no. Don’t tell me… You’ve been made redundant? I had a feeling something was up, you’ve been awfully quiet these past few weeks. Is that why you were so off your food at dinner last Sunday? I thought it was just stress with that presentation.      Yeah, pretty much. Redundancy. They’re saying it’s a ‘streamlining of roles’ and ‘efficiency savings’. Corporate buzzwords, basically. I’m gutted, though. I actually liked the job, and I was getting good at it. Project co-ordinating wasn't glamorous, but it was  something .      Oh, sweetheart. I’m so sorry. That's dreadful. You’ve worked so hard to get where you are, with that degree and all. It’s not a reflection on you, these companies just… they do what they do. Have they given you a package? Severance and everything?      A fairly standard one, apparently. Three months’ salary, help with job hunting, the usual. It’s not  nothing , but it’s not exactly a cushion, is it? Especially with the house deposit… we were hoping to start seriously looking after Christmas.      Right, well, we’ll figure something out. Don’t you worry about the deposit just yet. We can talk about that. Honestly, it'll be alright. Let's focus on you finding something even  better . Are you going to the gym tonight to blow off steam?      I was thinking about it. Needed to, actually. Just hit something hard, you know? Though thinking about it, I’m proper craving fish and chips. Comfort food is calling my name. Definitely not going to be sticking to my healthy eating plan tonight.      Oh, go on then! Treat yourself. You deserve it. Fish and chips sound lovely, actually. Perhaps we could get some in for Grandad later? He's been asking after you. Said he’s starting to forget where he put his glasses… again.      Oh, bless him. Definitely. I’ll give him a call later. He always manages to cheer me up. Remember when he tried to build that birdhouse last summer? It looked like a miniature leaning tower of Pisa!      Oh, don’t remind me! He was so proud of it, even though it nearly fell apart in the first breeze.

Right, dinner's nearly ready. Peas and fish fingers… a culinary masterpiece, I know. Leo, darling, please stop trying to build a tower out of your peas and  actually  eat some.      But Mum, it's… structural engineering. It needs a solid base. And fish fingers are boring.      Structural engineering? Leo, you're eleven. And boring is better than leaving perfectly good food to go cold. You were saying earlier you were really into that ‘Stick with Mick’ programme? Is that still a thing?      Yeah! It's brilliant. He goes on loads of adventures, even though he’s, like, really small. And he’s always building stuff. It’s kinda like… real structural engineering, actually.      Well, there you go then. Inspiration. Right, what are we doing tomorrow? Summer holidays are stretching out ahead of us like… well, a really long fish finger. We need a plan.      Ba! Mick! Ba!      He wants to watch Mick, obviously. But then what? I was thinking maybe going swimming? The pool’s open now, isn’t it?      It is. That’s a good shout. Though last time, you spent most of the time trying to teach Finn how to do a handstand in the shallow end. Which didn't go down well with the lifeguard.      He was  almost  getting it! And it was funny. He just… splashed everyone. But after swimming… I don’t know. Ben and Alfie are going to the skatepark. I asked if I could come, but Ben’s older brother was going too, and he always makes me feel rubbish. He’s learning Japanese and everything.      Japanese? Goodness me. That  is  impressive. He sounds like a little whiz kid. Maybe you could learn an instrument instead? You've got that guitar gathering dust in the corner.      Ugh, the guitar. I tried. It’s hard! My fingers hurt. And Mrs. Davies, the guitar teacher, keeps saying things like “articulate your notes” and I don’t even know what that  means .      It means play clearly, darling. It takes practice. Look, what about helping me with some jobs around the house? We could tackle the garden. It’s a jungle out there.      No way. Gardening is even  more  boring than fish fingers. Seriously.      Daa! Garden!      See? Finn agrees. Though I suspect his agreement is based purely on the joy of flinging food. What about… I don't know. You said you wanted to spend more time with your friends this summer.

Right, that bit was  brilliant . Properly unsettling. Reminds me a bit of that film ‘Under the Skin’ - all atmosphere and dread, not much explaining.      Aye, it's good. Bit slow burn, mind. You need to be in the mood for that kinda thing. Not like a Marvel blockbuster, needing constant explosions, eh? Speaking of needing things… I really need to book a dentist appointment. My wisdom tooth is giving me absolute hell.      Ugh, dentists. The absolute worst. I put mine off for, like, five years. Ended up needing a root canal. It wasn’t a fun week. Is it the pain, or just the… looming dentist-ness that’s getting you?      It's both, honestly. The dull ache is bad enough, but the  thought  of someone poking about in my mouth… gives me the shivers. They always ask if you want the radio on, like that's going to distract you from the drilling.      Yeah, like a bit of Radio 1 will magically erase the sound of metal scraping against enamel. Classic. You should go to that one down by the docks, Dr. Anya Sharma. She’s… surprisingly good. Doesn't judge you for your terrible flossing habits.      Good to know! I've been avoiding them all. Anyway, enough about my terrifying dental future. What you been writing lately? Still chipping away at that novel?      Trying to. It’s…stuck. I've got this whole subplot with a character who's obsessed with Citibikes – those hire bikes you get in cities - but I can't quite make it land. It feels… random. It's supposed to symbolize his fleeting sense of freedom, but it just seems like he really likes cycling.      Maybe that  is  all it is! Sometimes you overthink things. What's the book about again? Remind me. It's been ages since you properly told me about it.      It's set… mostly in Berlin.
